# Drone Dash: round 34 critic report

**Verdict:** Pass on all six items. The unstyled flash is gone. The bus push is smooth. Desktop pops leave the drone. The golden and dusk water at 1 m is clearly crisper. No regression found.

Build tested: commit 05cd223 (round 34). Control: an untouched export of commit 56353fb (round 33). My servers: 5191 (round 34 dev), 5192 (round 33 control dev, own Vite cache), 5193 (round 34 production preview). All three are stopped. The owner's server on 5188 was left alone. Note: my 5191 server shares `node_modules/.vite` with 5188 and re-optimized the deps once at start. If 5188 asked for a reload around 20:33, that was me.

Every browser ran alone, one job at a time, from `critic-scripts/queue34.sh` and `jobs34.txt`. I did not read `builder.md`. I read the diffs only to learn what to test. Bulk shots went to the session scratchpad. The chosen ones are in `critic/`.

New scripts in `progress/round-34/critic-scripts/`:

- `fouc34.mjs`: cold load (fresh context), 2 s. A rAF sampler checks every painted frame: is `#app` visible before `styles.css` applies? Plus a CDP screencast of every frame.
- `load34.mjs`: cold production load. Time to Play button, game code, street assets. Bytes moved. Then Play, and long tasks and new shaders after Play.
- `playearly34.mjs`, `playearly34b.mjs`: press Play as early as possible on a cold production load.
- `hud-probe34.mjs` + `pop34-init.js`: hud-probe28 plus every pop against the real drone box and every HUD box, every 50 ms.
- `perf-street34.mjs`: perf-street with `UNCAP=1` (no vsync, no frame cap), so frame time is the real cost.
- `bt34.py`: from boattrace33, the largest single-frame move beyond the drone's own speed.
- `ab34.py`: blind A/B, water (6) and street (6).
- `route-play-r33c.mjs`: the street medal bot pointed at the round 33 control.
- Changed copies: `water31.mjs` (tags r34 / r33c, files `water34-*`), `cruise33*.mjs` (tags), `contrast31.py` (reads the scratch folder). All `.mjs` take `OUTDIR`.

## Machine load

At the start: XprotectService 43% (perf), coreaudiod 11% (boats), Brave 70% (HUD runs), WindowServer under 25% elsewhere. During the street medal run, knowledgeconstructiond (92%) and duetexpertd (75%) were busy (`cpu-medal.txt`). Fixed-step probes do not care. The real-time medal bot does (see Regressions).

# Drone Dash: round 34 builder notes

Build: the round 34 work, not committed, on top of 56353fb (round 33).
Control: an export of 56353fb (git archive into my scratchpad) on port 5193.
My servers: 5190 served a snapshot copy of the working tree (all regression jobs). 5195 served the working tree (quick looks).
4193 and 4194 ran `vite preview` of the two production builds (round 33 and round 34). All are stopped.
I did not touch the owner's server on 5188. Every browser job ran alone, one at a time, from `builder-scripts/queue34.sh`
and `jobs34.txt` (log in `queue34.log`).

Scripts: I copied the critic scripts of rounds 25, 31, 32 and 33 into `builder-scripts/`. I changed only the ports
(5191 -> 5190, control 5192 -> 5193) and the output folders (`../builder-shots/`). Tags: `water31.mjs` writes
`water33-r34-*` and `water33-r33c-*`, `contrast31.py` reads them. New:

- `boattrace34.mjs`: boattrace33 with a 150-frame trace and a `SNAP` line per hover run (largest per-frame move beyond the drone's own speed, in m).
- `trisweep34.mjs`: trisweep31 plus a draw-call histogram and the draw calls per mesh at every spot with 119 calls or more.
- `breakdown34.mjs`: copy of my round 33 per-mesh breakdown.
- `waterlow34.mjs`: only the low water views, for tuning (shots went to the scratchpad).
- `ff34.mjs`: ff29 with a PORT option. `firstload34.mjs`: first load of a production build (bytes, timings, long tasks after Play).
- `ab34.py`: the critic's ab33.py for round 33 against round 34 (water pairs at full width). The key is written before judging.

Machine load: the Mac was restarted, no Bluetooth hog. CPU snapshots are in `cpu-*.txt`.
One stretch around 07:03 to 07:13 ran slow: the headless browser fell to about 60 frames a second. The round 33 control ran
just as slow back to back (`fr-d-58-r33c-b.log`: median 16.0 ms, mine `fr-d-58-b.log`: 16.6 ms), so that was the machine.
The final batch ran at the normal 8.3 ms median.


## 1. Desktop pops over the drone: fixed

**Cause.** On desktop all centre messages sat on the centre line (39% and 50% down). The drone sits on the centre line too.
The payout pop (`#slip-pop`) and the medal banner covered it most often.

**Fix** (`Hud.ts`, `Game.ts`, `styles.css`). Desktop now gets a pop slot like the round 24 phone slot:

- `Game.updateDeskPop` gives the HUD the drone's screen box every frame (centre projected, size from the distance, the same estimate as the touch framing).
- `Hud.deskPlace` puts the pop that is up just left of the drone, level with it. Its right edge stays 26 px clear of the drone box (it allows for the 1.15 pop-in scale).
- The slot starts right of the edge marker. It stays below the score panel and above the bottom meters and the view hint. The pop's rise as it fades is allowed for.
- While a pop is up it eases after the drone. Small moves are ignored, so the text does not shake.
- The HUD boxes are measured every 300 ms. The HUD measures the pop size one time, at show time. There is no layout read per frame.
- The objective pill and the centre column are untouched. Touch layout is unchanged.

**Test**: `hud-probe28.mjs` (the round 24/25 method: real DOM rects of the 4 pop elements against `droneBox()`,
every visible drone vertex through the render camera). Desktop, new player, 80 s low line.

| Seed | Round 33 (control, 5193) | Round 34 (first run) | Round 34 (final batch) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 22 | 23.1% (79 of 342) | 0.66% (2 of 301) | 0.33% (1 of 300) |
| 58 | 33.9% (87 of 257) | 0.74% (2 of 269) | 0.00% (0 of 284) |
| 130 | 29.9% (92 of 308) | 0.00% (0 of 255) | 0.33% (1 of 307) |

Pops over the controls 0, pops over the top panels 0, drone under a pill 0, other HUD on the drone 0, in every run.
The few hits left are a medal banner, an event banner or a delivery pop while the drone swings across the screen.
Shots: `builder-shots/hud34-d-22-payout-beside-drone.jpg` and `hud34-d-58-payout-beside-drone.jpg` (the payout pop beside the drone).
Round 33 control for comparison: `hud33c-d-22-payout-chain.jpg`.

## 2. Harbour bus snaps the drone sideways: fixed

**Cause.** `Drone.update`: when a boat's bow or stern pushed the drone, the code moved the drone's position sideways by
`(boat speed + 2) x 5 steps` in one sub-step. That is 0.55 m in one frame, and it repeated at every new contact.

**Fix** (`Drone.ts`). The sideways carry is now a velocity, not a position jump:

- At a bow or stern contact the drone gets a slide direction and a slide speed. The slide speed is the boat speed + 2 m/s, within the round 33 cap.
- For 0.3 s after the last contact, the slide speed is held after the lateral grip, and the grip does not eat it. It eases out in the last 0.12 s.
- The hull's own push-out (the drone leaves the face at least as fast as the face moves) is unchanged. The round 33 speed cap is unchanged.

**Test**: `boattrace34.mjs` (hover runs: the boat runs into a parked drone, 150 frames after first contact).
"Worst move" is the largest per-frame move beyond the drone's own speed.

| Run | Round 33 (control) | Round 34 |
|---|---|---|
| Bus, 2 m, seeds 4711 / 22 | 0.475 / 0.475 m | 0.012 / 0.012 m |
| Bus, 1 m, seeds 4711 / 22 | 0.421 / 0.457 m | 0.008 / 0.010 m |
| Sailboat, 0.9 m (4 runs) | 0.28 to 0.35 m | 0.001 to 0.013 m |
| Longest contact, bus hover | 11 to 45 frames | 20 to 22 frames |

All under the 0.15 m bar. The peak effective speed after a bus contact fell from 33.8 m/s to 7.3 m/s.
The drone's own speed peaks at 6.6 m/s (the cap: boat speed 4.6 + 2). The hull's push-out adds the last 0.7 m/s.
The sailboat hover runs on seed 4711 still reach 9 to 10 m/s. That is the soft city edge spring, as the critic found in round 33 (the drone sits 197 m out), not the boat.

## 3. Draw calls: 125 -> 114

`trisweep34.mjs` logged the draw calls per mesh at every spot with 119 calls or more (round 33 control, seed 130).
Each spot had the same top costs. The drone took 13 calls (9 meshes, 4 of them also in the shadow pass). The objective marker took 9.
Each instanced street mesh took 2 calls (main pass and shadow pass).

What changed:

- **A shadow-only layer** (`SHADOW_ONLY_LAYER` in `shadowSubset.ts`). The sun's shadow camera sees layer 2. The game cameras do not.
  A mesh on it costs one draw in the shadow pass and none in the main pass.
- **Drone**: the 4 hull meshes that cast a shadow now draw it as one merged proxy on that layer. 4 shadow draws -> 1. Same shape, same material side.
- **Near trees** (the two CC0 species): trunk and canopy cast one merged proxy per species. 4 shadow draws -> 2. The canopy sway was never in the shadow pass, so nothing changes there.
- **Objective marker**: the two tape bands on the parcel are one mesh. 2 draws -> 1.

Full sweep (`trisweep34.mjs`, the critic's trisweep31 spots: 3,256 to 3,296 spots, 1,920 of them on the water):

| Run | Round 33 critic | Round 33 control, today | Round 34 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop 22, draw calls | 123 | 123 | **114** |
| Desktop 130, draw calls | 125 | 123 | **114** |
| Desktop 33, draw calls | 122 | | **113** |
| iPhone 130, draw calls | 106 | | **97** |
| Desktop 130, max triangles | 444k | 446k | 431k |
| Desktop 22 / 33, max triangles | 429k / 433k | 424k / | 418k / 416k |
| iPhone 130, max triangles | 408k | | 397k |

Spots at 110 calls or more, desktop 130: 177 in the control, 10 now. Street runs (`perf-street.mjs`): desktop 108 / 113
(normal / rush, round 33: 117 / 122), iPhone 94 / 94.
In the blind street A/B (below) I saw no difference in any shadow.

## 4. Golden water at 1 to 2 m: the soft streaks are gone

**What I found** (`waterlow34.mjs`, layer switches in a temporary debug uniform, removed again):

- With the near normals flat, the bottom third of the golden low view is smooth. So the streaks are in the normal layers.
- They are not in the shadows (receiving shadows off changed nothing). They are not in the boats or their wakes (boats off changed nothing).
- Switching off any one layer (the 14 m, 5 m or 2 m detail layer, or the swell) left the streaks. All layers sample the same tile texture. It is a sum of only 18 waves, so each layer shows a few long crests. Close to a low camera they read as soft streaks that run toward the vanishing point.

**Fix** (`Water.ts`, desktop only, the phone's lite water is unchanged):

- A second tile texture for the near layer: 56 short ripples turned evenly round the circle (no few long crests), 256 px.
- Near a low camera this layer takes over 85% of the detail normals. It reaches 14 to 45 m and fades by pixel footprint (2 to 11 cm). It works only for a camera under 8 to 13 m.
- So the 14 m glint views and the play-height cruise view keep their round 33 look.

**Blind A/B** (`ab34.py`, round 33 control against round 34). The sides are random and the key was written first.
I wrote `builder-shots/ab/picks.txt` before I opened `.key.json`. The water pairs are at the full 1280 px width.

| Pair | Pick | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Dusk 33, g-low | new (crisp ripples in the bottom third, old smears) | **new wins** |
| Golden 130, g-low | new (old has radial streaks under the drone) | **new wins** |
| Golden 130, cruise | tie | tie |
| Golden 130, glint 14 m | old, weak (glitter a little more defined) | old wins |
| Dusk 33, glint 14 m | tie | tie |
| Noon 58, cruise | tie | tie |
| Street set, 6 pairs (art27 views) | tie in all 6 | 6 ties |

The one loss (golden glint at 14 m) came from the near layer reaching the 14 m camera. I then limited it to cameras
under 8 to 13 m (the camera-height fade above). After that change the 14 m glint views match round 33: mean pixel difference 1.0 to 1.8 (of 255) on all 4 moods, the noise of moving boats. The g-low views still differ (mean 11 to 18, bottom third 16 to 25). I did not run a second blind A/B. I know the look now, so it is not blind any more.

`contrast31.py` (desktop game camera, cruise must stay at most 0.6 of low):

| Mood | Round 33 control | Round 34 |
|---|---|---|
| Golden 130 | 18.1 / 35.0 = 0.52 | 18.2 / 35.1 = 0.52 |

| Dusk 33 | 16.4 / 40.7 = 0.40 | 16.7 / 40.6 = 0.41 |
| Noon 58 | 16.6 / 31.3 = 0.53 | 16.9 / 31.2 = 0.54 |

The metric's low band is rows 170 to 400 (water 30 m and more away), so it does not see the bottom-third change.
Cost: no more texture fetches (the near layer had one already). The near texture is built once at load. I also made the texture build faster: one row of sines per wave instead of one sine per pixel and wave. Same values (largest difference 3e-6), about 11 times faster.

# Drone Dash: round 33 critic report

**Verdict:** Pass. The harbour bus now runs all day. The render cost fell by about a quarter with no visible loss. The close glint water is crisp again. One miss by a hair: the draw-call peak is 125, and the target was under 125.

Build tested: the uncommitted round 33 work on top of commit 46b183d. Control: an untouched export of commit 46b183d (round 32). My servers ran on 5191 (round 33) and 5192 (round 32) and are stopped. The owner's server on 5188 was left alone. Every browser ran alone, one job at a time, from `critic-scripts/queue33.sh` and `jobs33.txt`. I did not read the round 33 builder notes. I read the diffs only to learn what to test.

New scripts in `progress/round-33/critic-scripts/`:

- `bus-stop33.mjs`: 700 s per seed, fixed step. Logs every bus stop, its length and pier.
- `cruise33.mjs`: fast flight at cruise height (24 m, 20 m/s, 60 Hz fixed step, every frame drawn) along two avenues. Logs frame change, pops, triangles, draw calls, detail chunks. Shots for the blind A/B.
- `cruise33b.mjs`: the same flight with a 32 x 18 tile grid, to catch small local pops.
- `boats33.mjs`: `boats32.mjs` plus peak drone speed for 1 s after a boat contact.
- `boattrace33.mjs`, `boattrace33b.mjs`: frame-by-frame trace of a boat running into a parked drone (b also logs the distance to the city edge).
- `ab33.py`: blind A/B, 3 sets of 6 pairs. `crash-classify-v-r32c.mjs`: the crash bot pointed at the round 32 control.
- Changed copies: `art27.mjs` and `water31.mjs` take PORT for the control, `water31.mjs` writes `water33-r33-*` and `water33-r32c-*`, `contrast31.py` reads them.

## Machine load (read first)

BTLEServer used 96 to 100% of one core in every check (`cpu-*.txt`). The headless browser still ran at 120 Hz vsync (median 8.3 ms). All wall-clock timings are marked contaminated. Every verdict on bus, boats, water, budgets, camera and pops comes from fixed-step probes.

## Results per item

### Harbour bus: pass

| Seed | Stops in 700 s | Piers | Stop length |
|---|---|---|---|
| 22 | 4 | -36, 40, -36, 40 | 9.0 to 9.25 s |
| 58 | 4 | -36, 40, -36, 40 | 9.0 to 9.25 s |
| 4711 | 4 | -36, 40, -36, 40 | 9.0 to 9.25 s |
| 9001 | 4 | 40, -36, 40, -36 | 9.0 s |

It alternates piers every time. The longest stop is 9.25 s against a limit of 11 s. It sails at 4.6 m/s and creeps under 0.3 m/s for only 2.75 s a run. `wake32.mjs` saw it leave a pier and sail on.

### Budget: triangles pass, draw calls miss by one

Full spot sweep (`trisweep31.mjs`), 1,920 water and marina spots in each:

| Desktop 22 | 429k | 123 | 566k |
| Desktop 130 | **444k** | **125** | 588k, 144 |
| Desktop 33 | 433k | 122 | |
| iPhone 130 | 408k | 106 | 524k, 128 |
| Water spots only | 348k | n/a | 463k |

Triangles: 444k, target under 480k. Pass. Draw calls: 125 at one city spot (desktop 130, x -60, z 90, 3 m high, facing west), target under 125. A miss by one call. Everywhere else it is at most 123. Street runs peak at 122 (desktop rush) and 103 (iPhone). Fast cruise peaks at 121. One more merged draw clears it.

### Blind A/B against round 32: pass

Picks were written to `critic/ab/picks.txt` before I opened `.key.json`. Top or bottom was random per pair.

| Set | New wins | Ties | Old wins | Result |

| Water | 3 | 2 | 1 | 5 of 6, pass |

- Street and cruise pairs look the same. I found no missing far building, no missing far shadow and no thinner city.
- Popping in motion: `cruise33.mjs` found 0 frame pops in 12 passes on both builds. Frame change is the same on both (median 11.2 against 11.2, golden). `cruise33b.mjs` tile pops are equal too (desktop 130: 2,887 against 2,950, phone 22: 6,445 against 6,432). ### Boats: pass

`boats33.mjs`, seeds 22, 58, 4711, 9001, 156 approaches:

- 0 frames inside a hull. 0 frames within 0.4 m of a mast. 0 stuck. 0 pushed down.
- **Low bus hits block like a wall.** 16 of 16 bus rams charged exactly one crash. The highest the drone rose after a 1 m hit was 1.81 m. No hop over the cabin (round 32: one hop to 4.3 m).
- **Bus wake toward a low sun.** Golden sunward views: 2.12, 1.54, 1.12. Dusk: 6.62, 2.40, 2.92. 5 of 6 are at least 1.3 (round 32: 0.93 and 0.67 in golden). In the shot the wake reads as a bright line behind the bus (`wake32-130-sunward-ferry.jpg`). The 1.12 view looks along the glitter path.
- **Sideways throw: no boat throws the drone above the cap.** A bus that hits a parked drone gives it 5.3 m/s at most. The bus moves at 4.6 m/s, so the cap is 6.6 m/s. The big sailboat number from round 32 (8.5 m/s, now 9.8 on seed 4711) is not the boat. `boattrace33b.mjs` shows the drone sitting 197 m out, past the soft city edge, and the edge spring pulls it inward. The probe parks the drone there. The round 32 control gives the same trace.
- **New find, not a regression: the bus snaps the drone sideways.** The bus bow pushes a parked drone. Then the drone jumps 0.55 m sideways in a single frame. This happens 3 or 4 times, about every 10 frames (33 m/s for one frame). Its real speed stays near 5 m/s. Round 32 does the same. On screen this can look like a stutter. **A human player must judge it.**

## Whole game after 33 rounds

The bot finds no gap left that clearly limits the game. Flight, camera, city, water, boats, scoring, medals, exploits, phone layout and budgets all pass. The open bot items are small. One draw call is over target. Pops cover the drone on desktop. The water at 1 m in golden hour is soft. The bus snap is possibly visible.

So in what a bot can measure, **only polish remains.** The real gate is a human playing. No person played a full run in many rounds. Feel decides the rest: crash fairness, near-miss thrill, the slipstream chain, medal pace, and touch controls.

## Ranked list

1. **Human playtest (needs a human player).** Desktop and phone, using the guide below. Everything else waits on this.
2. **Medal pace (needs a human player).** The street bot now reaches Gold on 2 of 3 seeds. Is Gold too easy, or just right for a good player?
3. **Desktop pops cover the drone** in 22.6% of pop samples (seed 22). Test: under 2% on desktop seeds 22, 58, 130.
4. **Bus snaps a parked drone 0.55 m sideways in one frame,** 3 or 4 times per contact. Test: in `boattrace33.mjs`, no single-frame move is over 0.15 m beyond the drone's own speed. **A human player must judge how visible it is.**
5. **Draw calls 125 at one spot.** Test: full sweep under 125 on desktop 22, 130, 33.
6. **Golden water at 1 m** still smears in the bottom third. Test: blind A/B of golden and dusk g-low against round 33, new wins or ties both, cruise ratio stays at most 0.6.
7. **JS chunk 952 KB,** over Vite's warning line. Not a load problem yet (3.0 MB total).

## Human playtest guide (15 minutes)

Play on a laptop first (10 minutes), then on a phone turned sideways (5 minutes). Write one line per point.

1. **First minute.** Start a fresh run without reading anything. Do you know where to go and what to do within 30 seconds? Note anything you had to guess.
2. **Crashes.** Fly low and fast between buildings for 2 minutes. After each crash, ask: did I deserve that? Count the crashes that felt unfair, and say where they happened (pad edge, corner, alley, tunnel).
3. **Slipstream chain.** Hug walls to build a chain, then deliver. Do you notice the bonus build up and pay out? Does it make you want to take more risk? Do the pops ever hide your drone?
4. **Medals.** Play one full run to the end. Which medal did you get, and did it feel earned? Do you want to try once more for the next one?
5. **Harbour.** Fly out over the water near the piers at low height. Does the water look good up close and from cruise height? Let the harbour bus run into your hovering drone. Does the push look smooth, or does the drone jump?
6. **Fast cruise.** Fly high and fast across the whole city. Do buildings, trees or people pop in or out? Does the city look full?
7. **Phone.** On the phone: are the stick and buttons comfortable? Do your thumbs hide anything important? In rush hour, with many pops on the screen, does the game stay smooth?
8. **One word.** At the end, describe the game in one word, and name the one thing to change first.

New scripts:

- `breakdown33.mjs`: triangles and draws per mesh at a spot.
- `slabverify33.mjs`: checks the city shadow slab (see part 2).
- `ab33.py`: blind pairs. It writes the key before any judging.
- `geo33.mjs`: instance counts.
- `slabcheck33.mjs`: a pixel diff. Not usable: two renders of the same frame already differ.

## 1. Harbour bus stall: fixed

**Cause.** `Boats.stepShuttle` braked on `sqrt(2 a (left - 0.05))`.
So the speed got to 0 at 5 cm before the stop. But the bus counted as "arrived" only under 2 cm.
The bus parked at speed 0 with 5 cm to go. Each step was 0, and the 9 s dwell never started.

**Fix.** The brake curve now aims at the stop itself.
While the bus has way to go, its speed stays at 0.25 m/s or more (`SHUTTLE.creep`).
Within 0.1 m of the stop, the bus is alongside (`SHUTTLE.arrive`).

**Test**: `bus-stop32.mjs`, fixed 0.5 s steps, seeds 22, 58, 4711 and 9001.

| Run | Stops per seed | Piers | Longest stop | Stalls |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 300 s | 2, one at each pier | in turn | 9 to 9.5 s | 0 (on seed 22, the second stop is in its dwell at 300 s) |
| 700 s | 4, two at each pier | in turn | 9 s | 0 |

"Both piers at least 3 times in 300 s" is not possible on this route.
The bus lane is 1,583 m long. At 4.6 m/s one loop takes 344 s.
The two piers are half a loop apart (about 790 m). The time between stops is 165 to 175 s.
The critic's round 32 bar passes on all 4 seeds: 700 s, at least 4 stops per seed, never more than 15 s at speed 0.
For 3 visits in 300 s, the bus needs about 9 m/s, a third pier, or a turn-round shuttle. I did not change the route.

## 2. Budget: triangles and draw calls

| Check | Round 32 (critic) | Round 33 | Target |
|---|---|---|---|
| Full sweep, desktop seed 130 | 588k, 144 draws | **449k, 122 draws** | under 480k, under 125 |
| Full sweep, desktop seed 22 | 566k | **426k, 121 draws** | |
| Full sweep, iPhone seed 130 | 524k, 128 draws | **408k, 106 draws** | |
| Water and marina spots (1,920 per run), max | 463k | 350k | |
| Street run (perf-street), desktop max | 146 draws | **122 draws** (395k) | |
| Street run, iPhone max | | 103 draws (358k) | |

The sweep is `trisweep31.mjs`, not changed (3,256 spots, water and marina included).
Worst spot: seed 130 at (-90, 3, 0). Before: 554k and 140 draws. After: 419k and 115 draws.
See `breakdown-before.log` and `breakdown-after.log`.

What changed:

- **The shadow pass draws only what the shadow map holds.** The sun's shadow box is ±75 m round the drone.
  Before, every instanced mesh drew all its instances into it.
  The new `shadowSubset` writes instances nearest first. The shadow pass draws only the first `shadowCount`.
  It uses `onBeforeShadow` and `onAfterShadow` on the mesh. A count of 0 skips the draw.
  Users: lamp poles (115 m), blob tree canopies (115 m), street props (45 m), far people (to 40 m) and pines.
  The lamps sort again after 12 m of camera travel. Each lamp's part indices move with it, so the occlusion pass still works.
  When a boat or a dock is within 115 m, it casts a shadow. Further out, it casts none.
- **City shadow slab.** I sort the merged city mesh one time, by the distance across the sun's direction.
  The shadow pass draws only the slab that the shadow camera can reach.
  The slab is ±75 m plus half the widest triangle.
  Long faces that point at the sky, and the 4 cm diagonal paint strips, are not in the slab.
  For this material, the shadow pass culls faces that point at the sky. So this change has no effect on shadows.
  The promenade edge boxes are now in 40 m pieces, so they sort into the slab.
  Check: `slabverify33.mjs`, 8 seeds, 338 spots each, exact triangle-to-plane test.
  Result: 0 left-out triangles inside the shadow frustum.
  City cost at the worst spot: 113k before, 93k after.
- **People.** The low-detail figure starts at 24 m (was 40 m). Far people still cast shadows to 40 m, as before.
  Far limbs are boxes with open ends (about 150 triangles a figure).
  The near head is 8x6 (was 9x7). Skirt and cap have 8 sides.
  The near shadow skips the small parts (hands, shoes, nose, phone, strap, brim, bun, hips). A draw range does this.
- **Lamps.** 66 triangles a pole (was 88): no hidden caps, 7 sides.
- **Building detail.** Draw distance 74 m on desktop and 62 m on the phone (was 95 m and 75 m).
- **Street props.** Range 66 m on desktop and 55 m on the phone (was 80 m and 60 m). Shadows only within 45 m.
- **Skyline.** The blocks have no bottom face now. They stay, in one draw.
- **Draw calls.** The 4 rotors are one mesh. The vertex shader turns each blade (no shadow).
  The 4 blur discs are one mesh in one pass. The red, green and white nav lights share one material.
  The duct lips and motor caps cast no shadow. The parcel is one mesh with vertex colours (was 6 meshes, 7 draws).
  Car wheels cast no shadow. They are inside the shadow of the body.
  The drone was 34 draws. Now it is 19.

**Blind A/B, round 32 against round 33.** `ab33.py` picks sides with SystemRandom and shuffles the order.
It wrote the key to `builder-shots/ab/.key.json` before any judging.
I wrote `ab/picks.txt` before I opened the key. Each side of a pair is 640 px wide.

- Street set (art27): golden street, shopfront and people, morning street and shopfront, phone golden street.
  **6 ties, 0 losses. Pass.** I saw no difference in any pair.
- Water set (golden and dusk g-low and 14 m glint, noon cruise, golden marina): **2 wins, 2 ties, 2 losses.**
  That is 4 of 6. **It fails the 5-of-6 bar.** I picked round 32 for dusk g-low and dusk glint.
  After I opened the key, I compared these two at full size. This check is not blind, so it does not count.
  At full size, round 33 has the crisper ripples and glitter in both.
  At half size, the larger, smoother shapes of round 32 looked more defined.
  The critic must judge these again at full size.

## 3. Leftovers

**(A) Hazy close water at a low sun.** Two changes in `Water.ts`:

- A fine near layer: ripples about 2 m across, from a third detail-texture sample.
  It shows only near the camera, where one pixel covers less than a few cm.
- The calm-with-height blend now goes from 6 m to 20 m of camera height (was 4 m to 15 m).
  The 14 m glint views keep their glitter. The game camera at cruise (29 m) does not change.

`contrast31.py`:

| Mood | Cruise | Low | Ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| Golden 130 | 18.2 | 35.1 | 0.52 |
| Morning 22 | 16.6 | 30.1 | 0.55 |
| Dusk 33 | 16.7 | 40.6 | 0.41 |
| Noon 58 | 16.8 | 31.2 | 0.54 |

All marks pass: ratio at most 0.6, low at least 25, cruise at least 15.
Open issue: the soft radial streaks at the bottom of the golden g-low frame are still there.
They are not the city's shadows: half the shadow on the water changed nothing, and I removed that change.
I did not find the cause in the time box. The near layer puts crisp ripples on top of them.

**(B) Sailboat hull kick: not fixed.** I added a cap on the boat's push.
After the push, the drone moves no faster than the boat speed plus 2 m/s, or its own speed before the hit.
I measured no change from the cap, because the 6.5 to 8.6 m/s does not come from the boat.
The inner sailboat lane is about 195 m from the centre. That is 3 m past the soft city bound (192 m).
The boat pushes the parked drone 6 to 12 m further out. Then the bound's spring (`over * 6` m/s²) throws it back.
I tried a cap on the spring's return speed (4 m/s and 5.5 m/s). The speed went down to 5.2 to 6.6 m/s.
But in 2 ram runs the drone then slid over a low hull for more than 2 s (the probe's "stuck"). I removed that change.
A slower slide off the bow (2x, not 5x) made the bus push the drone for longer. I removed that change too.
Next step: move the inner sailboat lane inside the bound (d about 26). Then run boats31 again for lane overlap.

**(C) Low bus hit hops over the cabin: fixed.** The rule "boats are never a ledge hop" missed one case.
That case is the belly on the hull's top edge (contact normal 0.35 to 0.7 up). The rule now applies there too.
A hull taller than a step is a wall.
`boats32.mjs`: 16 of 16 bus ram hits charged exactly one Crash, and 0 hops.
Round 32: 15 of 16, with one hop to 4.3 m.

**(D) Bus wake toward a golden-hour sun: better, but not 1.3 in all views.**

- A large hull now makes more foam than its speed gives, and its trail lasts longer.
- In the glitter path of a low sun, a wake's foam trail gets a minimum brightness.
  The minimum follows how directly the view looks down the glitter path. It stays under the bloom threshold.
  A stronger first version glowed like a laser beam. I removed it.

`water31b.mjs`, golden-hour views toward the sun (trail brightness over open water):

| Boat | Round 32 | Round 33 |
|---|---|---|
| Bus | 1.79 / 0.93 / 0.67 | **2.15 / 1.49 / 1.07** |
| Rib | 0.96 / 1.28 / 1.66 | 1.15 / 2.17 / 2.72 |
| Sail | 0.69 / 0.82 / 1.31 | 1.11 / 1.60 / 1.71 |

The last bus view stays under 1.3. There the open water ahead of the bow is 190 to 200 of 255.
For 1.3, the trail needs to be brighter than white.
All dusk views were 2.4 or more, but I measured them with the stronger first version.
I did not measure dusk again after the change. Shot: `wake32-130-sunward-ferry.jpg`.

critic.md
# Drone Dash: round 32 critic report

**Verdict:** Pass, with one new bug. The water now calms with height: the cruise to low ratio is 0.43 to 0.56 (round 31: 0.90 to 1.09). The grid pop is gone and boats are solid. But the new harbour bus stalls 5 cm short of its first pier and never moves again, on every seed, after 70 to 120 s.

Build tested: the uncommitted round 32 work on top of commit 1e9035e. My dev server ran on port 5191 and is stopped. The owner's server on 5188 was left alone. Every browser ran alone, one job at a time, from `critic-scripts/queue32.sh` and `jobs32.txt`. I did not read the round 32 builder notes. I read the diffs of `Water.ts`, `Boats.ts`, `CollisionWorld.ts`, `Drone.ts` and `Game.ts` only to learn what to test.

New scripts (in `progress/round-32/critic-scripts/`):

- `boats32.mjs`: flies the drone into boats (fixed step, 60 Hz). Modes: ram is 15 m/s with W held, let go 0.35 s after the hit. Slow is 4 m/s. In hover the boat runs into a parked drone. In press, W is held into an oncoming bow. Logs crashes, frames inside a hull box, frames within 0.4 m of a mast, overlap depth, time in contact, push distance and drop.
- `bus-stop32.mjs`: runs 700 s and logs every stop and start of the harbour bus.
- `wake32.mjs`: wake shots looking toward a low sun, and harbour bus scale shots.
- `ab32.py`: blind pairs of round 31 against round 32 water.
- Changed copies: `water31.mjs` (tag r32), `water31b.mjs` (3 extra sunward wake views per boat, waits until the boat is under way), `contrast31.py` (reads both rounds).

## Machine load (read first)

BTLEServer used 97 to 100% of one core all session (`cpu-*.txt`). XProtect used 40% at the start. The headless browser still ran at the 120 Hz vsync (median 8.3 ms), so all wall-clock numbers are marked contaminated. The water, boat, camera and triangle verdicts come from fixed-step probes.

## Water

**Calm with height: pass.** `contrast31.py` on the desktop game-camera views:

| Mood | Cruise (24 m) | Low (2 m) | Ratio | Round 31 ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Golden 130 | 18.2 | 34.1 | **0.53** | 1.01 |
| Morning 22 | 16.6 | 29.4 | **0.56** | 1.09 |
| Dusk 33 | 16.7 | 39.0 | **0.43** | 0.90 |
| Noon 58 | 16.8 | 29.9 | **0.56** | 1.04 |

All marks met: ratio at most 0.6, low at least 25, cruise at least 15. On the phone the ratio is 0.79 (round 31: 1.09). It calms, but less.

**Blind A/B against round 31: new water wins 4, ties 2, loses 4. Win or tie 6 of 10: pass, just.** Picks were written in `critic/ab/picks.txt` before I opened `.key.json`. Four pairs show a boat on one side only, so they were not fully blind.

- The new water wins every desktop cruise view (golden, dusk, morning, noon). The crumpled foil is gone. From play height the bay now shows broad dark and light swell shapes with sparkle near the sun.
- It loses all three close low-sun views (golden 2 m, golden glint 14 m, dusk glint 14 m) and the phone cruise view.
- **Close golden-hour and dusk views now look hazy.** The water right under and in front of the camera smears into soft radial streaks. It looks out of focus (`water32-r32-130-g-low.jpg`, `water32-r32-130-glint.jpg`, `water32-r32-33-glint.jpg`). At 14 m the glint path is a soft glow, not glitter. Round 31 was crisper here.

**Grid pop: fixed.** 2 cm camera move across a snap line against the same move elsewhere: 0.99 to 2.34% of pixels changed against 0.80 to 2.32% (ratio at most 1.23, target at most 2). Round 31: 14 to 18% against under 2%. In the 15 m/s motion sweep, snap frames and other frames now change by the same amount (for example 6.06 against 6.08 at cruise). Round 31 snap frames changed 13% more.

**Wakes toward a low sun: better, not solved.** Trail over open-water brightness, rib and harbour bus, 4 azimuths per mood: 29 of 32 views at 1.3 or more (round 31: 6 views under 1.2). The 3 low ones are 1.11 to 1.18. In the new sunward views (camera looking into the sun over the boat), dusk passes (all 1.14 or more). Golden hour has 3 of 6 under 1.0: rib 0.96, bus 0.93 and 0.67, where the wake lies inside the glitter path. In the shots the rib wake reads as a bright line toward a low sun. The bus wake is only a faint pale streak (`wake32-130-sunward-rib.jpg`, `wake32-130-sunward-ferry.jpg`, `wake32-33-sunward-rib.jpg`).

**Flat frames with bloom on: pass.** 960 frames over 8 water views and 4 moods, plus 240 on the phone: 0 flat, 0 black pixels, at least 39 distinct colours of 49.

**Water cost (throughput, contaminated):** +0.44 to 1.04 ms a frame on desktop water views (round 31: +0.53 to 0.94). The low view is at the +1.0 ms line (0.92 to 1.04). Phone +0.1 to 0.7 ms.

## Boats

**Collision: pass.** `boats32.mjs`, seeds 22, 58, 4711 and fresh 9001, 156 approaches into 12 moving boats (4 harbour buses, 8 sailboats) and 16 moored boats:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Frames with the drone centre inside any hull box | **0** |
| Frames with the drone centre within 0.4 m of a mast | **0** |
| Sphere deeper than touching a hull | 0 |
| Stuck states | **0** (longest contact 1.9 s, at the moored rib at 4 m/s) |
| Pushed down by a boat | 0 m (lowest 0.9 m, the drone's floor) |
| Bus side at 15 m/s, 1 m and 2 m high | 15 of 16 hits charged exactly one Crash (loss 9.9 to 15.3 m/s) |
| Bus at 4 m/s | 4 of 4 bumps, no crash |
| Masts at 15 m/s, 3 m high | 24 of 24 scrapes, 0 crashes, the drone glances by |
| Low hulls (sail, rib, row) at the lowest height | stepped over, no crash, drone sits on the deck (`boats32-22-moored-rib-low.jpg`) |

The odd one: one bus hit at 1 m (seed 9001) hopped the drone up over the cabin to 4.3 m with no crash. A ledge hop over a boat was meant to be off. The few other crashes in the log happened 47 to 95 m from the boat, after the drone flew on into the city. They are not boat hits.

Only the bus and the inner sailboats are reachable. The flight limit is 215 m from the centre. Ribs (203 to 216 m) and the outer sailboat (237 to 242 m) are out of reach, so they can never be hit.

**A boat hitting the drone feels fair (fixed step, a human must check it).** The bus hit a parked drone 8 of 8 times: no crash. The bus carries the drone at its own speed (4.2 to 4.6 m/s). The drone slides 5.5 to 7 m to the side and is free in 0.2 to 0.6 s. Holding W into an oncoming bow charged one Crash (4 of 4). The drone reached 15.6 m/s before the hit, so that is the player's own speed. A sailboat hull at the lowest height throws the drone sideways at 4 to 8.5 m/s, nearly three times the boat's speed. That can feel like a kick. **Needs a human player.**

**Routes and overlap: pass for 120 s.** `boats31.mjs`, seeds 22, 58 and fresh 9001: 0 hull overlaps, 0 hulls on a dock, 0 hull corners in a solid. Moving hulls come no closer than 17.4 m to the seawall (the bus lane). Heave within ±0.28 m. On seed 9001 two doorstep pads sit 21 m inland of the marina, clear of it.

**New bug: the harbour bus stops for good.** `bus-stop32.mjs` (700 s per seed): on seeds 22, 58, 4711 and 9001 the bus sails once, stops at its first pier after 88 to 119 s and never leaves. `wake32.mjs` shows the same at both piers (x -36.05 and x 40.05). 60 s later it still has not moved. In code, `stepShuttle` brakes so that the speed reaches 0 at 0.05 m before the stop, but it only counts as arrived under 0.02 m. So it parks 5 cm short with speed 0, and the 9 s wait never starts. After two minutes of every run the only big boat is a parked bus with no wake.

**Scale and life: mostly right.** At 14.4 m the bus reads as a small harbour ferry beside the drone and the docks (`bus32-22-from-promenade.jpg`, `bus32-130-at-pier.jpg`). Its shape is still a small cruise ship with funnels. Until it stalls, the bus braking into a pier is the best moment on the water. The sailboats' gusts are too slow to notice in a short look. **Needs a human eye** once the stall is fixed.

## Regressions

- **Flat-frame probe: pass.** 951 frames, 0 flat, 0 errors.
- **Crash-classify, 8 seeds: pass, 0 pad lips.** 12 m: 47 crashes in 541 s (5.2 a minute, round 31: 4.7), 14 near the target, closest 3.5 m below a top. 20 m: 36 in 722 s (3.0 a minute, round 31: 3.4), 13 near, closest 2.0 m below a top. 0 hop-like crashes.
- **Alley camera: pass.** cam-clip30 desktop 22 no orbit, cam-clip24 desktop 22 and 58 with orbit, iPhone 22 no orbit: 0 hidden frames, 0 in solid, 0 pops over 1 m in about 6,925 frames each.
- **climb30: pass.** 0 jumps over 1 m (max 0.90 m on desktop and phone). 0 frames in solid. Closest camera 5.4 m. Max drone share 39.4% (round 31 had one frame at 40.3%).
- **People probe: pass.** 0 people on active pads (48 legs, 1,536 samples).
- **Traffic overlap: pass.** 0 in all 6 runs.
- **Phone HUD probe: pass.** iPhone 22, 58, 130: marker on controls 0, drone under pills 0, pops on the drone 0%. Desktop 22: pops cover the drone in 29.6% of pop samples (round 31: 26%). Still open.
- **Chimes with pops: pass.** 43 of 43 chimes had the pop shown within 0.3 s.
- **Exploits: pass.** No-delivery farm 0 on 22, 58, 130. Carry farm 0.25, 0 and 0.24 of honest points a minute. Honest 4,559 / 4,892 / 6,859 (Gold), the same as round 31.
- **Medal gate, breakdown exact on all 6 runs: pass.** Street: 5,892 / 3,745 / 5,836, all Silver, total 15,473 (round 31: 15,439), strict delivery share 66%. Lazy: 1,226 / 1,165 / 1,031, all Bronze, total 3,422 (round 31: 3,231). Seed 58 lazy moved from no medal to a low Bronze. No lazy run gets near Silver.
- **No long task after Play: pass.** 0 long tasks and 0 shader compiles in 3 runs (2 desktop, 1 iPhone).

## Budgets

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Triangles, full spot sweep with 1,920 water and marina spots | Desktop 22: 566k. Desktop 130: **588k**. iPhone 130: 524k. Water spots max 463k. 0 spots over 600k. |
| Draw calls | Max 144 desktop, 128 iPhone. Street run max 146. 0 over 150. |
| First load | Production build 2.8 MB without source maps (JS 922 KB, boats.glb 234 KB), 7.0 MB with maps. Type check clean. |
| Street frame time (12 s, 120 Hz vsync, contaminated) | Desktop p95 9.3 / 9.2 ms (normal / rush), max 10.4. iPhone p95 9.5 / 9.4 ms, max 10.3. |
| HUD runs, 80 s | Only frames over 20 ms: the probe ending at 80.5 s, as in round 31. |

**Headroom is nearly gone.** 588k of 600k triangles (2% left) and 146 of 150 draw calls. Cut these first, before any more content. Draw people and cars beyond about 40 m with a lower-detail mesh. Remove the backdrop skyline boxes on the far horizon (they also look pasted on). Pull in the building-detail distance. Each of these frees tens of thousands of triangles.

## Whole game after 32 rounds

Against the best polished indie arcade flying and delivery games I know, Drone Dash now has most of what they have. A readable city with its own moods. A drone that flies with weight. A loop that pays for flying low and fast by the walls. Rush orders, medals, a daily city, sound, and a waterfront that finally looks like sea from play height. The camera holds in alleys and tunnels. The phone layout is clean. Exploits are closed.

What the best ones still do better is mostly feel, and a bot cannot measure feel. Does a near miss feel thrilling? Is 3 to 5 crashes a minute (for a bot) fair or annoying? Does the slipstream chain make a player want one more run? No human played a full run in many rounds. That is the real gate now.

So in what a bot can find, **only polish remains**, apart from the bus bug below.

## Biggest gap: the harbour bus stalls 5 cm short of its first pier

It is cheap to fix, it shows in every run after two minutes, and it undoes this round's "routes feel alive" work.

**Acceptance test:**

- `bus-stop32.mjs` on seeds 22, 58, 4711 and 9001 (700 s each): the bus stops at each pier, waits about 9 s and leaves again. At least 4 stops per seed. Never more than 15 s at speed 0.
- `boats31.mjs` lengthened to 400 s on the same seeds: still 0 hull overlaps, 0 hulls on a dock.
- `boats32.mjs`: still 0 frames inside a hull, 0 stuck.

## Other gaps, ranked

1. **Human playtest overdue (needs a human player).** Play one full run on a laptop and one on a phone. Judge crash fairness, boat pushes, the slipstream chain and the medal pace.
2. **Triangle and draw-call headroom about 2%.** Cut as listed under Budgets before adding content. Test: full sweep max under 540k, draw calls under 140.
3. **Close low-sun water looks hazy.** At 1 to 14 m in golden hour and dusk, the near water smears into soft streaks. It lost all three blind pairs there. Test: run a blind A/B of the golden and dusk g-low and glint views against round 31. The new water wins or ties at least 2 of 3. The cruise ratio stays at most 0.6.
4. **Desktop pops cover the drone** in 29.6% of pop samples (seed 22). Test: under 2% on desktop seeds 22, 58 and 130.
5. **Bus wake in the glitter path.** Golden-hour sunward views: 0.67 and 0.93. Test: all 6 rib and bus sunward views at least 1.2 in golden hour.
6. **A sailboat hull throws the drone sideways at up to 8.5 m/s,** and one low bus hit hopped the drone over the cabin. Cap the side kick near the boat's own speed plus 2 m/s, and keep boats out of the ledge hop. **Needs a human player** to judge how much it matters.
7. **Water cost at the +1.0 ms line** in the low view (0.92 to 1.04 ms, contaminated). Keep it from growing.

## Screenshots (progress/round-32/critic/), 63 files

# Drone Dash: round 32 builder notes

Brief: the water must get calmer with height. Leftovers: A boat colliders, B wakes toward a low sun, C grid-snap pop, D ferry and routes (optional).

Dev server: my own on port 5190, stopped at the end. The owner's server on 5188 was left alone. Browsers ran one at a time, from `builder-scripts/queue32.sh` (`jobs32.txt`) and `queue32b.sh` (`jobs32b.txt`, the reruns on the final build).

Machine: BTLEServer used 99 to 100% of one core in every `cpu-*.txt`. XProtect used 40% during the water run. Headless Chromium still ran at 120 Hz. All wall-clock numbers are marked contaminated. The camera, boat and pop verdicts come from fixed-step probes.

Scripts: the round 31 critic scripts are copied to `builder-scripts/`. In the copies only the output folder (`./out/`) and the port (5190) changed. Some tools got extra switches that are off by default: `water31b.mjs` has `WAKEONLY`, `WAKESHOT` and `OPENWATER`. In `builder-scripts/out/` the file tag `r31` means "this build" (the tag comes from the port test in `water31.mjs`). New scripts: `wfast.mjs` + `cfast.py` (tuning loop), `boatcol32.mjs` (A), `pop32.mjs` (C), `bus32.mjs` (D shots), `ab32.py` (blind A/B), `dbg32*.mjs` (debug traces).

## 1. Water calms with height (`src/world/Water.ts`)

Design:

- `hiK` is 0 below 4 m camera height and 1 above 15 m. All the calming scales with it, so a low skim keeps the full close chop.
- The fine ripple layer fades by distance. It also fades by the metres one pixel covers on the water (`fwidth` of the world position). So it is mip-aware. Both limits are tighter from above. From play height the finest layer is gone past about 18 to 90 m.
- The middle layer fades the same way, to a 20% floor.
- A new broad, slow layer (74 m texture period, very slow scroll) carries the look from above. Its height channel also makes soft calm and ruffled wind patches tens of metres across.
- The analytic swell slopes ease off by up to 60% with distance from above. The vertex swell is unchanged near the camera (see C).
- Low sun: with a low sun and a high camera, the key light sees up to 60% less of the fine layer (`nL`). The fine slopes that fade out widen the glint instead (roughness 0.16 to 0.30, a Toksvig-like trade).
- Per mood `chop` (golden 1.0, morning 1.15, dusk 1.15, noon 0.68) sets how breezy the bay looks from above.
- Cost: the shader skips the finest layer where it is faded out (`textureGrad` with gradients taken outside the branch). The foam noise blends over to the coarser layer, so there is no seam.

Results (`water31.mjs` then `contrast31.py`, desktop, final build):

| Mood (seed) | Cruise | Low | Ratio | Round 31 ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Golden hour (130) | 18.2 | 34.1 | 0.53 | 0.90 to 1.09 range |
| Morning (22) | 16.6 | 29.4 | 0.56 | |
| Dusk (33) | 16.7 | 39.0 | 0.43 | |
| Hazy noon (58) | 16.8 | 29.9 | 0.56 | |

Pass marks: ratio at most 0.6 (pass on all 4), low at least 25 (pass), cruise at least 15 (pass).

Blind A/B against the round 31 views (`ab32.py`, hidden random key, picks by a fresh agent that saw only the 10 pairs):

- Final build: new 4, tie 4, old 2. New wins or ties 8 of 10 (target 6). `out/ab/picks.txt`.
- The first build of this round: new 5, tie 4, old 1 (`out/ab-first/`).
- Both losses are close or glint views in golden hour (130 g-low, 22 glint). The judge called the new side "hazy, smeared" there. Every cruise pair went to the new water or was a tie.

Water cost (`water31b.mjs`, throughput, contaminated): desktop +0.44 to 1.03 ms a frame in water views (round 31 critic: +0.5 to 0.9), about 0 in a city view. Phone +0.06 to 0.51 ms. The 1.03 is seed 33 low. Treat it as at the +1.0 ms line.

## A. Boat colliders (`CollisionWorld.ts`, `Boats.ts`, `Drone.ts`)

Design:

- `CollisionWorld` has a new list of turning boxes (`DynBox`: centre, heading as sin / cos, half sizes, height range, soft flag, velocity). `resolveSphere` and `surfaceBelow` check them every query (about 25 boxes, an early bounds check). A sphere never leaves one downwards. So a boat can push the drone sideways or up, never into the sea.
- `Boats` builds the boxes from the model sizes (`PARTS`): a hull box for every boat, a thin soft mast-and-sail column for sailboats, and the bus hull, deckhouse and funnel. Each frame the box centres come from the instance matrix (so heave, pitch and roll move them). The soft mast column widens by the lean, so the drone is held clear of the mast at every height. Moored boats and the three docks have static boxes. The hull boxes reach 1.5 m below the waterline.
- After the assets load, `Game` adds the boxes to the collision world.
- Crash rules: hulls go through the normal wall path. Soft parts glance like a lamp post (a scrape, never a crash). One change in `Drone`: a boat is never skimmed with the ledge hop. A gunwale low enough to step over (up to 0.9 m above the skids, like a kerb) is still free. Anything taller is a wall.
- A moving boat never bulldozes the drone. The crash test uses the drone's own speed only, so a boat running into a hovering drone is never a crash. After a contact with a closing boat face, the drone leaves at least as fast as the face moves. Off a bow or stern it also slides out to the side, so the boat goes past.

Results (`boatcol32.mjs`, fixed step, seeds 22, 58, 130, final build):

| Runs | What | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 30 into moving boats (10 per seed) | lane-31 sailboats (hull low, mid, mast, twice each) and the harbour bus (deckhouse, high, bow, stern, low hull) | bus: 12 crashes (tier rules), 3 wall hits under the threshold (bow, head-on). Sailboats: 15 scrapes (they step over the gunwale and glance off the sail) |
| 15 into moored boats (5 per seed) | sail hull, sail mast, two rowing boats, the rib | 9 step-overs, 3 scrapes, 3 none (the moored rib's top sits below the drone's lowest flight height) |
| 9 boats run into a hovering drone | bus head-on, bus 1 m off the centre line, sailboat | 0 crashes. The drone slides off the bow in under 1 s |
| All 54 runs | | 0 frames with the drone centre inside a hull. Deepest overlap 0. 0 stuck (a climb frees the drone every time). 0 frames under the flight floor |

Only the lane-31 sailboats, the bus and the marina are inside the flight bounds (soft edge 190 m from the centre, hard edge 215 m). The drone cannot reach the ribs on lane 52 or the lone sailboat on lane 74.

The critic's `boats31.mjs` fly-through at 4 m (seeds 22, 58, 4711, 130): 0 crashes, 0 frames in a solid, closest drone to the boat centre 0.84 to 1.01 m (round 31: 0.54, it flew through).

## B. Wakes toward a low sun (`Water.ts`)

Looking toward a low sun, the open water is bright sky reflection plus glint, brighter than sunlit foam. Foam is now always brighter than the bare water round it: by up to 150% at full foam, colour kept, capped at 1.4. The trail of slow boats is stronger and longer (floor 0.35 instead of 0.12, decay length +1 m +0.4 s of speed).

Results (`water31b.mjs` wake block, trail over open water, rib and ferry, 4 azimuths, 4 moods, final build):

- 28 of 32 at 1.3 or more. Under 1.3: 130 rib 1.12, 33 ferry 1.04 and 1.08, 58 ferry 1.17. Round 31 critic: 6 of 32 under 1.2.
- The ferry is now the harbour bus on a lane 19 m off the wall. Its side samples ("open water" 14 m to the island side) land 5 m from the wall, in the shore foam, or on the promenade. With samples closer than 8 m to the wall left out (`OPENWATER=1`, `wake-open.log`): ferry 15 of 16 at 1.3 or more (58 noon 1.22). The golden-hour rib at 0.96 has its open samples in the bright glint path. Its wake is plain to see (`r32-wake-130-rib0.jpg`).
- Screenshots toward a low sun: `r32-wake-130-rib0.jpg`, `r32-wake-130-ferry0.jpg` (golden hour), `r32-wake-33-rib2.jpg`, `r32-wake-33-ferry2.jpg` (dusk).

## C. Grid-snap pop (`Water.ts`)

Cause: only the centre vertex of the grid was world-stable. A 2.5 m snap moved every other vertex to a new place. Far vertices sampled waves too short for their cells. So the surface height, and the point where the view ray hits it, jumped.

Fix:

- The grid now has 10 even 2.5 m steps round the centre (8 x 3.2 m on phones), then grows by 8% (10% on phones). A one-step snap maps every even vertex exactly onto an old one.
- The vertex swell lives only inside that even part: full to 12 m, gone by 21 m from the camera. It keeps only the waves the cells can carry (5.1 m wave out, 8.3 m wave about half). Further out the swell stays in the per-pixel normals, as before.
- The swell fade is now per pixel, not a varying.
- The boats still ride the full swell (`waveHeight` with the distance fade), as in round 31. New hook `waterShown(x, z)` gives the height as drawn. `waterAt` is unchanged.
- Triangles: desktop water grid 26.9k (was 22.5k), phone 16.9k (was 14.1k).

Threshold: a move across a snap line must change the water band no more than the same move without a line (ratio at most 1.1).

Results (`pop32.mjs`, time frozen, band from the horizon down to the near water):

| Test | Across a line | Control | Round 31 (critic) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 cm move at 20 lines, 4 m up, desktop 130 | 3.30% big pixels, mean 6.00 | 3.27%, mean 5.98 | 14 to 18% against 0.1 to 1.7% |
| same, 25 m up | 0%, mean 0.76 | 0%, mean 0.76 | |
| sweep, 0.25 m a frame over 20 lines, 4 m up | mean 69.0 (20 frames) | 68.8 (180 frames) | |
| desktop 33, phone 22 | across equals control within 0.1 | | |

The critic's own pop block in `water31.mjs` agrees: across equals control on all 4 moods at 4 m and 25 m.

## D. Ferry and routes (`Boats.ts`)

- The 20 m cruise ship is now drawn at 0.72 scale (14.4 m) as a harbour bus. No new model, no Blender run, no generation (ASSETS.md has a line).
- The bus has its own lane 19 m off the wall, inside the sailboats. It brakes, stops alongside a pier head for 9 s, then pulls out. There are two stops: the marina and a new landing pier on the north wall (the same CC0 dock model, 2 more instances, with leg foam and colliders). It starts each city under way, part of the way between stops. So it does not sit still during the first tests.
- Sailboats speed up and slow down with slow gusts (up to 30 to 35%). The gust is the same for every boat on a lane, so the spacing holds.
- Each city moves the lanes by up to 2.5, 3 and 6 m, so the loops differ. The lone sailboat now sails a tighter loop (74 m off the wall, 2.3 m/s).
- `boats31.mjs`, 120 s at 30 Hz on seeds 22, 58, 4711 and 130: 0 hull-hull, 0 hull-dock, 0 hull corners in a solid. Its `minGap` is the centre distance minus the half lengths. It goes to -0.98 m as the bus and a sailboat pass side by side on their lanes. That is a crude metric. The oriented test finds no overlap, and the closest hull edges are 6.5 m apart.
- Not done: a better CC0 ferry or tug model (optional).

## Regressions (final build unless marked)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Flat frames, bloom on | `acceptance-probe.mjs`: 945 frames, 0 flat, 0 errors. `water31b.mjs` water and glint views: 960 desktop + 240 phone frames, 0 flat, 0 black pixels, at least 39 distinct colours of 49. New `pow` bases: none. One new division, guarded |
| Crash-classify, seeds 22, 58, 130 (first build of this round, Drone change already in) | 12 m: 20 charged crashes in 183 s, 0 pad lips, 0 hop-like rises. 20 m: 9 in 253 s, 0 pad lips |

"First build" means the build before the last three small changes. (1) The mast column widens with the lean. (2) The broad layer is weaker at low height. (3) The shader skips the finest layer where it is faded out. Those touch only the water shader and the soft mast box. After them I reran the water, flat, pop, boat-collider, boat-route and triangle tests. The bloom clamps in `src/entities/ObjectiveMarker.ts` and the debug hooks are untouched.

## Known gaps

# Drone Dash: round 31 critic report

**Verdict:** Pass. The new water beats the old flat plane in 10 of 10 blind pairs. The boats never touch each other, the docks or the shore. The alley camera fix holds (0 hidden frames). One water gap is left. At play height the fine chop is as busy as it is 2 m above the sea. In golden hour and dusk the bay then looks like crumpled foil.

Build tested: the uncommitted round 31 work on top of commit b003276. My dev server ran on port 5191. A copy of b003276 (round 30) ran from a scratch worktree on port 5192 for before and after views. Both are stopped and the worktree is removed. The owner's server on 5188 was left alone. Every browser ran alone, one job at a time, from `critic-scripts/queue31.sh` and `jobs31.txt`. I did not read the round 31 builder notes. I read `src/world/Water.ts`, `src/world/Boats.ts` and the hooks in `Game.ts` only to learn what to test.

New scripts this round (in `progress/round-31/critic-scripts/`):

- `water31.mjs`: water views on both builds, desktop and iPhone 13, game camera and free camera. Moods: seed 130 golden hour, 22 morning, 33 dusk, 58 hazy noon.
- `water31b.mjs`: a flat-frame check (pixel reads in the same task as the render) and wake contrast per mood. It also does a motion sweep for the grid snap and a frame cost test with the water on and off.
- `boats31.mjs`: 120 s fixed-step boat probe on seeds 22, 58 and the fresh seed 4711, plus a drone fly-through of a sailboat.
- `trisweep31.mjs`: trisweep29 plus 1,920 water and marina spots.
- `ab31.py` (blind pairs), `contrast31.py` (fine chop metric), `spells31.py` (hidden spells from cam-clip rows).

## Machine load (read first)

BTLEServer used 98 to 100% of one core all session (`cpu-*.txt`). XProtect also used about 90% of a core at the start. The headless browser still ran at the 120 Hz vsync (median 8.3 ms). All wall-clock numbers below are marked contaminated. The camera and boat verdicts come from fixed-step probes. The GPU timer query (EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2) gave noisy and sometimes negative water costs. So I used a throughput test instead (30 renders, one sync, best of 3).

## Water

**Blind A/B against round 30: new water picked 10 of 10** (`critic/ab/pair-01..10.jpg`, picks written in `ab/picks.txt` before the key was opened). Three pairs show a boat, so those three were not fully blind.

What works:

- **Motion and scale.** Four swell waves (5 to 21 m, peak 0.28 m) plus two scrolling detail layers. Low over the water it reads as real chop with soft rolling shapes (`water31-r31-*-g-low.jpg`). Boats ride the same swell: heave stayed within ±0.27 m on all seeds.
- **Shore.** A clean foam line laps along the whole seawall, with a shallow teal band and a darker wall foot. It matches the wall on every view I took, including top-down (`water31-r31-58-tiling.jpg`, `water31-r31-22-shoreline.jpg`, `water31-r31-m-22-g-shore.jpg`). Foam rings sit round the dock legs.
- **Sun glint and Fresnel.** The glint path sits under the real sun in all four moods. Grazing views go to sky colour, steep views show water colour. No blown-out blob with bloom on.
- **Colour per mood.** Turquoise in morning and noon, deep blue in golden hour, violet in dusk. None of them clash with the city.
- **Horizon.** The swell fades out from 150 to 380 m and the fog takes over. I found no hard seam on any of the 4 moods. The old backdrop skyline boxes still float on the far horizon, as in round 30.
- **No visible tiling** in the top-down shot from 70 m or at cruise height.
- **No blank frames.** 960 frames over 8 water views and 4 moods with bloom on, plus 960 on round 30 and 240 on the phone: 0 flat, 0 black pixels, at least 33 distinct colours of 49 samples.

What still looks fake:

1. **Fine chop does not calm with height.** The `contrast31.py` metric is the same at 24 m and at 2 m. Cruise: 31 to 35. Low: 29 to 39. Ratio: 0.90 to 1.09. Round 30 was 12 to 14 at cruise. In morning and noon the busy surface looks like a bright Mediterranean bay and is fine (`water31-r31-22-g-cruise.jpg`). In golden hour and dusk the same pattern turns into orange or pink flecks on dark troughs. It fills the screen and looks like crumpled foil (`water31-r31-130-g-cruise.jpg`, `water31-r31-33-g-cruise.jpg`). The detail only starts to fade at 60 m, and cruise views look at 30 to 300 m of water.
2. **Wakes vanish toward a low sun.** In morning and noon the rib and ferry wakes are bright and read well. In golden hour, looking toward the sun, the rib and ferry wakes are gone (`water31-r31-130-boat-rib.jpg`, `water31-r31-130-boat-ferry.jpg`). Measured as trail brightness over open-water brightness from 4 camera angles: rib and ferry views under 1.2 were 5 of 16 in golden hour and dusk, and 1 of 16 in morning and noon.
3. **The reflection is sky only.** The seawall, the docks and the buildings never show in the water. So the island edge looks a little pasted on at the shoreline. This is polish.
4. **Grid snap.** The water grid jumps 2.5 m (3.2 m on phones) with the camera. A 2 cm camera move across a snap line changes 14 to 18% of pixels by more than 24 levels. The same move elsewhere changes 0.1 to 1.7%. In flight at 15 m/s the snap frames change only 13% more than other frames, so it hides in motion. A drone that hovers right on a line can make it flicker. Polish.

Phone: the same look at lower detail. The shore foam and the marina read well at 844 px wide (`water31-r31-m-22-g-shore.jpg`, `water31-r31-m-58-g-marina.jpg`).

## Boats

- **Routes: pass.** Seeds 22, 58 and fresh 4711, 120 s each at 30 Hz (3,600 steps): 0 hull overlaps between boats (0.3 m margin), 0 hulls on a dock, 0 hull corners inside a solid. Moving hulls stay at least 28.6 m off the seawall. Moored hulls stay 3.5 m off. Every lane keeps one speed and one direction, so boats cannot meet.
- **Marina and pads: pass.** All pads sit at least 17.5 m inside the seawall (furthest pad 146.5 m from centre). The docks and moored boats start at the wall (164 m). On seed 4711 two doorstep pads sit 19 m inland of the docks and are clear. Boats have no colliders, so they cannot block a route or an arch.
- **Style: good match.** Flat-shaded low poly, the same family as the CC0 cars. The rib (5.2 m) and the rowing boats (4.6 m, about one car) look right beside the cars on the promenade. The docks look good, with foam at the legs (`water31-r31-130-marina.jpg`).
- **Weak spots.** The 20 m "ferry" is a scaled cruise ship and reads as a toy liner. The sailboat is a rustic wooden boat with a brown sail, a bit old-fashioned for the modern city. The boats sail fixed rounded squares at constant speed in every city. Nothing docks or leaves. After a minute it feels like a carousel. **Needs a human eye.**
- **Bobbing and roll: believable.** Pitch and roll follow the swell under bow, stern and both sides. Sailboats heel and sway. A moving rib lifts its bow.
- **The drone flies through boats.** I flew the drone at 4 m straight through a moving sailboat: no crash, no bump, 0 frames in a solid. The screenshot shows the mast through the drone (`boats31-22-drone-in-sail.jpg`). The marina's moored sailboat sits 8.5 m off the promenade, well inside the flight bounds.

## Alley camera (round 30 gap): fixed

| Run | Frames | Hidden frames | Longest spell | In solid | Jumps over 1 m |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cam-clip30, desktop 22, no orbit | 6,925 | **0** | none | 0 | 0 |
| cam-clip24, desktop 22, random orbit | 6,918 | **0** | none | 0 | 0 |
| cam-clip24, desktop 58, random orbit | 6,927 | **0** | none | 0 | 0 |
| cam-clip24, iPhone 22, no orbit | 6,938 | **0** | none | 0 | 0 |

Round 30 on the same cam-clip30 run: 69 hidden frames, one 0.575 s spell on Quill Row. Now the drone sits in the middle of Quill Row (`cam-clip30-22-r31-noorbit-6-alley.jpg`).

`climb30.mjs` still passes: 0 jumps over 1.0 m on desktop (max 0.91 m) and iPhone (max 0.89 m), 0 frames in solid, closest camera 5.39 m. One desktop frame reached a 40.3% drone height share (round 30: 0, max 39.4%). That is one frame at the line, not a snap.

## Budgets

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Triangles, 3,256 spots per run (1,336 city spots plus 1,920 water and marina spots) | Desktop 22: 571k. Desktop 130: **585k**. iPhone 130: 518k. Water spots max 452k. **0 spots over 600k.** |
| Draw calls | Max 143 desktop, 126 iPhone. 0 over 150. Street run max 144. |
| Water cost, desktop (throughput, contaminated) | +0.5 to 0.9 ms a frame in water views. About 0 in a city view. Against round 30's water: +0.4 to 0.5 ms. |
| Water cost, iPhone 13 (throughput, contaminated) | +0.0 to 0.5 ms a frame. |
| Street frame time (12 s, 120 Hz vsync, contaminated) | Desktop p95 9.0 / 8.8 ms (normal / rush), max 10.4. iPhone p95 9.4 / 9.6 ms, max 10.4. |
| First flight | 0 long tasks and 0 shader compiles after Play in 3 runs (2 desktop, 1 iPhone). |
| First load | Production build 3.0 MB in total, all lazy assets included (JS 935 KB, boats.glb 240 KB). Type check clean. |

## Regressions

- **Flat-frame probe: pass.** Round 1 probe: 894 frames, 0 flat, 0 errors. Water and glint views: 0 flat (see above).
- **Crash-classify, 8 seeds, 0 pad lips: pass.** 12 m: 41 crashes in 523 s (4.7 a minute), 8 near the target, closest 3.0 m below a top. 20 m: 36 in 639 s (3.4 a minute), 15 near the target.
- **People probe: pass.** 0 people on active pads (48 legs, 1,536 samples).
- **Traffic per-frame overlap: pass.** 0 in all 6 runs at 120 Hz.
- **Phone HUD probe: pass.** iPhone 22, 58, 130: marker on controls 0, drone under pills 0, pops on the drone 0%.
- **Chimes with pops: pass.** 41 of 41 chimes had the pop shown within 0.3 s.
- **Medal gate, breakdown exact on all 6 runs: pass.** Street: 5,695 / 3,779 / 5,965, all Silver, total 15,439 (round 30: 13,230), strict delivery share 64%. Lazy: 1,256 Bronze / 927 none / 1,048 Bronze, total 3,231.
- **Exploits: pass.** No-delivery farm 0 on 22, 58, 130. Carry farm 0.24, 0.25 and 0 of honest points a minute. Honest 4,559 / 4,892 / 6,859 (Gold). One delivery: best 1,149 Bronze.
- Only frames over 20 ms in the 80 s HUD runs: the probe ending at 80.5 s.

## Biggest remaining gap in the water and boats

**At play height the water is too busy.** It is as busy as at 2 m above the sea. The fine chop keeps full strength out to 60 m and fades slowly after. So from 15 to 30 m up the whole bay is one even field of fine flecks. In golden hour and dusk it reads as crumpled foil, not as sea. Good stylized water gets calmer and broader with distance: big soft colour shapes, with sparkle mostly in the glint path.

**Acceptance test:**

- Rerun `water31.mjs` (desktop, seeds 130, 22, 33, 58), then `contrast31.py r31`.
- Pass marks: cruise to low ratio at most 0.6 on all 4 moods. Low view still at least 25 (keep the close-up chop). Cruise still at least 15 (do not go back to the flat plane).
- Blind A/B against round 30 (`ab31.py`) still picks the new water in at least 8 of 10 pairs.
- Flat-frame probe stays at 0. Water cost stays under +1.0 ms a frame on desktop.

## Other gaps, ranked

1. **The drone flies through boats.** No colliders on hulls or masts, and the marina is inside the flight bounds. Test: fly at 4 m into the moored marina sailboat's mast and into a lane-30 sailboat. The drone must bump or crash (contact or crash count over 0). There must be 0 frames with the drone centre within 0.4 m of the mast line.
2. **Wakes vanish toward a low sun.** Test (`water31b.mjs` wake block): trail over open-water brightness at least 1.3 in all 32 rib and ferry views over the 4 moods. Today 6 of 32 are under 1.2.
3. **Boat traffic feels like a carousel.** Fixed rounded squares, constant speed, the same pattern in every city, and no boat ever docks or leaves. Add a ferry run to a pier, or a boat that pulls in and out of the marina. **Needs a human eye.**
4. **Desktop pops cover the drone** in 26% of pop samples on seed 22 (round 30: 32 to 48%). The phone keeps them clear. Test: under 2% on desktop seeds 22, 58 and 130.
5. **Grid snap.** 14 to 18% of pixels change on a 2 cm camera move across a snap line (control under 2%). Test: across-line change at most 2 times the control in the `water31.mjs` pop block.

## Screenshots (progress/round-31/critic/), 83 files

- **Blind A/B pairs:** `ab/pair-01.jpg` to `ab/pair-10.jpg`, key in `ab/.key.json`, picks in `ab/picks.txt`.

- **Water, all moods:** `water31-r31-{130,22,33,58}-{g-shore,g-marina,glint}.jpg`, `water31-r31-58-tiling.jpg`, `water31-r31-22-horizon.jpg`, `water31-r31-58-postcard.jpg`, `water31-r31-22-marina-high.jpg`, `water31-r31-130-marina.jpg`. The first free-camera shots per seed still show the title fading out.
- **Boats:** `water31-r31-{130,22,33,58}-boat-{rib,ferry,sail}.jpg` (golden hour 130 shows the missing wakes), `water31-r31-m-58-boat-rib.jpg`, `water31-r31-m-58-g-marina.jpg`, `water31-r31-m-22-g-shore.jpg`, `boats31-22-drone-in-sail.jpg`.

# Drone Dash: round 31 builder notes

Owner request: some boats in the water next to the island, and more realistic water.
Plus the round 30 leftover: the alley camera hid the drone behind a wall (Quill Row seed 22, Thimble Lane seed 58).

Dev server: my own on port 5190 (stopped at the end). The owner's 5188 was left alone. Browsers ran one at a time.
Machine: BTLEServer at 99 to 100% of one core in every `cpu-*.txt`. The NordVPN helper used up to 13%. Headless Chromium still ran at
120 fps this session. Wall-clock frame numbers are marked contaminated. The water cost comes from GPU timer queries.

## 1. Water (`src/world/Water.ts`, new)

- **Mesh:** a grid that follows the camera (snapped to the 2.5 m step in `onBeforeRender`, so near vertices never swim).
  2.5 m cells near the camera, growing 7% per ring out to 1.3 km. 23k triangles. Phone: 3.2 m cells, 9% growth, about 11k.
- **Swell:** four sum-of-sines waves: 21, 13, 8.3 and 5.1 m long, 0.13, 0.08, 0.045 and 0.025 m high, deep-water speeds slowed 20%. The
  vertex shader lifts the grid, fading the swell out between 150 and 380 m from the camera. The GLSL is generated from the
  same `WAVES` table as the TypeScript `waveHeight()` that the boats sample, so there is one source.
- **Normals:** per pixel, the analytic swell gradient plus two scrolling, rotated samples of a tileable detail normal map
  (made in code at start, 18 sine waves, 256 px). Phones use one sample and 128 px. Detail fades with distance.
- **Colour and reflection:** Fresnel (Schlick, F0 0.02, base clamped before `pow`) between a deep-to-shallow water colour and an
  analytic reflection of the mood's own sky gradient (the same uniforms as the sky dome: horizon, mid, top, sun halo). The sun
  glint is the key light's GGX specular at roughness 0.16, so building shadows remove it. Indirect env specular is not used.
- **Shore:** exact signed distance to the seawall box (`|x|, |z| = 164`). Shallow colour within about 16 m. A darker band
  shows the wall's foot. Lapping foam moves in and out along the wall, broken by the noise channel. Scattered foam patches
  reach out to 6 m. Foam round the marina docks from their rectangles. Foam also catches sky light, so it stays white in
  building shadow.
- **Wakes:** up to 8 moving boats sent each frame (position, speed, half sizes, heading as sin/cos). Per boat: a Kelvin V
  (19.5 degree arms) with ripples that tilt the normal, a foam trail and a bow wave. Strength grows with speed. Fragments more
  than about 20 m plus the wake length from a boat skip it.
- **Moods:** deep, shallow and foam colours plus reflection strength per mood (golden hour, bright morning, rose dusk, hazy noon).
- **NaN safety (round 1 lesson):** every `pow` base is clamped to [0, 1]. Normals are built as `normalize(vec3(.., 1.0, ..))`.
  The reflection vector gets a tiny +y before `normalize`. Reversed `smoothstep` edges (undefined in GLSL) were rewritten.
  Flat-frame probe with bloom: 877 frames, 0 flat, 0 errors.

Before / after (desktop and phone, cruise height, low over the water, at the seawall, every mood):
`builder-shots/before-water-*.jpg` (24) and `builder-shots/after-water-*.jpg` (40, adds the marina and a wide view).

## 2. Boats (new `src/world/Boats.ts`, assets in `public/assets/models/boats.glb`)

- **Assets:** CC0 Quaternius models from Poly Pizza through the Blender MCP: Sail Boat, Lifeboat (used as a fast rigid
  inflatable), Cruise Ship (scaled to a 20 m harbour ferry), Boat (rowing / fishing boat), Dock (marina). The round 28
  pipeline (`flatten`) plus `builder-scripts/blender_boats.py`: vertex colours, bow on +Z, keel at 0, one GLB, 240 KB,
  3,116 triangles. Logged in ASSETS.md. No generation, no paid credits, nothing saved to a .blend file. At the start, Poly Pizza
  and Poly Haven were off in the Blender session. I switched both on in the add-on panel (scene properties).
- **Loading:** with the street assets after the first frame (`Game.loadAssets`), compiled with `compileAsync` before they are
  added. One `InstancedMesh` per kind plus one for the docks: 5 draw calls (10 with the shadow pass).
- **Layout:** 10 boats. 6 move on four lanes, rounded squares at 30, 52, 78 and 104 m from the seawall: 2 sailboats
  (2.8 m/s), 2 speedboats (8.5 m/s), the ferry (4.4 m/s), 1 sailboat (3.2 m/s). One speed and one direction per lane, so
  no boat can meet another, the shore or the marina. Start positions shift per city seed. 4 boats are moored in a small marina
  on the south wall (two 16 m docks at x = -52 and -36).
- **Motion:** heave from the swell at the hull centre (same fade as the shader), pitch and roll from four samples at bow,
  stern and both sides. Sailboats heel 7 degrees plus a slow sway. Speedboats trim bow-up 3.4 degrees.
- **Rules:** boats and docks have no colliders (like the hover-vans), so they never charge a crash. They are all on the water,
  more than 3.5 m from the seawall, so never on a delivery pad.

## 3. Alley camera (`src/systems/CameraRig.ts`, `smoothRel`)

Cause, found with a per-frame log of the glide's choice: on Quill Row the glide's target was itself hidden. The per-frame cap
upstream (`MAX_REL_STEP`) kept the target within 1.7 m of a camera behind the alley corner. With a hidden target, the glide
skips its sight test. So the camera glided along out of sight for 0.26 to 0.57 s.

Fix (the climb fix is untouched):
1. A hidden target is replaced by the clear part of the line from the drone to the target. The ideal chase point is the second
   choice. The new target must be free of walls and at least the glide gap from the drone.
2. If no step along the glide sees the drone, search all round the last camera within one smooth step (26 directions, three
   radii up to 0.9 m) for a wall-free point that does, nearest the target.
3. The drone stays hidden for at most 0.045 s (`HIDE_MAX`). After that, the camera cuts to the nearest clear view further out.
   (Never needed in the tests below.)

## Acceptance results

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Boat kinds visible | 4 (sail, speedboat, ferry, rowing boat) |
| Moving boats | 6, each with a wake (`after-water-*-wide.jpg`, `after-boat-*.jpg`) |
| 120 s fixed-step probe, seeds 22 and 130 (`boat-probe.log`) | 7,200 steps each: 0 hull-shore, 0 hull-hull, 0 hull-dock overlaps. Closest hull corner to the wall 3.5 m |
| Bob against the water (instance matrices against `waterAt` with the fade) | max error 0.0056 m (limit 0.1). Heave range per kind matches the water's within 0.01 m (about -0.27 to +0.28 m) |
| Camera: `cam-clip30` seed 22, no orbit | 0 hidden frames (round 30: 115), 0 in solid, 0 jumps over 1 m |
| `cam-clip24` seed 22 / 58 random orbit, iPhone 22 no orbit | 0 / 0 / 0 hidden frames, 0 in solid, 0 jumps over 1 m |
| `climb30` desktop / iPhone | 0 of 4,800 frames over 1.0 m (max 0.896 m), 0 in solid, max height share 0.395 |

## Budgets

GPU time per frame (EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2, whole pipeline, 40 frames per pose, `perf-water-*.log`):

| Pose | Desktop 1280x720, bloom on: frame / water share / boats | iPhone 13 (wide): frame / water |
|---|---|---|
| Cruise over the bay | 8.1 ms / 2.1 to 2.3 ms / under 0.4 ms (noise) | 4.3 ms / 1.6 ms |
| Low over the water | 7.6 to 7.8 ms / 1.8 to 3.4 ms | 4.0 ms / 1.4 ms |
| Marina | 8.5 ms / 2.1 ms | 3.6 ms / 0.4 ms |
| Downtown street (water hidden) | 9.1 to 9.7 ms / 0.1 ms | 5.1 ms / 1.4 ms |

The GPU-timer p95 per pose is 12.5 to 14.6 ms on desktop. It is the same with the water off (14.2 ms in the city pose). So
that spread is timer noise, not the water.

Real time (contaminated, BTLEServer at 100%):
- Circling low over the marina (`perf-shore-*.log`): desktop median 8.3 ms, p95 9.8 / 10.0 ms. iPhone p95 9.7 ms. No long tasks.
- Street (`perf-street-*.log`): desktop p95 9.7 / 9.5 ms (normal / rush), iPhone 9.5 / 9.7 ms.
- Draw calls: trisweep max 145 (desktop 130), 142 (desktop 22), 128 (iPhone 130). All under 150.
- Triangles: trisweep max 584k (desktop 130), 559k (desktop 22), 518k (iPhone 130). 0 spots over 600k. Round 30 was 542k.
  The water grid adds 23k and the boats about 8k. This is now the tightest budget.
- First load: production build 3.0 MB without source maps (round 30: 2.7 MB). boats.glb is 240 KB of it.. JS 935 KB.
- First flight: 0 long tasks and 0 new shader programs after Play (2 desktop runs, 1 iPhone run). Max frame 16.7 ms.

## Regressions (all on port 5190, `builder-scripts/`)

- Crash-classify, seeds 22, 58, 130: 12 m: 24 charged crashes in 201 s, 0 pad lips (closest 2.4 m below a top). 20 m: 9 in
  211 s, 0 pad lips (closest 2.6 m). Only 3 seeds here. The critic ran 8.
- People on active pads: 0 (48 legs, 1,536 samples).
- Traffic per-frame overlap: 0 on seeds 22, 130, 58 (12,001 frames each).
- Phone HUD (iPhone 22, 58, 130): marker on controls 0, pops on the drone 0. Drone under a pill: 1 of 798 samples on the
  first seed 22 run, 0 on a repeat and on 58 and 130.
- Flat frames with bloom: 0 of 877.
- Street medal gate (low line), breakdown exact on all 3: 5,428 Silver (22), 2,930 Silver (58), 5,284 Silver (130).
  Total 13,642 (round 30 critic: 13,230).
- No-delivery farm: 0 points on 22, 58 and 130.
- `npm run build`: passes (type check clean). The bloom clamps in `ObjectiveMarker.ts` and every bot hook are unchanged.

## Not done / open

- No real reflections of the city or boats in the water (sky only). A planar reflection costs a second scene pass.
- Boats do not react to the drone, and the drone flies through them. That matches the vans. A human player must judge it.
- Rowing boats and docks are plain kit models. A human eye must check the boats' scale against the cars and people.
- After the after-shots I made slow boats' wake trails weaker (sailboats and the ferry). The water shots were taken just
  before that, `after-boat-*.jpg` just after.
- The critic's other round 30 gaps (slow re-centre after turns, desktop pops) were not touched.

## Files changed

- `src/world/Water.ts` (new): water mesh, shader, swell table and `waveHeight`, shore distance.
- `src/world/Boats.ts` (new): boats, lanes, marina, bobbing, wakes, probe data.

- `src/vite-env.d.ts`: hook types.

Scripts in `builder-scripts/`:
