# Drone Dash: round 30 critic report

**Verdict:** The climb snap is fixed. The new camera does not mislead players in turns. But in one alley (Quill Row, seed 22) it now hides the drone behind a wall for up to 0.6 s. Round 29 did not do this.

Build tested: the uncommitted round 30 work (CameraRig.ts, a `camSmooth` probe hook) on top of commit c0b5238. My dev server ran on port 5191. A copy of commit c0b5238 (round 29) ran on port 5192 for A/B checks. Both are stopped. The owner's server on 5188 was left alone. Every browser ran alone, one job at a time, from `critic-scripts/queue30.sh` and `jobs30.txt`. I did not read the round 30 builder notes. The round 29 scripts were copied to `progress/round-30/critic-scripts/`. Their output folders are relative, so they now write to round 30.

New scripts this round:

- `climb30.mjs`: climb29 with a 1.0 m jump line, a camera-in-solid check and the closest distance per frame.
- `heading30.mjs`: a fixed-step flight (boost, sharp turns, hover turn, zig-zag). Per frame, it compares the camera's view direction with the drone's heading and travel direction. It also logs trail distance, sideways offset and the nav marker position against the true bearing.
- `marker30.mjs`: a "human model" that steers only by the screen. It turns until the projected nav marker sits over the drone (or over screen centre). It runs with a yaw-truth bot as the baseline.
- `padview30.mjs`: glides onto 24 real pads, mostly beside walls (4 approach headings). After the pickup or drop, it logs where the camera looks.
- `route-play-hd30.mjs`: the street medal bot, unchanged except for a port setting and a log of its heading error.
- `cam-clip30.mjs`: cam-clip24 with a port setting. It also takes a screenshot of each moment that a wall hides the drone.

## Machine load (read first)

BTLEServer used 58 to 100% of one core all session. At the start, NordVPN also used 100% of a core (`cpu-ff.txt`). Unlike round 29, the headless browser was not capped at 30 fps this time. First-flight and perf runs held 120 fps (median 8.3 ms). The 80 s HUD runs swung between 8.4 and 16.5 ms median. All wall-clock times are still marked contaminated. The camera verdicts come from fixed-step probes.

## Camera results

### Fixed-step climb test (32 climbs, 31 beside walls, seeds 22 and 130): pass

| Build | Frames with a jump over 1.0 m | Max jump | Frames in solid | Closest camera | Frames at 40% or more | Max height share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Round 30 desktop | **0** of 4,800 | 0.90 m | 0 | 5.42 m | 0 | 0.394 |
| Round 30 iPhone 13 | **0** of 4,800 | 0.91 m | 0 | 5.42 m | 0 | 0.394 |
| Round 29 desktop (control) | 50 (in 11 climbs) | 3.70 m | 0 | 4.32 m | 10 | 0.516 |

The snap is gone in all four climb modes (up, up+back, up+turn, up+forward).

### Wall-side framing (real time, 3 s after each pickup or drop): pass

| Run | Wall samples | 40% or more | Max |
|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop 22 / 58 / 130 | 62 / 62 / 63 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.32 / 0.34 / 0.27 |
| iPhone 22 / 58 / 130 | 60 / 0 / 58 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.33 / 0.32 / 0.27 |

That is 0 of 365 wall samples at 40% or more (round 29: 3 of 454). iPhone seed 58 had no wall-side event in its 80 s, so it adds nothing. Per-frame open-street minimum: 2.53 m. Camera in solid: 0. Drone hidden in open streets: 0.

### Tunnels and alleys: fail (new regression)

| Run (10 passes each) | In solid | Closest | Jumps over 1 m | Drone hidden |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop seed 22, random orbit | 0 | 3.74 m | 1 | **39 frames** (Quill Row) |
| Desktop seed 58, random orbit | 0 | 4.17 m | 0 | **16 frames** (Thimble Lane, 0.32 s) |
| iPhone seed 22, no orbit | 0 | 2.72 m | 0 | **20 frames** (Quill Row) |
| A/B desktop seed 22, no orbit, round 30 | 0 | | 1 (2.46 m) | **115 frames: 0.57 s and 0.38 s** |
| A/B desktop seed 22, no orbit, round 29 | 0 | | 1 | 4 frames (0.03 s) |

Round 29's own runs had 0 hidden frames. On Quill Row the round 30 camera stays outside the alley mouth, so the screen shows a brick wall and the drone is gone. The player gets no input from the screen for half a second, in a narrow passage. See `cam-clip30-22-r30-noorbit-6-alley.jpg` (only wall) against `cam-clip30-22-r29-noorbit-6-alley.jpg` (the same moment on round 29: drone centred in the alley). `cam-clip30-22-r30-6-hidden.jpg` shows the corner hiding the drone. The code comment says the view of the drone comes back "a frame or two later". The real figure is 23 to 34 frames.

### Laggy or floaty?

Measured with fixed-step inputs, same drone path on both builds (`heading30.mjs`). The yaw bot shows that the physics are identical.

- **Full boost (peak 24 m/s):** the camera trails less. Distance is 14.5 m against 15.8 m at 25 m altitude, and 13.1 against 14.2 m at street level. Distance changes now lag about 0.3 to 0.5 s in both directions.
- **Sharp turns:** the view now lags *less*. Mid-turn, the view direction is 35° off the heading (round 29: 42°) and 9° off the travel direction (round 29: 16°).
- **After a turn: slower re-centre.** Round 29 is back behind the drone 0.5 s after the turn ends. Round 30 stays 0.5 to 0.8 m to the side and 2 to 4° off for 2 s. Its time constant is about 0.9 s (round 29: 0.2 s). After a hover turn, it is still 4 to 6° off 1.5 s later (round 29: 0.6°). On screen, the heading point drifts 30 to 80 px over those 2 s. It is a slow sideways settle, not a lag in the turn itself. Does it feel floaty? **Needs a human player.**
- Does the view still show where you are going? Yes. Turn shots match round 29 almost exactly (`heading30-r30-*` against `heading30-r29-*`).

## Seed 58: only the bot is fooled, and the Bronze did not reproduce

1. **The marker is true on both builds.** The nav marker, arch tags and pad marker are projections of the real target through the real camera. My probe compared the marker's screen offset with the true bearing every frame, and the relation is the same on both builds.
2. **A screen-steering player does better on round 30.** The human model turns until the marker sits over the drone. It finished 6 seed 58 legs in 67 s on round 30 against 106 s on round 29. Steering by screen centre took 66 s against 90 s. The yaw-truth bot took 60.1 s on both. Seed 22: 117 s against 125 s. Seed 130: 143 s against 173 s. When this player thinks it is "aimed", the true heading error is 20 to 23° on round 30 and 42 to 44° on round 29. So the new camera misleads a screen-steering player less, not more.
3. **The bot reads the camera wrong on both builds.** Under 4 m/s, the bot takes its heading as the line from the camera to the drone. That happens after every pad and hover turn. That is wrong by a median 30° on round 30 and 46° on round 29. Round 30 has a fatter tail (90th percentile 93 to 95° against 57°), from the slow re-centre after hover turns.
4. **No Bronze here.** Street bot on seed 58, round 30: 3,575, 4,311 and 3,482, all Silver. Round 29: 4,042 and 3,667, both Silver. The 1,443 and 1,702 runs look like bot variance plus the old 30 fps cap. To fix the bot, make it use drone yaw when slow.
5. After a wall-side pad, the camera ends 30° or more off the heading in 10% of frames (round 29: 7.9%). It is never over 60° on either build.

## Regressions

- **Crash-classify, 8 seeds, 0 pad lips: pass.** 12 m: 50 crashes in 547 s (5.5 a minute), 10 near the target, closest 4.4 m below a top. 20 m: 30 in 641 s (2.8 a minute), 11 near the target, closest 1.6 m below.
- **People probe: pass.** 0 people on active pads (48 legs, 1,536 samples).
- **Traffic per-frame overlap: pass.** 0 in all 6 fixed 120 Hz runs (seeds 4, 4, 4, 22, 130, 58).
- **Phone HUD probe: pass.** iPhone 22, 58, 130: marker on controls 0, drone under pills 0, pops on drone 0 / 0 / 0.39%, pops on "Fly" 0.
- **Flat-frame probe: pass.** 1,011 frames, 0 flat, 0 errors.
- **Chimes with pops: pass.** 63 of 63 chimes had `#slip-pop` shown within 0.3 s.
- **Medal gate, breakdown exact (bdOk) on all 10 runs: pass.**
  - Street: 4,003 / 3,575 / 5,652, all Silver, total 13,230 (round 29: 13,546). Strict delivery share 62.6%.
  - Lazy (cruise 10, no boost): 1,250 Bronze / 884 none / 1,035 Bronze, total 3,169.
- **Exploits: pass.**
  - No-delivery farm: 0 on 22, 58 and 130.
  - Carry farm: 0.23, 0 and 0.24 of honest points a minute. Honest runs: 4,559, 4,892 and 6,859 (Gold).
  - One delivery: best 1,149 Bronze (seed 130), so no better than Bronze.
- **Triangles and draw calls: pass.** Desktop 130: 542k, 135 calls. Desktop 22: 528k, 134 calls. iPhone 130: 489k, 117 calls. 0 spots over 600k.
- **First flight: pass.** 0 long tasks and 0 shader compiles after Play in 3 runs (2 desktop, 1 iPhone). Max frame 16.6 ms.
- **First load: pass.** Production build without maps: 2.7 MB. JS 921 KB, CSS 40 KB. Type check clean.

## Performance (contaminated, BTLEServer at 98%)

| Run (12 s) | Frame median / p95 | Max | Calls max | Triangles max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Street desktop, normal / rush | 8.3 / 9.3 ms | 9.5 ms | 132 / 137 | 461k / 473k |
| Street iPhone 13, normal / rush | 8.3 / 9.3 ms | 9.5 ms | 116 / 117 | 419k / 416k |

p95 is under 12 ms at the 120 Hz vsync, even with one core busy. The 80 s HUD runs had two short bursts of three frames at 90 to 110 ms. They came at 52 s on desktop 130 and at 55 s on iPhone 58. The probe takes screenshots during play, so these are probably probe stalls. The roughly 80.8 s frame in every run is the probe ending. Recheck on a quiet machine.

## Biggest remaining gap

**In an alley, a wall can hide the drone for up to 0.6 s.** The round 30 glide keeps the camera outside the alley mouth on Quill Row (seed 22). It also does this for a moment on Thimble Lane (seed 58). This happens with and without orbit input, on desktop and phone. Round 29 showed the drone in the same passes.

**Acceptance test:**

- Run `cam-clip30.mjs` (NOORBIT=1 SEED=22, desktop).
- Run `cam-clip24.mjs` on seeds 22 and 58 (random orbit) and on iPhone seed 22 (no orbit).
- Pass marks: no hidden spell longer than 0.1 s, and at most 10 hidden frames per run. Round 29 had 4 frames, 0.03 s. Camera in solid 0. Per-frame jumps over 1 m: at most 1 per run.
- `climb30.mjs` must still show 0 jumps over 1.0 m.

## Other gaps, ranked

1. **Slow re-centre after turns.** After each turn, the camera stays 0.5 to 0.8 m to the side and 2 to 4° off for about 2 s. Round 29 took 0.5 s. It likely comes from the new glide stacking on top of the old follow lerp. Test: in `heading30.mjs`, the sideways offset is under 0.2 m within 0.6 s after a turn ends, while keeping today's lower mid-turn lag. Is it floaty? **Needs a human player.**
2. **Desktop pops cover the drone** in 32 to 48% of pop samples (round 29: 28 to 44%). The phone keeps them clear. Test: under 2% on desktop seeds 22, 58 and 130.
3. **The street and roof bots steer by the camera when slow.** Their heading input is 30 to 46° wrong on both builds. So their scores change with each camera change. Switch them to drone yaw under 4 m/s before you use them as a medal gate again.
4. **Real-time perf on a quiet machine.** Recheck the 90 to 110 ms bursts and the p95 with BTLEServer idle.
5. **Shop signs and faces** (from round 28). Sign plates are white blobs, and people have no faces. **Needs a human eye.**

## Screenshots (progress/round-30/critic/), 53 files

- **Alley regression:** `cam-clip30-22-r30-noorbit-6-alley.jpg` against `cam-clip30-22-r29-noorbit-6-alley.jpg`, plus `cam-clip30-22-r30-6-hidden.jpg`, `cam-clip30-22-r30-7-hidden.jpg`, `cam-clip30-22-r29-7-hidden.jpg`, `cam-clip30-22-{r29,r30}-noorbit-{5-tunnel,10-alley}.jpg`, `cam-clip-22-*`, `cam-clip-58-*`, `cam-clip-22-m-noorbit-*`.
- **Turns, same frame on both builds:** `heading30-{r29,r30}-d-58-a25-{boostTurnL,cruiseTurnR,hoverTurnL,zigR}.jpg`.
- **Round 29 climb snaps (control):** `climb30-r29-d-22-4-spike.jpg`, `climb30-r29-d-22-9-spike.jpg`, `climb30-r29-d-130-6-spike.jpg`. Round 30 had no frame worth a shot.
- **Desktop pops on the drone:** `raw/fr30-d-{22,58,130}-h04-low-payout-pop.jpg`, `raw/fr30-d-{22,58,130}-h05-low-payout-chain.jpg`. Phone for contrast: `raw/fr30-m-22-h04-low-payout-pop.jpg`.
- **Medal runs:** `M-low-seed{22,58,130}-pass*.jpg`, `M-low-c10-seed{22,130}-pass1.jpg`.
- **Other:** `tris29-{d-22,d-130,m-130}-worst.jpg` (written by the reused trisweep29 script) and 4 crash-classify near-target shots (`N-alt*`).

# Drone Dash: round 30 builder notes

Main concern from the round 29 critic: the camera snaps 2 to 3.7 m in one frame in fast climbs out of wall-side pads.
Small leftovers: (A) the carry farm on seed 130 at 0.52 of honest points a minute, (B) the roof bot stall on seed 22.

## How I worked and tested

- My own dev server on 127.0.0.1:5190 (stopped at the end). The owner's server on 5188 was not touched.
- A round 29 snapshot (`git archive c0b5238`, no repo state changed) ran on 5193 for the A/B jobs and was stopped.
- The round 29 critic scripts are copied to `progress/round-30/builder-scripts/`. Only the output paths changed (scratch
  folder for raw output, port 5190). One browser at a time from one queue (`queue30.sh`, `jobs30.txt`, log `queue30.log`).
- Machine load: BTLEServer at 99 to 100% of one core in every check (`cpu-start.txt`, `cpu-hud.txt`, `cpu-ff.txt`,
  `cpu-medal.txt`). Real-time runs were held at 30 fps again. Every camera number below comes from fixed-step (60 Hz)
  probes, except the hud-probe and cam-clip runs, which are real time.
- New scripts:
  - `climb30.mjs`: the critic's `climb29.mjs` plus per-frame camera-inside-solid (pad 0 and 0.1), a thin-line occlusion
    test (the `cam-sampler.js` one) and the count of frames with a jump over 1.0 m. Same events, same keys, same 60 Hz.
  - `climbdbg.mjs`: the same with the camera rig's glide state per frame (debug only).
  - `climbshots.mjs`: a filmstrip of the critic's worst climb (seed 22, event 4, the one in `climb29-d-22-4-spike.jpg`).
  - `capfarm-yaw.mjs`: `capfarm.mjs` steering by the drone's yaw instead of the camera (camera-independent bot).
  - `route-play-trace.mjs`: the deterministic `route-play.mjs` with a trace every 0.5 s, `HEAD=yaw` and `FIX=1`.
  - `route-play-rt-x-m-esc17-fix30.mjs`: the real-time medal bot with one bot fix (see B) and an optional trace.
  - `route-play-rt-x-m-esc17-port.mjs`: the medal bot taking `PORT` (round 29 A/B).
  - `geo22.mjs`, `geo22b.mjs`: solid geometry (and every collider) around the seed 22 stall spot.
  - `ab58.sh`, `ab58b.sh`: the deterministic street bot on seed 58, round 30 against round 29, steering by camera or yaw.
- New debug hook: `camSmooth()` (the camera glide's last check). Bot hooks and the bloom clamps in
  `ObjectiveMarker.ts` are unchanged.

## 1. Camera snaps in fast climbs out of wall-side pads

**Cause.** Three round 29 parts fought each other every frame. The follow pulled the camera toward the chase ideal (about
4 to 5 m behind). Then the room floor (`keepRoom`) wanted 8.8 m for 3.2 s after a pickup or drop. Beside a wall the
straight push-out was blocked, so it took the "rise" branch toward a point almost straight over the drone, at most 2.4 m
a frame. That move is a chord through the sphere, so the camera came closer while moving 2.4 m, on top of the 1.7 m the
per-frame cap had already allowed. The hard gap (`hardGap`, 2.35 m) could add its own 2.0 m step after that. Next
frame the follow pulled in again. So the camera swung between about 6 and 8.8 m, up to 3.7 m in one frame. A trace
(`climbdbg.mjs`) also showed a second case. The test turns the drone as it lands it on the pad, so the chase heading
is still swinging round when the climb starts, and that swing sweeps the view into the wall beside the pad. The clip
pull-in then cut the camera in by 2 to 3 m in one frame.

**Fix (`src/systems/CameraRig.ts`).**
- The floor, rise and hard-gap code now produce only a target. They place it in one step (the round 29 per-frame
  caps `RISE_STEP`, `PUSH_STEP`, `SOFT_GAP` are gone, which ends the 6 to 8.8 m swing).
- A new last stage, `smoothRel`, moves the camera. It works on the camera's offset from the drone, in a frame that
  turns with the chase heading and the player's orbit. So turning with the drone passes straight through, and the
  orbit control and ease-back are unchanged. Changes of distance, height and side follow a critically damped spring
  (0.09 s). It runs at up to 20 m/s, or 45 m/s when it backs away from the drone, and never moves more than 0.92 m
  relative to the drone in one frame.
- The glide is checked every frame. If it would put the camera in a wall (0.3 m pad), under 2.15 m from the drone, or
  out of sight of the drone, it tries the same glide with this frame's turn held back. Then it tries small steps toward
  the target, with a clear view first, then a thin-line view. Then it tries a step round the wall (over, under or
  aside, whichever ends nearest the target). Only if none of these works within 0.92 m does it take a bigger step, so
  the hard gap is now a soft limit that bites only where geometry forces it.
- The rise beside a wall now tries tilted-up spots on the camera's own side first (0.72 back and 0.7 up of the floor
  distance, then 0.45 and 0.9), and only then the near-vertical ones. The target stays near the camera, and the
  view keeps its heading.
- A teleport (the drone moved more than 3 m in a frame: a respawn or a probe placing it) restarts the glide, as before.
- The shake is now an offset on top of the smoothed camera. It is taken off at the start of the next frame, so it
  cannot build up in the glide.
- Unchanged: tunnel and alley framing, arrival framing, orbit limits, the swing, the per-frame cap of round 23, the
  push-out from walls, `keepInFrame`.

**Numbers (fixed 60 Hz steps, the critic's 32 climbs: seeds 22 and 130, Space, Space+S, Space+A, Space+W).**

| Climb test, 32 climbs, 4,800 frames | Jumps over 1.0 m | Over 1.7 m | Max jump | Inside solid (pad 0 / 0.1) | Drone hidden | Closest camera | Frames at 40% or more | Max height share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Round 29 code, desktop (`climb30-base-d.log`) | 48 | 30 | 3.71 m | 0 / 0 | n/a | 4.34 m | 8 | 0.514 |
| Round 30, desktop (`climb30-d.log`, `climb30-final-d.log`) | **0** | 0 | 0.88 m | **0 / 0** | 0 | **5.43 m** | 0 | 0.395 |
| Round 30, iPhone 13 (`climb30-m.log`, `climb30-final-m.log`) | **0** | 0 | 0.91 m | **0 / 0** | 0 | **5.42 m** | 0 | 0.395 |
| Critic's own `climb29.mjs`, round 30, desktop / iPhone | 0 / 0 (it counts over 1.7 m) | | 0.91 / 0.90 m | | | 5.42 / 5.42 m | 0 / 0 | 0.394 |

The filmstrip of the critic's worst climb (seed 22, event 4, a pickup then Space) is
`builder-shots/climb30-{d,m}-22-4-up-f00..f70.jpg`. The camera stays 7.4 to 10 m away and the drone stays at 17 to 33% of the
screen height. Round 29 snapped 3.6 m there in one frame and reached 51%.

**Wall-side framing (hud-probe28, first run, street bot 80 s, real time at 30 fps, every 100 ms for 3 s after each
pickup or drop; "beside a wall" = a solid within 4 m; `fb27.py`).**

| Run | Samples after events | Beside a wall | Drone box 40% or more | Max share | Closest camera (whole run) | Inside solid / hidden |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop seed 22 | 150 | 61 | 0 | 0.356 | 3.92 m | 0 / 0 |
| Desktop seed 58 | 122 | 61 | 0 | 0.348 | 4.69 m | 0 / 0 |
| Desktop seed 130 | 116 | 55 | 0 | 0.241 | 7.78 m | 0 / 0 |
| iPhone seed 22 | 121 | 62 | 0 | 0.347 | 2.75 m | 0 / 0 |
| iPhone seed 58 | 90 | 30 | 0 | 0.333 | 5.67 m | 0 / 0 |
| iPhone seed 130 | 104 | 61 | 0 | 0.228 | 8.03 m | 0 / 0 |
| Android seed 317 | 89 | 60 | 0 | 0.344 | 3.10 m | 0 / 0 |

So 0 of 390 wall-side samples reached 40%; round 29 had 3 of 454. No open-street frame came under 2.5 m.

**Tunnel and orbit test (`cam-clip24.mjs`, real time at 30 fps, 62 s each).**

| Run | Frames | Inside solid (pad 0 / 0.1) | Drone hidden | Under street | Camera jumps over 1 m | Closest |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop seed 22, random orbit | 1,060 | 0 / 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 (round 29: 44) | 3.81 m |
| Desktop seed 58, random orbit | 1,060 | 0 / 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 (round 29: 28) | 6.47 m or more |
| iPhone seed 22, no orbit | 1,057 | 0 / 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 (round 29: 0) | |

All ten passes per run (tunnels and alleys) are PASS. Orbit share 0.88, as in round 29.

## 2. Leftover A: carry farm on seed 130

**Answer: it is the bot. I did not change the street bonus cap.** `capfarm.mjs` picks its heading from the camera
whenever it is slow or turning, and the farm phase is all slow U-turns. So a camera change changes the farm path.

| capfarm, SIMT 600 (round 30 build) | Honest pts/min | Carry pts/min | Carry / honest | Carry farm time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Seed 130, camera heading (critic's script) | 2,893 | 691 | **0.24** | 54.6 s |
| Seed 130, yaw heading (`capfarm-yaw.mjs`, no camera at all) | 2,478 | 689 | **0.28** | 61.3 s |
| Seed 22, camera heading | 2,592 | 603 | 0.23 | 38.1 s |
| Seed 58, camera heading | 2,627 | 0 (no drop) | 0 | 47.7 s |
| Round 29 seed 130 (critic) | 2,972 | 1,537 | 0.52 | 33.4 s |

In round 29 the carry bot only farmed for 33 s and then made two plain deliveries, so it scored like a slow honest run.
With a camera-independent bot the farm earns 0.28 of honest. "Both" farms scored 0 on all three seeds. The no-delivery
farm (`farm-probe.mjs`) scored 0 on 22, 58 and 130. The per-leg cap (`bankPerMetre` 4.25) holds, and tightening it would
only cost honest street runs.

## 3. Leftover B: the roof bot on seed 22

**Answer: it is the bot, not the camera and not the game.**
- Deterministic runs (`route-play-trace.mjs`, 50 ms control steps): the roof bot steering by the camera made 8 drops
  on seed 22 (7,968). The same bot steering by the drone's yaw (no camera) made 1 drop and stalled on the same leg.
- The stall spot is the same in every stalled run on seed 22, my real-time ones too: (-98.5, 14.5, -54.3), 2.7 m from the
  Florist pad (-98.6, 0.4, -57). `geo22.mjs` and `geo22b.mjs` show why. The pad sits beside a 13.05 m building with a
  roof lip (12.85 to 13.75 m) along its edge. The roof bot starts its descent to pad height as soon as it is within 25 m.
  So it lands on that roof, holds "down", and pushes into the 0.7 m lip, 2.7 m short of the pad. Its unstick rule only
  fires more than 3 m from the pad, so it never lifts off. A plain descent from above the pad delivers at once (critic,
  `leg22-29.mjs`).
- The same pattern stalls it on seed 58 in some runs (on a roof at about 25 m, 6 m from a street pad).
- Real-time medal runs with the critic's bot this round: seed 22 856 (1 drop), seed 58 851 (1 drop), seed 130 8,598
  Gold (8 drops). Breakdown exact on all three. Round 29: 982 / 4,521 / 4,759. The 30 fps cap makes these runs noisy.
  Which leg ends on a roof depends on the bot's path.
- Bot fix tried (in `builder-scripts` only): `route-play-rt-x-m-esc17-fix30.mjs` and `route-play-trace.mjs FIX=1`. The
  unstick also fires when the bot is stuck high near a pad, and then it climbs to 16 m over the pad and comes straight
  down. Deterministic, yaw steering, seed 22: 1 drop became 3. Real time at 30 fps: seed 58 went from 851 (1 drop) to
  3,835 (4 drops), but seed 22 still dithers on that leg (982, 1 drop). The roof bot's arrival rule needs a proper rewrite (stay high until over the pad). I did not finish that.

## 4. Regression checks

| Check | Result | Round 29 (critic) |
|---|---|---|
| Crash-classify 12 m, 8 seeds (`ccv12.log`) | **0 pad lips**. 55 crashes in 558 s (5.9 a minute), 19 near the target, closest 1.5 m below a wall top | 0 pad lips, 5.3 a minute |
| Crash-classify 20 m, 8 seeds (`ccv20.log`) | **0 pad lips**. 28 crashes in 620 s (2.7 a minute), closest 2.7 m below | 0 pad lips, 2.0 a minute |
| People probe (`pad-people23.mjs`, 48 legs) | 0 people on active pads | 0 |
| Traffic per-step overlap (`traffic-det29.mjs`, 6 runs, 120 Hz) | 0 in all 6 | 0 |
| Phone HUD probe (iPhone 22, 58, 130; Android 317) | route mark on controls 0, drone under pills 0, pops on Fly 0, pops on the drone 1.05% / 0% / 0.36% / 0% | at most 0.40% |
| Flat-frame probe (`acceptance-probe.mjs`) | 271 frames, 0 flat, 0 errors | 0 |
| Chimes with pops (7 hud-probe runs) | 72 of 72 chimes with a pop on screen | 88 of 88 |
| Street medal gate, real time (`m-low-a.log`) | 4,766 Silver / **1,443 Bronze** / 5,317 Silver, breakdown exact on all 3 | 5,863 / 2,437 / 5,246, all Silver |
| Roof medal run, real time (`m-high-a.log`) | 856 / 851 / 8,598 Gold, breakdown exact | 982 / 4,521 / 4,759 |
| No-delivery farm (`farm-probe.mjs`) | 0 on 22, 58, 130 | 0 |
| Triangles / draw calls (`trisweep29.mjs`, desktop 130, iPhone 22) | max 547k / 471k, 0 over 600k; calls max 135 / 116 | 549k, 136 |
| First flight (`ff29.mjs`, desktop, 3 runs) | 0 long tasks after Play, 0 shaders compiled after Play | 0 |
| `npm run build` | passes, type check clean; JS 973 KB (first load about 1 MB, the CC0 assets still lazy-load) | 2.7 MB total, 918 KB JS |

**Street gate on seed 58 is a real worry.** The street bot fell from Silver to Bronze there twice (1,443 and 1,702, 2
drops each). The round 29 code on the same machine, minutes later, made 4,052 Silver with 3 drops (`m-low-58-r29.log`).
The street bot steers by the camera whenever it is slower than 4 m/s, at every pad and corner. So the new camera changes
its path. Evidence that the game itself plays the same: the deterministic street bot steering by the drone's yaw (no
camera) scored 5,369 with 4 drops on round 30 and 5,290 with 4 drops on round 29 (`rp-low-58-yaw-5190.log`,
`rp-low-58-yaw-5193.log`). Steering by the camera it scored 2,434 on round 30 and 3,984 on round 29, both with 3 drops
(`rp-low-58-cam-*.log`). In a 100 s trace of slow moments (under 4 m/s), the median angle between the camera direction
and the drone's heading is 0.53 rad on round 30 against 0.75 on round 29. But the worst 10% reach 1.44 rad against 0.95
(`rp-low-58-cam-trace-*.log`). So at some slow moments beside walls the new camera stays further off the heading, and
that steers the bot wrong. A human sees the drone turn, so this may not hurt play. But it is worth a human check
(hover beside a wall on seed 58 and turn), and the gate should be rerun with a yaw-steered street bot.

## 5. Known limits and what I did not finish

- The roof bot's arrival rule (descend once within 25 m) still lands it on roofs beside street pads. My bot fix helps
  in deterministic runs and on seed 58 in real time, not yet on seed 22. This is bot work, not game work.
- In the climb test the view can sit behind a building corner for a few frames, so the drone is half hidden by the
  facade mesh while the colliders say the line of sight is clear. The round 29 code shows the same view at the same
  moment (`builder-shots/r29code-climb-d-22-4-up-f16.jpg` against `climb30-d-22-4-up-f16.jpg`). The facade meshes stand
  a little proud of their colliders. Not fixed.
- Real-time frame time is still not measurable on this machine (30 fps cap). The glide adds a handful of segment and
  point tests per frame. I did not time it separately. First flight showed no long tasks.
- Desktop pops over the drone (critic's ranked gap 1) were not in scope this round.

## Files changed

- `src/systems/CameraRig.ts`: `smoothRel` (the glide in the drone's turning frame, with the wall, gap and sight checks
  and the step round a wall), shake as an offset, floor / rise / hard gap place their target in one step, tilted
  rise spots first, `SMOOTH` and `NUDGE` constants. `RISE_STEP`, `PUSH_STEP`, `SOFT_GAP` removed.
- `src/game/Game.ts`: debug hook `camSmooth()`.
- `src/vite-env.d.ts`: its type.
- `progress/round-30/`: this file, `builder-scripts/` (copied critic scripts and the new ones above, all logs),
  `builder-shots/` (30 JPEGs: the climb filmstrips for round 30 and the round 29 code, the round 29 snap frame,
  tunnel and alley views, desktop and phone pop shots, the worst triangle spots).

# Drone Dash: round 29 critic report

**Verdict:** Round 29 fixes four of the five round 28 gaps. Cars now have wheels, rush-hour cars no longer overlap, triangles stay under 600k, and the first flight has no hitch. The wall-side camera passes by a hair. It crowds the screen far less now. But after a wall-side pickup, a fast climb makes it snap back and forth for up to a second.

Build tested: the uncommitted round 29 work on top of commit 0a60215. My own dev server ran on port 5191 and is stopped. A copy of commit 0a60215 (round 28) ran on port 5192 for A/B checks and is stopped too. The owner's server on 5188 was left alone. Every browser ran alone, one job at a time, from one queue (`critic-scripts/queue29.sh`, `jobs29.txt`). I did not read the round 29 builder notes. The round 28 scripts were copied to `progress/round-29/critic-scripts/`, and only their output folders changed.

New scripts this round:

- `cars29.mjs`: a wheel probe (count, ground contact, spin, steering) and street-level car shots.
- `traffic-det29.mjs`: per-frame traffic overlap at fixed 120 Hz steps.
- `trisweep29.mjs`: the round 28 sweep, but it reads the frame just drawn (`renderStats`). `DIAG=1` uses diagonal headings.
- `popcheck29.mjs`: looks for culled trees inside the view during fast camera turns.
- `ff29.mjs`: first flight. It logs long tasks and shader compiles after Play.
- `climb29.mjs`: a real pickup or drop beside a wall, then an instant climb, at 60 Hz steps.
- `hover29.mjs`: desktop framing at hover, cruise and boost (round 29 against round 28).
- `perf-street-port.mjs` plus `work29-init.js`: main-thread work per frame.
- `route-play-yaw29.mjs`: the roof bot steering by drone yaw.
- `leg22-29.mjs`: checks the seed 22 leg where the roof bot stalls.
- `medal-sum29.py`, `ab-make.py`: summaries and the blind pairs.

## Machine load (read first)

BTLEServer used 97 to 100% of one core during the whole session. I logged it before each timing block (`cpu-start.txt`, `cpu-ff.txt`, `cpu-tr.txt`, `cpu-perf.txt`, `cpu-medal.txt`). Every real-time browser run was held at exactly 30 fps (median frame 33.3 ms, every frame "over 20 ms"). Round 28 ran at 120 fps. So **all wall-clock frame times in this report are contaminated**. They only show the 30 fps cap. Where possible, I used deterministic or per-frame probes instead: fixed-step simulation, long-task and shader-compile logs, and main-thread work per frame. Real-time bot runs (medal gates, hud probes) also ran at 30 fps, so their control loops saw a quarter of the frames.

## Results for items 1 to 5

### 1. Camera after a pickup or drop beside a wall: pass, with one new flaw

| Device (first run, seeds 22, 58, 130, plus one more run) | Wall samples | 40% or more | Max | Closest camera |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop 1280x720 (3 first runs, returning seed 22) | 233 | 2 (0.86%) | 0.431 | 5.94 m |
| Phone (iPhone 13 seeds 22, 58, 130, plus Android 317) | 221 | 1 (0.45%) | 0.42 | 5.76 m |

- Pooled per device, both pass the 99% line (99.1% and 99.5%). Per run, desktop seed 22 (1 of 58) and seed 130 (1 of 56) are just over 1%. Round 28 desktop had 20 of 62 at 40% or more, up to 77%.
- **2 m test: pass.** All post-event samples were 5.76 m or more. Per-frame open-street minimum: 3.21 m in 7 runs (about 17,000 frames). Alleys and tunnels, desktop random orbit seeds 22 and 58 plus iPhone seed 22: minimum 3.39 m. In solid 0, drone hidden 0, drone under the camera 0.
- **The three spikes are one-frame camera snaps.** Each came while the bot climbed at about 10 m/s just after a pickup or drop. The camera went 8.8 m, then 5.9 m, then 8.8 m in 200 ms. A deterministic repro (`climb29.mjs`, 32 real pickups and drops beside walls on seeds 22 and 130, climbing at once) shows the pattern:

| Build | Climbs touching 40% | Frames at 40% or more | Max height share | Frames where the camera jumps over 1.7 m |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Round 28 | 14 of 32 | 313 of 4,800 | 0.81 | 8 |
| Round 29 | 6 of 32 | 8 of 4,800 | 0.53 | **29** (max 3.7 m) |

  So crowding is much better, but the camera now jerks more. In 9 of 32 climbs it jumps 2 to 3.7 m in one frame. Then it swings between about 6 m and 8.8 m for up to a second (`climb29-d-22-4-spike.jpg`). The phone shows the same numbers. The 1.7 m per-frame cap from round 23 does not hold here.
- **As a player (desktop hover):** the drone is only a little smaller. At hover in an open street it fills 18.6% of the screen height at 8.8 m (round 28: 20.5% at 8.1 m). Cruise (9 to 17 m/s) and boost framing are identical to round 28 to the third decimal (`hover29-r29-*.jpg` against `hover29-r28-*.jpg`). It is still easy to read, and speed still feels close and fast. The view at a slow drone beside a wall is now a higher overview. Is that less exciting? **Needs a human player.**
- New side finding: on desktop the centre pops sit on the drone. Examples are "Parcel secured!" and the slip "+24 BANKED". They cover it in 28 to 44% of samples where a pop shows (round 28: 20 to 29%). See `fr29-d-22-h05-low-payout-chain.jpg` and `climb29-d-22-4-spike.jpg`. The phone moves its pops clear of the drone (0 to 0.4%). Desktop does not.

### 2. Wheels: pass

`cars29.mjs` read every near car and every wheel instance per frame. It ran on seeds 22 and 130: 720 steps, 5,818 car samples, six spots, rush on and off.

- Wheels per car: 4 on every compact, estate, taxi and van sample. The box truck has 6 (three axles). There were 0 cars with missing wheels and 0 stray wheels.
- Ground contact: every wheel bottom sits at road height (within 0.00000003 m).
- Spin: wheel turn times radius equals the distance the car moved, with median and 95th percentile error 0. None spin backwards. Wheels on a stopped car move under 0.01 m.
- Steering: front wheels turn into the curve on all 233 turning samples, up to 0.34 rad. Rear wheels never steer. Straight-lane cars: 95th percentile 0.004 rad.
- Street-level shots: `car29-22-t0..t4-side6m.jpg`. The wheels fill the arches and sit on the road. The style matches the low-poly cars. `car29-22-turning.jpg` is a van from the front: its skirt hides the wheels, which is fine.

## Biggest remaining gap

**The camera snaps back and forth in a fast climb out of a wall-side pickup or drop.** Round 29 fixed the crowding. The worst frame is now 53% of the screen height instead of 81%. Only 8 of 4,800 frames reach 40%. But the new room floor and hard gap fight each other during a fast climb beside a wall. In 9 of 32 climbs the camera jumps 2 to 3.7 m in one frame. It then swings between about 6 m and 8.8 m for up to a second. You get a visible shake right at the moment you leave a pad, which you do every leg. Round 28 had 8 such frames in the same test. Round 29 has 29.

**Acceptance test:** run `climb29.mjs` on desktop and iPhone 13. It makes 32 real pickups and drops beside walls on seeds 22 and 130. Each is followed by an instant climb (Space, Space+S, Space+A, Space+W), at 60 Hz steps. The pass marks:

- 0 frames where the camera moves more than 1.7 m relative to the drone.
- Drone box under 40% of the screen height in 99.5% of frames.
- Camera at least 2 m from the drone in every frame.
- The tunnel test and the 2 m open-street test still pass.

If that counts as polish, then **only polish remains**, ranked as below.

## Other gaps, ranked

1. **Desktop pops cover the drone.** "Parcel secured!", the slip "+N BANKED" and medal pops sit at screen centre, on the drone. That happens in 28 to 44% of samples where a pop shows (round 28: 20 to 29%). The phone already moves its pops clear of the drone. Test: the hud-probe pop-on-drone share on desktop seeds 22, 58 and 130 under 2%.
2. **Roof bot stall on seed 22 (bot or feel?).** The game target is reachable. But two roof bots stall on the same leg, and the roof scores fell. Test: a human flies the roof line on seed 22 for one run. If the human is fine, retune the bot. If not, look at the approach to that pad.
3. **Carry farm on seed 130 at 0.52** of honest points a minute, just over the 0.5 line. It is probably a bot path change, but check again with `capfarm.mjs` on a quiet machine.
4. **Real-time perf was not measurable** (30 fps cap from machine load). Rerun `perf-street.mjs`, `perf18.mjs` and the 80 s runs on a quiet machine, with BTLEServer idle. The pass mark is a p95 under 12 ms.
5. **Shop signs and faces** (from round 28). Sign plates are white blobs on a dark plate, and people have no faces. **Needs a human eye** at play speed.

# Drone Dash: round 29 builder notes

The round 28 critic named five concerns. I worked on them in this order:

1. The desktop camera after a pickup or drop beside a wall.
2. Wheels on the CC0 cars.
3. The traffic overlap at the outer ring corners.
4. Triangles near parks.
5. The desktop first-flight hitch.

## How I worked and tested

- Two production snapshots, both served by `vite preview` and built by `builder-scripts/rebuild29.sh`:
  - the new build on 127.0.0.1:5191
  - the round 28 code, built before my first edit, on 5192
- The owner's server on 5188 was not touched. Both of my servers are stopped.
- The round 28 critic scripts are copied to `progress/round-29/builder-scripts/`. Only the output folder changed (`../builder-shots/`). `trisweep28.mjs` and `art28.mjs` also take `PORT`, and `art28.mjs` takes `TAG`.
- One browser at a time, from one job queue (`queue29.sh`, `jobs29.txt`, log `queue29.log`).
- A queue bug cost some time. A job line with `for i` overwrote the queue's own line counter `i`, so two old jobs ran a second time. The counter is now `QL`.
- New scripts:
  - `hitch29.mjs` and `hitch29-init.js`: a first-flight trace. They time the blocking WebGL calls and `new AudioContext()` per frame. They also list the shader programs compiled after Play.
  - `trisweep29.mjs`: the critic's sweep with the true count of each render, and a per-mesh breakdown at any spot over 600k.
  - `cars29.mjs`: every vehicle type from the side at 6 m and 30 m. Also a moving front wheel in two frames 0.06 s apart, and a car in a turn.
  - `ab29.py`: labelled before and after pairs of the art27 spots (`builder-shots/ab/ba29-*.jpg`).
- New debug hooks: `triBreakdown`, `renderStats`, `programs`, `meshInfo`. The bot hooks and the bloom clamps in `ObjectiveMarker.ts` are unchanged.

## 1. Desktop camera after a pickup or drop beside a wall

**Cause.** The slow-drone room floor (`CameraRig.keepRoom`) was 4.2 m on desktop and 8.8 m on touch screens. Both use a 60 degree view, so the desktop drone filled up to 77% of the screen height after a drop by a wall.

**Fix (`CameraRig.ts`, `Game.ts`).**
- One rule for every device: the 8.8 m floor (`CAMERA_TOUCH_ROOM`, 2.1 times 4.2 m) for a slow drone and for 3.2 s after each pickup or drop. A hovering drone on desktop now sits a little further away, as on the phone.
- The wider floor made the camera jump. With the player's orbit, a camera rose 8 m in one frame. Three changes stop that:
  - The floor never jumps out. When it wants more room, it holds the camera where it is and backs it off at 9 m/s.
  - A push straight out moves at most 2.0 m a frame. A rise over the drone moves at most 2.4 m a frame. I tried 0.6 and 0.9 m first. Then a drop by a wall filled 60 to 70% of the screen for 0.2 s (2 of 62 samples). So I raised them.
  - A camera already at its floor (within 2 cm) is left alone.
- A hard gap in every mode, alleys and tunnels too (`hardGap`). The camera never stays closer than 2.35 m to the drone's look point (0.4 m above its centre, the point the critic measures to). It picks the nearest clear spot: straight out, out along last frame's direction, back along the corridor or behind the heading, or over the drone. Above 2.1 m the move is a glide of at most 2.0 m a frame.
- The orbit camera, the tunnel framing and the arrival framing are otherwise unchanged.

**Numbers.** `hud-probe27` with the critic's `fb27-init.js` (first run, street bot 80 s, every 100 ms for 3 s after each pickup or drop). "Beside a wall" means a solid within 4 m at the event.

| Build | Device, seed | Wall samples | 40% or more | Largest | Closest camera |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Round 28 (critic) | desktop 22 | 62 | 20 (32%) | 0.77 | |
| First fix | desktop 22, 130, 58, 22 returning | 62, 62, 62, 62 | 0, 0, 0, 0 | 0.35 | 5.8 m |
| First fix | iPhone 22, 130 | 62, 62 | 0, 0 | 0.37 | 3.05 m |
| Step limits 0.6 / 0.9 m | desktop 22, iPhone 22 | 62, 62 | 2, 2 | 0.70 | |
| Step limits 2.4 / 2.0 m | desktop 130, 58, 22 returning | 62, 61, 62 | 0, 0, 0 | 0.40 | 5.8 m |
| Step limits 2.4 / 2.0 m | iPhone 22, 130 | 61, 60 | 0, 0 | 0.37 | 2.71 m |
| Step limits 2.4 / 2.0 m | desktop 22 (machine slow, p95 33 ms) | 62 | 3 (4.8%) | 0.44 | 6.0 m |
| Final (frame-rate independent steps) | desktop 22, 130 | 62, 62 | 0, 0 | 0.38 | 5.6 m |
| Final | iPhone 22, 130 | 61, 61 | 0, 0 | 0.40 (not by a wall) | 5.9 m |

- The last desktop 22 run before the final fix had 3 big samples. The machine was slow then (p95 33 ms, see "Test conditions"). The rise moved at most half the gap a frame, so at 30 fps it fell behind a wall cutting the view. In the final build, a camera well inside its floor takes the full step. The steps also scale with frame time. The final runs were also at 30 fps and pass.
- Final build, desktop 22 returning and desktop 58 (both at 30 fps): 0 of 62 and 0 of 62 at 40% or more. Largest 0.40 and 0.399. Closest camera 6.2 m.
- 2 m test: in every run above, the closest camera to the drone's look point was 2.71 m or more (critic sampler, every frame).
- Camera tunnel test: `cam-clip24`, seed 22, desktop with random orbit. This run was at a normal 120 fps, on the build with step limits 2.4 / 2.0 m:
  - 6,919 frames, in solid 0, under 0, occluded 0
  - closest 2.39 m in Marble Lane (round 28: 1.86 m)
  - jumps over 1 m: 11 (round 28: 9 to 12). Largest 3.31 m, a wall hit at the Marble Lane mouth with the camera lifted over the drone (round 28: 2.27 m).
  - The same test on the final build ran at 17 fps (slow machine): closest 3.42 m, in solid, under and occluded 0. Its jump count (48) is not comparable at that frame rate.
- iPhone, no orbit (`cam-clip24`): 6,924 frames, in solid 0, under 0, 1 jump over 1 m (round 28: 0), closest 3.2 m.
- Screenshots: `fr29-*`, `fin29-*`, `fin3-*` (title, 10 s, 31 s, 45 s, and any frame with the drone box at 40% or more), `cam-clip-22-*`.

## 2. Wheels on the cars

**Cause.** The Kay Lousberg cars lost their wheels in the round 28 decimation. About 200 broken shards of each car's wheels stayed in its `trim` part, inside the arches.

**Fix (`StreetKit.ts`, `Traffic.ts`).**
- One new InstancedMesh (`traffic-wheels`) holds every wheel of the near vehicles. It costs one draw call plus its shadow. Near means within the 55 m detail range.
- The wheel is procedural and flat shaded like the kit. It has a dark tread, a dark sidewall, a light rim with five dark holes, and a hub, on both faces. That is 132 triangles a wheel.
- Wheel spots: the arch centres measured on the meshes (rear -1.25 m, front +1.15 m, radius 0.31 m) for the three CC0 cars. The round 22 spots for the vans (4 wheels) and box trucks (6 wheels). Their baked wheels are gone, so every ground vehicle uses the same wheel.
- The model bodies ride 7 cm higher (`MODEL_RIDE`), so the arches sit just over the tyres. The lamps and taxi sign move with them. The trim shards inside the wheel volume are dropped at load.
- Wheels spin with the distance driven. The front pair steers by the heading's turn rate (bicycle model), clamped to 0.34 rad and smoothed.
- A camera can jump, for example a teleport in a test or a `renderFrom` shot. Then the near or far split is redone for the camera drawn (`Traffic.relod`). Before, a car next to a jumped camera was sometimes drawn far: no wheels, no trim.

**Check.** `cars29.mjs` on seeds 22 and 130:
- Every vehicle type from the side at 6 m and 30 m: `car29-new-22-t{0..4}-{6,30}m.jpg`, `car29b-new-130-t{0..4}-*.jpg`. Every car shows 4 wheels in its arches, touching the road. The box truck shows 6.
- Spin: `car29-spin-f0.jpg` and `-f1.jpg`, 0.06 s apart. The rim holes turn between the frames.
- A car mid-turn: `car29-steer.jpg` (the front wheels are mostly hidden by the body from this angle).
- Cost: 12k to 15k triangles at busy spots (main pass plus shadow), one draw call plus one shadow draw.

## 3. Traffic overlap at the ring corners

**Causes (`Traffic.ts`).** I found three.
- A car commits to a junction up to 32 m before its stop line. The exit-lane check skipped any car whose heading was not along the exit lane. A car still in its turn into that lane points across it, so it was skipped. The next car committed into a full lane.
- A turning car only followed cars ahead along its nose's heading. For most of the arc that heading points across the exit lane, so it drove into the queue there. At the outer corners every car turns, and the exit lane queues in rush hour.
- Rush-hour spawns. A new car sometimes appeared 5 m in front of a moving car in the same lane. That car was too close to stop (seed 58: a taxi spawned in front of a moving truck).

**Fixes.**
- `turnPathGap`: a turning car keeps its gap along the rest of its arc and on into the exit lane. It counts cars in that lane and cars further along a turn into the same lane.
- Exit-lane rule: a car does not commit while a car from another approach is turning into, or committed to, the same exit lane at the same junction.
- Spawns keep clear of a car behind in the same lane: its stopping distance plus 8 m. They also keep clear of any car turning at the junction just behind. A tick now tries up to three spawns, so rush hour fills about as fast as before.

**Numbers.** The critic's real-time probe `traffic-rt28.mjs` (every frame, 20 s normal then 80 s rush, seed 4 three times, then 22, 130, 58):

| Build | 4 | 4 | 4 | 22 | 130 | 58 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Round 28 (critic) | 0 | 2,055 | 99 | 336 | 920 | 0 |
| Turn fixes, 120 fps | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Turn fixes, second run, 120 fps | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | **388** (spawn) |
| Plus the spawn rule, 30 to 58 fps | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Final (people fix too), 30 fps | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

- The 388 frames on seed 58 were the spawn case: a taxi spawned 5 m ahead of a moving box truck, mid-block on the west ring road. The spawn rule fixes it.
- The deterministic street probe (`street-probe.mjs`, seeds 22, 4, 130, 58, normal and rush): overlaps 0, cars in solids 0, off lane 0, people in solids 0, people hit 0, people on pads 0. Rush fills to 136 cars and 18 vans as before.
- Rush hour density (`perf-street`, desktop): 105.9 cars on average over the window, round 28: 115.1. That run was before the three-tries spawn change.

## 4. Triangles near parks

**Cause.** The breakdown at the worst seed 130 spot (650k, a park with people), main pass plus shadow pass:
- people 141k near and 63k far
- city 113k, lamp posts 42k
- trees about 60k, street props about 65k

People and near trees were drawn all round the camera, also behind it.

**Fixes (`Pedestrians.ts`, `Environment.ts`, `Game.ts`).**
- People further than 14 m are only drawn in or near the camera's view: a sphere test against the view frustum, 3.5 m plus 4% of the distance of margin.
- Trees further than 22 m keep the CC0 model only inside a cone of plus or minus 78 degrees round the view direction. Outside it they use the light blob, so their shadows stay. When the camera looks steeply down, every tree in range keeps its model.
- These cones use the camera of the previous frame. A camera can turn more than about 6 degrees or move more than 1.5 m since then. In that case the cones are redone just before the frame is drawn (`Environment.syncView`).
- A measuring trap: `__THREE_GAME_DIAGNOSTICS__.renderer` is published before the render, so it lags one frame. The critic's sweep max is still right, but its worst spot is the one after the real one. `renderStats` gives the count of the last render.

**Numbers.** The critic's `trisweep28.mjs` (1,336 to 1,376 spots, 3, 16 and 38 m, 4 headings, rush on):

| Run | Round 28 max | Round 29 max | Spots over 600k | Draw calls max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop, seed 130 | 662k | 544k | 0 | 135 |
| Desktop, seed 22 | 599k | 521k | 0 | 137 |
| iPhone, seed 130 | | 499k | 0 | 116 |
| iPhone, seed 22 | 540k | 458k | 0 | 118 |
| Final build, desktop 130 / iPhone 130 | | 548k / 500k | 0 | 135 / 120 |

- p95 over the sweep, desktop 130: 486k. My first run, with only the tree cone in, gave a max of 655k and a p95 of 575k.
- Art views: 306k to 467k triangles (round 28 builder: up to 588k), 91 to 131 draw calls.

## 5. First-flight hitch

**Causes, from the trace (`hitch29.mjs`).**
- `new AudioContext()` took 189 to 215 ms inside `start()`. The round 28 prewarm ran 1.2 s after boot. The critic's probe presses Play about 1.7 s after load, before that timer fired.
- Five or six shader programs compiled on the first playing frame (about 25 ms): the route gates, pad marker sprites and beams, which are hidden on the title. A plain `renderer.compile` did not help. It compiled for the canvas, but desktop draws through the post-processing buffer, so the programs did not match and compiled again.

**Fixes (`Game.ts`, `Renderer.ts`).**
- The audio context is made 30 ms after the first frame. The cost moves into the loading frames.
- `warmPrograms` runs at 400 ms, and again when the assets are in. It shows every hidden object for one synchronous compile and hides it again before any frame is drawn. `RenderPipeline.compileScene` compiles for the target the scene is really drawn into.

**Numbers.** `hitch29.mjs`: fresh profile, Play 1.74 s after load (the critic's timing), then 3 s of flight.

| Run | Largest frame in the first 3 s of play | Programs compiled after Play |
|---|---|---|
| Round 28 code | 275 ms (AudioContext 211 ms plus 5 programs) | 5 to 6 |
| Desktop, 3 runs | 10.3, 16.7, 10.2 ms | 0 |
| iPhone 13, 3 runs | 16.6, 16.8, 16.7 ms | 0 |
| Final build, desktop / iPhone (30 fps machine, so every frame is about 33 ms) | 34.9 / 35.0 ms | 0 |

- `new AudioContext()` still costs 182 to 215 ms in headless Chromium, now at 0.7 to 0.85 s after load, during the loading frames.
- The critic's own hitch log in the first-run probes shows no frame over 40 ms in the first 80 s, on desktop or phone. Its only entry is the probe's final read at 80.5 s, as in round 28.
- Real desktop browser: not checked. Headless Chromium only.

## Regressions

### Test conditions

From about 18:12 the machine slowed down. `BTLEServer` (macOS Bluetooth) ran at 100% CPU, and the headless browser then ran at 30 fps or less instead of 120. Real-time results from then on are marked. Frame-time budgets come from the runs before that.

### Results

- **Blind look, street views:** before (round 28 build) and after, same art27 spots, both moods, desktop and iPhone: `builder-shots/ab/ba29-*.jpg` (28 pairs). Buildings, props, people, trees and light are the same. Cars now have wheels.
  - The one visible change is on desktop. The drone sits further away in these views (the shared 8.8 m floor for a still drone). So it is smaller and more street shows. The iPhone views are unchanged.
  - The traffic layout differs (stricter spawns).
  - I judge it unchanged or better, but this is not a blind pick.
- **Crash-classify, seeds 22, 58, 130 (120 fps):**
  - 12 m: 23 crashes in 211 s (6.5 a minute. Round 28: builder 5.9 to 6.1, critic 5.4 over 8 seeds). 6 within 30 m of the target, none within 8 m: 0 pad lips. Closest 3.8 m below a wall top.
  - 20 m: 9 crashes in 284 s (1.9 a minute. Round 28: 3.1 to 3.8). 2 near the target, none within 8 m. Closest 2.7 m below a wall top.
- **People:** `street-probe.mjs` on the final build: 0 in solids, 0 on roads, 0 hit by cars, 0 on pads, all four seeds, normal and rush. `pad-people23.mjs`: 48 legs, 1,536 samples, 0 on the live pad.
  - A first version of the people culling broke this (3 legs, 96 samples). It skipped people out of view before the pad rule ran, so their positions were stale. The cull now only skips the drawing.
- **Camera tunnel test:** see section 1.
- **Phone HUD probe (iPhone 22, 120 fps):** route marker on controls 0. Drone under pills 0.13% (1 of 793). Pops on the drone 0, pops on "Fly" 0. p95 9.7 ms. Closest camera 2.87 m.
- **Flat-frame probe:** 971 frames, 0 flat, 0 errors.
- **Payout chimes with their pop (`hud-probe28`):** desktop 22: 10 of 10, iPhone 130: 12 of 12 shown with `#slip-pop`.
- **Medal gate (`route-play-rt-x-m-esc17`), breakdown exact (`bdOk`, `domOk`) on all 8 runs:**
  - Street: 5,940 Silver, 3,957 Silver, 5,632 Silver (seeds 22, 58, 130), total 15,529 (round 28 critic 13,767).
  - Roof: 2,518 Silver, 977 none, 6,971 Gold, total 10,466 (round 28 critic 11,812 before its rerun). Seed 58 stalled again (1 drop, 7.9 m/s), as in round 28.
  - Roof reruns on the slow machine (30 fps): seed 22 856 none (1 drop, 6.9 m/s), seed 58 3,015 Silver.
  - Watch point: the roof bot takes its heading from the camera position (`atan2(drone - camera)`). On desktop the camera now rises over a slow drone beside a wall (as it already did on the phone), so that heading gets noisy. The game itself steers by the drone's yaw.
- **Exploits:** no-delivery farm 0 points on seeds 22, 58 and 130.
- **Frame time (`perf-street`, 120 fps, before the slowdown):** desktop p95 9.2 ms (normal and rush), iPhone 9.6 and 9.5 ms. Max 10.4 ms, 0 frames over 20 ms. The first-run probes at 120 fps: p95 9.4 to 9.9 ms.
- **First load:** `npm run build` passes (type check clean). Vite warns that the main chunk is over 900 kB. Without source maps the build is 2.64 MB. First load: HTML 11 KB, CSS 40 KB, JS 918 KB. The street assets (1.57 MB) still load after the first frame.

## Files changed (no new assets)

- `src/systems/CameraRig.ts`: eased floor, push and rise limits, `hardGap`.
- `src/game/Game.ts`: room floor on all devices, earlier audio prewarm, `warmPrograms`, view sync before each render, new hooks.
- `src/core/Renderer.ts`: `RenderPipeline.compileScene`.
- `src/world/StreetKit.ts`: wheel geometry and wheel spots, ride height, trim shards dropped, baked wheels removed.
- `src/world/Traffic.ts`: wheels, `turnPathGap`, exit-lane rule, spawn rule, `relod`.
- `src/world/Environment.ts`: tree view cone, people frustum, `syncView`.
- `src/world/Pedestrians.ts`: frustum culling of far people.
- `src/vite-env.d.ts`: hook types.
- `ASSETS.md`: a note on the car GLBs (no new files).

## Not done or open

- A blind before and after pick by a fresh critic.
- The roof-line bot's camera-based heading (see Regressions). I did not change the bots.
- A real desktop browser check of the hitch. Headless Chromium only.
- `progress.html` was not updated.
- No git commands were run.

critic.md
# Drone Dash: round 28 critic report

**Verdict:** Round 28 passes its street-level test. The new build wins 21 of 24 blind pairs. The props, shop fronts and trees are a real step, and the phone camera now passes. New flaws: the cars have no wheels, and a few park views go over 600k triangles. The desktop camera still crowds the screen after a drop by a wall.

Build tested: the uncommitted round 28 work on top of commit 56f8d65. My own dev server on port 5191, stopped at the end. The owner's server on 5188 was left alone. Every browser ran alone, one at a time, from one job queue (`critic-scripts/queue28.sh`, `jobs28.txt`). I did not read the round 28 builder notes. The round 27 scripts were copied to `progress/round-28/critic-scripts/`. New scripts this round:

- `art28.mjs`: the art27 spots, with audits and a 3 m people close-up.
- `ab-make.py`: the blind pairs.
- `closeups28.mjs` and `cars28.mjs`: props that float or sink, and close-ups.
- `traffic-rt28.mjs`: real-time traffic overlap.
- `trisweep28.mjs`: worst-case triangles.
- `chime28-init.js` and `hud-probe28.mjs`: each chime against its pop.

## Acceptance (round 27 test)

All four art views per mood used the same seeds and spots as round 27 (golden hour seed 130, bright morning seed 22). Every round 27 view had a match, so nothing was skipped. The CC0 assets loaded in 220 to 243 ms in every run.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| At least 3 prop kinds within 40 m | **Pass.** 7 or 8 kinds at every spot (bollard, bin, bench, hydrant, planter, cafe table and chairs, sandwich board, bike rack). |
| At least 1 prop per 10 m of pavement | **Pass.** 1.11 to 1.88 per 10 m (35 to 58 pieces in 309 to 372 m). Bollards are about 40% of the count. |
| No two neighbouring shop fronts share sign, door and awning | **Pass by the hook:** 0 of 445 pairs (seed 130) and 0 of 421 (seed 22). By eye, the sign plates still read as one dark plate with white blobs for letters. Some rows of doors look alike (`art28-d-morning-22-shopfront.jpg`, left building). |
| At least 3 car models, 2 tree species with real shape | **Pass, with a flaw.** Compact, estate and taxi models, and round and oak trees. **The car models have no wheels.** The wheel arches are empty and the body sits on the road (`car28-new-22-t1-6m.jpg`, `close28-22-car0.jpg`). Vans and trucks are still procedural. |
| People: no box heads, knees and elbows bend | **Pass.** Round heads with hair and caps, round limbs and hands. Three frames 0.15 s apart show a bent back knee and a bent elbow (`art28-d-hour-130-people-close-f0..f2.jpg`). Torsos are still boxy and there are no faces. |
| Blind A/B, new view wins at least 5 of 6 per mood | **Pass** on both devices (table below). |
| Budgets | **Mostly pass.** p95, draw calls and load pass. Triangles go over 600k at a few park spots. The desktop first-flight hitch is still 241 ms. See Performance. |

### Blind A/B

`ab-make.py` put each round 27 and round 28 view side by side in random order (A left, B right). It shuffled the pairs (`critic/ab/pair-01..24.jpg`). The key went to `critic/ab/.key.json`. I wrote every pick and reason to `critic/ab/picks.txt` before I opened the key.

| Device, mood | street | shop front | facade mid | mid | cruise | cruise down | New wins |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop, golden hour | new | new | new | new | old (tie) | new (tie) | **5 of 6** |
| Desktop, bright morning | new | new | new | new | new (tie) | new | **6 of 6** |
| iPhone, golden hour | **old** | new | new | new | new (tie) | new | **5 of 6** |
| iPhone, bright morning | new | new | new | new | new | old (tie) | **5 of 6** |

- Per mood: golden hour 10 of 12, bright morning 11 of 12. **Pass.**
- Where it was clear, the reasons were the same every time: furniture on the pavement, cobbled paving and cracked asphalt with grain, coloured doors and varied awnings, and trees and cars with real shapes. The old views have spotless ground and one red and white awning along a block.
- From 38 m (cruise views) the two builds look almost the same. Five of the six cruise pairs were near ties, and the misses came from those.
- The one clear miss (iPhone golden hour street) was judged on the shrunk pair. At full size the new view has a hydrant, bollards, planters, cobbles and an estate car (`art28-m-hour-130-street.jpg`). I keep the recorded pick.

## Consistency and scale

- **Style fits.** Kay Lousberg, Kenney, Quaternius and procedural pieces are all flat-shaded with vertex colours and sit well with the low-poly buildings. Nothing clashes in colour or detail (`close28-22-street-props-*.jpg`). The bike racks and bus-stop poles (procedural) match the kit.
- **Cars are the weak spot.** The empty wheel arches make them look like toys sliding on the road. You see it every time a car crosses in front of the drone at street level. The old procedural cars had wheels.
- **Scale is right.** The compact car is 3.8 m long and 1.46 m high. The estate and taxi are 4.5 m long. A person is about 1.75 m tall. Benches and tables sit at the right height next to walkers (`close28-22-street-props-bench.jpg`, `-table.jpg`).
- **Nothing floats or sinks.** A ray down under each prop found its base on the ground. That held for all 1,404 pieces (seed 130) and all 1,430 (seed 22). Tree trunks: 1 of about 450 sits 0.25 m low (a kerb edge).
- **Props never block the play space.** On both seeds the placement hook finds 0 props on pads, in alleys or tunnels, or on the diagonal. It also finds 0 over a road and 0 touching a lamp or tree. Props have no colliders.
- Lit-window "TV static" from round 27 is still there on brick walk-ups at street level (`art28-m-hour-130-street.jpg`, left).
- Trees switch from the model to the old blob at 80 m (62 m on a phone). Is the swap visible? **Needs a human eye.**

## Traffic overlap

**Real, and not new in round 28.** The deterministic probe (`street-probe.mjs`) shows 0 overlaps. I ran it on seed 4 three times and on 22, 130 and 58. It cannot see the bug, because it waits 2 s after rush starts and steps the simulation in big steps. A real-time probe that checks every frame (`traffic-rt28.mjs`, run clock held open, 20 s normal then 80 s rush) does see it:

| Build | Seed 4 (run 1, 2, 3) | 22 | 130 | 58 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Round 28 | 0, 2,055, 99 frames | 336 | 920 | 0 |
| Round 27 (commit 56f8d65) | 0, 814, 435 frames | 0 | 0 | 0 |

- Every overlap is at a corner of the outer ring road (x or z near plus or minus 157), during rush hour, while playing. A car turning onto the edge road cuts into a car already in that lane, 4.1 to 5.4 m apart. The two stay merged for up to about 17 s (2,055 frames at 120 fps). One case is a box truck and a compact nose to tail in one lane.
- Round 27 has the same bug at the same corners, so it is old. It shows up more on the round 28 build here (4 of 6 runs against 2 of 6). With this few runs, the difference is not significant.
- The first real-time run (no clock hold) also found overlaps after the game-over screen, because traffic keeps running there.
- Players rarely fly the edge ring, but some pads are near it. Fix: in `Traffic.ts`, a turning car must check the target lane before it enters it.

## Regressions

- **Crash-classify, 8 seeds, 0 pad lips: pass.** 12 m: 58 crashes in 643 s (5.4 a minute, round 27: 4.6), 8 near target, closest 3.6 m below a wall top. 20 m: 39 in 658 s (3.6 a minute, round 27: 3.2), 10 near target, 2.1 m below. Props have no colliders. The higher rate is probably bot timing in real time. Check it again next round.
- **People probe: pass.** 0 people in solids, 0 on roads (about 610,000 samples), 0 hit by cars, 0 on active pads (48 legs, 1,536 samples).
- **Camera tunnel test: pass, with one frame.** Desktop with random orbit: 6,892 frames, drone in frame 100%, 0 in solid, under or hidden. One frame had the camera at 1.86 m in Marble Lane alley, with a 2.27 m jump. All other frames were 2.5 m or more (round 27: all of them). iPhone no orbit: 6,933 frames, minimum 3.45 m, max jump 0.97 m. The desktop camera code did not change. This is the random orbit.
- **2 m test in open streets: pass.** 0 frames under 2.5 m in 7 runs with the per-frame sampler (about 67,000 frames). Closest 3.93 m.
- **Phone camera after wall-side pickups: pass (it failed in round 27).** I got 274 samples beside a wall in 6 phone runs. The runs: iPhone 22, 58 and 130 (first run), iPhone 22 (returning and screenshot run), and Android 317. Drone box 40% of screen height or more: **0** (round 27: 7.4%). Largest: 0.365.
- **But on desktop the same thing still happens.** Desktop seed 22: 20 of 62 wall samples were at 40% or more, up to 77% of the screen height. It lasts about 1.4 s after each drop by a wall (camera 4.2 m away). Round 27 desktop runs gave 3 to 16%. The phone fix (`touchRoom`) only applies to touch screens.
- **Phone HUD probe: pass** (about 4,800 samples). Route marker on controls 0. Drone under pills at most 0.13%. Pop on drone at most 0.53%. Gate tag on controls or "Fly" 0. Pops on "Fly" 0.
- **Flat-frame probe: pass.** 941 frames, 0 flat, 0 errors.
- **Payout chimes never without their pop: pass.** The chime now plays at the moment its pop shows. A new probe read the game's own chime counter: 32 of 32 chimes in 3 runs had `#slip-pop` on screen in the same frame. The old round 27 probe reports 4 payouts "without a pop". It times from the payout, not from the chime, so it no longer applies.
- **Medal gate runs (seeds 22, 58, 130): pass.** Street 4,336 / 3,898 / 5,533 Silver, total 13,767. Strict delivery share 62.6% (lowest 59%). Roof 7,491 Gold, 851 none and 3,470 Silver. On seed 58 the bot stalled (7.8 m/s average, 1 drop, no crashes). The rerun gave 5,228 Silver, so the roof total is 16,189. Street divided by roof is 0.85, just at the line (1.17 with the stalled run). No Ace. Breakdown exact on all 7 runs.
- **Exploits: pass.** No-delivery farm 0 on 22, 58 and 130. Carry farm 0.25, 0.23 and 0 of honest points a minute. Farming both legs 0. One-delivery best 1,190 Bronze (carry farm, seed 130), the same as round 27.
- First-run pacing (desktop 22, iPhone 22, 58, 130): longest quiet stretch in the first 60 s is 10.6 s. At most one introduction per 8 s after 30 s. No hint within 3 s of a pickup or drop. Same as round 27.

## Performance

| Run | Median | p95 | Max | Over 20 ms | Calls (max) | Triangles (max) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Street, desktop | 8.3 | 9.5 | 10.3 | 0 | 130 | 547k |
| Street rush, desktop | 8.3 | 9.3 | 10.3 | 0 | 135 | 555k |
| Street, iPhone 13 | 8.3 | 9.7 | 10.4 | 0 | 112 | 475k |
| Street rush, iPhone 13 | 8.3 | 9.6 | 10.3 | 0 | 117 | 477k |
| Tunnels/alleys, desktop | 8.3 | 8.6 | 10.4 | 0 | 115 | 553k |
| Tunnels/alleys, iPhone 13 | 8.3 | 9.2 | 10.3 | 0 | 102 | 492k |
| 80 s runs, 7 runs | 8.3 | 9.3 to 9.7 | see below | 0 to 1 | | |

- **p95 under 12 ms: pass** everywhere. Headless Chromium caps at 120 Hz, so this shows hitches, not GPU headroom.
- **Draw calls under 150: pass.** Worst over a full-city sweep (1,336 to 1,376 spots at 3, 16 and 38 m, 4 headings, rush on) was 135.
- **Triangles under 600k: fail at a few spots.** Seed 130 desktop: max **662k**, 37 of 1,336 spots over 600k (2.8%), all near parks full of trees and people (`tris28-d-130-worst.jpg`). Seed 22 desktop: max 599k. iPhone seed 22: max 540k. In normal street flight 547k to 555k. Round 27 peaked at 464k, so round 28 added about 100k to 130k. Frame time did not move.
- **First load under 15 MB: pass.** Production build without source maps: 2.6 MB in total. First load is about 1.0 MB (HTML 11 KB, CSS 40 KB, JS 910 KB, 255 KB gzipped). The CC0 assets **lazy-load after the first frame**: 1.57 MB (GLBs 385 KB, WebP textures 1.18 MB, a 45 KB loader chunk). Until they arrive, the city runs on the procedural stand-ins. lil-gui (31 KB) only loads with `?debug`. Type check clean.
- **No first-flight hitch over 100 ms: fail on desktop.** Desktop seed 22, fresh profile: one **241 ms** frame on the first playing frame, the same as rounds 25 and 27. The audio prewarm did not remove it in headless Chromium. No first-flight hitch on any of 6 phone runs. One 50 ms frame at 26.5 s on iPhone 22. The 117 to 125 ms frames at 80.5 s are my probe's final read, as in round 27. **Needs a check in a real desktop browser.**

## Biggest remaining gap

**The desktop camera after a pickup or drop beside a wall.** The phone now passes the round 26 test (0 samples at 40% or more). On desktop the camera still pulls in to about 4.2 m from close above. For about 1.4 s after each drop by a wall the drone covers 60 to 77% of the screen height. That hides the route diamond, the distance and the street ahead, at the moment the player needs to find the next target. One desktop run had 20 of 62 wall samples at 40% or more (round 27 desktop: 3 to 16%). The phone fix (`touchRoom`) shows the way. It is just not applied to desktop.

**Acceptance test:** desktop 1280x720, seeds 22, 58 and 130, first run, street bot 80 s, plus one returning run on seed 22. For 3 s after each pickup or drop, sample the drone's screen box every 100 ms. The box is under 40% of the screen height in 99% of samples beside a wall. The 2 m test and the tunnel test still pass.

If that counts as polish (it is short and only beside walls), then **only polish remains**, ranked as below plus this one first.

## Other gaps, ranked

1. **Cars have no wheels.** All three CC0 car models show empty wheel arches and sit on the road (`car28-new-22-t1-6m.jpg`). It is the most visible flaw at street level. Test: every car model has 4 wheels at 6 m in a side view, in near and far detail.
2. **Traffic overlap at the outer ring corners in rush hour** (old bug). A turning car merges into a lane car for up to about 17 s. Test: `traffic-rt28.mjs` (real time, every frame), seed 4 three times plus 22, 130 and 58: 0 overlapping frames.
3. **Triangles over 600k near parks** (max 662k on seed 130). Test: `trisweep28.mjs` on seeds 22 and 130, desktop and phone: max under 600k. The near-tree range or the near people are the likely levers.
4. **Desktop first-flight hitch, 241 ms.** Test: desktop fresh profile, first playing frame under 100 ms. **Needs a real desktop browser** to check that it is not a headless artefact.
5. **Shop signs and faces.** Sign plates are still white blobs on a dark plate, and people have no faces. The window static from round 27 is still there. Does it matter at play speed? **Needs a human eye.**

## Screenshots (progress/round-28/critic/)

- Art, same spots as round 27: `art28-{d,m}-{hour-130,morning-22}-{street,shopfront,facade-mid,mid,cruise,cruise-down}.jpg`, people `-people-f0..f2.jpg` and close-ups `-people-close-f0..f2.jpg`.

builder.md
# Drone Dash: round 28 builder notes

Concern: street-level realism with free CC0 assets (the round 27 critic's biggest gap).
Order of work: street props, cars and trees, Poly Haven textures, shop-front variety, people, tests. Then the three leftovers (phone camera, payout chimes, Slipstream hint), and one fix the tests found (the first-flight hitch).

No paid generation. No Meshy, Retro Diffusion, PixelLab, ElevenLabs or `generate_3d` calls. Sketchfab stayed off. Only CC0 assets.

## How I worked and tested

- Blender 5.2 through the Blender MCP. The owner's Blender had an unsaved default file (cube, light, camera). I worked in a new scene `dd_assets` and saved nothing. At the end I switched back to the original scene, removed my scene and purged the orphan data. No file was saved.
- Production snapshot served by `vite preview` on 127.0.0.1:5190 (`builder-scripts/rebuild28.sh`). The round 27 code (`git archive HEAD`, read only) was built and served on 5191 as the baseline. The owner's server on 5188 was not touched. Both of my servers are stopped.
- One browser at a time, from job queues (`queue28*.sh`, `jobs28*.txt`, logs `queue28*.log`).
- New scripts in `progress/round-28/builder-scripts/`:
  - `art28.mjs`: the critic's `art27.mjs` views (same spots, both moods, desktop and iPhone), plus prop and shop audits per view. `OUT_PREFIX=before27 PORT=5191` makes the before set.
  - `closeup28.mjs`: free-camera close-ups (a walking person in 3 frames 0.15 s apart, the curb strip, the road).
  - `prop-audit28.mjs`: placement audit (pads, alleys, tunnels, diagonal, roads, poles), props near six spots, shop audit, on 5 seeds.
  - `tri-probe28.mjs`, `start-profile28.mjs`, `audio-cost28.mjs`: small diagnostics.
  - `blender_pipeline.py`: the Blender code used, for the record.
  - `critic27/`: copies of the round 27 critic scripts, pointed at 5190 and at `builder-shots/`. `fb27-init.js` and `fb27.py` also log each played payout chime and whether its pop showed.
- Copied from round 27 and used as before:
  - `crash-classify-v`, `cam-clip24`, `street-probe`, `pad-people23`
  - `acceptance-probe` (flat frames), `hud-probe26`, the three medal bots
  - `perf-street`, `perf27`, `firstframe27`, `layout-check27`, `detail-audit27`
- `perf-street`, `perf27`, `crash-classify-v` and `street-probe` now take `PORT`. `perf-street` also takes `HOOK` and `DUMP`.

## Assets (all CC0, full table with sizes in `games/drone-dash/ASSETS.md`)

- Cars (Kay Lousberg, City Builder kit): Car Hatchback, Stationwagon, Taxi.
- Street props: Fire Hydrant, Bench, Fence Pillar (bollard) by Kay Lousberg. Trashcan by Kenney. Medium Pot (planter) by Isa Lousberg. Table Large Circular by CreativeTrio. Chair and Sign (sandwich board) by Quaternius.
- Trees (Quaternius): two species, a round multi-crown tree and an oak-like tree.
- Poly Haven textures at 1k: Plastered Wall 02 (facade detail), Concrete Pavement 02 (sidewalk), Asphalt 02 (road). Albedo and normal each.
- People: Poly Pizza has no CC0 animated low-poly people (search "person walking", animated, CC0: no results). I improved the round 27 figures in code instead.
- Tried and not used:
  - Road Bits and Traffic Light (Kay Lousberg): no use for them.
  - Pine (Quaternius) and Bush: alpha-leaf textures.
  - Trash Bin: an indoor pedal bin. Mailbox: a rural post box.

## Pipeline

1. `search_assets` (Poly Pizza with the CC0 filter, and Poly Haven) and `import_asset` into the fresh scene.
2. Flatten each model: every face takes one colour, sampled from the kit's palette texture at the face's UV centre (or the material colour). This removes all textures and materials. Each model becomes plain vertex colours.
3. Scale to the game's sizes. The cars fit the round 22 boxes exactly: compact 3.8 x 1.72 x 1.46 m, sedan and taxi 4.5 x 1.82 m. Front on +Z, wheels on the ground.
4. Split into roles. Cars: `paint` (stored as a grey shade, so each car still takes its own colour per instance), `glass` (glossy) and `trim` (own colours). Trees: `canopy` (grey shade, tinted per tree with the old palette, so autumn colours stay) and `trunk`. Props: one part.
5. Decimate (collapse) per role: car trim 0.38, car paint 0.8, round-tree canopy 0.13, oak canopy 0.33, trunks 0.45 to 0.55.
6. Export GLB without materials and UVs: `car_compact.glb` (628 triangles), `car_wagon.glb` (624), `car_taxi.glb` (654), `street_props.glb` (8 props, 1,468 triangles), `trees.glb` (2 species, 802).
7. Poly Haven JPEGs converted to WebP with `cwebp` (albedo q72, normal q80). Originals stay in `asset-src/` (now in `.gitignore`).

## What changed in the game

### 1. Street props (`CityGenerator.placeStreetProps`, new `StreetProps.ts`)
- Ten kinds:
  - from the CC0 models: bench, litter bin, hydrant, bollard, planter (with a procedural shrub), cafe table with two chairs, sandwich board
  - procedural: bike rack (three hoops), bus stop (a pole and sign, with a bench)
- Placement: slots every 2.8 m along each curb, 0.42 to 1.0 m in from it (the strip the lamps and trees use). The kind comes from a position hash. No draws from the city's random stream, so the layout is unchanged. Bollards at both ends of each curb, by the crossings. At most one hydrant per curb. One bus stop on about 4 of 6 blocks.
- Kept clear:
  - pads: any ground site, its radius plus 1.8 m
  - alley mouths, tunnel arches and the diagonal (the same clear zones as the trees)
  - lamp posts (1.2 m), trunks (1.5 m) and roads
  - no cafe or sandwich board on park blocks
- Nothing collides. Everything is small and stays in the curb strip, outside the walkers' paths (1.75 and 2.35 m in).
- Drawing: one InstancedMesh per kind, only for pieces within 80 m of the camera (60 m on touch). The range shrinks above 18 m of camera height. Thin pieces (bollards, hydrants, chairs, bus-stop poles) cast no shadow.
  - A BatchedMesh (one draw call) was tried first. Without WEBGL_multi_draw it draws piece by piece. In the headless tests it pushed desktop p95 to 16.7 ms. The instanced version fixed that.

### 2. Cars and trees
- Traffic types 0, 1 and 2 (compact, sedan, taxi) use the three CC0 car models (`StreetKit.modelBody`, `Traffic.setCarModels`). Same sizes, lanes, lights and traffic code as round 22. The paint still takes the per-car colour. Small glowing head and tail lamp boxes keep dusk and brake lights. The van, box truck and hover-van stay procedural.
- Trees: near the camera, street and park trees use one of the two species (picked by position hash). Near means 80 m (62 m on touch), less from high up. Further away they keep the old blob. The blob canopies are now compacted, so only far trees are drawn. Pines stay procedural. Colliders and the hide-near-camera rule are unchanged. The occlusion pass now only sets `hidden`, and `Environment.updateTreeLod` writes the matrices.

### 3. Poly Haven textures (`CityMaterial.ts`, `Environment.ts`)
- Walls near the camera (full to 20 m, gone at 52 m) get the plaster albedo detail and the plaster normal map. The detail is relative to the texture's own mean, so each wall keeps its colour and light mood. The normal map uses a world-aligned tangent frame. Brick walls get half strength, so the mortar pattern stays.
- Sidewalks: near the camera the procedural tile grid fades into the Poly Haven concrete slabs (albedo and normal).
- Road: the Poly Haven asphalt (3 m tile, albedo and normal, slightly warm tint) replaces the canvas texture. The ground material has a flat normal map from the start, so the swap needs no shader recompile.
- Everything is lazy: the loader (`StreetAssets.ts`, with GLTFLoader) is its own 45 KB chunk, fetched after the first frame. The models' materials are compiled with `compileAsync` before they go into the scene. Until then the city runs on its procedural stand-ins. `?assets=0` keeps the stand-ins (for A/B checks).

### 4. Shop-front variety (`CityGenerator.ts`, `CityMaterial.ts`)
- Each shop bay (two window columns) has a sign variant, `(seed + bay) mod 8`. There are 7 sign colours with light, gold or dark letters, and variant 7 is a home entrance. It also has a door colour, `(3 seed + 3 bay) mod 7`, from 7 colours, with a glazed panel and a brass handle.
- Within a building, neighbouring bays always differ. Across a party wall, the generator steps the building's seed (no random draw) until the touching bays differ in both sign and door colour.
- Awnings are now one colour per bay, from the same palette, stepped so that no two neighbouring bays match. The old single colour draw is kept, so the random stream is unchanged.
- Audit hook `shopAudit()`: neighbouring bays along each street-face line, within and across buildings.

### 5. People (`StreetKit.buildPedGeometry`)
- Near figures: tapered round limbs (6-sided), rounded hands, a smooth sphere head, a round neck. No box is left except the shoes. Knees and elbows bend as in round 27.
- Fixed a round 27 bug: the shoulder-bag strap was rotated about the world origin, so it floated as a stick beside about a fifth of the people.

### Leftovers
- **Phone camera after pickups and drops:** on touch screens the slow-drone room floor is now 8.8 m instead of 4.2 m (2.1 times, `CameraRig.touchRoom`, used in `keepRoom`). Desktop is unchanged.
- **Payout chimes:** the chime, shake and sparks now play at the moment the payout pop shows (`Hud.slipPop(..., onShow)`). A pop held behind a hint waits with them. A pop dropped as stale stays silent. Diagnostics: `slipstream.chimes`.
- **Slipstream hint:** it is only introduced while drafting (before, any meter above 0.05 counted).
- **First-flight hitch:** profiling showed `start()` took 222 ms, and about 198 ms of it was `new AudioContext()`. The context is now made on the title screen (`AudioSystem.prewarm`, 1.2 s after boot), and `start()` only resumes it.
