critic.md
# Drone Dash: round 27 critic report

**Verdict:** Round 26 works: medals now reward skill and the first run is paced. The phone camera still swallows the screen after some pickups by a wall. Round 27 is a real step up for the buildings. Street level (shop fronts, people, cars, trees, pavements) is now the part that looks basic.

Build tested: commit 48a28e7 (rounds 26 and 27). My own dev server on port 5191, stopped at the end. The owner's server on 5188 was left alone. Every browser ran alone, one at a time, from one job queue (`critic-scripts/queue27.sh`, `jobs27.txt`). I did not read the round 26 or 27 builder notes. The round 25 scripts were copied to `progress/round-27/critic-scripts/`. Only the output folders changed (they write to `progress/round-27/critic/`). New scripts this round: `fb27-init.js` and `hud-probe27.mjs` (early feedback, camera after pickups and drops, pops on the "Fly" label), `art27.mjs` (art views), `firstleg27.mjs`, `fb27.py`, `acc27.py`.

## Round 26: medals for skill

Medal lines now: Bronze 1,000, Silver 2,400, Gold 6,000, Ace 15,000.

Twelve fresh cities, real time, one run at a time. Street = the low bot. Lazy = 10 m/s, no boost.

On 62513 it took 38 s on a 109 m leg and crashed at the end. All four reruns are Silver with 3 or 4 drops. With the reruns, 12 of 12 cities give the street pilot Silver.

- **First pickup within 15 s: 3 of 6 for the bot.** The slow ones are the bot, not the game. The first pickup is 65 m (22), 55 m (58) and 52 m (130) away by street (`firstleg.log`). A human at 12 to 16 m/s gets there in 4 to 7 s. On seed 130 the bot takes 21 to 23 s for 52 m. **A human gets there in time. Pass for the game.**
- **No stretch over 15 s without visible feedback in the first 60 s: pass.** Longest is 11.7 s (spawn to first pickup, phone 58). The slipstream now arrives at 8 to 15 s and fills the first carry. Round 25 had 15 to 18 s with only metres counting down.

Weak spot: the Slipstream hint fires at 8 s on 3 runs with the meter at 0.06 to 0.20 and not drafting. The code counts it as active (meter above 0.05). When the hint says "Fly low by walls", the drone is no longer next to a wall.

After that, 7 of 74 payouts played the chime and shake under a hint or banner. Their "+N Banked" pop never showed. The bonus in the objective pill still goes up. Small fail: the bar is 0.
- Human side (three new players on a phone) still **needs a human player.**

## Round 27: the art

Views: street (3 m), shop fronts (3 m), mid (14 to 16 m), cruise (38 m), cruise looking down, and people. Golden hour (seed 130) and bright morning (seed 22), desktop and iPhone. HUD hidden. `art27-*.jpg`.

**What works.** This is a real step. The city no longer reads as boxes. Six building types show up. One frame holds 2 to 4 types and, at street level, 3 to 11 shop fronts. Look at the red brick walk-up with blue shutters and a striped awning, next to a stone block with tall windows (`art27-d-hour-130-shopfront.jpg`). It reads as a street, not a test level. Bay-window apartments make a nice zigzag silhouette from above. There is a water tower, AC units, solar panels, antennas, fire escapes (`cam27-m-22-big2-hf45.jpg`) and gabled red roofs on the townhouse rows. Golden hour with long tower shadows across the street is the best look in the game so far. The look is consistent: warm, painterly, low poly.

**What still reads as basic or procedural, most visible first:**

1. **Wall surfaces are flat colour.** Brick is a flat red. Stone is a flat beige with faint lines. Nothing at the base of a wall (no grime, no darker plinth, no contact shadow where wall meets pavement). In bright morning light every facade looks like painted card (`art27-d-morning-22-street.jpg`, right side). From cruise height this is fine. At 3 m it is the main tell.
2. **Ground level is the weakest part.** Doors are identical black rectangles. Each shop has the same gold or orange sign plate with white blobs for letters. The same plate repeats along a whole block (`art27-d-morning-22-people-f1.jpg`, left building). Every awning is the same red and white stripe. Pavements and asphalt are perfectly clean: no kerb detail, drains, manholes, cracks or patches. No street furniture except lamps and benches in parks (no bins, hydrants, bollards, signposts, bike racks, cafe tables).
3. **Lit windows.** The lit glass uses a speckled noise that looks like TV static up close (`art27-d-hour-130-street.jpg`, left building and shop window). In bright morning some ground-floor glows blow out to plain white boxes with bloom (`art27-d-morning-22-people-f1.jpg`, right). Unlit glass has no sky reflection.
4. **People are blocky.** Box heads, box limbs, no faces or hands, stiff scissor stride. Hats, bags and coats help the colour, but at 3 m they read as voxel figures, a step behind the buildings now. At cruise height they are fine as dots.
5. **Rooftops are sparse.** Most flat roofs are an empty slab with at most one AC block. The skyline from cruise is flat boxes with a cornice. Only the townhouse gables break it.
6. **Cars and trees did not get the upgrade.** The taxi, sedan and van are simple boxes with a stripe. Trees are all the same low-poly blob in three greens. Next to the new facades they now look the most basic thing on screen.

**Can CC0 assets close it? Yes for most items. Shopping list, in order of value:**

| Item | CC0 source | Fixes |
|---|---|---|
| Brick, plaster, concrete and stone facade textures (albedo plus normal, 1K, tiling) | Poly Haven textures | Item 1. Blend them into the existing shader at street range only, keep the flat colour far away. |
| Asphalt, paving slabs, kerb stone | Poly Haven textures | Item 2 ground. |
| Street props: bins, hydrants, bollards, benches, bike racks, signposts, newspaper boxes, cafe tables, planters | Poly Pizza (Kenney City Kit, Quaternius) | Item 2. Instanced, a few hundred near the camera. |
| Low-poly cars (taxi, sedan, van, bus) | Poly Pizza (Kenney Car Kit, Quaternius) | Item 6. |
| Low-poly trees (2 or 3 species) | Poly Pizza (Quaternius nature) | Item 6. |
| Animated low-poly people (walk, idle) | Poly Pizza (Quaternius animated characters) | Item 4. Needs a baked-animation instancing path to keep 300 people cheap. That is real work. |
| Rooftop props: water tanks, vents, AC units, antennas, roof doors | Poly Pizza (Kenney City Kit) | Item 5. |
| One sky HDRI per light mood, for window and car reflections | Poly Haven HDRIs | Item 3 partly. |

What CC0 will not fix: shop signs and doors (generate varied sign text and door colours in code), the window static (a shader change: use a calmer interior pattern or a small interior atlas) and the blown-out daytime glows (cap lit-window brightness in bright moods). Budget is not a worry: about 10 textures at 1K plus 30 small GLBs stay well under 15 MB. Draw calls need watching: instance every prop.

- First-flight hitch: one 242 ms frame at the first playing frame on desktop, identical to round 25 (241 ms). None on the phone. The 116 ms frames at 80 s are my probe's final read, not the game.

## Biggest remaining gap

**Street level still looks basic next to the new buildings.** The facades now carry the city from mid and cruise height. At 3 m, the walls are flat colour and the doors are identical black boxes. One sign plate and one awning repeat along a block. Pavements are spotless, with no street furniture. People are blocky, cars are boxes and trees are blobs. The owner's ask ("more realistic") is half met: the upper floors are there, the ground floor is not.

Suggested order of work. First, street props, cars and trees from CC0 kits (Poly Pizza: Kenney City Kit, Car Kit, Quaternius). Second, Poly Haven facade and paving textures near the camera. Third, varied signs, doors and awnings in code. Last, better people.

**Acceptance test** (6 fixed street views per light mood, golden hour and bright morning, desktop and iPhone, the same spots as `art27.mjs`):
- Within 40 m of the drone at street level: at least 3 kinds of street prop and at least 1 prop per 10 m of pavement (count with a test hook).
- No two neighbouring shop fronts share the same sign, door colour and awning (test hook audit).
- Cars and trees: at least 3 car models and 2 tree species with real shape (not a recoloured box or blob).
- People: no box heads, with a walk cycle that bends knees and elbows (3 frames 0.15 s apart, checked by eye).
- A fresh critic, blind, picks the new street views over the round 27 views in at least 5 of 6 pairs, per mood.
- Budgets hold: p95 under 12 ms on desktop and phone in busy street flight, draw calls under 150, triangles under 600k, first load under 15 MB.

## Other gaps, ranked

1. **Phone camera after a pickup or drop by a wall** (round 26 test, failed). The drone box is 40% of the screen height or more in 7.4% of samples (bar: 1%), up to 74%. It hides the route diamond and the slipstream meter (`cam27-m-22-big2-hf45.jpg`). Same test next round.
2. **Payout chime under a hint.** 7 of 74 payouts played the chime and shake while a hint or banner hid their pop. At 8 s the Slipstream hint can fire with the drone no longer drafting (meter 0.06 to 0.20). Test: 0 payout chimes without their pop, and the Slipstream hint only while drafting.
3. **Lit windows.** Speckle noise reads as TV static up close, and some daytime glows blow out to white boxes in bright morning (`art27-d-morning-22-people-f1.jpg`). A shader fix, no assets needed.
4. **People stand in the drone at drop pads.** A walker beside the pad stands inside the rotor ring as the drone lands (`fr27-d-22-t031.jpg`). Test: no person within 1.5 m of the drone while it is under 2 m on a pad.
5. **Desktop pops cover the drone** in 27 to 42% of pop samples (round 25: about 20%), mostly the slip pop. Does it hurt? **Needs a human eye.**

## Screenshots (progress/round-27/critic/)

- Art, desktop: `art27-d-hour-130-{street,shopfront,facade-mid,mid,cruise,cruise-down,people-f0..f2}.jpg` (golden hour), `art27-d-morning-22-*.jpg` (bright morning).
- Art, iPhone 13: `art27-m-hour-130-*.jpg`, `art27-m-morning-22-*.jpg`.
- First run: `fr27-d-22-t003.jpg` to `t060.jpg`, `fr27-m-58-t003.jpg` to `t060.jpg`, `fr27-{d,m}-{22,58,130}-t010/t031/t045.jpg`.
- Phone camera after a pickup by a wall: `cam27-m-22-big1-hf42.jpg`, `big2-hf45.jpg`, `big3-hf44.jpg`.

# Drone Dash: round 27 builder notes

Concern: visual detail of buildings and people (owner: "still very basic, add more detail to make it more realistic").
Everything is procedural in code. No downloaded or generated assets.

## How I tested
- I served a production build of the working tree with `vite preview` on 127.0.0.1:5190 (`builder-scripts/rebuild27.sh`).
- For before/after comparisons I built the round 26 code (the working tree without my changes) and served it on 5191.
- The owner's server on 5188 was not touched. Both of my servers are stopped.
- One browser at a time, from one queue (`queue27.sh`, `jobs27.txt`, log `queue27.log`). The final build was locked before the queue started.
- New scripts:
  - `shots27.mjs`: fixed camera poses (street, second street, junction, facade, mid 10 m, cruise 24 m, high 45 m, park, shop door). It also logs calls, triangles and archetypes in view.
  - `perf27.mjs`: frame cost with vsync off, so costs under the 8.3 ms cap show. It toggles the detail kit and people on and off.
  - `firstframe27.mjs`: load time, the title frame, `start()` time and the first-flight hitch, with a cold browser.
  - `layout-check27.mjs`: every solid collider, every site and the pad audit, new against baseline.
  - `detail-audit27.mjs`: detail geometry inside pad landing columns, alley or tunnel corridors, or over roads.
  - `diag27.mjs` and `console27.mjs`: small helpers.
- I copied the rest from round 26 (and `pad-people23.mjs` from round 25, set to port 5190).

## Design

### Buildings
**1. Six archetypes, picked per lot.** Code: `archetypeOf` in `CityGenerator.ts`.
- The pick uses the window style, the height and a hash of the lot position. The hash draws nothing from the city's random stream, so the layout is unchanged (checked below).
- The archetypes:
  - brick walk-up
  - painted-plaster townhouse
  - precast-concrete apartments
  - stone classic
  - office (metal and glass)
  - glass tower
- The wall material is packed into the existing seed attribute (seed + 256 × material). No new vertex attribute.

**2. Facade shader.** Code: `CityMaterial.ts`, one material for the whole city, as before.
- Brick: running bond, a tone per brick and mortar joints. The joints fade out where a brick gets smaller than a pixel. There are three brick colours plus painted brick.
- Concrete: a panel per bay and storey, with joints and a tone per panel.
- Stone: courses with staggered joints. The ground floor is rusticated (deeper joints).
- Plaster: soft mottling.
- Office: metal spandrels with seams.
- Wear on every material: vertical weathering, grime and splash-back near the ground, rain streaks under the sills, and a ledge line at each storey.
- Windows look set into the wall:
  - a frame, a sill and a lintel (brick and stone)
  - shadow along the top and one side of each opening (the reveal)
  - a glazing-bar cross
- Behind the glass there is an interior: a dark floor, a back wall and a lighter ceiling. Homes have curtains in three widths and colours. Offices have blinds lowered to random heights.
- Painted townhouses get shutters with slats.
- Lit windows get brighter toward the ceiling and dimmer behind curtains.
- How many windows are lit now follows the light mood: golden hour 22%, morning 7%, rose dusk 36%, noon 5%. Before, it was 16% in every mood.
- Ground-floor shop fronts on every street-facing building with punched, ribbon or tall windows:
  - a coloured fascia sign with blocky letters (the letters glow a little at dusk)
  - big windows with a centre bar, a door in some bays, and a dark kick plate
  - inside: shelves of coloured goods, lit in some shops
- About 20% of ground-floor bays are a home entrance instead of a shop: a panelled door with a lit transom window.
- Glass towers have a lit lobby.
- The relief (mortar, joints, reveals, sills, sign boards) is a bump in the shader: the normal is bent using screen-space derivatives. No textures. All pattern detail and bump fade out with distance (`far`), so nothing shimmers far away.
- Flat roofs get membrane seams and patches.

**3. Detail kit.** Code: new `BuildingDetail.ts`. Real geometry, merged, using the city material (no new shader).
- On street faces only:
  - window sills
  - apartment balconies: slab, solid front and a rail (0.6 m deep)
  - Juliet balconies with iron rails, and flower planters, on townhouses
  - fire escapes on walk-ups (platforms, rails, stair flights and a drop ladder), up to 0.58 m deep
  - window AC units
  - drain pipes
  - corner quoins on stone buildings
  - vertical fins on offices and glass towers
  - blade signs over shops: a board with a glowing edge and a bracket
- Rooftops: vents, exhaust stacks, skylights, satellite dishes, antennas with cross bars, and a rail on rooftop-pad roofs. They stay off the existing roof colliders and at least 5.2 m from rooftop pads.
- Park benches beside the four park paths, clear of the park pad, trees and lamps.
- Awnings are now sloped, striped canvas with a valance (new `Style.awning`). They are drawn inside the same box as before, so the pad audit is unchanged.
- **Collision:** nothing new collides. The collider list is identical. Every added part is within 0.62 m of its face (the drone's radius is 0.95 m) or small.
- **Kept clear:**
  - In blocks with an alley or tunnel, only flush parts are added: sills, pipes, quoins and fins.
  - In the column above a doorstep pad (2.9 m along the face), only sills.
  - No fire escape over a doorstep, and no blade sign within 3.8 m of one.
  - Corner fins are clamped onto their face. One stuck 7 cm into an alley on seed 317. The audit found it, and it is fixed.
- **Distance detail:** the kit is a 4 × 4 grid of merged chunks. A chunk draws only while the camera is within 95 m of it (75 m on touch devices). Above 30 m, that range grows by 0.5 m for every metre of height. Only chunks within 30 m cast shadows. That keeps the draw-call rise small.

### People
Code: `StreetKit.ts` and `Pedestrians.ts`.
- **New figure:** separate thighs and shins, upper arms and forearms, hands, shoes, a neck and a nose. The shoulders are wider than the waist. The head is a smoother sphere (detail 1). The hair is a cap over the back and top of the head, so the face shows.
- **Smoother walk:** knees bend in the swing phase, elbows bend with the arm swing, and the upper body sways a little with each step.
- **Outfits** (per person, from their own random stream, so placement is unchanged): shirt and trousers, T-shirt and shorts (bare lower legs and forearms), dress (skirt, bare legs), jacket, long coat.
- **Hair:** short cap, long hair, a bun, or cropped, in four hair colours.
- **Accessories:** caps with a brim (18%), shoulder bags with a strap (20%), backpacks.
- Hats and bags take a second and third accent colour, so nobody is one colour head to toe. Some people wear white sneakers.
- **Poses:**
  - Phone: walking or standing, the forearm is raised with a phone and the head tilted down. 10% of walkers walk 15% slower with a phone. About half of the people standing alone at a shop door read a phone.
  - Talking pairs: two people at a shop door stand together, turned toward each other, and gesture.
  - Sitting: people sit on the new park benches (one or two per bench).
- A sitting person reacts to a low pass with the arms and head only (the legs stay seated), and does not side-step.
- Kept from round 22 and 23:
  - instancing (a near mesh and a far mesh, one draw call each) and thinning with distance
  - the paths, the pad rules and the reaction to low passes
- The far figure is now its own smaller geometry (about 110 triangles). Far people (40 m and more) no longer cast shadows.

### Camera tunnel and 2 m tests

### People (`street-probe.log`, `pad-people.log`)

  - people on the live pad: 0
  - share of people on roads: 0 (about 100,000 samples a seed)

### Other regressions

- Flat-frame probe: 931 frames, **0 flat**, 0 errors.

  - marker on the "Fly" label 0, pops over the controls 0, gate tag on "Fly" 0

### Medals and gates, seeds 22, 58, 130 (`m-low-a.log`, `m-high-a.log`, `m-lazy-a.log`, `m-high-rep22.log`)

# Drone Dash: round 26 builder notes

Main concern: medals counted drops, not flying. Bundled: the first run taught in a burst. Leftover: the phone camera at its floor after a pickup, and the pickup pop on the "Fly" label.

## How I tested
- Bots played a production build of the working tree. My own `vite preview` served it on 127.0.0.1:5190.
- I rebuilt it between jobs (`builder-scripts/rebuild26.sh`). So an edit never reached a running page.
- The owner's server on 5188 was left alone.
- Every browser ran alone, one job at a time, from one queue (`queue26.sh`, `jobs26.txt`).
- The scripts are the round 25 critic's. Only the output folder (`../builder-shots/`) and the port changed.
- New scripts: `hud-probe26.mjs` is hud-probe25 plus `fly26-init.js`. That init script samples the drone box after pickups and drops, and pops on the "Fly" label.
- Also new: `fr26.py` (first-run pacing from the FIRSTRUN log) and `acc26.py` (medal test at any medal lines).

## Design

### 1. Each drop's score shows how it was flown
Code: `DeliverySystem.update`, `RUN` in `config.ts`.
- **Par is judged on the run clock.** Seconds that the slow clock gave back on the drop leg count as time saved (`legClockGain`). A street pilot who drafts toward the marker beats par by more. A slow, centred flier gets nothing extra. The clock is the timer the player sees.
- **The fast bonus is mostly per second.** It was 100 flat plus 15 a second under par (up to 8 s). It is now 40 flat plus 30 a second (up to 10 s). A drop 1 s under par gets 70. At 6 s it gets 220. At 10 s it gets 340.
- **Only a sharp drop builds the combo.** A drop at least 3 clock seconds under par (`comboSharp`) adds a combo step. A drop that only scrapes in keeps the combo. A late drop breaks it, as before. The lazy flier now rarely gets past x1.
- **The base is a little lower:** 200 to 160 points, and 2.4 to 2.2 points a metre. A slow drop is worth less. A sharp drop gets it back through the time bonus.
- **The pop names the measure.** Example: "+752 delivered / Fast +281 · 8 s under par · +533 street bonus". If the combo grew, the pop shows it ("· x1.3"). A late drop says "Late · no fast bonus".
- All of this is paid with the drop. So it counts as delivery in the strict share.
- The street bonus, the slow clock and the job sequence did not change.
- **Medal lines, retuned last:** Silver 2,800 to 2,400. Bronze 1,200 to 1,000. Gold (6,000) and Ace (15,000) did not change. The numbers are below.
- Job selection: no change. For the first-run test I tried a shorter first pickup leg (35 to 75 m, then 25 to 55 m). The street bot overshot the nearer depot pad on seed 22. Its first pickup took 18.5 to 20.7 s. So I went back to the round 25 spec (45 to 95 m). The pacing change closes the first-run gap instead.

### 2. Paced teaching on a first run
Code: `Game.updateTeach`, `TEACH`, `teachActive`, `arrivalDue`.
- **One introduction at a time, at least 8 s apart.** It was 4 s.
- **No introduction within 3.5 s of a pickup or delivery pop.** An introduction waits 3.5 s after a pop. It also waits while the drone will reach its pickup or drop within 4 s (distance left over speed).
- **Each hint shows only while its system runs:**
  - Slipstream: while drafting.
  - Slow clock: while the clock is slowed.
  - High wind: above 30 m, in a real headwind.
  - Shortcuts: while an arch marks a shortcut on this leg.
- **The slipstream comes first, on the first draft from 8 s.** The flight to the first pickup now has something to watch. The player sees the payouts before hearing them. Everything else still waits until 30 s.
- **No reward sound or shake without something visible.** Before the slipstream is introduced, a payout banks silently: no chime, no shake, no sparks, no meter ticks. The boost still refills. After the introduction, every payout has its pop.
- **The medal banner fires at its cause.** On a first run, a drop that crosses a medal line introduces the medal layer at once. The banner follows the delivery pop that caused it, about 1 s later. A returning player gets the same order. The banner is the delivery's own result. So it is the one introduction that can come next to a delivery pop.
- **Rush hour** keeps its start time, so scoring is the same for every player. On a first run, the 8 s before 60 s stay free of introductions. If a pop is near at 60 s, the banner and horn wait for a clear moment. Seed 22: 63.6 s, 4.5 s after a drop.
- Combo hint text: "Drops 3 s under par in a row raise the multiplier".

### 3. Phone camera and the "Fly" label
- **Camera floor for a slow drone** (`CameraRig.keepRoom`). It is 4.2 m at 4 m/s or slower. It eases to the old 2.4 m at 9 m/s. For 3.2 s after a pickup or a drop it stays at 4.2 m at any speed (`holdRoom`). At a pad, right after a pickup or a drop, the drone no longer fills the screen. Fast flying in open streets keeps the 2.4 m floor. Without room, the camera uses the existing rise (up and a little back, with a line-of-sight check).
- **The drone stays in frame** (`CameraRig.keepInFrame`). After the camera rises over the drone, the look point ahead could leave the drone under the bottom edge. Now the look point blends toward the drone, just enough to keep the drone's centre inside the frame.
- **Shorter parcel reel** (`Drone`). The parcel snaps up from 1.0 m below, not 1.6 m. Drone and parcel stay compact in the first half second after a pickup.
- **Compact pops for a tall score column** (`Hud.touchLayout`). The pop slot sits between the score column and the stick. With the combo chip showing, the slot was pushed down onto the "Fly" label. Now, if that room is under 118 px, the pops go compact: no icon, smaller type (`#hud.pop-tight` in `styles.css`). They sit in the middle of the room. With more room, the slot centre stays at least 54 px above the label. A tall message (a two-line hint, the rush hour or medal banner) is lifted when it shows, so its bottom stays above the label.

## Numbers

Medal and gate runs used builds with the final scoring code. The last camera and pop fixes came after them (they do not touch scoring). The phone, first-run and regression runs below used the final build, unless noted.

### Medals, 12 fresh cities, real time (`acc-low.log`, `acc-lazy.log`, reruns `rep-low-*.log`)
Scores are from the runs. The medal column uses the new lines (Bronze 1,000, Silver 2,400).

| City | Street (low bot) | Lazy |
|---|---|---|
| 31847 | 2,825 Silver, 2 drops | 1,804 Bronze, 3 drops |
| 52906 | 4,591 Silver, 3 | 1,084 Bronze, 2 |
| 74413 | 3,828 Silver, 3 | 1,050 Bronze, 2 |
| 19582 | 3,178 Silver, 3 | 1,403 Bronze, 2 |
| 63170 | 4,406 Silver, 4 | 1,119 Bronze, 2 |
| 88241 | 3,248 Silver, 3 | 1,089 Bronze, 2 |
| 27659 | 5,106 Silver, 4 | 1,725 Bronze, 3 |
| 45318 | 3,406 Silver, 3 | 966 none, 2 |
| 90724 | 3,619 Silver, 3 | 1,286 Bronze, 2 |
| 36085 | **1,945 Bronze, 2**. Reruns: 4,542 Silver, 3 and 3,756 Silver, 3 | 1,167 Bronze, 2 |
| 58861 | 5,801 Silver, 4 | 2,080 Bronze, 3 |
| 14492 | **1,888 Bronze, 2**. Reruns: 2,870 Silver, 3 and 4,666 Silver, 3 | 998 none, 2 |

- Street Silver or better: first pass 10 of 12. Both misses are bot runs whose second pickup came at 69 s and 77 s (the bot lost 20 s or more). Each city was rerun twice: 4 of 4 reruns are Silver with 3 drops. With the reruns: **12 of 12 cities**.

# Drone Dash: round 25 critic report

**Verdict:** Delivery is now the main reward in every bot run. The camera and phone leftovers are closed. The medal guard now fails. Delivery pays twice as much, so medals follow the number of drops. A slow 3-drop flier lands within a few points of a 2-drop street pilot. The first run is calm before 30 s. Then it teaches eight things in 34 s.

Build tested: commit 258206f plus the uncommitted round 25 changes. My own dev server on port 5191, stopped at the end. The owner's server on 5188 was left alone. Every browser ran alone, one at a time, from one job queue (`critic-scripts/queue25.sh`, `jobs25.txt`). I did not read the builder notes. Bot scores are the same in first-run and returning mode (teaching only hides HUD parts), so a fresh browser profile is a fair bot test.

## Round 24 gap: delivery is the main reward. Closed (bot side).

Strict count: what the drop itself pays (base, fast-drop time bonus, rush bonus, combo). The banked street bonus paid with the drop and the time-up share are not counted. "At the drop" adds the street bonus paid in the same pop (everything the player sees arrive at a delivery).

| Run (real time) | 22 | 58 | 130 | Total | Strict delivery share | Street bonus share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Low (street line) | 6,384 Gold, 4 drops | 3,757 Silver, 3 | 5,217 Silver, 3 | **15,358** | **61.1%** (each run 58 to 67%) | 38.9% |
| High (roof line) | 7,777 Gold, 7 drops | 1,876 Bronze, 2 (5 crashes) | 5,122 Silver, 5 | **14,775** | **96.3%** (each 86 to 100%) | 3.3% |
| Lazy | 1,205 Bronze, 2 | 1,400 Bronze, 2 | 1,241 Bronze, 2 | 3,846 | 84.4% | 15.6% |

- Delivery at least 55% of total: **pass**, on all 6 low and high runs (lowest 58%, seed 130 low). Round 24 had slipstream at 56% of the low total. Now it is 39%.
- At the drop (strict plus the street bonus in the same pop): 100% of low, 99.6% of high. Every point except the time-up share now arrives with a delivery.
- Street total over high: 15,358 / 14,775 = **1.04**. Pass (needs 0.85). Note: the roof line now matches the street line and earns almost no street bonus. Slipstream has become an optional extra. That fits the goal, but it is a design change worth knowing.
- Lazy Bronze or below: **pass** (1,205 to 1,400, all just over the 1,200 Bronze line).
- No Ace: **pass**. Best score of any run is 7,777 (Ace is 15,000).
- Breakdown exact (bot sum and game-over card): **pass** on all 37 real-time bot runs.
- The new delivery pop reads well: "+731 delivered" big, "Fast drop +193 · +512 street bonus" below (`fr25-d-22-t036.jpg` area, and `hud25-m-130-ov1.jpg` for the pickup pop "Deliver for +499").
- Player side (three new players say "delivering parcels" scores most) still **needs a human player**.

## Medal guards (12 fresh cities, real time, one run at a time)

Silver is now 2,800, Bronze 1,200, Gold 6,000, Ace 15,000.

| City | Street (low bot) | Lazy |
|---|---|---|
| 31847 | **2,695 Bronze**, 2 drops | **2,504 Bronze, 3 drops** |
| 52906 | 4,859 Silver, 4 | 1,347 Bronze, 2 |
| 74413 | 4,462 Silver, 3 | 1,289 Bronze, 2 |
| 19582 | 3,474 Silver, 3 | 1,683 Bronze, 2 |
| 63170 | 4,764 Silver, 4 | 1,372 Bronze, 2 |
| 88241 | 3,177 Silver, 3 | 1,606 Bronze, 2 |
| 27659 | 5,757 Silver, 4 | 2,426 Bronze, 3 |
| 45318 | 3,555 Silver, 3 | 1,161 none, 2 |
| 90724 | 3,634 Silver, 3 | 1,434 Bronze, 2 |
| 36085 | 3,900 Silver, 3 | 1,056 none, 2 |
| 58861 | 5,466 Silver, 4 | **2,617 Bronze, 3 drops** |
| 14492 | **2,620 Bronze**, 2 drops | 1,403 Bronze, 2 |

- Street Silver or better: **fail, 10 of 12.** Both Bronze cities are 2-drop runs that miss Silver by 105 and 180 points.
- Lazy Bronze or below: **pass**, 12 of 12.
- Best lazy at least 300 below worst street: **fail.** Best lazy 2,617 (58861) against worst street 2,620 (14492): a gap of 3 points. Without the two Bronze street cities the worst street is 3,177, a gap of 560.
- Strict delivery share on the 12 street runs: 68.7% (lowest 56%). On the 12 lazy runs: 92.8%.

**The two Bronze street cities: one is the game, one is the bot.**
- 31847: two drops by 59 s. The third job is a 134 m street leg picked up at 73.5 s. The clock runs out at 85% of the leg, overtime gives 8 s, and the bot ends 95% of the way (17 m short). The time-up share pays 391. On the same city, the lazy bot got 3 drops from a different job sequence. Two reruns: 2,641 and 2,728, both Bronze with 2 drops. Three of three runs miss Silver by 70 to 160 points. **Game:** this city gives a street pilot 2 drops, and 2 drops is not Silver.
- 14492: the pickup leg after the first drop takes 26 s (109 m). The second drop lands at 76 s with 10 s left, too little for a third. Two reruns: 1,372 (1 drop, the bot got stuck for 50 s on a pickup) and 4,018 Silver (3 drops). **Mostly bot and luck.**
- The pattern is in the numbers, not one bad bot run. A street run with 2 drops scores 2,600 to 2,700. A lazy run with 3 drops scores 2,400 to 2,600. Silver (2,800) sits just above both. So the medal now says "how many parcels", with little room for how well you flew. The street bonus used to be the gap between a good and a lazy pilot (round 24: lazy best 1,559 vs street worst 2,207). Moving points into the drop removed most of that gap.

## First run for a new player (cleared storage)

Probe: `hud-probe25.mjs` with `NEW=1` and `firstrun-init.js`. Every 100 ms it logs which HUD parts are really visible: element and parents shown, opacity 0.15 or more, on screen. It also logs every banner text with its time. The low street bot flies, 80 s. Desktop seed 22 and iPhone 13 seed 58.

| First visible (s) | Desktop 22 | iPhone 58 |
|---|---|---|
| Score, clock, objective pill, parcel count, boost bar, speed and altitude, pad marker, pause | 0.1 | 0.1 (plus stick and buttons) |
| "Parcel secured! Deliver for +N" pop | **15.4** | **11.8** |
| Slipstream meter, street bonus, Slipstream hint | 30.0 | 30.0 |
| First delivery pop | 31.8 (drop at 30.8) | 31.8 (drop at 30.2) |
| Combo chip and hint | 34 | 34 |
| Medal goal row and Bronze banner | 38 (Bronze was reached at 31.8) | 75 |
| Slow clock hint | 42 | 46 |
| Camera hint | 46 | 38 |
| High wind hint | 50 | 42 |
| Rush hour banner | 60 | 60 |
| Shortcuts hint and arches | 64 | 79 |

- Nothing new before 30 s except the first pickup and its marker: **pass**, both devices.
- Each hint once: **pass.** Seven hints, each shown once.
- Returning player (played key set): full HUD from the first frame (medal goal, route pill, and the slipstream meter as soon as it fills), no teaching class, no hints. **Pass** on 4 phone runs and 1 desktop run.

**Problems the probe shows:**
1. **The layers arrive as a burst.** Eight introductions in 34 s (30 to 64 s), 4 s apart, on both devices. Two of them land on the first delivery. The Slipstream hint appears at 30.0 s and the first delivery pop has to wait behind it (`fr25-d-22-t031.jpg`, `fr25-m-58-t031.jpg`: the score already shows 920 or 1,243, but the screen says SLIPSTREAM).
2. **Hints out of context.** "High wind: up high the wind slows you" shows at 42 to 50 s while the drone is at street height. It was queued at the spawn, at 18 m. On the phone the first slipstream pop a new player sees is "Off route · No bonus" at 37.5 s.
3. **The medal moment comes late.** On desktop the run reaches Bronze at the first delivery (31.8 s). The banner shows at 38 s, after the Combo hint.
4. **Quiet banking is not quiet.** Before 30 s, the bot banks 4 to 5 slipstream payouts (up to 512 points). The pop is hidden, but the payout chime, the camera shake and the boost refill still happen. A new player hears and feels a reward with nothing on screen to explain it.

## First 30 s as a player

- **Is it clear what to do?** Yes. One pill ("PICK UP Records · Juniper & 4th Ave"), one marker with a distance, a clock. Nothing else competes (`fr25-d-22-t010.jpg`, `fr25-m-58-t018.jpg`). This is the cleanest start the game has had.
- **Is there enough feedback?** It is thin but not empty. The first visible reward comes at 12 to 15 s ("Parcel secured! Deliver for +437"). It names the prize, which is good. Then 15 to 18 s pass with only the distance counting down, plus the unexplained chimes above. For a delivery game, a 12 to 15 s flight to the first pickup is fine. The quiet 15 s carry after it is the weaker part, because the player cannot yet see any progress except metres. Does it drag? **Needs a human player.**
- **Is the pickup pop at 15 to 22 s a problem?** Not by itself. The real issue is the shape of the first minute: 30 s with almost nothing, then 34 s with almost everything.
- **The early-feedback test I recommend** (replaces "first payout within 10 s"): on a first run, measured on 3 seeds, desktop and phone, with the street bot:
  - The first pickup lands within 15 s. Now 11.8 and 15.4 s: pass.
  - In the first 60 s, no stretch longer than 15 s without visible feedback (a pop, a marker change or a meter).
  - Every sound or shake that means "reward" comes with something visible that explains it.
  - From 30 s on, at most one new introduction per 8 s. None within 3 s of a delivery or pickup pop.
  - Each hint fires only while its system is active. Wind only above 30 m. Slow clock only while the clock is slowed.
  - Human side: 3 new players play a first run on a phone. Each can say what to do within 10 s. None stops to ask why it chimed.

## Camera and phone HUD (round 24 leftovers)

**Camera near a wall: closed.** I measured the camera to drone distance in every frame in open streets (not alley or tunnel framing). 6 runs with deliveries, about 55,000 frames: desktop 22 and 130, iPhone 22, 58 and 130, Android 317.

- Flat-frame probe: 1,008 frames, 0 flat, 0 errors. **Pass.**

## Performance

| Run | Median | p95 | Max | Over 20 ms | Calls | Triangles |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Street, desktop | 8.3 | 9.6 | 10.4 | 0 | 95 | 327k |
| Street rush, desktop | 8.3 | 9.5 | 10.4 | 0 | 99 | 332k |

- p95 under 12 ms everywhere: **pass.** Headless Chromium caps at 120 Hz, so these show hitches, not GPU headroom.
- My long probe runs with the per-frame camera sampler showed one 108 to 126 ms frame each. Two clean reruns without the sampler show none (max 25 and 17 ms). It is my sampler's start-up, not the game.
- First load, production build (to a scratch folder): HTML 11 KB, CSS 39 KB, JS 831 KB (230 KB gzipped). About 0.88 MB. Type check clean. **Pass.**

## Biggest remaining gap

**Medals now count drops, not how well you fly.** A lazy 3-drop run scores 2,400 to 2,617. A skilled 2-drop street run scores 2,620 to 2,728. That is about the same. Both sit just under Silver (2,800). One city (31847) gives the street pilot Bronze in 3 of 3 runs. The best lazy run is 3 points below the worst street run. Skill still shows on the good cities (street 3,177 to 5,757). But the Silver line sits right on the step from 2 drops to 3.

Options for the builder (not a prescription):
- Let the fast-drop time bonus and the combo carry more of the skill gap. A lazy drop scrapes in. A street drop beats par by 4 to 9 s.
- Or set Silver where a 2-drop street run lands (about 2,500), and check that lazy 3-drop runs stay below it.
- Or pick jobs so that a street pilot fits 3 drops in a run on every city.

**Acceptance test.** 12 fresh cities, real time, one run at a time, with the street (low) bot and the lazy bot. Rerun any Bronze street city twice.
- Street Silver or better on 12 of 12.
- Lazy Bronze or below on 12 of 12.
- Best lazy at least 300 below worst street.
- On the same city, a lazy run with as many drops as the street run scores at least 25% less.
- The delivery share rules from this round still hold (strict at least 55% on the gate runs).

## Other gaps, ranked

1. **The first run teaches in a burst, and some hints come at the wrong time.** Eight introductions arrive in 34 s. One hides the first delivery pop. The wind hint shows at street level. The medal banner comes 6 s after its cause. Payout chimes play before anything explains them. Test: the early-feedback test above. A bot can check all of it except the human line.
2. **Run variety.** Every city has the same features in the same mix (round 24 item 1). **Needs a human player.**
3. **The roof line now equals the street line** (1.04) and earns almost no street bonus. If slipstream must matter, the street line needs some edge back. If not, make the meter and its hints simpler. **Design call, needs a human player.**
4. **At its 2.4 m floor, after a pickup beside a wall, the camera still lets the drone fill the phone screen** (`hud25-m-130-ov1.jpg`). The pickup pop's "Deliver for" pill sits on the "Fly" label there. Test: within 3 s of a pickup or drop, the drone box is under 40% of the phone screen height in 99% of samples. Pops on the "Fly" label: 0 samples. A bot can check this.
5. **Promenade from above** still reads as a red road with stop bars (round 24). **Needs a human eye.**

- Camera near walls: `camwall25-d-130-p20-y1.jpg`, `p40-y1.jpg` (drone on the pavement by a wall, framed fine).

builder.md
# Drone Dash: round 25 builder notes

Main concern: delivery is not yet the main reward, and the systems are not taught in layers. Leftovers: the camera squeezed against a wall after a delivery (A) and the phone route tag on the "Fly" label (B).

Bots played a production build of the working tree. My own `vite preview` served it on 127.0.0.1:5190. I rebuilt it between jobs (`builder-scripts/rebuild25.sh`), so code edits never reached a running page. The owner's server on 5188 was left alone. Every browser ran alone, one job at a time, from one queue (`builder-scripts/queue25.sh`, `jobs25.txt`). Scripts are the round 24 critic's, with only the output folder (`../builder-shots/`) and the port changed. New scripts: `teach-probe25.mjs` (hud-probe plus `teach-init25.js`) and `share25.py`.

## Design

### 1. Score shape: the delivery is the headline
- **Bigger drop payout.** Base 100 -> 200 points, 1.2 -> 2.4 points per metre of leg (`RUN.baseScore`, `RUN.perMetre`).
- **Fast-drop time bonus.** A fast drop paid a flat 75. It now pays 100 plus 15 per second under par, counted up to 8 s (`RUN.fastBonus`, `fastPerSec`, `fastSecCap`): 100 to 220 before the combo. A lazy flier scrapes in 0 to 3 s under par. A street pilot comes in 4 to 9 s under. I tried 80 + 25/s up to 12 s first: the roof line beats the street-route par by 6 to 11 s, so it overtook the street line (low/high 0.95). The cap of 8 s fixes that.
- **Rush order** 150 -> 200 (a delivery reward, paid with the drop).
- **Street bonus** banks a little less: `bankCarry` 1.15 -> 1.0, `bankPickup` 0.86 -> 0.74, `bankPerMetre` 5 -> 4.25, `bankLegMin` 150 -> 130 (about 14% less). Drafting still fills the meter, chains, refills boost, slows the clock and banks points exactly as before.
- **The delivery moment.** The pop now reads "+N delivered" with the time bonus and the street bonus as add-ons in the line under it: "+813 delivered / Fast drop +164 · +477 street bonus". The big number is only what the delivery itself pays. The pickup pop promises the drop: "Parcel secured! / Deliver for +543". The game-over breakdown keeps its rows (Deliveries, Fast drops, Rush orders, Combo bonus, Street bonus), so the two views stay separate.

### 2. Layered teaching (new player's first run)
- A **new player** has no saved progress. That means no `drone-dash-played-v1` flag, no best score and no medal. The flag is set when any run ends. Everyone else is **returning**: full HUD from the start, no hints.
- On the first run the HUD starts with the score, the clock, the objective pill and the pad marker. The fixed boost meter, telemetry, parcel count and pause button also show. CSS hides everything else until the game introduces it (`#app.teach:not(.l-<key>)` in `styles.css`). Their normal show/hide logic keeps running underneath, so nothing changes for returning players.
- `Game.updateTeach` notes the first time each system happens. It then queues the introduction. Nothing is introduced before 30 s. After 30 s, one system comes at a time, at least 4 s apart. When several wait, a fixed order applies (street bonus first). Each comes with one short hint in the event banner slot, which on a phone is the round 24 pop slot:

| Layer | Happens when | Shows | Hint |
|---|---|---|---|
| slip | first draft near a wall, or the first delivery | slipstream meter, banked bonus in the pill and by the score, payout pops | "Slipstream: Fly low by walls: bonus paid on delivery" |
| combo | first fast drop | combo chip | "Combo: Fast drops in a row raise the multiplier" |
| medal | first medal line crossed | medal goal chip, medal banners | the medal banner itself: "Bronze! First medal · next: Silver 2,800" |
| clock | first slow clock, after slip | slow clock badge | "Slow clock: Drafting toward the marker slows the clock" |
| route | second delivery | route arches in the world, the route hint pill, the gate tag | "Shortcuts: Arches mark alleys and tunnels" |
| view | first delivery | the camera hint (it used to show at 1.5 s) | its own line |
| wind | first high wind | wind chip | "High wind: Up high the wind slows you" |
| rush | rush hour (60 s) | rush tag in the pill | the Rush hour banner (no extra hint) |
| overtime | overtime starts | (timer look) | the Overtime banner |

- Before the slip layer is introduced, payouts bank quietly (no pop). Scoring is identical for new and returning players. Teaching only changes what is shown. The arches are hidden through a parent group (`gateRoot`), so the bots' route-mark hooks are unchanged.
- The old in-meter slipstream hint is off (the layer hint replaces it). `__THREE_GAME_DIAGNOSTICS__.teach` logs the introductions.

### 3A. Camera never squeezed onto the drone in open streets
`CameraRig`: two parts, both only outside alleys and tunnels (corridor weight under 0.05).
- **Swing** (`updateSwing`): this is for a slow drone (under 6 m/s, at or near a pad). The view straight behind it can have less than 2.6 m of clear room. Then the camera swings round the drone, at most 0.6 rad. It goes to the nearest angle with the full chase room, or else at least 3.2 m. It eases back after 0.9 s of a clear view. The sweep runs at most 10 times a second. A first version allowed up to 3.2 rad at any speed: it pulled the view off the heading and the roof-line bot (which steers by the camera) crashed more. Hence the speed and angle limits.
- **Floor** (`keepRoom`): after all other moves the camera is never closer than 2.4 m to the drone. With a clear line it keeps its direction from the drone. Without one, it rises over the drone, a little behind it.

### 3B. Phone route tag
`Game.gateTagPlace`: the tag's pill is kept fully on screen (its measured width, `Hud.gateTagSize`). On a touch screen the game tests its footprint (pill plus edge arrow) against the stick with its "Fly" label, the buttons, the top panels and a showing pop. On a hit, it walks the screen edge to the nearest free spot, as the pad marker does. The phone pop slot's right edge also moved from 72 to 100 px left of centre (hint and delivery pops reached a close drone's rotors).

## Numbers

"Delivery" counts only what the delivery itself pays: drop base, fast-drop time bonus (rush included), combo. The second view also counts the banked street bonus that is paid with a delivery. `share25.py` prints both.

Counting the street bonus paid with each drop as part of the delivery (view 2), every run is 99 to 100% (only a time-up share is not paid with a drop). View 2 is relabelling. View 1 is the honest test.
- Street line over roof line: **1.15** in total (pass, line 0.85). The street line wins on each seed too (22: 5,628 v 5,309, 58: 4,861 v 3,472, 130: 5,252 v 4,908). Round 24 was 1.45.

This is the cost of the shape: a slow, centred flier that delivers three parcels now earns most of what delivering pays. Per city the street bot is always well ahead (1,085 to 4,964).

## Open points
- **New player's first visible reward is at 15 to 22 s**, not under 10 s. Banked payouts are quiet before the slipstream layer. A fix to try: a shorter first pickup leg (`JOBS.first` 45 to 95 m of street), or let the first banked payout pop once with "+25 for your delivery".
- **City 52417**: the street bot makes two drops there. The best lazy run on another city (2,449) is above it. More fresh cities would show whether this is one city or the shape.
- Everything in the brief ran. Each bot set ran once on the final scoring (low, high, guards), so per-run noise of about one delivery is not averaged out.

critic.md
# Drone Dash: round 24 critic report

**Verdict:** The phone HUD gap is closed on all five phone runs, with no regressions. The route mark no longer changes its mind. Only polish remains in the HUD and the camera. The biggest gap left is game-level and needs a human player.

Build tested: commit d0ecc62 plus the uncommitted round 24 changes. My own dev server on port 5191, stopped at the end. The owner's server on 5188 was left alone. It is still running. Every browser ran alone, one at a time, from one job queue (`critic-scripts/queue24.sh`, `jobs24.txt`). I did not read the builder notes.

## Round 23 gap: phone HUD. Closed.

Probe: the builder's `hud-probe.mjs`, copied, with my own init script `hud-probe-init24c.js`. I checked that it measures the real thing. Every box is `getBoundingClientRect` of the visible element (the nav arrow, diamond and distance pill, not the 0-size wrapper). The drone box projects every visible drone vertex through the real render camera, view shift included. I drew that box onto the screenshots (`hud24-m-22-p60-y41.jpg`, `hud24-m-22-h08-end.jpg`): it hugs the drone. Sampled at 10 Hz while playing. 80 s per run: 50 s low street line, then 30 s at 40 m with boost.

| Run | Samples | 1. Marker on stick or button | 2. Drone under top pills (all / above 30 m) | 3. Pop on drone (of samples with a pop) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone 13, seed 22 | 795 | 0 | 0% / 0 of 83 | 0 of 183 (0%) |
| iPhone 13, seed 130 | 790 | 0 | 0.25% / 0 of 87 | 5 of 203 (2.5%) |
| iPhone 13, seed 130, 72 s at 40 m | 794 | 0 | 0% / 0 of 338 | 5 of 151 (3.3%) |
| Android 915x412, seed 317 (fresh) | 797 | 0 | 0.63% / 0 of 105 | 7 of 165 (4.2%) |
| Android 915x412, seed 22 | 793 | 0 | 0% / 0 of 84 | 3 of 188 (1.6%) |
| **All phone runs** | 3,969 | **0** | **0.18%**, 0 of 697 at height | **20 of 890 (2.2%)** |

- Test 1: **pass.** 0 of 3,962 samples with a marker. The marker also never touched the "Fly" label or the top panels on iPhone. It touched a top panel twice on Android.
- Test 2: **pass**, including 34 s in a row at 40 m. The 7 hits were all at 6 to 14 m, right after a delivery, with the camera squeezed against a wall. The drone then fills the screen (`hud24-a-317-ov2.jpg`, `hud24-m-130-ov1.jpg`).
- Test 3: **pass** on every run. The worst run is 4.2%, so there is little margin. Most hits come from the same moment: the camera is squeezed against a wall, and "Fast drop!" lands on a huge drone. The rest are the Rush hour and Overtime event pops on the narrow Android screen.
- Round 23 bad shot vs now, same moment on seed 130 at 40 m: `../round-23/critic/hud23b-m-h06-high-wind.jpg` (only the rotors show) vs `hud24-m-130-h06-high-wind.jpg` (drone clear below the route pill).
- Pops now sit left of the drone and above the stick (`hud24-m-22-h04-low-payout-pop.jpg`). That reads well. My check flags them against the top panels in up to 21% of iPhone samples. In the shots there is no visible overlap, so I think the centre column's box is wider than its pills. Not a fail.

**Phone view shift (player judgement).** It feels natural. The view moves about 50 px down at 40 m (max 86 px of 390). That shows more of the city ahead and the horizon, and less of what is right under and behind the drone. At height the drone now sits 40 to 60% down the screen in 92 to 99% of samples. At street level the shift is 0 most of the time. It does not hide road ahead. The shift eases in and out as you climb. A phone player must still judge how that feels (**needs a human player**).

### Small leftovers
- The route tag ("Gallery Tunnel 13 m") can run off the left edge and sit on the "Fly" label (`hud24-a-317-ov2.jpg`). The marker avoids the controls, but the route tag does not.
- When the drone sits low on screen, the look hint and the slipstream meter can overlap it. This happens in 1 to 7% of samples. Small.
- On the narrow Android screen the marker can sit in the gap between the score panel and the timer (`hud24-a-317-h04-low-payout-pop.jpg`). It is readable.

## Round 23 leftovers

**Promenade lane line: closed.** No centre line on the diagonals, desktop or phone (`prom-d-22-1-16m.jpg`, `prom-m-4-0-5m.jpg`, all `prom-*`). Only light stone bands across the red paving remain. As a look, from 16 m it still reads a bit like a wide red road with stop bars. No benches or planters. **Needs a human eye.**

**Route mark: closed in substance.** Sign bot, the same 12 round 20 cities, `route-sign24.mjs` (round 20 control, plus a log line per mark change). 86 legs (round 23: 97).

| | Round 23 | Round 24 | Per 100 legs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Re-plans (the old counter) | 18 | 15 | 18.6 to 17.4 |
| Drops before entry | 11 | 1 | 11.3 to 1.2 |
| Legs with more than one name | 6 | 7 | |

- Drops: **pass**, cut to a tenth.
- Re-plans: **fail as written**, only 7% fewer. But the per-change log shows that none of the 15 is the mark jumping from one alley to another. 3 are a mark at the start of a leg. 3 are a new mark after the drone finished a run. 9 are a mark that first appears 2 to 10 s into the leg. The old counter counts all of these. True changes of mind at the entrance (move or drop): 1 in 86 legs. I cannot split the round 23 number the same way.
- The 9 late marks are a small leftover: a shortcut that appears after you have set off. Low stakes.

**Lag on a real change of route.** I ran a grid bot that ignores the mark on the same 12 cities. In 84 legs, the mark had to give way 44 times. My clock starts at the drone's closest point to the marked entrance. Median: 2.5 s and 12 m. 90% within 3.4 s and 22 m. The worst was 8.8 s and 75 m, once. After you turn away, you still see the arch for about 2 s. That reads as "it noticed", not as lag. One worst case is long (**needs a human player**).

## Regressions

- Desktop HUD: all rects identical to round 23 (timer, objective, slip, wind, pause, telemetry). The view shift is 0 on desktop. Pops on desktop are still centred and cover the drone in 50% of pop samples, as before. **Unchanged.**
- Hand-fly first payout: desktop 5.4 s, iPhone 13 6.6 s. **Pass.**
- Flat-frame probe: 1,029 frames, 0 flat, 0 errors. **Pass.**
- Crash-classify, all 8 seeds: 12 m: 64 crashes in 695 s (5.5 a minute, round 23: 6.8 on 3 seeds), 13 near target, closest face 2.3 m below the top, **0 pad lips**. 20 m: 44 crashes in 683 s (3.9 a minute, round 23: 3.5), 16 near target, closest 2.2 m, **0 pad lips**. **Pass.**
- Low bot: 22: 4,347 Silver. 58: 2,407 Silver. 130: 3,716 Silver. **Total 10,470** (round 23: 12,421). Rerun: 58: 2,499, 130: 3,866 (total 10,712). The drop is one fewer delivery on 58 and 130. This bot does not read the mark or the marker. On seed 130, 3 deliveries is the norm (rounds 18 to 22). Round 23 got 4, once. Seed 58 alone went from 1,792 to 4,982 over rounds 12 to 23. Noise, not a regression. 0 crashes.
- High bot: 22: 2,446 Silver. 58: 3,014 Silver. 130: 1,755 Bronze. **Total 7,215** (round 23: about 7,080 after a rerun). 10 crashes, 1.9 a minute (round 23: 1.3). None were pad lips.
- No-delivery farm: 0 points on seeds 22, 58, 130, and 0 on smart-farm near. **Pass.**
- Van slipstream: the same 325 and 153 draft points on seeds 58 and 130. Capfarm van on 22: 2,814 Silver, the same as round 23. **Pass.**
- Traffic probe, 4 seeds, normal and rush: 0 car overlaps, 0 cars in solids, 0 people in solids, 0 people hit by cars, 0 on pads, 0 off lane. **Pass.**
- Breakdown exact (the bot's own check, sum and game-over screen) on all 8 bot runs. **Pass.**
- Camera tunnel test (round 23 `cam-clip` and `frame-check`, plus a phone run to test the view shift):

| Run | Tunnel frames | Camera at 2.5 m+ | Drone in frame (tunnel / all) | In solid / under / hidden | Max jump |

## Performance

Headless Chromium caps at 120 Hz, so these show hitches, not GPU headroom.

| Run | Median | p95 | Max | Over 20 ms | Calls | Triangles |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Street, desktop | 8.3 | 9.5 | 10.4 | 0 | 95 | 328k |

| Tunnels/alleys, iPhone 13 | 8.3 | 8.9 | 16.7 | 0 | 72 | 299k |

- p95 under 12 ms everywhere. **Pass.** One 25 ms frame in two phone runs, as in round 23.
- First load, production build: HTML 11 KB, CSS 39 KB, JS 824 KB (231 KB gzipped). About 0.87 MB. Type check clean. **Pass.**

## Whole game, as a player

The phone now plays cleanly. The stick, buttons and marker never fight. The drone stays clear of the top pills at any height, and pops land beside it. Camera, traffic and route marks are all steady. What is left in the HUD and camera is polish.

## Biggest remaining gap

**Delivery is not yet the main reward. The systems are not taught in layers.** Street bonus, chains, rush, overtime, the slow clock and medals all fire in the first two minutes. In the low bot runs, slipstream is 56% of the points (5,907 of 10,470). In the 80 s hand-fly on seed 22, the player banks 8 slipstream payouts and makes 1 delivery. A new player is likely to read this as a slipstream game with parcels on the side. **Needs a human player.**

**Acceptance test.** Three new players, each plays 3 runs on a phone with no explanation. Afterwards, each can say in one sentence what scores the most. At least 2 of 3 say "delivering parcels". Bot side: use the low and high bot runs on seeds 22, 58 and 130. Delivery points (drops, fast and combo) are at least 55% of the total. Apart from the first pickup, no new HUD element shows before 30 s.

## Other gaps, ranked

1. **Run variety.** Every city has the same features in the same mix. **Needs a human player.**
2. **Promenade still reads as a red road with stop bars from above.** Add benches, planters or a paving pattern along it. **Needs a human eye**, plus screenshots.
3. **The phone route tag ignores the controls.** It can sit off the left edge and on the "Fly" label (`hud24-a-317-ov2.jpg`). Test: the `#gate-tag` box overlaps the stick, its label or a button in 0 samples, and stays fully on screen. A bot can check this.
4. **Camera squeezed against a wall after a delivery.** The drone fills the screen, and the pop and top pills land on it (`hud24-m-130-ov1.jpg`). All the remaining HUD hits come from this. A bot can check this: camera within 2 m of the drone in open streets, 0 samples.
5. **Late route marks.** 9 in 86 legs show a shortcut 2 to 10 s after the leg starts. Desktop pops still cover the drone in half of the pop samples. Both small. A bot can check them.

builder.md
# Drone Dash: round 24 builder notes

Main concern: the phone HUD. Small leftovers: the promenade centre line (A) and route mark steadiness (B).

Own dev server on 127.0.0.1:5190, stopped at the end. The owner's server on 5188 was left alone. Every browser ran alone, one after the other.

Timing note: the Mac went to sleep during headless runs three times. Each time the clock jumped 30 to 90 minutes, and the run came back with few frames. Those runs were thrown away and run again. This used up a large part of the time box, so several regression checks were **not run** (see the end).

## Design

### 1. Drone clear of the top pills (touch only)
`Game.updateTouchFraming` runs after the camera rig each frame. On a touch screen it shifts the rendered view down with a projection offset (`camera.setViewOffset`). It moves just far enough to keep the drone's top edge 12 px below the centre column. The centre column holds the timer, objective and route pills. It never pushes the drone into the bottom meters, and it never moves more than a third of the screen. The offset engages fast and lets go slowly. The camera's position, its collision handling and the desktop view do not change. The pad marker, the gate tag and the probes all use the same projection matrix, so they stay consistent.

### 2. Pad marker never on the stick or buttons (touch only)
`Hud.touchLayout(w, h)` reads boxes from the DOM. It measures the stick with its "Fly" label, the buttons, the score panel, the centre column, the right chips and the meters. It measures every 300 ms, never every frame. `Game.navTouch` then tests the marker's real footprint against those boxes. The footprint covers the diamond and the distance pill. A clamped marker also adds the arrow's whole box, turned to its angle. While a centre pop shows, the pop slot is tested too. If the footprint hits a box, the marker walks the screen edge in both directions and takes the first free spot. The arrow then points from that spot to the target. On an iPhone 13 held sideways, a pad to the lower left now shows just right of the stick, not on it.

### 3. Centre pops off the drone (touch only)
On touch, all four centre pops (delivery/pickup/crash, payout, medal, event) share one slot. The slot sits left of the drone, between the score panel and the stick. Its right edge is 72 px left of the screen centre. Its left edge is the safe-area gutter. The HUD sets `--pop-x`, `--pop-y` and `--pop-w` from the measured layout. Long lines wrap inside the slot. Fonts are a little smaller on touch, and the payout pop rises less, so it never climbs into the score panel. Desktop CSS is unchanged.

### A. Promenade
The white-looking "lane line" came from emissive amber dashes (`#ffd27a`, `Style.emissive`), drawn where the diagonal crosses a road. They bloomed to near white. They are gone. Road crossings now get the same light stone bands as the block parts (`CityGenerator.ts`), so the diagonal has no centre line anywhere.

### B. Route mark hysteresis
In `Game.updateMark`:
- Inside the marked run (stage "through", in the run or within 10 m of its exit), the mark never moves or drops. Before, a neighbouring alley took over the mark at times.
- Otherwise the mark moves or drops only after one of two things. One: the planner disagrees with it for 2 s in a row (`MARK_COMMIT`). Two: the drone is 20 m further from the marked entrance than its closest point so far (`MARK_AWAY`). A single agreeing re-plan resets the count.

## Numbers

New probe: `builder-scripts/hud-probe.mjs` with `hud-probe-init.js`. It is hand-fly23 (low street line, then a straight line at 40 m), sampled at 10 Hz from the DOM. It reads the visible `.nav-arrow`, `.nav-diamond` and `#nav-distance` boxes, the stick and buttons, the timer, objective and route-hint pills, and the 4 pops. The drone box is new: `__GAME__.droneBox()` projects every visible drone vertex through the real render camera. The earlier world-AABB box was about 3x too big.

| Run | Samples | Marker on stick/buttons | Drone under pills (all / above 30 m) | Pop covers drone (of pop samples) | First payout | p95 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before, iPhone 13, seed 22 | 791 | **119** (15%) | **34.1%** / **89.2%** (74 of 83) | **90.9%** (170 of 187) | 5.3 s | 9.3 ms |
| After, iPhone 13, seed 22 | 644 | **0** | **0%** / **0%** (48 high samples) | **0%** (0 of 131) | 6.7 s | 9.3 ms |
| After, iPhone 13, seed 130 (40 s at 40 m) | 739 | **0** | **0%** / **0%** (104 high) | **1.4%** (2 of 141, event banner) | 5.5 s | 9.7 ms |
| After, Android 915x412, seed 22 | 696 | **0** | **0%** / **0%** (93 high) | **0.7%** (1 of 137) | 6.8 s | 9.6 ms |
| After, desktop 1280x720, seed 22 | | (touch only) | | | 5.8 s | 9.4 ms |

Acceptance 1 to 3: pass on all three phone runs. Max frame 16.7 ms on iPhone, one 158 ms hitch on Android. Logs: `before-m-22.log`, `after-m-22.log`, `after-m-130.log`, `after-a-22.log`, `after-d-22.log`.

Promenade (acceptance 4): `promenade24.mjs` (critic's script, port changed). `builder-shots/prom-d-22-*` and `prom-d-4-*` show stone bands across the diagonal and no centre dashes. The short white marks still visible at crossings are the cross road's own markings.

`npm run build`: pass. Type check clean. JS 824 KB (231 KB gzip), CSS 38.8 KB.

## Not run (time box, lost to the sleeping Mac)
- Route mark before/after per 100 legs (acceptance 5). The hysteresis is in, but it is **not measured**. Next step: run the critic's `route-sign20.mjs` against it.
- Phone runs on seed 22 and 130 ran once each. Promenade screenshots for the phone (`prom-m-*`) did not finish. Only desktop shots were taken.
- Flat-frame probe, crash-classify on 22/58/130, low and high bots, cam-clip and frame-check, and a side-by-side desktop HUD diff. Desktop code paths are untouched by the HUD work, because `touchLayout` returns null and the shift stays 0 without the `touch` class. The route mark change does affect desktop and bots.

## Screenshots (`builder-shots/`)
- Before, phone: `before-m-22-h04-low-payout-pop.jpg`, `before-m-22-h06-high-wind.jpg`, `before-m-22-h08-end.jpg`, `before-m-22-ov*.jpg`.
- After, phone: `after-m-22-h04-low-payout-pop.jpg` (pop left of the drone, marker beside the stick), `after-m-22-*`, `after-m-130-*`, `after-a-22-*`, `after-iphone-22-b-high.jpg` (60 m, drone below the pills).
- After, desktop: `after-d-22-*`. Promenade: `prom-d-*`.

## Files changed
- `src/game/Game.ts`: touch framing (`updateTouchFraming`) and touch marker placement (`navFootprint`, `navTouch`, a touch branch in `updateNav`).
- `src/game/Game.ts`: route mark hysteresis (`MARK_COMMIT`, `MARK_AWAY`, `markDisagree`, `markMinGate`) and the `droneBox` test hook.
- `src/ui/Hud.ts`: `isTouch`, `touchLayout`, `popShowing`, and the `Box` and `TouchLayout` types.
- `src/styles.css`: touch pop slot and its sizes, `slip-rise-touch`.
- `src/world/CityGenerator.ts`: diagonal dashes replaced by stone bands.
- `src/vite-env.d.ts`: `droneBox` in the debug API type.
- Bloom clamps in `ObjectiveMarker.ts` and the existing bot hooks are untouched.

# Drone Dash: round 23 critic report

**Verdict:** The tunnel camera is fixed and passes every acceptance line on four seeds, with and without orbit. Traffic density and the triangle count are fixed too. No regressions. The biggest gap left is the phone HUD, which still covers the pad marker and, at height, the drone.

Build tested: commit 7453512 plus the uncommitted round 23 changes. My own dev server on port 5191, stopped at the end. The owner's server on 5188 was left alone. Every browser ran alone, one at a time, from one job queue (`critic-scripts/queue23.sh`, `jobs23.txt`). I did not read the builder notes.

## Round 22 gap: tunnel camera. Closed.

I copied the round 22 scripts and changed only output folders. One addition: the per-frame sampler (`cam-sampler.js`) now also grabs the real render camera and projects the drone onto the screen. The round 22 "in frame" number guessed the camera aim. The new one is exact. Analysis: `cam-accept23.mjs`. Settled playing frames only.

| Run | Tunnel frames | Camera at 2.5 m or more (tunnel) | Drone in frame (tunnel + alley) | Camera in solid / under ground / drone hidden | Max jump per frame |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Seed 22, orbit | 3,465 | 99.7% | 98.1% | 0 / 0 / 0 | 1.70 m |
| Seed 22, no orbit | 3,465 | 100% | 99.9% | 0 / 0 / 0 | 1.15 m |
| Seed 130, orbit | 2,768 | 100% | 96.7% | 0 / 0 / 0 | 1.75 m |
| Seed 130, no orbit | 2,763 | 100% | 99.5% | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.29 m |
| Seed 44 (fresh), orbit | 3,468 | 100% | 97.9% | 0 / 0 / 0 | 1.70 m |
| Seed 44, no orbit | 3,464 | 100% | 100% | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.56 m |
| Seed 203 (fresh), orbit | 3,463 | 99.9% | 96.4% (tunnel alone 94.6%) | 0 / 0 / 0 | 1.12 m |
| Seed 203, no orbit | 3,463 | 99.8% | 99.7% | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.68 m |

- Needed: 95% at 2.5 m without orbit, 90% with orbit. Got 99.7 to 100%. **Pass.**
- Camera within 1.5 m of the drone: round 22 had 25 to 60%. Now 0 to 0.13%.
- Drone in frame at least 95%: **pass** on the combined number in all 8 runs. Seed 203 with orbit is 94.6% on tunnel frames alone. A near miss, not a fail of the test as written.
- No jump over 2 m: **pass**. The worst is 1.75 m (round 22: 12 m). The builder caps the step at 1.7 m per frame. A hard orbit into a wall can still slide the camera from 7 m to 2 m in 5 frames. I saw this once on seed 130 and once on 22. That is 40 ms here and about 80 ms at 60 Hz. It reads as a quick zoom, not a snap.
- Where the drone leaves the frame with orbit, it is one of two cases. The player pitched the view to its steepest (over 1.1 rad), and the drone sits on the bottom edge. Or the player swings sideways in a corridor. The camera stays on the tunnel axis, so the drone sits on the side edge (seed 203 Vault Tunnel, 100 frames). Both are mild.
- Ease-back still 1.13 s (drag), 0.89 s (trackpad), 1.1 s and 1.0 s (touch). Open-street desktop camera: max jump 1.12 m, 0 in solid. Unchanged.
- Looks right. In `dbg-22-organ-6.jpg` and `cam-clip-44-noorbit-1-tunnel.jpg` the camera sits low and centred under the bridge, the drone is clear, and the exit is in view. That is good tunnel framing.
- Script note: `cam-clip-22-5-tunnel.jpg` and `cam-clip-44-noorbit-3-tunnel.jpg` show no drone. That is the script, not the game. It takes the shot on a stale position right after a teleport. A real flight through the same tunnel (`dbg-22-organ-0..8.jpg`) is clean.

**Gaps between buildings (`gap-fly23.mjs`).** On seeds 22 and 44, every narrow gap at street level is a marked alley. So I flew the unmarked gaps at 8 m and 16 m (4 to 11 m wide), 10 passes per seed, with and without orbit. 0 frames in a solid. The camera was at 2.5 m or more and the drone in frame in 98 to 100% of every real pass. One exception: on seed 44 with orbit, at 8 m behind a pitched roof, the drone hid behind the roof and chimney (`gap-22-3-y8w5.5.jpg`). Pitched roofs have no full collider, so the camera does not see them as blockers. Minor. (One pass wedged the drone into a 0.9 m slot between two boxes where my script placed it. I discount it.)

**Arrival framing near low pads, no input (`arrival-metrics.mjs`, seeds 22 and 44).** 17 legs, 15 to street pads. The nav marker was off screen in 0.4% of final-approach samples (round 3 to 19 baseline: 1.2 to 2%). It still works. The one timeout is the known bot stall on a rooftop edge with the pad in plain view (`A-seed44-stall-final-approach.jpg`).

## Round 22 leftovers

- **Too few cars: closed.** Cars within 50 m of a street point: 5.8 normal, 7.3 to 7.4 in rush (round 22: 2.3 and 3.9). Seeds 130 and 44 match. Share of nearby cars standing still: 15 to 17% normal, 18 to 24% rush (round 22: about 25%). One soft spot: downtown in rush on seed 4 drops to 3.4 cars, as vans take over (`density23.log`).
- **Person on an active pad: closed.** 48 legs (24 pickups, 24 drops) on seeds 22, 58, 130, 44. 1,536 samples while hovering nearby, plus the trigger moment. 0 people on the pad by the game's count and by mine. People do walk close by (about 3 within 6 m). The street probe also shows 0 on pad on four seeds.
- **Triangles doubled: closed.** Street level 327k (round 22: 508k), rush 334k (651k). Phone 300k (438k). Draw calls rose a little: 95 desktop (83), 98 to 102 in rush (84), 79 phone (67). Fine.
- **Promenade looks like a road: not closed.** The diagonal is still red with a white dashed centre line, now partly lit, plus cross bands. No benches or planters. From 16 m it still reads as a red road with people walking down the middle (`prom-d-22-1-16m.jpg`, `prom-m-4-0-5m.jpg`, `hud23b-m-h06-high-wind.jpg`).

## Regressions

- Hand-fly first payout: desktop 5.7 s, iPhone 13 6.6 to 7.2 s. **Pass.**
- Flat-frame probe: 1,024 frames, 0 flat, 0 errors. **Pass.**
- Crash-classify, seeds 22, 58, 130: at 12 m, 22 crashes in 194 s (6.8 a minute, round 22: 6.4), 2 near the target, closest face 2.2 m below the top, **0 pad lips**. At 20 m, 13 crashes (3.5 a minute, round 22: 2.9), 4 near target, closest face 2.8 m below the top, **0 pad lips**. Pass. The small rise is within run-to-run noise.
- Low bot: 22: 4,463 Silver. 58: 2,923 Silver. 130: 5,035 Gold. **Total 12,421** (round 22: 11,426). 0 crashes.
- High bot: 22: 366 (two early crashes, run ended at 66 s). Rerun: 2,611 Silver. 58: 2,030 Silver. 130: 2,439 Silver. **Total 4,835, or 7,080 with the rerun** (round 22: 5,476). 6 crashes, 1.3 a minute (round 22: 2.3). The seed 22 drop is the known straight-line bot hitting towers. None were pad lips.
- No-delivery farm: 0 points on seeds 22, 58, 130, and 0 on smart-farm near. **Pass.**
- Van slipstream: draft works, the same 325 and 153 points on seeds 58 and 130. Capfarm van on 22: 2,814 Silver (round 22: 2,690). **Pass.**
- Traffic probe, four seeds, normal plus rush: 0 car overlaps, 0 cars in buildings, 0 off lane, 0 people in solids, 0 people touching cars, 0 people on roads. **Pass.**
- Breakdown exact (the bot's own check) on all 6 bot runs. **Pass.**

## Performance

Headless Chromium caps at 120 Hz, so these show hitches, not GPU headroom.

| Run | Median | p95 | Max | Over 20 ms | Calls | Triangles |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Street, desktop | 8.3 | 9.2 | 10.3 | 0 | 95 | 327k |
| Street rush, desktop | 8.3 | 9.3 | 10.4 | 0 | 98 | 334k |
| Street, iPhone 13 | 8.3 | 9.6 | 10.4 | 0 | 79 | 300k |
| Street rush, iPhone 13 | 8.3 | 9.7 | 25.1 | 1 | 81 | 304k |
| Tunnels/alleys route, desktop | 8.3 | 9.2 | 16.8 | 0 | 84 | 321k |

| Hand-fly 80 s, iPhone 13 (3 runs) | 8.3 | 9.6 to 10.1 | 17 to 25 | 0 to 1 | | |

- p95 under 12 ms everywhere. **Pass.** One 25 ms frame on the phone in two runs. Not the old 200 ms hitch.
- First load, production build: HTML 11 KB, CSS 38 KB, JS 819 KB (229 KB gzipped). About 0.87 MB. lil-gui loads only with `?debug`. Type check clean. **Pass.**

## Whole game, as a player

After rounds 21 to 23 the camera feels finished. Tunnels look great from behind. The street is busy and believable. Deliveries, rush orders and medals all fire.

**Phone HUD (re-checked).** Still the clearest problem on a phone:
- The edge arrow and distance for the pad sit on the Fly stick (`m-h04-low-payout-pop.jpg`) and under the climb button (`m-h08-end.jpg`). Open since round 20.
- At 30 to 40 m height the drone rides up into the top band and hides under the objective and route pills (`hud23b-m-h06-high-wind.jpg`: only the rotors show).
- Centre pops land on the drone. "Short job · no time bonus" and the slipstream meter cover it in `m-h08-end.jpg`. "+25 Banked", the look hint, the slipstream cue and two meters stack over the street in `m-h04-low-payout-pop.jpg`.
- The pop over the route pill happens 30 to 42 times per 80 s run (`hf23-mobile*.log`).
- The round 20 overlap sampler does not see the nav marker (its box is 0 by 0). So "0 marker overlaps" in older logs is not proof.

**Route mark (re-checked, sign bot, the same 12 round 20 cities).** Unchanged. 97 legs, 40 with a mark. The game re-planned the mark 18 times (round 20: 18), dropped it 11 times (8), and showed more than one name on 6 legs (8).

## Biggest remaining gap

**The phone HUD covers what the player steers by.** It covers the pad marker, and at height the drone itself. The phone is a target platform. A bot can see this gap on every run.

**Acceptance test.** Use an iPhone 13 held sideways. Run `hand-fly23.mjs` on seeds 22 and 130, plus a 40 m cruise on seed 130. Sample at 10 Hz. Use the visible child boxes of `#nav-marker`, not its 0-size wrapper. Use the drone's projected screen box.
1. The nav marker (diamond, arrow and distance) overlaps the stick, climb, dive or boost buttons in 0 samples.
2. The drone's screen box overlaps the objective pill, the route pill or the timer in under 2% of samples, including at 40 m.
3. A centre pop covers the drone's screen box in under 5% of the samples where a pop is showing.
4. Nothing else gets worse: first payout under 10 s, p95 under 12 ms, and the desktop HUD unchanged.

## Other gaps, ranked

1. **Delivery is not yet the main reward. The systems are not taught in layers.** Street bonus, chains, rush, overtime, the slow clock and medals all fire in the first two minutes. In a low run, slip is 2,400 of 4,463 points. **Needs a human player.**
2. **Route mark still changes its mind.** 18 re-plans and 11 drops in 97 legs. Test: 0 drops while inside the marked run, and at most 1 name per leg. A bot can check this.
3. **Promenade still reads as a road.** Remove the centre dashes or add benches and planters. **Needs a human eye**, plus screenshots.
4. **Run variety.** Every city now has the same features in the same mix. **Needs a human player.**
5. **Camera polish.** The drone can hide behind pitched roofs, which have no collider. With orbit inside a corridor it can sit on the screen edge (seed 203 tunnels 94.6% in frame). Steep look-down puts it on the bottom edge. Small. A bot can check this.

Only polish remains in the camera. The rest above is game-level.
