builder.md
# Drone Dash: round 23 builder notes

Main concern: in tunnel passes the chase camera came too close to the drone. Orbiting made it worse, and the camera snapped in by up to 12 m.
Small leftovers: thin traffic, the road-style line on the promenade, a person on a live pad, and the triangle count.

I used my own dev server on port 5190 and stopped it at the end. I did not touch the owner's server on 5188.
Every browser ran alone, from one queue (`builder-scripts/queue23.sh`, `jobs23.txt`).
The critic's scripts are copied into `builder-scripts/`. I changed only the port (5191 to 5190) and the output folders.
Screenshots go to `../builder-shots/`. The low bot's raw audio goes to `../builder/audio/raw/`.

## What really happened in the tunnel passes

`cam-clip.mjs` puts the drone 10 m before each feature, on the axis that the script detects.
On seeds 22 and 130, some "tunnel" passes detect the wrong axis.
Then the drone starts in a slot between two buildings next to the tunnel. The slot is 1.25 to 1.5 m wide (`solid-grid2.mjs` maps it).
The drone gets stuck in the slot and hovers there for the whole pass.
So most of the bad "tunnel" frames came from a camera behind a drone in a very narrow slot:
- The line-of-sight probe used a 0.5 m pad. In a 1.25 m slot it was blocked at once, and the camera fell to its 0.9 m minimum.
- An orbit turned the view into the slot walls. Then the camera snapped from 9 m to less than 1 m in one frame.

Real tunnels are 7 m wide and 7 m high. Without orbit they were mostly fine. With orbit, the same wall problem applied.

## Camera design (src/systems/CameraRig.ts)

1. **Aim at a view that the walls allow.** Before the camera follows its target point, a spherecast from the drone pulls that point in.
   So the camera moves in smoothly. Before, it was pulled in only after it was already behind a wall.
   If the line is blocked close to the drone, the rig tries small moves of the target point.
   It tries 0.3 to 1 m to the side and 1.5 m or 3 m up. It keeps the point with the most clear room.
   So the camera finds the gap and does not fall onto the drone.
2. **Thinner probe.** The pad is now 0.34 m (was 0.5 m). The last pull-in on the actual camera uses 0.2 m.
   The 0.3 m push-out still keeps the near plane out of walls.
3. **Orbit only as far as the view is clear.** During an orbit, the rig tests a row of angles (0.12 to 3.2 rad).
   The test starts straight behind the drone and goes out to the player's angle.
   It stops at the first angle with a blocked view. So the camera cannot go through a wall to get to an angle.
   On the open street nothing blocks the view, so the player's angle is used as before.
   The round 21 orbit, zoom and ease-back do not change.
   A held-back angle moves to its new limit smoothly (14/s in, 5/s out), and it handles the wrap at 180 degrees.
4. **Corridor framing in alleys and tunnels.** Game gives the straight alleys and tunnels to the rig as known bounds (`setCorridors`).
   The bounds come from `narrowRects`, and the bridge underside comes from the colliders.
   When the drone flies along a corridor, the framing applies inside it and 9 m before and after each mouth.
   It blends in at 3.2/s and out at 1.8/s.
   The camera stays on the corridor axis, 5.2 m behind the drone (4.2 to 6.6 m with zoom) and 1.6 m above it.
   It stays 1.15 m from each wall, 1 m under the bridge, and at least 3.6 m back along the axis.
   The orbit range in a corridor is 0.42 rad.
   The "lift" for a blocked view is off in a corridor. It raised the camera into the bridge, and then the camera had to snap back in.
5. **No snaps.** The camera moves at most 1.7 m relative to the drone in one frame.
   This limit is off while the camera is more than 18 m away, for example after a teleport or the title orbit.

Kept: the round 3 arrival framing (same code path), the round 21 controls and ease-back, the push-out, and all debug hooks.
New test hook: `camCorridors()`. New diagnostics: `camera.corridor`.

## Acceptance (critic's cam-clip.mjs and frame-check.mjs, unchanged, settled playing frames)

Numbers per kind come from `cam-accept.mjs`. It uses the same settled-frame rule and in-frame test as frame-check.mjs.

| Run | Tunnel frames | Camera at 2.5 m or more (tunnel) | Drone in frame (tunnel / alley) | Largest jump relative to drone | Inside solid / under ground / drone hidden |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Seed 22, orbit, 64 s | 3,459 | **99.2%** (need 90) | 95.9% / 99.0% | 1.70 m | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| Seed 22, no orbit | 3,464 | **100%** (need 95) | 99.8% / 100% | 0.26 m | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| Seed 130, orbit, 45 s | 2,771 | **100%** | 97.9% / 98.6% | 0.85 m (1.74 m alley) | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| Seed 130, no orbit | 2,771 | **100%** | 99.8% / 98.6% | 0.26 m | 0 / 0 / 0 |

Camera within 1.5 m of the drone (the critic's column):
- Seed 22 with orbit: 9 frames (was 1,723).
- Seed 130 with orbit: 0 (was 1,765).
- Seed 130 without orbit: 0 (was 696).

Jumps over 1 m: 13, 4, 0 and 0 (were 60, 25 and 0). Jumps over 2 m: 0 in all four runs.
Screenshots: `builder-shots/cam-clip-*-tunnel.jpg` and `cam-clip-*-alley.jpg`.

Orbit controls are the same as in round 22 (`cam-desktop.mjs`, `cam-touch.mjs`):
- Right-drag of 300 px: 94.5 degrees, ease-back 1.14 s. Tilt: 37.7 degrees, ease-back 1.14 s.

## Leftovers

**A. Traffic (src/world/Traffic.ts).**
Cars: 40 to 100 (rush 62 to 136). On mobile: 34 to 84 (rush 52 to 112).
The signal cycle is 12 s (was 18 s): 5 s green for each axis and 1 s all-red. So cars wait less at the stop line.
- Cars within 50 m (`density-probe.mjs`, 200 street points):
  - Seed 22: 2.33 to **6.10** (downtown 2.37 to 6.25). Rush: 3.71 to **7.96** (downtown 3.55 to 9.83).
  - Seed 4: 2.27 to **5.84**. Rush: 4.05 to **7.43**.
- Share of cars standing still (`street-probe.mjs`, speed below 0.5 m/s): 26 to 31% before. After: **15 to 17%** normal, 18 to 22% rush.
- Street probe on seeds 22, 130, 58 and 4 (40 s normal and 30 s rush): 0 car overlaps, 0 cars in buildings, 0 cars off lane.
  Also 0 people in solids, 0 people touching cars, 0 people on the live pad, 0 stuck cars.
- Cost: traffic takes 0.13 ms a frame (0.18 ms in rush). Before: 0.04 and 0.08 ms.

**B. Promenade (src/world/CityGenerator.ts).**
Where a boulevard crosses a block, people walk on it. There, light stone bands across the paving replace the amber centre dashes.
The amber dashes stay only where the boulevard crosses a road.
This change uses no city random numbers, so the layouts do not change.
Screenshots: `builder-shots/promenade-22-*.jpg` and `promenade-4-*.jpg`.

**C. Pad keep-out (src/world/Pedestrians.ts).**
When a pad lights up, the game finds walkers on it (pad radius plus 0.9 m).
These walkers move on along their loop to a point past the pad.
Last step: if a sidestep or a nudge puts a person within 0.15 m of the live pad, the person is pulled back.
If the person is still on the pad, the person is not drawn. The `padHidden` counter counts this.
`pad-probe.mjs` watched 36 live pads (12 pickups and drops each on seeds 130, 22 and 58).
It sampled every 0.1 s. Each pad was watched from the time it lit up to the end of its job.
Result: **0 people on a pad and 0 hidden**. No person came within the pad radius plus 1 m.
The critic's street probe also shows 0 people on the live pad on all 4 seeds.

**D. Triangles (src/world/StreetKit.ts, Traffic.ts, Pedestrians.ts).**
- The real cost: the six vehicle bodies were one merged mesh, and every car drew all six. The shader then hid five of them.
  Now each vehicle type has its own instanced mesh, and it draws only its own part of the shared buffer.
- LOD for cars: past 55 m, a car draws only its body and glass, and it casts no shadow.
- LOD for people: past 40 m, a person draws legs, arms, torso, head and hair cap (104 of 188 triangles).
- Both LODs use a shorter draw range on the same buffers, so they need no extra memory.
- I saw no popping near the drone. The switch is 40 to 55 m from the camera.

| Run | Triangles before (round 22) | After | Draw calls before / after | p95 after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Street level, desktop | 508k | **327k** (with 2.5 times the cars) | 83 / 95 | 9.5 ms |
| Same, rush | 651k | **332k** | 84 / 98 | 9.4 ms |
| Street level, iPhone 13 | 438k | **300k** | 67 / 79 | 9.8 ms |
| Same, rush | 567k | **303k** | 68 / 81 | 9.8 ms |
| perf18 route, desktop | 502k | **321k** | 73 / 84 | 9.0 ms |
| perf18 route, iPhone 13 | 439k | **299k** | 57 / 72 | 9.4 ms |

Draw calls go up by about 12: one mesh for each vehicle type and LOD, and one for far people. Headless Chromium caps at 120 Hz.

## Regressions

- Hand-fly first payout: desktop **5.7 s**, iPhone **6.6 s** (round 22: 5.6 s and 6.6 s). In the 80 s runs, p95 is 9.5 and 9.6 ms, with 0 frames over 20 ms.
- Flat-frame probe: 1,019 frames, **0 flat**, 0 errors.
- Crash-classify on seeds 22, 58 and 130:
  - 12 m: 21 charged crashes in 225 s (5.6 a minute, round 22: 6.4). 0 hop-like. 4 near the target. The closest face is 2.5 m below the top, so **0 pad lips**.
  - 20 m: 13 crashes (3.5 a minute, round 22: 2.9). 0 hop-like. 5 near the target. The closest face is 2.8 m below the top, so **0 pad lips**.
- Van slipstream (`van-draft.mjs`): the same as round 22. It banked 325 on seed 58 and 153 on seed 130.
- Low bot (`music-run-esc.mjs`, LINE=low): seed 22 4,294 Silver, seed 58 3,075 Silver, seed 130 4,036 Silver. **Total 11,405** (round 22: 11,426). 0 crashes. The breakdown equals the score in all 3 runs.
- High bot (`route-play-rt-x-m-esc17.mjs`): seed 22 3,371 Silver, seed 58 2,405 Silver, seed 130 1,547 Bronze. **Total 7,323** (round 22: 5,476, round 20: 5,966). 9 crashes (1.6 a minute, round 22: 2.3). The breakdown equals the score in all 3 runs.
  This total is higher than in round 22. Seed 58 did not stall this time. I did not change the flight or the scoring.
- `npm run build`: passes, type check clean. JS 819 KB (229 KB gzip), CSS 38 KB, HTML 11 KB.
- I did not change the bloom clamps in `src/entities/ObjectiveMarker.ts`. The debug hooks are unchanged, and I added `camCorridors`.

## Files changed

- `src/systems/CameraRig.ts`: corridor framing, clear-view aim with small moves, orbit held to the clear angle, thinner probe, step limit for each frame.
- `src/game/Game.ts`: camera corridors (`cameraCorridors()`), the `camCorridors` hook, `camera.corridor` diagnostics.
- `src/vite-env.d.ts`: types for the hook and the diagnostics.

- `src/world/StreetKit.ts`: vehicle parts sorted by type with far parts first, and ranges for each type. Far parts first for people too.

New builder scripts: `cam-accept.mjs` (acceptance numbers), `pad-probe.mjs`, `promenade-shots.mjs`, `cor-debug.mjs`, `solid-grid.mjs`, `solid-grid2.mjs`, `queue23.sh` and `jobs23.txt`.

  The drone is stuck there, so those frames test a slot, not the tunnel. The camera now handles both.

# Drone Dash: round 22 critic report

**Verdict:** Both rounds land. The orbit camera is smooth and easy on desktop and phone, and the street now has believable cars and lively people at no frame cost. One real gap remains: under tunnel bridges the camera crowds the drone, and orbiting makes it much worse.

Build tested: commit 49c3b2c plus the uncommitted round 21 and 22 changes. My own dev server on port 5191, stopped at the end. The owner's server on 5188 was left alone. Every browser ran alone, one at a time, from one job queue (`critic-scripts/queue22.sh`, `jobs22.txt`). I did not read the builder notes.

## Camera (round 21)

**Controls are easy to find.** The title lists "Right-drag or swipe look · scroll zoom" and the touch line adds "drag the screen to look". In play, a small hint fades in after about 2.5 s. On desktop it says "Right-drag or two-finger swipe to look around". On the phone it says "Drag the screen to look around".

**Desktop, real input in flight (`cam-desktop.mjs`):**
- Right-drag of 300 px swings the view 94 degrees. It eases back behind the drone 1.1 s after release, with no overshoot.
- Right-drag down tilts the view up to 38 degrees. Eases back in 1.1 s.
- Mouse wheel: 3 notches zoom the chase distance from 8.5 m to 13.8 m. 6 notches back gives 5.4 m. No orbit on a mouse wheel. The zoom is saved.
- Synthetic trackpad two-finger swipe (fractional pixel deltas): orbits 73 degrees, no zoom. A vertical-only swipe tilts 29 degrees and does not zoom. So the trackpad and mouse wheel are told apart correctly.
- Ctrl-pinch (real Ctrl plus wheel, and a synthetic ctrl wheel): zooms in and out, no orbit.
- Left-click boost: on within 18 ms, off on release. Left press during a right-drag also boosts and stops on release. Boost still feels right.
- Right-click opens no browser menu over the canvas.

**iPhone 13 held sideways, real CDP touch (`cam-touch.mjs`):** one finger holds the stick forward, a second finger drags empty screen.
- A 160 px drag orbits 69 degrees. The stick keeps flying at 15 m/s during the drag.
- Eases back in 1.1 s (yaw) and 1.0 s (tilt).
- Pressing Boost does not orbit. A drag that starts on the pickup pill does orbit (36 degrees). That is fine.
- 0 camera pops, 0 page errors.

**Clipping (`cam-clip.mjs`, `frame-check.mjs`).** Real-time flights through every alley and tunnel, with random real right-drags (held 92% of the time) and wheel zoom. Seed 22 for 64 s, seed 130 for 45 s, and seed 130 for 45 s with no orbit as the baseline. Settled frames only (the first 90 after each teleport are skipped).

| Run | Frames | Camera inside a solid | Under ground | Drone hidden by a solid | Camera within 1.5 m of drone | Pops over 1 m a frame |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Seed 22, orbit, 64 s | 6,925 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1,723 (25%) | 60 |
| Seed 130, orbit, 45 s | 4,850 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1,765 (36%) | 25 |
| Seed 130, no orbit, 45 s | 4,852 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 696 (14%) | 0 |

- **It never clips.** Not in walls, not in alleys, not under ground. The push-out works.
- **But it pays for that by crowding the drone in tunnels.** With no input, the camera sits within 1.5 m of the drone in 25% of tunnel frames. While orbiting, it is 39 to 60%. Then the drone fills the screen or leaves the frame (`cam-clip-130-5-tunnel.jpg`, `cam-clip-130-6-alley.jpg`, `cam-clip-22-5-tunnel.jpg`). In alleys it is 0% without orbit and 5 to 11% with orbit.
- **The pull-in snaps.** Orbiting toward a wall drops the camera from 9 m to 1 m in one frame (worst 12 m). 60 such pops in 64 s of heavy orbiting, none without orbit. See `cam-d-07-trackpad.jpg`: the drone was pushed into a wall and the view is all rotor.
- **Arrival framing:** I saw no fight with the round 3 framing. The approach framing fades out while the player steers and returns after the ease-back. I did not measure pad visibility in numbers this round.
- **Game over (minor, old):** the slow title and game-over orbit has no collision. In one run it sat inside a building for 118 frames.

## Street life (round 22)

**Measured (`street-probe.mjs`, deterministic, seeds 22, 4, 130, 58, 40 s normal plus 30 s rush, every 0.25 s):**
- Car overlaps: 0. Cars inside buildings: 0. Cars off their lane: 0.
- People inside solids: 0. People touching a car: 0. People in car lanes: 0 of about 400,000 samples.
- A person on the live pad: 1 sample on seed 130, then they walked off.
- About 25% of cars stand at stop lines at any time (40% in the frames I shot). Turns run on smooth arcs.
- 815 to 850 people per city, 290 to 400 drawn near the camera.

**How it looks.** Against good stylized indie city games:
- **Cars:** chunky low-poly sedans, taxis, vans and box trucks with wheels, windows and a body line. They read well from 2 m and from 24 m, and the paint fits each mood. At dusk the headlights glow and look good (`sl-d-4-e-rush-street.jpg`). The "looking basic" complaint is fixed.
- **People:** small blocky figures with a clear walk cycle, mixed shirt and trouser colours, kids among adults. At 30 m they read as people, not dots. They do not look like clones. The low pass is a highlight: people duck and throw their arms up (`sl-d-4-g-lowpass.jpg`, 4 reactions in one pass).
- **Too few cars.** From 200 random street points, a player has 2.3 cars within 50 m (1.7 to 2.3 downtown) and 3.9 in rush hour. With a quarter of them stopped, long avenues and junctions often look empty (`sl-d-4-c-street.jpg`, `sl-d-4-d-junction.jpg`, `sl-d-22-f-rush-cruise.jpg`). People are dense (22 to 34 within 30 m), so the street feels like a pedestrian zone with a few cars. A busy indie city shows a car every 15 to 30 m on a main road.
- **Boulevards read as roads.** People stroll on the red diagonal promenade, which has a dashed road-style centre line. From some angles they seem to walk down the middle of a road (`cam-d-07-trackpad.jpg`, `cam-m-03-drag-held.jpg`).
- No z-fighting seen. No pop-in seen at normal cruise heights. People are drawn within 105 m (82 m on phones), and at 45 m up the cutoff is not obvious.

## Performance

Headless Chromium caps at 120 Hz, so these numbers show hitches, not real GPU headroom.

| Run | Median | p95 | Max | Over 20 ms | Draw calls | Triangles |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Street level 4 m, busy avenue, 12 s, desktop | 8.3 | 9.7 | 10.4 | 0 | 83 | 508k |
| Same, rush hour, desktop | 8.3 | 9.7 | 10.4 | 0 | 84 | 651k |
| Street level, iPhone 13 | 8.3 | 9.7 | 10.4 | 0 | 67 | 438k |
| Same, rush hour, iPhone 13 | 8.3 | 9.7 | 10.3 | 0 | 68 | 567k |
| perf18 route (tunnels, alleys, diagonal), desktop | 8.3 | 9.0 | 10.3 | 0 | 73 | 502k |
| perf18 route, iPhone 13 | 8.3 | 9.3 | 25.0 | 1 | 57 | 439k |
| Hand-fly 80 s, desktop | 8.3 | 9.6 | 16.8 | 0 | | |
| Hand-fly 80 s, iPhone 13 | 8.3 | 9.5 | 16.6 | 0 | | |

- p95 is the same as round 20 (about 9.6 ms). Traffic costs 0.04 to 0.08 ms a frame. People cost 0.2 ms.
- The round 20 phone hitch (200 to 280 ms) is gone.
- **Triangles doubled:** 254k in round 20, now 500k, and 650k in rush hour. Draw calls barely moved. This is the one perf risk for a mid laptop or older phone, and headless cannot show it.
- First load, production build: HTML 11 KB, CSS 38 KB, JS 813 KB (226 KB gzipped). About 0.86 MB, far under 15 MB. lil-gui (31 KB) loads only with `?debug`. Type check clean.

## Regressions

Scripts are copies of the round 20 critic scripts in `critic-scripts/`. Only the server port (5188 to 5191) changed. Output goes to `../critic/`.

- **Hand-fly first payout:** desktop 5.6 s, iPhone 6.6 s. Pass.
- **Flat-frame probe:** 1,023 frames, 0 flat, 0 errors. Pass.
- **Crash-classify, seeds 22, 58, 130:** 12 m: 25 charged crashes in 233 s, 6.4 a minute (round 20: 6.5). 5 were near the target. The closest face was 2.2 m below the top. **0 pad lips**, 0 hop-like. 20 m: 11 crashes (2.9 a minute), 3 near the target, closest face 3.1 m below the top, **0 pad lips**. Pass.
- **Low bot:** 22: 4,483 Silver. 58: 2,778 Silver. 130: 4,165 Silver. **Total 11,426** (round 20: 10,769). 0 crashes.
- **High bot:** 22: 2,526 Silver. 58: 1,837 Bronze. 130: 1,113 Bronze. **Total 5,476** (round 20: 5,966). 11 crashes (2.3 a minute, round 20 was 1.0).
- **The high bot's seed 58 stall is the bot, not the game.** This time seed 58 reached 4 drops. Its crashes, and seed 130's, cluster 10 to 13 m from the target at 20 to 27 m height against a 29.5 m tower. The faces are 3 to 9 m below the top, so these are not pad lips. The bot flies a straight line at a fixed height and drops into the tower next to the pad. Then it bounces and tries the same line again. The low bot and crash-classify show nothing similar. Traffic flies no higher than the vans at about 3 m, so it cannot cause this.
- **No-delivery farm:** 0 on seeds 22, 58, 130 (farm-probe), and 0 on smart-farm near. Pass.
- **Van slipstream:** works. With rush on, a bot tailing a van 5 m behind at van height sets the van draft flag. It banked 325 and 153 points on seeds 58 and 130. The capfarm van run on 22 scored 2,690 Silver. Pass.
- **Breakdown exact, card equals score:** all 6 bot runs. Pass.
- Still open from round 20: on the phone the pad marker sits on the stick (`cam-m-03-drag-held.jpg`) and on the climb button (`sl-m-58-a-cruise24.jpg`).

## Biggest remaining gap in these three areas

**The camera crowds the drone under tunnel bridges, and orbit makes it worse.** It never clips. But under a bridge it sits within 1.5 m of the drone in a quarter of the frames with no input. While orbiting, it is up to 60%. It also snaps in by up to 12 m in one frame. Players meet this on every marked tunnel shortcut.

**Acceptance test** (rerun `cam-clip.mjs` and `frame-check.mjs`, seeds 22 and 130, with and without `NOORBIT=1`, settled playing frames):
1. Camera inside a solid, under ground, or with the drone hidden by a solid: 0 frames (unchanged).
2. In tunnel passes, the camera is at least 2.5 m from the drone in 95% of frames without orbit, and in 90% with random orbit.
3. The drone is inside the frame in at least 95% of tunnel and alley frames, with and without orbit.
4. No frame-to-frame camera jump over 2 m relative to the drone (now up to 12 m).
5. Desktop and touch ease-back stay at or under 1.3 s, and the open-street numbers in this report do not get worse.

## Other gaps, ranked (whole game)

1. **Too few cars on the street.** 2.3 cars within 50 m (3.9 in rush), about a quarter of them stopped. Aim for 6 or more within 50 m downtown. Traffic costs under 0.1 ms, so there is room. Check the triangle count while doing it.
2. **Triangle count doubled to 500k to 650k.** It is invisible headless. Test on a real mid laptop and an older phone before adding more cars or people. Use lower-detail cars and people beyond about 40 m.
3. **Phone HUD overlap is still open** from round 20: the pad marker sits on the stick and the climb button.
4. **The boulevard reads as a road with people in the middle.** Drop or soften the dashed centre line on the promenade. Or add benches or planters. Then it reads as a walkway.
5. **From round 20, still the larger game-level gaps:** a human playtest is overdue. Make delivery the main reward again. Teach the systems in layers.

- Camera, desktop: `cam-d-01-title.jpg` (controls), `cam-d-02-start-hint.jpg`, `cam-d-03-rightdrag-held.jpg` (good), `cam-d-04-drag-pitch.jpg`, `cam-d-05-wheel-out.jpg`, `cam-d-06-wheel-in.jpg`, `cam-d-07-trackpad.jpg` (bad: wall pull-in, drone fills the screen), `cam-d-08-pinch-in.jpg`, `cam-d-09-leftboost.jpg`.

- Camera in features: `cam-clip-130-5-tunnel.jpg` (bad: crowded under the bridge), `cam-clip-130-6-alley.jpg` (bad: drone out of frame), `cam-clip-22-5-tunnel.jpg`, `cam-clip-22-6-alley.jpg`, `cam-clip-22-10-alley.jpg`, `cam-clip-130-noorbit-*.jpg` (baseline).
- Street life, desktop, Rose dusk (seed 4) and Bright morning (seed 22): `sl-d-4-e-rush-street.jpg` (good: van, sedan, headlights), `sl-d-4-g-lowpass.jpg` (good: people react), `sl-d-4-a-cruise24.jpg`, `sl-d-4-b-high45.jpg`, `sl-d-4-c-street.jpg` and `sl-d-4-d-junction.jpg` (empty roads), `sl-d-22-c-street.jpg`, `sl-d-22-f-rush-cruise.jpg` (rush, no cars in view).

# Drone Dash: round 22 builder report (street life)

Concern: the owner said "the cars in the street are looking basic. also add some people walking." This round replaces every vehicle with procedural low-poly vehicles. They drive like traffic. It also adds people on the sidewalks and in the parks.

My own dev server ran on port 5190 and is now stopped. The owner's server on 5188 was not touched. Every browser ran alone, one at a time. No assets were generated or downloaded.

## What was there before

- `Environment.createCars`: 44 identical boxy cars (one InstancedMesh), random colours, each on a straight road line at a fixed speed, wrapping from edge to edge. They drove through each other at every junction (visible in `before-d-s22-normal-street.jpg`: a pink car inside a white one) and never stopped or turned.
- Round 18 hover-vans: 18 boxes plus a separate glow-pad mesh, at 3.1 m on the two rush lanes. Same-lane vans overtook through each other, and the two lanes' vans crossed through each other at their shared junction.
- No people.

## Part 1: vehicles

**Models** (`src/world/StreetKit.ts`). Side profiles extruded across the width give real silhouettes, not stacked boxes. Every type has a narrower glass house, body-colour roof and pillars, dark bumpers and sills, a chrome grille strip, wheels, and head and tail lamps.
- Compact hatchback (3.8 m) and sedan (4.5 m, three-box).
- Taxi: the sedan in taxi yellow, with a lit roof sign and a dark check band.
- Delivery van (5 m): tall, sloped nose, orange depot stripe like the Dash Depot.
- Box truck (6.3 m): cream cargo box with the orange band, six wheels.
- Hover-van (rush hour) is redesigned as a rounded pod with a wrap-around windscreen, an orange belly band and four glowing cyan hover pads on struts. It keeps its 3.1 m height and lanes.
- Mix: 30% compact, 25% sedan, 15% taxi, 17% van, 13% truck.
- Paint comes from a palette per light mood, taken from the city's own walls and awnings: warmer at golden hour, deeper at rose dusk, lighter at bright morning and hazy noon. Vans are mostly cream white.
- Glass is glossy and slightly metallic, so it reflects the baked sky environment. Head and tail lamps are emissive, scaled by mood: weak in daylight, strong at rose dusk (they bloom on desktop). If a car brakes or stands, its tail lamps get brighter. **There is no night mood in the game** (the four moods are golden hour, bright morning, rose dusk, hazy noon). I used rose dusk (seed 4) as the "night" case and did not add a mood.

**One draw call for all vehicles.** All six body types sit in one merged geometry (about 5,000 vertices). Each instance has a type, and the vertex shader collapses every vertex that is not its type to a point. A matching depth material does the same for the shadow pass. Lamp glow, glass and paint are per-vertex roles in that same material. So cars, taxis, vans, trucks and hover-vans together are 1 draw plus 1 shadow draw. Before, that was 5 (cars, vans, van glow, and two shadows).

**Driving** (`src/world/Traffic.ts`):
- Right-hand lanes 2.9 m off the centre line. I moved the painted stop lines to match. They were on the other side before, and the old cars ignored them.
- At each junction a car goes straight or turns right on a quarter arc (3.1 m radius). It turns left (8.9 m arc) only where nothing can come the other way (edge and corner junctions). It slows to 4.6 m/s (right) or 6.4 m/s (left) before the arc.
- Every junction has a two-phase signal (18 s cycle, offset per junction) with all-red gaps.
- Three checks come before a car enters a junction. Its axis must have green. No car from the other axis can still be in the box. Its whole length must fit past the exit. If a check fails, the car brakes to the stop line. Thus paths never cross.
- Each car keeps a gap to the car ahead (and to the tail of a car turning out of its lane). It accelerates at 2.6 m/s² and brakes at up to 7 m/s².
- Cars never leave the road grid, so they never touch buildings, alleys or tunnels.
- Rush hour: 40 cars normally, 62 at rush hour (34 / 52 on touch devices). Cars are added and removed only more than 70 m from the camera. The 18 hover-vans run on top.
- Hover-vans keep a gap to the van ahead. At the one point where the two rush lanes cross, they take turns: a van that must wait hovers before the crossing. If the van before it is not yet 9 m into the lane, a van waits.
- Truck height is 2.1 m and the hover-van pads' lowest point is 2.2 m, so ground traffic under a rush lane never touches a van.
- Unchanged: vehicles are still not colliders and crash rules are untouched. `vanDraft` (the round 19 slipstream rule) is the same code, moved into `Traffic`.

## Part 2: people

`src/world/Pedestrians.ts`:
- **Figures**: legs, shoes, hips, a tapered torso, arms with hands, neck, head and hair. That is about 330 vertices. Per person: shirt and trousers from palettes, 4 skin tones, 4 hair colours, height 0.92 to 1.08, and 7% children.
- **Walk cycle**: in the vertex shader. Legs and arms swing about the hip and shoulder, with a small bob and rotated normals. The phase follows distance walked, so feet match speed.
- **Where they walk**: two loops round every block's sidewalk, 1.75 m and 2.35 m in from the curb, one each way, so people keep right. Walkers keep a gap and queue behind someone who stops. Nobody walks through anybody on the same loop. There are 9 to 26 walkers a block: more downtown, and +6 next to parks. In parks, walkers go out and back along the four paths to the fountain. At build time, each loop is checked against all colliders, trees and lamp posts. If a loop touches one, it is dropped. On the seeds tried, 0 were dropped.
- **Standing**: at a corner, 30% of walkers stop for 1.5 to 5.5 s. They face the road, like people who wait to cross. The queue builds behind them. Some people stand beside shop doorsteps near the facade, facing out or toward the door. Others stand round the fountain. About 810 to 850 people per city in total.
- **Reaction**: the trigger is a drone pass within 6 m, below 7.5 m, at more than 8 m/s. The person stops, ducks and throws the arms up over the head. The head tips back to look up. The person steps up to 0.55 m away from the drone and stays on the sidewalk. It lasts 1.4 s, then a 2.5 s cooldown.
- **Pads**: walkers inside the live pickup or drop pad (+0.6 m) jog off it at 2.6 m/s and never pause there. Walkers about to step onto it turn round onto the other loop. Nobody is ever placed to stand on any pad.
- **Never in the way**: people are not colliders and are not in the crash logic.
- **Cost**: people are drawn and updated only within 105 m of the camera (82 m on touch). They fade out over the last 10 m. About 300 to 375 are drawn, in 1 draw call plus 1 shadow draw.

# Drone Dash: round 21 builder report (player camera control)

Concern: let the player move the chase camera with the mouse, the trackpad or a finger. Owner feedback from his own playtest.

Build: f52e1b9 plus the uncommitted round 20 and 21 changes. My own dev server ran on port 5190 and is now stopped. The owner's server on 5188 was not touched. Every browser ran alone, one at a time.

## Controls chosen, and why

| Device | Orbit | Zoom |
|---|---|---|
| Mouse | **Right-drag** (middle-drag works too) | Mouse wheel, 3 notches = full range |
| Mac trackpad | Two-finger swipe: sideways turns the view, up and down tilts it | Pinch (ctrl + wheel). Safari pinch gesture events too |
| Touch | One finger dragged on empty screen | (none) |

- **Left button stays boost.** I did not use "left-drag past a threshold". With that, boost starts on the press and stops once the drag is seen. That wastes boost and blips the FOV. Right-drag has no conflict. A left press during a right-drag still boosts, and releasing it stops boost. The browser menu is blocked on the canvas.
- **Telling a trackpad from a wheel.** Ctrl+wheel always means pinch. Line or page deltas (deltaMode 1 or 2) mean a mouse. Any sideways delta means a trackpad. Chrome and Safari give a trackpad away with wheelDeltaY = -3 x deltaY. A whole 120-step notch means a mouse. After that, fractional deltas mean trackpad, and small whole numbers under 40 px mean trackpad. Once a gesture reads as a trackpad, it stays on that path for 250 ms, so its inertia tail does not switch to zoom halfway.
- **Directions.** Drag right looks right. Drag up looks up. A trackpad swipe acts like scrolling the view: scrolling right looks right, and scrolling down looks down from higher up. To flip it, change one line in `InputController.ts`.
- **Release.** The view holds still for 0.4 s, then eases back behind the drone. It is within 2 degrees about 1.2 s after release. The view stays where it is for as long as the right button or the finger is down. This is true also with no pointer movement.
- **Flight stays relative to the drone.** It was drone-relative before. A/D and the stick turn the drone's own heading, and the camera never feeds the steering. So looking around never changes what the keys do. The orbit is an offset on top of the chase yaw, so it turns with the drone.
- **Limits.** Camera elevation over the drone stays between 3 and 69 degrees. So the camera never goes under the drone or over the top. Zoom runs from x0.64 to x1.73 of the chase distance (about 4 to 11 m). It is saved in localStorage (`drone-dash-cam-zoom`, try/catch) after 0.6 s of no zoom input. Each new run resets the orbit and keeps the zoom.
- **Free look toggle: not added.** C is already "descend". A sticky view also needs a HUD badge to explain it. Holding the right button or a finger already keeps the view.
- **Arrival framing.** With no view input, the round 3 pitch-down near low targets is unchanged. With no input, every camera formula is the same as before. While the player orbits, that framing blends out, then comes back as the orbit eases home.
- **Collision.** The existing pull-in (spherecast from the drone to the camera) now runs on the orbited position. The follow is tighter while orbiting (lag 6.5 to 16.5 per second), so the camera swings round the drone instead of cutting across it. New last step: `CollisionWorld.pushOutPoint` moves the camera out of any solid box grown by 0.3 m. This covers orbiting toward the wall the drone is hugging, near-plane grazes, and impact shake. The 0.8 m street floor clamp is still there.

## Hints (kept small)

- Title, desktop: one new chip, "Right-drag or swipe look · scroll zoom" (`d-00-title.jpg`). Touch title line: "... · drag the screen to look".
- First-run hint: on the first two runs on a device, a small pill above the right end of the bottom bar. Desktop: "Right-drag or two-finger swipe to look around". Touch: "Drag the screen to look around". It shows from 1.5 s to 7.5 s and hides the moment the player orbits or zooms. When the slipstream meter comes on, the pill moves up above the meter and its own hint, so they never overlap. Measured gap: 13 px on desktop and on iPhone (`d-08-…`, `m-08-…`). Nothing else was added to the HUD.

## Acceptance (scripts in `builder-scripts/`, logs next to them)

| Test | Result | Pass |
|---|---|---|
| Desktop right-drag 200 px (`orbit-desktop.mjs`) | Camera swung 63 degrees round the drone. It held there for 1.2 s while the button stayed down | Yes |
| Release back behind | Within 2 degrees at 1.30 s (0.5 degrees by 1.5 s) | Yes |
| Left click without movement | Boosts (meter 1.00 to 0.83), view yaw 0, boost ends on release | Yes |
| Left press during a right-drag | Boosts. Releasing left stops boost, and the orbit carries on | Yes |
| Context menu | 0 menus got through | Yes |
| Pitch limits | Drag up: 3.4 degrees (minimum). Drag down: 68.8. A huge drag clamps at 68.6, no flip | Yes |

Full held turn with the pitch rocking into both limits, at max and min zoom, then release. Checked every frame, including the moves between spots. **153,440 frames: 0 inside, 0 within 0.15 m (near plane), 0 below street** | Yes |

At low speed, the bots steer from the camera direction (`atan2(p - camera)`). With no orbit input the camera is unchanged, so this still works. Any future bot that orbits must steer from the new `player.yaw` instead (`orbit-fly.mjs` does).

## Files changed

- `src/core/InputController.ts`: `ViewIntent` and right/middle-drag orbit with pointer capture. Chorded-button boost and the context menu block. Wheel sorting (trackpad orbit, wheel zoom, pinch zoom) and Safari gesture pinch. Touch orbit on empty screen. `readView()`, `onView` and the test hook `injectView()`.
- `src/systems/CameraRig.ts`: smoothed orbit yaw and pitch offsets, the 0.4 s hold, then the ease home. Pitch clamp, and zoom with localStorage. Approach framing blended by `free`. Tighter follow while orbiting. The final push-out, `resetView()` and the `view` getter.
- `src/systems/CollisionWorld.ts`: `pushOutPoint()`.
- `src/game/Game.ts`: wires the view input into the camera, resets the orbit and arms the hint each run. Diagnostics: `camera.view`, `camera.behind` (yaw and elevation relative to straight behind), `player.yaw`, `player.boosting`. Hooks: `__GAME__.view()`, `insideSolid()`, `solidAt()`.
- `src/ui/Hud.ts`: `armViewHint()`, `viewUsed()`.

## Open points for the critic

- Sensitivities are guesses tuned on synthetic input: mouse 0.0055 rad/px, touch 0.0075, trackpad 0.0045, pinch 0.008 per px. Please try a real Mac trackpad by hand. Swipe direction and pinch speed are the likeliest to feel off.
- Max zoom-out (11 m) makes the drone small in narrow streets. It is the player's choice, but it could be capped lower.

critic.md
# Drone Dash: round 20 critic report

**Verdict:** The round 19 gap is mostly closed. Every marked alley or tunnel now has an arch with its name, and the HUD tag points at it from the first frame. The hint always matches the board. A bot that follows only the marks gains 9% on those legs, almost as much as a bot that knows the street map (12%). It misses the 15% line because shortcuts now save only about 10% of real time. Two checks fail narrowly: one fresh city gives the street pilot Bronze twice, and 5 of 28 marked legs do not show the arch itself within 3 s. Low over high passes at 1.81, but that now means the roof line is far too weak. After 20 rounds, the bot metrics tell us little that is new. The next step is a human playtest, not another tuning round.

Build tested: commit f52e1b9 plus the uncommitted round 20 changes. Dev server on port 5188, stopped at the end. Every browser ran alone, one at a time. The deterministic batch ran first, then a strict real-time queue.

Scripts are in `progress/round-20/critic-scripts/`. They are round 19 copies. Only the output folders changed: they write to the relative `../critic/`. I edited the absolute path in `legs18.py` and `legs19.py`. New this round:
- `route-sign20.mjs`: route-feat19 plus a sign-following bot and per-leg mark logging. The grid and shortcut bots keep their control.
- `legs20.py` and `rt20.py`: summaries.
- `overlap-init.js` and `hand-fly20.mjs`: hand-fly plus a 10 Hz HUD overlap sampler. Log-only.
- `det20.sh`, `rtqueue20.sh`, `rtjobs.txt`, `chain20.sh`: the run order.

Fresh cities, from a seeded random draw, checked against all earlier progress files and builder scripts: 30397, 67861, 71635, 73297, 18304, 20024, 41556, 38060, 21060, 15384, 20323, 55608.

## Part 1: acceptance test

### Route marks

The sign bot never sees the street graph. It flies the plain street grid to the street in front of the marked arch. Then it flies straight through to the exit arch, out to the street, and along the grid to the pad marker. If the game moves or drops the mark, it re-plans from the new mark or from the grid.

| Test (12 fresh cities, deterministic) | Needed | Result | Pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| Marked legs | | Grid bot run: 84 legs. 35 have an alley or tunnel on the shortest route. 28 are marked at the start | |
| Arch in view within 3 s, or by 80 m | every marked leg | Grid bot 23 of 28. Shortcut bot 34 of 36. Sign bot 25 of 25 | **No, near miss** |
| HUD tag on screen at leg start | | 0.0 s on every marked leg, all bots (in the frame or as the edge arrow) | Yes |
| Hint matches the world board, same instant | every leg | 55 of 55 legs with the pill visible: same name, same kind | Yes |
| Tunnel marked to a raised pad | 0 | 1 leg | Small fault |
| Sign bot faster than grid bot on marked legs | 15% | **9.2%** on 23 matched legs (307 s against 338 s) | **No** |
| Sign bot crashes | at most 0.5 a minute | 0.05 a minute overall. 0.20 a minute on marked legs | Yes |
| Shortcut bot gain on the same legs | report | 11.7% on 25 matched legs. 10.3% on legs with a 15% alley or tunnel cut | |

- **The 5 misses** all start next to the mark, 9 to 27 m away, with the arch behind or beside the camera. On three, the arch came into view at 3.05 to 3.55 s. On two tunnel legs it never did, because the grid bot flew another way. The edge arrow pointed at the arch from 0 s on all five. So the player is always told where to go. The arch itself is not always in view.
- **Unmarked legs.** The 7 unmarked alley legs save under 10 m or under 8%, as designed. Three legs that also take a boulevard get the "Fast lane" hint and no arch.
- **Do alleys still save real time?** Yes, but less. The street-graph bot is 8.5% faster than the grid bot over all legs. On marked legs it is 10 to 12% faster. In round 19 it was 24% on cut legs. The marks now skip alleys that save little. A fast pilot must also brake into the slot. The sign bot gains 9%, close to the graph bot. So the marks work. The shortcuts themselves are now worth about 10%.
- **The mark is not steady.** On 84 sign-bot legs, the game re-planned the mark 17 times. It dropped the mark 7 times before the bot reached the entrance. 8 legs showed more than one name. A typical case is city 30397. Two alleys lie in one column. The mark jumps between them. Then it vanishes while the drone is inside the first alley, and comes back as "Way out". A player who follows the sign sees it change its mind.
- **Shortcut bot crashes:** 0.33 a minute overall (8 in 1,460 s: 6 alley, 2 tunnel). Round 19 was 0.62. On marked legs alone it is 1.09 a minute. The alley exits are better but not fixed.
- **Deterministic scores:** grid bot 1,719 to 5,015 (Bronze on 38060 and 20323). Shortcut bot 2,459 to 8,782 (Gold on 4). Sign bot 2,189 to 4,391 (all Silver).

### Guards (real time, one run at a time)

| City | Street | Lazy |
|---|---|---|
| 30397 | 3,199 Silver | 976 none |
| 67861 | 3,214 Silver | 956 none |
| 71635 | 2,831 Silver | 683 none |
| 73297 | 2,910 Silver | 675 none |
| 18304 | 2,345 Silver | 851 none |
| 20024 | 4,917 Gold | 877 none |
| 41556 | 3,299 Silver | 1,021 Bronze |
| 38060 | 2,601 Silver | 682 none |
| 21060 | 3,624 Silver | 840 none |
| 15384 | 3,263 Silver | 867 none |
| 20323 | **1,767 Bronze**. Rerun 1,752 Bronze | 1,252 Bronze |
| 55608 | 2,275 Silver | 898 none |

- **Street Silver: 11 of 12. Fail.** City 20323 gives Bronze in both real-time runs and in the deterministic grid run (1,835). Its street bonus is low (655 to 679 points). This is a city effect, not machine load.
- Lazy Bronze or below: 12 of 12. Pass.
- No Ace: best score of anything is 8,782 (shortcut bot). Best real time is 4,917. Pass.
- Best lazy 1,252 against worst street 1,752: gap 500. Pass.

### Gates (seeds 22, 58, 130, real time)

| Run | 22 | 58 | 130 | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Low (music-run) | 3,867 Silver, 4 drops | 2,798 Silver, 3 | 4,104 Silver, 3 | 10,769 |
| High | 2,063 Silver, 5 drops | 1,519 Bronze, 3 | 2,384 Silver, 5 | 5,966 |

- **Low over high is 1.81.** It passes the 0.85 line. **But the roof line is now far too weak.** On 22 and 130 the high line delivers more parcels and scores about half as much. Street bonus is 53 to 65% of every low score. It is 6 to 13% of every high score. The ratio went from 0.78 to a reported 1.65 and now 1.81. The score now pays more for flying style than for delivering.
- **Carry farms.** The table gives points a minute against the honest run in the same controller.

| Farm | 22 | 58 | 130 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Old carry farm (60 s cap) | 0.35, 1 drop | 0, 0 drops | 0.32, 1 drop |
| Alley 12 s | **0.87**, 3 drops, Silver | 0.60 | 0.51, 2 drops, **Silver** |
| Alley 25 s | 0.21 | 0.20 | 0.15 |
| Tunnel 12 s | 0.61 | 0.64 | 0.45 |
| Tunnel 25 s | 0.33 | 0.24 | 0.32 |
| Van 12 s | 0.80 | **0.86** | 0.77 |
| Van 25 s | 0.54 | 0.61 | 0.69, 2 drops, **Silver** |

  The new stale rule kills long farms: the 25 s farms fell to 0.15 to 0.69. Short 12 s farms are unchanged at 0.45 to 0.87. Two runs with only 2 drops still reach Silver. No farm beats honest flying. Part 2 explains why the 12 s line is a weak test.
- One-delivery runs: all Bronze or below (best 1,112). Pass.
- No-delivery farms: 0 on every run (farm-probe on 22, 58, 130, farm-loop, smart-farm near and spendpickup). Pass.
- Breakdown exact, and the card matches the score, in all 31 real-time runs. Pass.
- Rush hour started at 60.0 s in every run that reached it. Pass.
- Overtime started and finished with a drop once (high line, 22). Pass.
- Saved medal: after a reload, the title best and tier equal the card on 22, 58 and 130. Pass.

### Regressions

- **Crash-classify at 12 m:** 611 s, **66 charged crashes (6.5 a minute, round 19: 4.6)**. 18 near the target. The closest face is 2.7 m below the wall top, so 0 pad lips. One rise of 1.3 m without climb (seed 58) hit a face 12.7 m below the top: a wall hit, not a lip.
- **Crash-classify at 20 m:** 676 s, 46 charged (round 19: 32), 11 near the target, faces 2.7 m or more below the top, 0 hop-like.
- Pass on pad lips. But the same blind bot hits about 40% more walls than in round 19. I did not find the cause. The arches are not colliders. This needs a builder check.
- Flat-frame probe: 991 frames, 0 flat, 0 errors. Pass.
- Music: chain 0 to 3 gives layers 1 to 4 on all 3 low runs. Mean intensity rises from 0.35 to 0.86. The final layer starts in the last 10 s. Pass.
- Hand-fly first payout: desktop **5.7 s**, mobile **6.7 s**. Pass.
- **iPhone pops against the meters: pass.** In 250 s of real touch play (two runs), no centre pop touched the slipstream meter, the boost meter or the cue line.
- **New iPhone overlaps.** At leg start the hint matters most, and centre pops sit on the route hint pill then (`long-m-ov1.jpg`). The sampler counted the pickup pop on it 54 times, the event pop 32, the medal pop 12. The pad marker, clamped to the bottom edge, sits on the slipstream meter. The gate tag, clamped to the right edge, slides under the Boost and up and down buttons (`long-m-ov3.jpg`). On the left edge the pad marker sits on the "FLY" stick label (`m-h04-low-payout-pop.jpg`). My sampler missed the edge markers. I found them in the screenshots.

## Part 2: a step back

### (a) Which bot metrics still mean something

Still worth tracking. Each one measures something a player meets directly:
- **No-delivery farm scores 0.** A real exploit test. A curious player will try circling for points.
- **First payout time.** It is how the first 10 seconds feel.
- **Crash classification near pads.** A crash you did not cause is the worst feeling in an arcade game.
- **Frame times, load size, flat frames, page errors.** Plain facts.
- **HUD overlap on a phone.** Plain facts. This round it caught the edge markers on the controls.
- **Breakdown exact, card equals score, saved medal.** Trust in the score.
- **Mark on screen, hint matches board.** These show that a sign exists. They do not show that a person reads it.

Now mostly noise, or tuned to the bots' own quirks:
- **Low over high.** It compares two scripted pilots: a grid bot at 7 m and a straight line at 40 m. No person flies either line. It uses three seeds, one run each, 3 to 5 drops a run. One extra drop moves a total by 10 to 20%. That is why it swung from 0.78 to 1.81. Tuning to it pushed the score toward style over deliveries.
- **Carry farm ratio at 12 s.** A 12 s detour through an alley looks the same as a slightly poor honest route. The ratio cannot fall far without punishing ordinary mistakes. It failed in several rounds because it measures the per-leg cap, not an exploit. No farm beat honest flying in any round since round 14.
- **Medal lines set by the grid bot.** The grid bot is one skill level that never learns. Whether Silver feels earned is a human question.
- **Shortcut gain and crash rate of my bots.** They measure my bots' cornering as much as the game. One braking rule made the sign bot crash about 5 times less than the graph bot on marked legs.
- **Single real-time runs.** Round 19 lost two guard runs to machine load. One run per city is a thin sample.

### (b) Would a human playtest teach more than another bot round?

Yes, clearly. The open questions are now about what a person sees and feels. No bot can answer them:
- Can a new player read an arch at 15 m/s and turn into it?
- Does the "Off route" rule feel fair, or like the game taking points for no reason?
- Do the many layers (street bonus, chain, bank, boost, combo, rush, overtime, stale, shortcuts, medals) read as one game or as noise?
- Does a delivery feel worth more than flying style? Today it is worth less.
- Is Silver on a first run too easy, about right, or out of reach?
- Do people press "Fly again"?

Five people, two runs each, with a screen recording and three questions afterwards, will teach more than five more bot rounds.

### (c) The whole game against the best indie arcade flying and delivery games

- **First 10 seconds:** strong. A pretty title, one key to start, a first payout in about 6 s.
- **Onboarding:** a weak point. Every system is explained by a text pop, and there are many systems. Good games of this kind teach one verb, then add the next. Here the first minute shows slipstream, banked bonus, chain, combo, shortcut, clock frozen and rush hour.
- **Core loop:** pick up, thread the streets, drop. Sound. But the score now pays more for style than for the job. The best games keep the job as the main reward and style as the bonus.
- **Game feel:** the best part. Wall-hugging draft in narrow streets and alleys is a real hook. Braking into a slot and bursting out feels good.
- **Art:** a warm, cohesive low-poly city with good light. The arches read well. This is at the level of a good indie game.
- **Audio:** adaptive music that climbs with the chain, and a clear medal fanfare. Good.
- **UI:** clean on desktop. Busy on a phone. Two pills, a tag, a pad marker, two meters, a cue line and touch controls share a small screen. The edge markers now land on the controls.
- **Difficulty curve:** flat. Rush hour at 60 s is the only step, and every run is about the same length. The best games ramp inside a run (more traffic, tighter windows) and across runs (new districts, new drones).
- **Run variety:** random cities and a daily city. But every city plays alike: a grid, some alleys, a boulevard, the same jobs.
- **Replay pull:** medals, a daily best and a real score ceiling. But nothing unlocks and nothing carries over. The best games give a reason for the next run beyond a number.

Overall, the moment-to-moment flying is close to the bar. Structure, onboarding and progression are well below it. The scoring is now tuned past the point where tuning helps.

### Next steps, ranked

1. **Freeze scoring and balance, and run a human playtest:** 5 players, 2 runs each, desktop and phone. Needs a human.
2. **Make delivery the main reward again.** Keep the street bonus well under half of a run's score, so the drop count leads. Judge by feel, not by low over high. Needs a human to judge.
3. **Teach in layers.** The first run shows only fly, pick up, drop and the clock. Slipstream comes on the second leg, shortcuts on the third, rush on run two. Needs a human to judge.
4. **Fix the phone HUD.** Keep the edge markers clear of the meters and touch buttons. Keep centre pops off the hint pill. A bot can check this.
5. **Steady the route mark.** No jump between neighbour alleys, and no drop while inside the marked run. A bot can check this.
6. **Give runs a reason to differ.** One or two of: districts with their own rules, a traffic ramp inside the run, a goal list or unlocks. Needs a human to judge the fun.
7. **Check two regressions:** 40% more crash-classify wall hits, and a 200 to 280 ms hitch on phones. A bot can check these.

## Performance

Headless Chromium caps at 120 Hz.
- Flight through 2 tunnels, 2 alleys and a boulevard (`perf18.mjs`, 12.5 s). Desktop: 1,499 frames, median 8.3 ms, p95 9.2, max 16.7, 0 over 20 ms, 74 draw calls, 254k triangles. iPhone 13 (wide view): median 8.3, p95 9.4, max 16.4, 0 over 20 ms, 58 draw calls.
- Hand-fly 80 s, desktop: 9,570 frames, median 8.3, p95 9.6, max 17.2, 0 over 20 ms.
- Hand-fly 80 s, mobile: 9,544 frames, median 8.3, p95 9.6, **max 283 ms**, 2 over 20 ms. The long mobile run had max 208 ms, 1 over 20 ms. Round 19 max was 24.7 ms. One long hitch per mobile run is new. My guess is the first board texture or arch build.
- First load, production build: about 0.83 MB. JS 778 KB (214 KB gzipped), CSS 37 KB, HTML 11 KB. lil-gui (31 KB) loads only with `?debug`. Type check clean. Page errors 0.

## Order and load

The deterministic batch ran 09:52 to 10:00, one browser at a time. The real-time queue ran 10:00 to 11:02, one job at a time, with nothing else of mine running. Machine load from other processes was 3 to 5 on 10 cores.

# Drone Dash, round 20 builder: the suggested route marked in the world

Time box: 07:23 to 09:53. Scripts: `progress/round-20/builder-scripts/`. The critic's round 19 scripts are copied there. Only the output folder (`../builder-shots/`) and the log path in `legs18.py` and `legs19.py` changed. Logs: `progress/round-20/builder/`. Shots (JPEG): `progress/round-20/builder-shots/`.

## Short version

- The marks are in. The marked alley or tunnel gets an arch in the objective colour. A board on the arch shows the feature's name. The far mouth gets a plain arch. A HUD tag leads to the entrance, then to the way out. After that, the pad marker leads.
- The hint names exactly the board's text: 59 of 59 marked legs.
- Leftover B: farming now earns nothing more than holding still. But the farm ratios stay over 0.5, and one 2-drop farm reaches Silver (section 4).
- Leftover C: the shortcut bot crashes 0.16 times a minute.
- Leftover D: the centre pops stay clear of the meters.
- Leftover A: low over high is 1.65 in real time on the final code (needed 0.85). The low line reached Gold on seed 22.
- **The main speed test fails.** A bot that follows only the marks is 3.7% slower than the grid bot. The target is 15% faster. The critic's shortcut bot uses the full street graph. It is only 5.3% faster on the same legs.

## 1. Leftovers

### A. Low over high

- **Cause.** I ran the round 19 code with the job picker switches on and off (deterministic). The tune hook now also takes `JOBS`.
  - Round 19 as it is: low 8,586, high 9,066 (0.95).
  - No `narrowBias` (no alley-line pads first): low 8,739, high 7,849.
  - No shortcut bias at all: low 8,934, high 10,583.
- So the gain came from the round 19 alley-line legs. These go from a mouth pad to a mouth pad on one straight line. The roof line flies them straight. The street line must go round the block.
- The tunnel slow clock and the vans do not help the roof line. Its slow clock is 3 to 6 s a run, and it never tails vans.
- **Fix.** The street bonus banks 15% more: `SLIPSTREAM.bankCarry` 1 to 1.15 and `bankPickup` 0.75 to 0.86. The street line earns most of the street bonus (1,500 to 2,000 a run). The roof line earns 200 to 400. Flight and headwind did not change, so the roof line is as fast as in round 17.
- This is safe for farming only because of the fix for B.

### B. Carry farms

- **Cause.** A payout banked its full value, whatever the drone did. Shuttling in a tunnel, circling an alley or tailing a van filled the leg cap.
- **Fix: a parcel must go somewhere.**
  - Four times a second, the game measures the route left to the objective. It uses the street graph and the plain grid, plus any climb.
  - Each payout banks by the progress made while the meter filled. The measure is route metres gained divided by metres flown. At 0.4 or more, the payout banks in full (`bankProgress`).
  - When neither route gets 2 m shorter in 5 s, the parcel goes stale (`staleStep`, `staleAfter`). Then payouts bank 0 and the slow clock stops. So the tunnel's slow clock does not count while farming. The bank also fades by 20% a second (`staleDrain`).
  - Within 25 m of the pad, a parcel never goes stale (`staleNear`). Landing is not farming.
  - HUD: the cue "Off route · bonus fading" and the payout pop "Off route".
  - The leg cap is now 5 points per metre of route, not 7 (`bankPerMetre`).
- **Honest flying is not hit.** I switched the new rules off for the grid bot on two cities. The scores did not change: 16541 1,743 both times, 72537 1,200 both times. The deterministic grid bot went stale once in 12 cities and lost 0 points.

### C. Shortcut bot crashes

- The round 19 crash list shows most hits at an alley mouth, at 14 to 16 m/s. The bot turned into or out of the slot. Some hits were not near a mouth pad.
- Two changes in the final code:
  - Alleys are 7 m wide, not 6 m (`ALLEY_WIDTH`).
  - A doorstep beside a mouth now sits 2.4 m from the lot's outer corner (`MOUTH_PAD`). That is about 7 m from the alley wall. It was 2.2 m from the wall.
- I also tried a deeper mouth setback (2.5 m, `MOUTH_SET`). It set back whole street faces, so the street draft got weaker. The grid bot fell to Bronze on 3 cities (16541: 1,743, with 1.5 m: 2,642. 74215: 1,970 against 2,800. 48251: 2,168 against 2,716). I put it back to 1.5 m.
- Result on the final code: the critic's shortcut bot (`route-sign20.mjs FEAT=1`, control unchanged) on 12 fresh cities: **4 charged crashes in 1,489 s, 0.16 a minute** (round 19: 0.62). Kinds: 3 alley, 1 tunnel.

### D. iPhone pops over the meters

- On a short screen, the centre slot is higher. The pop moved from 62% to 50% of the height. The banner and medal moved from 58% to 47%. The payout pop moved from 57% to 47%.
- Static check at peak size, iPhone 13 sideways (`pop-rects.mjs`): 0 overlaps with the slipstream meter, its cue, the boost meter, the route hint and the objective pill.
- The nav marker now stops at 140 px from the top on a phone (150 on desktop). It was 120 and covered the hint pill. The gate tag uses the same limit.
- Fault found late: on a phone the edge **arrow** of the nav marker still reached 46 px up into the hint pill (shot K-m-seed22-arch). I fixed the limit to leave room for the arrow. This fix was built after the real-time queue (see section 5).

## 2. Main concern: the route on screen

### Design

- **Which legs get a mark.** At the start of a leg, the game takes the shortest street route. The game also finds the best route that stays out of alleys and tunnels (boulevards allowed). When the route through an alley or tunnel saves at least 10 m and 8%, that run gets a mark. An alley that saves almost nothing gets no mark and no name. (In round 19, the hint named those too.)
- **In the world** (`src/entities/RouteGate.ts`). Drawn only, no collider.
  - An arch over the entrance mouth, in the objective colour: amber for a pickup, teal for a drop.
  - The posts stand just outside the slot. The arch does not make the slot narrower.
  - A dark board with the feature's name sits above the beam.
  - A chevron moves up and down above the arch at 14 m. You can see it over traffic and from down the street.
  - The far mouth gets a plain arch that pulses: the way out.
  - Plain colours at normal brightness. The bloom clamps in `ObjectiveMarker.ts` did not change.
- **On the HUD.** A tag with an arch icon, the name and the distance sits over the board. When the arch is off screen, the tag stays at the screen edge with an arrow, like the pad marker. After the entrance, the tag says "Way out" and points at the far arch. After the run, the tag and the arches go, and the pad marker leads. The pad marker did not change. A pilot who ignores the marks flies as before.
- **Hint and board match.** The hint names only the marked feature. The label is "Shortcut" for an alley and "Tunnel" for a tunnel. When there is no mark and the route takes a boulevard, the hint names the boulevard. Otherwise it names nothing.
- **Re-plan.** Four times a second, the game plans again from the drone. If the pilot goes another way, the mark moves to the new route's alley or tunnel, and the hint gets the new name. If the new route has no alley or tunnel, the mark and the hint go away. A mark stays while its run saves at least half the limit. So it does not flicker.
- **Diagnostics.** `routeMark` gives the kind, the names, the stage (entrance or through), the gate and exit positions and directions, and the width. It also gives the leg start, the time the HUD tag showed, the first time the arch came into view (and the distance then), and the board text. `progress` gives the route left, stall seconds, stale state, stale points lost and the stale count.

### Acceptance (12 fresh cities, deterministic)

Scripts: `route-sign20.mjs` and `legs20.py`. Output: `builder/legs20.out`.

Fresh cities (random loads with `pick-seeds.mjs`): 72692, 72834, 50400, 50160, 16541, 74215, 48251, 72537, 63888, 26829, 32548, 38954.

| Test | Needed | Result | Pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| Marked legs | | 29 of 92 grid-bot legs, 0 to 5 a city | |
| Hint label = world board = feature name | every case | 29 of 29 (grid bot), 30 of 30 (sign bot) | Yes |
| HUD tag on screen at the leg start | within 3 s | 28 of 29 at 0.0 s. The other one is a mark that changed in the leg | Mostly |
| Arch in view within 3 s or by 80 m | every mark | Grid bot 28 of 29. Sign bot 28 of 30 (median 1.4 s, max 3.5 s). Misses: legs that start 19 to 21 m from the arch with the camera facing away | No, 3 misses |
| Sign bot faster than the grid bot on marked legs | 15% | 23 matched legs: 347.3 s against 334.9 s, **3.7% slower** | **No** |
| Sign bot crashes | at most 0.5 a minute | 6 in 1,334 s, 0.27 a minute | Yes |

These numbers are from the final code (dev server on port 5189, logs in `builder/detF/`). An earlier build gave the same picture: 0.8% faster.

**The sign bot** (`route-sign20.mjs FEAT=2`) has no street graph. It flies the plain grid (roads every 44 m), as the grid bot does. It goes to the road in front of the marked arch (`routeMark.gate`). Then it flies through the alley to the exit arch. Then it flies the grid to the pad marker. When the mark changes, it plans again. It uses the critic's shortcut bot control. One change: it does not brake at a stop that is in line with its path.

**Why the sign bot is not faster.** On these legs, the alley saves 10 to 40% of the distance. The sign bot flies about 15% less. But it is slower per metre:
- it brakes to 7 m/s for the 90-degree turn at the mouth,
- it drops to 5 m in alleys, and to 3.5 m in tunnels (at 4 m/s while above 6.5 m),
- it seldom boosts, while the grid bot boosts on long straight streets.

The critic's shortcut bot uses the full street graph. On the same marked legs (25), it is only 5.3% faster. So the marks lead the bot onto the shortcut (it went through the marked entrance on 25 of 30 legs). But with this control, an alley gives almost no time. A human who keeps speed through the slot gains more, but I did not measure that.

## 3. Shots

- K-d-seed22-start, K-d-seed22-arch, K-m-seed22-start, K-m-seed22-arch: arch, board, tag and hint, on desktop and on an iPhone 13 held sideways. The arch shots are 12 to 30 m in front of the mouth.
- T-sign-seed*: the sign bot in marked alleys and tunnels.

All real-time runs were one at a time, on the frozen production build (`vite preview` on port 5188, so no source edit could reload a page mid-run). A deterministic batch (one process, nice 19) ran beside the street guard on a second server; the load stayed at 4 to 7 on 10 cores.

|---|---|
| 72692 | 3,561 Silver |
| 72834 | 3,978 Silver |
| 50400 | 3,340 Silver |
| 50160 | 4,474 Silver |

- Lazy guard: **not run** on the final code (time box). So "lazy Bronze or below" and "best lazy 300 below the worst street" are not measured.

### Gates (seeds 22, 58, 130)

| Run | 22 | 58 | 130 | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Low, real time, final code (`music-run-esc`) | 4,524 Gold, 4 drops | 3,388 Silver, 4 | 3,937 Silver, 3 | 11,849 |

- The high bot's roof-edge stall (round 18 and 19 critics saw it on 130) now shows on 22 on some runs. It hovers over a roof 6 m from a street pad and pushes down. I did not change the high bot.

### Farms (deterministic, final code, `farms20.py`, `builder/farmsF/`)

Ratio = sum of farm points a minute over sum of honest points a minute (honest = capfarm honest: 3,969, 3,435, 3,843). Null farm = same trigger and farm time, but the drone holds still.

| Farm (12 s farm phases) | Ratio | Null farm ratio |
|---|---|---|
| Tunnel shuttle | 0.56 | 0.56 |
| Alley shuttle | 0.65 | 0.58 |
| Van tailing | 0.81 | 0.78 |

- Shuttling in a tunnel scores the same as holding still in it (seed 22: 1,389 both). Tailing a van scores about the same as hovering. So a farm phase now earns nothing. What is left is the cost of the lost time: these farms fly honestly between phases.
- **The 0.5 line is not met.** A farm that wastes 12 s a leg and earns nothing still scores 0.55 to 0.8 of an honest run, because the rest of the run is honest flying. Getting under 0.5 would mean punishing a pause more than its time. I did not do that.
- 2-drop farms at Silver: alley farm on 130 (2,161) and the null alley farm on 130 (2,198). Holding still gives the same, so the Silver comes from the two honest drops, not from farming. Still, the line as written fails.
- No-delivery farms (farm-probe 22/58/130, farm-loop 22, smart-farm near 22, pickupline 130): all **0** (earlier build, same bank rules).
- One-delivery farms (capfarm both, 12 s): 792, 890 and 0. Bronze or below.

### Regressions (deterministic, final code)

- Crash-classify, 8 seeds. 12 m: 643 s, 55 charged crashes, 14 near the target, all on faces 7 to 33 m above the pad: **0 pad lip**. The summary counts 1 hop-like rise; every rise I listed had climb held, so I did not find it. 20 m: 670 s, 37 charged, 0 hop-like, 14 near the target on faces 3.4 to 33 m above the pad: 0 pad lip.
- Pad audit, 30 seeds: 2,772 pads, **0 issues**, 0 in an alley strip.
- Phone pops at peak size: 0 overlaps (static check above). The real-time phone probe (`hud-overlap20.mjs`) did **not run** (time box).
- **Not run on the final code:** flat-frame probe, music, hand-fly, perf. On this round's code they were queued last and cut. The production build is 0.83 MB at first load (JS 778 KB, CSS 37 KB, HTML 11 KB), far under 15 MB. `npm run build` passes.

# Drone Dash: round 19 critic report

**Verdict:** The round 18 gap is closed on route variety and naming: alleys and tunnels now decide the route on most legs and every real shortcut is named at the leg start. But the name points at nothing a player can find. No alley or tunnel shows its name in the world and there is no map, so the hint says "a shortcut exists" without saying where. One gate also fails: the high line now beats the street line (low over high 0.78).

Build tested: working tree on commit 38a35fa plus the uncommitted round 19 changes. Dev server port 5188, stopped at the end. Scripts in `progress/round-19/critic-scripts/` (round 18 copies. Their output folder is the relative `../critic/`, so only the folder changed. I also edited the path in `legs18.py`). New: `route-feat19.mjs` (route-feat18 with logging only, control unchanged), `legs19.py`, `capfarm-narrow.mjs`, `looks19.mjs`, `det19.sh`, `det19b.sh`. `alley-entry19-unused.mjs` is a broken probe (my pilot cut corners). I use no numbers from it.

Pad audit: 19860, 85749, 96382, 14820, 29724, 70006, 84383, 23893, 61564, 39178, 94202, 49588, 72214, 65264, 34173, 50169, 36880, 98757, 46825, 65279.

## Round 18 gap: shortcuts one-note and silent. Closed, with one clause missed

| Test (12 fresh cities, deterministic) | Needed | Result | Pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| Alley or tunnel on the shortest route | 25% of legs | 55 of 93 (59%). Round 18: 13% | Yes |
| Alley or tunnel alone gives a 15% shortcut | 1 in 8 | 30 of 93 (32%). Round 18: 2 of 97 | Yes |
| Kinds on 15% shortcut legs | | alley 36, tunnel 8, boulevard 21 (of 52) | Varied now |
| Shortcut bot faster on alley/tunnel cut legs | 10% | 23.9% faster on 27 matched legs (327 s against 430 s) | Yes |
| Shortcut bot crashes | at most 0.5 a minute | 0.62 a minute (16 in 1,554 s). Grid bot 0. Without one city where the bot hit the same alley 4 times (22132): 0.48 | No, just |
| Feature named within 1 s of leg start | 12 of 12 | Shown at 0.0 s on every leg with a real shortcut. 157 of 169 feature legs. The 12 misses: 10 first hops (16 to 23 m, never hinted) and 2 legs where the route from the pad has no shortcut | Yes |
| No name repeats in a city | 0 | 0 repeats, 21 to 25 features per city | Yes |
| Centre messages never overlap | 0 | 443 centre messages, 232 kind changes, smallest gap 650 ms, 0 shown together | Yes |

- 15 of the 16 shortcut-bot crashes are in alleys (12) or tunnels (3). Most hit at 14 to 18 m/s, many at 25 m from the pad: the bot leaves an alley mouth fast and turns hard onto a doorstep pad set 2.2 m beside the mouth. Same control as round 18, which had 0.19 a minute. The new mouth pads make the end of an alley leg sharper.
- Straight through every alley and tunnel at 20 m/s, 4.5 m, W only: 447 of 452 passes clean, 5 scrape (bumps, no charged crash). Same as round 18 (5 of 398).
- Scores: grid bot 1,838 to 3,866 (median 3,340). Shortcut bot 0 to 8,658, Gold on 7 of 12, best 87% of Ace. Round 18 gap 3 (Gold needs shortcuts, Ace far) is mostly fixed. The 0 (22132) and 1,184 (34471) are my bot. On 22132 it hit one alley 4 times. On two tunnel legs to 20 m rooftop pads it stayed under the tunnel roof for 46 s.
- Hint honesty, small faults: 3 hints say "Tunnel" but name only two alleys (the tunnel is the third feature and is cut off by the two-name limit). 6 of 61 alley or tunnel hints point at a raised pad. The job picker avoids tunnels to raised pads, but the hint does not.
- Repetition: 21 of 77 hinted legs (grid bot) and 31 of 91 (shortcut bot) share a named feature with the leg before. Back and forth along one alley line (V-d-seed20540-leg2/leg3: "Sparrow Row + Ink Alley" twice in a row).

## Exploits

- **Van tailing:** not an exploit. Tailing a van gives full draft, but the bank is capped per leg and the slow clock has its per-leg budget. A carry farm that tails vans scores 0.66 to 0.83 of honest points a minute (25 s and 12 s a leg). It never beats honest flying on any seed (best 0.85 on 130). "Forever" does not pay: the 25 s version scores less than the 12 s one.
- **Tunnel shuttle:** the full slow clock under a tunnel roof does not stack: whole-run slow-clock seconds stay 12 to 15 s, as for honest runs. No exploit.
- **But the street bonus can carry a run.** A tunnel carry farm on seed 58 scores 2,132 Silver with 2 drops. Street bonus is 1,666 of it (78%). Leg caps on long legs reach 1,106.
- **No-delivery farms:** all 0 (farm-probe on 22, 58, 130, farm-loop, smart-farm near, pickupline, spendpickup).

## Guards (real time, one run at a time)

| City | Street (grid bot) | Lazy |
|---|---|---|
| 16068 | 2,556 Silver | not run |
| 20540 | 2,480 Silver | 1,116 Bronze |
| 22132 | 2,872 Silver | not run |
| 34471 | 1,151 Bronze (under load), rerun 2,705 Silver | not run |
| 32134 | 1,818 Bronze (under load), rerun 2,985 Silver | not run |
| 34372 | 3,642 Silver | not run |
| 99113 | 3,978 Silver | not run |
| 20188 | 3,736 Silver | not run |
| 47664 | 3,657 Silver | 1,255 Bronze |
| 20823 | 2,713 Silver | 847 none |
| 26635 | 2,286 Silver | 987 none |
| 96680 | 2,501 Silver | not run |

- Street Silver or better: 12 of 12 on clean runs (10 first runs plus the 2 reruns). The two Bronze runs ran 06:35 to 06:39 while my deterministic farm batch pushed the load to 12 to 17 on 10 cores. The deterministic grid bot scores Silver on both (2,817 and 3,399). I count them as contaminated but flag it.
- Lazy: cut to 4 cities for time. All Bronze or below (best 1,255). Not 12 of 12 measured.
- No Ace: best of anything 8,658 (shortcut bot, deterministic). Best real time 4,876.
- Best lazy 1,255 against worst clean street 2,286: gap 1,031. Pass on the cities measured.

## Gates (seeds 22, 58, 130, real time)

| Run | 22 | 58 | 130 | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Low (music-run) | 2,941 Silver, 3 drops | 3,099 Silver, 4 | 1,757 Bronze, 3 | 7,797 |
| High | **4,876 Gold**, 8 drops | 2,290 Silver, 5 | 2,832 Silver, 6 | 9,998 |

- **Low over high 0.78. The line is 0.85, so this fails.** In round 18 it was 0.84 once the 130 stall was set aside. 130 did not stall this time. The high line on 22 made 8 drops and Gold.
- No-delivery farms 0. Carry farm (round 18 capfarm, 60 s cap) 0.47 of honest, as the builder measured. New narrow farms: tunnel 0.50 (25 s) and 0.69 (12 s), alley 0.32 and 0.74, van 0.66 and 0.83. **Over 0.5 as written** for the short farm phases, but none beats honest flying, so this is a weak gate, not an exploit.
- One-delivery farms: every 1-drop farm run is Bronze or below (best 1,379). Pass.
- Breakdown exact, card medal equals tier from score and saved tier, in all real-time runs. Rush at 60.0 s in all 15 runs that reached it. Overtime: started in 3 street runs, finished in 2, ran out in 1.

## Regressions

- Crash-classify, 8 seeds. 12 m: 594 s, 46 charged, 0 hop-like, 17 near the target, all on faces at least 2.8 m below the wall top: 0 pad lip. 20 m: 518 s, 32 charged, 5 near target (faces 3.5 m or more below the top). 1 rise of 0.9 m without climb (seed 130, face 7.7 m below the top), a real wall hit. Pass.
- Pad audit, 20 fresh cities: 1,987 pads, 0 issues, 0 inside an alley strip, 160 within 22 m of a tunnel (round 18: 72), none flagged.
- Flat-frame probe: 942 frames, 0 flat, 0 errors.
- Music adaptive: chain 0 to 3 gives layers 1 to 4, mean intensity 0.34 to 0.86. Pass.
- Hand-fly first payout: desktop **5.6 s**, mobile **6.5 s** (round 18: 8.8 and 9.9). Pass.

## Player feel (desktop 1280x720 and iPhone 13 landscape, touch)

- **Alley entries at speed:** you must brake, and then they are fair. A straight line through is clean at 20 m/s. Turning in off a cross street at 15 m/s or more hits the mouth corner (V-d-seed20540-leg2-t5, V-m-...-leg2-t8). The wider apron and lit posts help you see the slot. The harsh part is the exit: doorstep pads now sit 2.2 m beside the mouths, so an alley leg often ends with a hard turn at speed.
- **Route hint:** it does not fly the game for you. It does not really help either. "Shortcut · Sparrow Row + Ink Alley −41 m" names places the world never labels: the mouth "name boards" are plain glowing boxes, and the nav marker points straight at the pad. In a new random city each run, a name tells you nothing. What a player can use is "there is an alley shortcut on this leg" plus the lit mouths they happen to see.
- **Mobile HUD:** less clear than desktop. The centre pop ("Parcel secured!", "Crash! -3 SEC") lands on the slipstream and boost meters and the cue line (V-m-seed20540-leg2-t3, -t8). The pad marker and distance sit on the shortcut pill. The pill itself reads well.

## Whole game against the best polished indie arcade flying and delivery games

- **First 10 seconds:** strong. A pretty city, a clear first pickup, a payout in about 6 s.
- **Onboarding:** good. The draft rule teaches itself. The cues name the next thing to do.
- **Core loop:** pick up, thread streets, drop, bank. Shortcuts now matter on most legs and double a good pilot's score.
- **Game feel:** still the best part. Alleys with both walls feeding the draft are the best moments.
- **Art:** warm, cohesive low-poly with lit alleys and tunnels. Good.
- **Audio:** adaptive music that follows the chain. Good.
- **UI:** clean on desktop, crowded at the bottom centre on phones.
- **Difficulty curve:** rush hour at 60 s, then every parcel a rush. Fine.
- **Run variety:** random cities and named features, but legs often go back along the same alley line.
- **Game over and restart:** clear card with an exact breakdown and medal. Fast restart.
- **Replay pull:** medals, daily city, a real score ceiling. But a player cannot learn a city, so mastery comes from reading streets live, and the game gives no way to read the route ahead.

## Single biggest remaining gap: the route is not readable from the screen

**The concern.** Route choice is now the game's depth: on 59% of legs the best route goes through an alley or tunnel, and taking it is 24% faster. But nothing on screen shows where that route starts. The hint names a feature the world never labels, the marker points as the crow flies, and every city is new. Good players will find shortcuts by luck or by flying high to look. The best games of this kind make the line visible: a sign, a glow on the right entrance, a small map.

**Acceptance test** (12 fresh cities, desktop and iPhone 13 landscape):
1. On every leg whose shortest route uses an alley or tunnel, the entrance the route uses is marked on screen in a way that differs from other mouths (for example its name in the world, or a lit arrow on that mouth only). The diagnostics expose the marked mouth position. A probe confirms it projects inside the viewport within 3 s of the leg start, or as soon as it is within 80 m in front.
2. A "sign follower" bot that steers only by what is marked (the marked mouth, then the pad marker), with no street graph, is at least 15% faster than the grid bot on those legs, at most 0.5 charged crashes a minute.
3. The hint's label matches its names (no "Tunnel" without a tunnel), and no hint suggests a tunnel to a raised pad.
4. All guards and gates still pass, including low over high at least 0.85.

## Other gaps (ranked)

1. **The high line beats the street line** (low over high 0.78, high Gold on seed 22). The game's identity is low street flying. Test: low over high at least 0.85 on 22, 58 and 130, high bot at most Silver.
2. **Mobile HUD crowding.** Centre pops cover the slipstream and boost meters. The pad marker covers the shortcut pill. Test: on iPhone 13 landscape in 3 full runs, no centre message rectangle intersects a meter, cue or pill rectangle, and the nav marker never covers the pill.
3. **Alley exits into mouth pads are sharp.** The shortcut bot crashes 0.62 a minute, mostly at alley ends next to pads. Test: shortcut bot at most 0.4 charged crashes a minute on 12 fresh cities, same control.
4. **Street bonus can carry a run.** A 2-drop tunnel farm reaches Silver with 78% street bonus. Test: no run with 2 drops or fewer scores Silver on 22, 58, 130. Narrow carry farms under 0.6 of honest at 12 s farm phases.
5. **Back-and-forth legs.** About a third of hinted legs reuse the last leg's alley line. Test: at most 15% of consecutive legs share a named feature.

## Performance

Headless Chromium caps at 120 Hz.
- Flight through 2 tunnels, 2 alleys and a boulevard (`perf18.mjs`, 12.5 s): desktop 1,502 frames, median 8.3 ms, p95 9.6, max 10.4, 0 over 20 ms. iPhone 13 landscape: median 8.3, p95 9.4, max 10.4, 0 over 20 ms. 262k triangles, 58 to 74 draw calls.
- Hand-fly 80 s mobile: 9,580 frames, median 8.3, p95 9.8, max 24.7, 1 over 20 ms.
- First load, production build: about 0.81 MB (JS 767 KB, 211 KB gzipped, CSS 36 KB, HTML 11 KB). lil-gui 31 KB only for `?debug`. Budget 15 MB: pass. Page errors 0.

## Screenshots (progress/round-19/critic/)

- V-d-seed20540-leg1..3-t* and V-m-seed20540-leg1..3-t*: first three legs, desktop and iPhone (hint pill, alley entry crash, mobile HUD crowding: V-m-...-leg2-t3, -leg2-t8).
- T-feat-seed*-alley*/tunnel*/diagonal*: shortcut bot in features. P-feat-seed*-crash*: its crashes (22132 alley pile-up).
- A-seed*: alley-fly scrapes. C-capfarm19-*: narrow carry farms. C-capfarm-*, F-farm-*, S-smartfarm-*: farms. M-low-*, Q-*: gate medal moments. N-alt12-*, N-alt20-*: crash-classify. d-h*, m-h*: hand-fly.

## Order and contamination

Deterministic batches (nice 19) ran 06:30 to 06:39 beside the first real-time street runs. Street runs 34471 and 32134 ran at load 12 to 17. Everything after 06:40 ran with nothing in parallel. Lazy guard was cut to 4 cities and the lazy gate on 22, 58, 130 was not run, to stay near the time budget.
