# Drone Dash, round 19 builder: shortcuts you choose, and the game names them

Concern from the round 18 critic: shortcuts are one-note and silent. Boulevards made 33 of 35 shortcut legs. An alley or tunnel was on the shortest route in 13% of legs and decided the route alone on 2 of 97. No route was a trade, and the game never named a shortcut. Centre messages stacked.

Time box: 04:31 to 07:01. Dev server on port 5188, stopped at the end. Scripts and logs: `progress/round-19/builder-scripts/`. Shots: `progress/round-19/builder-shots/`. The critic's round 18 scripts are copied unchanged except their output folder (`../builder-shots/`) and the log path in `legs18.py`.

**Result in short:** every acceptance line passes on 12 fresh cities. An alley or tunnel is on the shortest route in 47% of legs (needed 25%). It alone gives a 15% shortcut on 19% of legs (needed 12.5%). The shortcut bot is 21.8% faster on shortcut legs and 24.8% faster on alley and tunnel legs, with 0.25 crashes a minute (limit 0.5). The HUD named the feature within 1 s on 140 of 140 legs whose shortest route uses one (desktop and iPhone). No name repeats. Centre messages never overlapped. Guards, gates, pad audit and regressions: see sections 4 and 5.

## 1. Design

### Alleys and tunnels on useful lines
- **Alley lines** (`CityFeatures.planAlleys`). Each city gets three lines of alleys along z and three along x, 3 to 5 blocks long, through the middle of the blocks. An alley now carries on across the street into the next block. So it is a narrow straight lane through part of the city, not a lone slot. Parks and depots break a line. 16 to 22 alleys a city. The most central ones are tunnels (at least 2 a city).
- **Pads at the mouths** (`CityGenerator`). A lot beside an alley mouth gets a doorstep more often (0.8 against 0.42). The doorstep sits 2.2 m from the alley wall, on the alley's line, not in the middle of the face. So a leg can start at one mouth and end at another mouth further down the line. Going round the block costs about 12 m more at each end than going through.
- **Job picker** (`DeliverySystem.pickLeg`, `JOBS.narrowBias` 0.5). The existing shortcut bias (0.85) stays. Inside it, half the legs first look for a special pad. Its shortest route takes an alley or tunnel, no boulevard, and is at least 15% shorter. Then any shortcut, then the old rules. The leg spec (kind, height, distance band) is unchanged. A shortcut leg never goes back to one of the last 4 pads (no ping-pong along one alley). A raised pad is never offered for a tunnel route. The climb to the roof must not start under the bridge.

### Each route is a readable trade
- **Alley:** shorter, and the draft runs at full strength: inside the strip the wall factor is 1 and the hug bonus is full (1.6x fill). HUD cue "Alley draft!". The entry is a 90-degree turn into a 6 m slot: a fast turn-in can hit a wall and costs the usual crash (3 s, combo, bank cut). Crash rules unchanged.
- **Tunnel:** shorter and darker (ice-blue lights). Under the bridge the slow clock runs at full strength. It uses the leg's existing budget (8 s a leg, only toward the objective), so it cannot be farmed. HUD cue "Tunnel · clock slowed". Clear height 7 m, so a fast high line has to drop to get in.
- **Boulevard:** wide, open, no tight entry. When an alley line points your way, the boulevard is usually longer.
- **Fair mouths** (drawn only, flush on the faces): glowing corner posts on both sides of every mouth and a lit board on each side. Two chevrons on the apron point in. They are amber for an alley and ice blue for a tunnel. The faces at an alley mouth are set back 1.5 m (`MOUTH_SET`). This gives a 4.5 m apron between the street and the slot to finish a turn. This is the funnel: a wider space before the slot, not a wider slot.

### The game names the route
- **Route hint** (`Hud.setRouteHint`, `Game.newLeg`). At the start of every leg, the game finds the shortest street route to the objective. It uses the same graph as the `streetRoute` hook. If the route uses a feature, a small pill shows under the objective pill at once, in the same glass style. Examples: "SHORTCUT Lantern Alley −24 m", "TUNNEL Clock Tunnel −31 m", "FAST LANE Kestrel Boulevard −27 m". If the saving is under 3 m, the label is "VIA". Alleys and tunnels are named first, at most two names. It stays 10 s. Diagnostics: `routeHint` (kind, names, saving, grid and route length, leg start and shown time).
- **Unique names:** alleys draw a distinct first word from 30 (Lantern, Tinker, Quill, Walnut ...) with Alley, Lane, Row, Passage or Walk. Tunnels draw from 10 names, boulevards from 6, all without repeats.

### Centre messages one at a time
`Hud.centre` is a small queue for the four centre messages (delivery and pickup and crash pop, medal banner, rush hour and overtime banner, payout pop). Only one is visible. A message of the same kind replaces the one up (as before). Another kind waits until the one up has been read (0.65 to 1.8 s). Then it takes its place. A crash jumps the queue. A newer message replaces an older queued one of its kind. A payout pop that waited more than 1.2 s is dropped. The medal fanfare is still timed to its banner. The extra "Street bonus paid" pop on a delivery is gone (the delivery pop's line already says "street bonus +N"). All four share one slot below the HUD column and the route hint: 39% down on desktop, 53% on a phone held sideways (the old spots overlapped the objective pill on iPhone).

### Rush-hour vans (optional)
Tailing a hover-van (2 to 10 m behind it, in its lane, at 8 m/s or more) is a full draft, cue "Van draft!". The vans still have no collider, so rush hour cannot get unfair. `van-probe19.mjs`: behind a van the draft was on for 20 to 94 of 160 frames and banked up to 630.

### Small extra
The run's first meter is 2.5 draft metres (was 3), so the first payout comes a little sooner on a phone (mobile hand-fly was 9.9 s against a 10 s line).

## 2. Acceptance (12 fresh cities)

Fresh cities from `pick-seeds.mjs` after the last game change (16 loads with no `?seed`, first 12 used): 77984, 51714, 55642, 15336, 80212, 55130, 41128, 23571, 72971, 37812, 15756, 63138. Pad audit adds the other 4 loads (57267, 96431, 24640, 47005) and 1001 to 1014.

Deterministic, the critic's `route-feat18.mjs` (FEAT=0 grid bot, FEAT=1 shortcut bot), 6 processes each, logs merged into `feat-grid.log` and `feat-feat.log`, then `legs18.py` (output `legs19.out`) and `legsum19.py`.

| Test | Needed | Result | Pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| Alley or tunnel on the shortest route | 25% of legs | 40 of 86 (47%) | Yes |
| Alley or tunnel alone gives a 15% shortcut (no boulevard) | 1 in 8 | 16 of 86 (19%) | Yes |
| Shortcut bot faster on 15% shortcut legs | 10% | 37 matched legs: 614 s against 481 s, 21.8% faster. Alley or tunnel only legs (13): 24.8% faster | Yes |
| Shortcut bot crashes | at most 0.5 a minute | 7 in 1,653 s (0.25 a minute). Grid bot 0. 5 of the 7 are fast entries into an alley (10 to 15 m/s), 1 a tunnel mouth, 1 a boulevard | Yes |
| Feature named within 1 s of the leg start | every leg whose shortest route has one | `hint-probe19.mjs`: desktop 122 of 122 legs (144 legs, 12 cities), iPhone 13 sideways 18 of 18 (24 legs, 4 cities). Shown at 0.0 s every time | Yes |
| No name repeats within a city | 0 | 0 of 12 cities (and 0 of 30 in the pad audit list) | Yes |

Per city (grid bot legs; on route / alone 15%): 77984 5/2 of 8, 51714 4/2 of 6, 55642 2/2 of 8, 15336 4/0 of 8, 80212 5/1 of 6, 55130 3/1 of 6, 41128 2/2 of 8, 23571 1/1 of 8, 72971 6/3 of 8, 37812 4/1 of 8, 15756 1/0 of 6, 63138 3/1 of 6.

## 3. Centre messages

`msg-probe19.mjs`, real time, one browser, nothing else running. One run fires every trigger, several close together. It finishes legs by placing the drone on the pad (deliveries, pickups, medals). It places the drone fast in an alley (payouts) and fast at a wall with W held (crashes). It does a delivery and a crash right on the 60 s rush hour. Then it lets the clock run out with a parcel aboard (overtime) and makes the overtime delivery. Every 50 ms it reads the four centre elements. Two visible at once with overlapping boxes counts as an overlap.

| Run | Frames | Overlaps | Triggers seen | Centre message over the objective pill or route hint |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop, seed 22 (`msg-d-22e.log`) | 3,358 | **0** | 13 deliveries, 6 crashes, 5 payouts, Bronze to Gold, rush hour at 60 s, overtime and its delivery | 0 frames |
| iPhone 13 sideways, seed 58 (`msg-m-58e.log`) | 3,167 | **0** | 12 deliveries, 6 crashes, 1 payout, Bronze to Gold, rush hour at 60 s, overtime and its delivery | 0 frames |

Earlier runs (`msg-d-22.log`, `msg-d-22b/c.log`, `msg-m-58*.log`) also had 0 overlaps between centre messages. Their crash trigger missed (W was not held), and on the phone the pop still touched the route hint as it faded. The fix: the centre slot is lower on a short screen, the pop is a little smaller, and it rises less as it fades. Shot: O-d-seed22-overtime.

- `src/systems/DeliverySystem.ts`: `JOBS.narrowBias`, alley or tunnel shortcut first, no return to the last 4 pads on a shortcut leg.
- `src/game/Game.ts`: shortcut classes for the picker (no tunnel route to a raised pad), route hint at each leg start, alley and tunnel strips (full draft, tunnel slow clock), van draft, centre queue tick, diagnostics (`routeHint`, `narrow`, `vanDraft`, `centreLog`), test hook `vans()`.
- `src/systems/Slipstream.ts`: `narrow` and `van` inputs.

- `src/ui/Hud.ts`: centre message queue, route hint, new cues.

New scripts: `hint-probe19.mjs`, `msg-probe19.mjs`, `van-probe19.mjs`, `legsum19.py`, `det19.sh`, `rtqueue19.sh` with `rtjobs19.txt`.

# Drone Dash: round 18 critic report

**Verdict:** Route choice is real now, but it is one-note. The diagonal boulevards make 33 of the 35 shortcut legs. The alleys and tunnels look great and fly cleanly. But they almost never change the best route. The game also never names or points out a shortcut. Both leftovers are closed. All guards and gates pass, with two notes: one street run under heavy machine load scored Bronze (clean reruns: Silver), and the high-line bot still stalls on seed 130 (a bot fault, explained below).

Build tested: working tree on commit 893b17b plus the uncommitted round 18 changes. Dev server port 5188, stopped at the end. Scripts in `progress/round-18/critic-scripts/`. The round 17 copies are unchanged: their output folder is the relative `../critic/`, which now points at round 18.

Fresh cities (loads with no `?seed`, none found in any builder script, builder shot or round 17 file): 44840, 66352, 86749, 69865, 66633, 54075, 81658, 53713, 39728, 82412, 43361, 40118. Pad audit adds 13051, 21382, 58825, 82579, 35020, 44243, 30287, 65430, 17060, 28610, 57888, 52131, 87301, 10869.

## Round 17 gap and leftovers

### Leftover 1: one-delivery farms reached Silver. Closed.
- capfarm "both" with 12 s and 20 s farm phases on seeds 22, 58, 130: best 1,639 Bronze (round 17: 2,243 and 2,356). Time-up share paid 0 in all of them (it now needs 2 drops).

### Leftover 2: stale saved medal. Closed.
- 24 deterministic runs (12 cities, two bots): run tier, tier from score, saved best tier and localStorage best tier agree 24 of 24. 6 of those runs were paid a time-up share.
- 41 real-time runs: state tier equals the tier from the score, and the game-over card names the same medal, 41 of 41.

### Round 17 gap: no route choice and nothing new in the world. Mostly closed.

| Test | Needed | Result | Pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| Legs with a draftable shortcut at least 15% shorter (12 cities) | 1 in 3 | 35 of 97 (0.36). Median saving 20%, range 15 to 34% | Yes, just |
| Which feature makes the shortcut | | Boulevard on 33 of 35. Alley or tunnel alone on 2 of 35 | (see gap) |
| Shortcut bot faster on those legs | 10% | 16.3% faster on 31 matched legs (427 s against 510 s). It flies about 22% less distance | Yes |
| Crashes per minute, shortcut bot against grid bot | not more | 0.19 a minute (5 in 1,612 s) against 0 (0 in 1,498 s) | No |
| Kinds of feature on 6 fresh loads | 3 | Every load has 4 boulevards, 7 to 18 alleys, 2 to 5 tunnels, plus 2 rush lanes | Yes |
| Rush hour changes something visible | yes | Two streets light up in amber with chevrons and hover-vans stream in (R-d-seed44840-rush-before and -after) | Yes |

How I measured: `route-feat18.mjs`, deterministic (external clock, 50 ms steps). FEAT=0 is the round 17 grid street bot, control unchanged. FEAT=1 is my shortcut bot with the same control. Each leg, it checks the shortest route on the game's street graph (the `streetRoute` hook). If that route is at least 3% shorter than the grid route, it takes it. It flies tunnels at 3.5 m and alleys at 5 m, and it merges straight-through boulevard stops so they do not count as corners. The first version did not merge them and was only 9.7% faster. That was my bot, not the game (`legs18-v1.out`). Legs are matched by from-pad and to-pad. Analysis: `legs18.py`, output `legs18.out`.

Is the graph honest about the geometry? `alley-fly18.mjs` flies straight through every alley and tunnel on the 12 cities, both ways, at 4.5 m, holding W only. 393 of 398 passes are clean at 14 m/s and again at 20 m/s. 5 passes (the same ones at both speeds) scrape a wall near one mouth and drop to about 2.7 m/s, with no charged crash. At least one is where an alley opens onto a boulevard (A-seed44840-GalleryTunnel--1).

The crashes: 4 of the 5 happen in alleys, 3 of them in one alley on 66352. The bot turns into a 6 m alley and speeds up to 15 to 18 m/s. At impact it is 2 to 3 m off the centre line (P-feat-seed66352-crash1). The 5th is at a tunnel mouth. This is a real risk of the feature, not broken geometry. A 6 m slot entered off a 90-degree turn is tight. That is fine as a trade-off, but the acceptance clause asked for no extra crashes.

Score effect (deterministic): grid bot 2,557 to 5,416 (median about 3,300). Shortcut bot 1,644 to 6,503 (median about 4,550). The 1,644 on 43361 is my bot stuck for 48 s at a rooftop beside a tunnel: it held 3.5 m because the route ran through the tunnel. That is a bot limit.

## Feature feel (desktop 1280x720 and iPhone 13 held sideways, touch)

- **Boulevards:** the best new thing. Red paving with an amber dashed line, stepped facades, a diamond you can see from the title screen (L-d-load1-seed69870-title). At street height they read as fast lanes. They create the only real decision: "does a diagonal point my way?"
- **Alleys:** cosy and readable. Warm lanterns and two close walls to draft. The camera stays 2.9 m above and 7 to 9 m behind the drone, with no clipping (T-feat-seed82412-alley2, F-d/F-m-seed44840-alley-*). But they are mid-block, so on a grid they rarely shorten a leg. The shortest route used an alley on 8 of 97 legs.
- **Tunnels:** a lit ceiling, a glowing sign band, 7 m clear. At 3.5 m the camera sits at about 6.1 m, below the ceiling, and the view through is clear on desktop and iPhone (F-d-seed44840-tunnel-inside, F-m-seed44840-tunnel-enter). A tunnel is on the shortest route on 5 of 97 legs. Most players will fly through one by chance, not by choice.
- **Fair or cramped?** Fair. A straight line through is clean at 20 m/s. A turn into an alley at speed is risky and costs a 3 s crash charge. That is a good risk, but the game does not reward the risk: the alley route is just shorter, with the same draft as a street.
- **Readability of the choice:** weak. The nav shows a direction arrow and distance only. Feature names exist in code but are never shown. One city reuses names: 66352 has two each of Ginger Alley, Cobble Row, Paper Lane and Kite Lane. A player cannot plan "take Clock Tunnel", and is never told that a shortcut paid off.
- **Rush hour:** visible but not alive. The lanes glow and vans fly in. The vans are drawn only: no collider, no draft, no effect on jobs. You can fly through them. On iPhone the rush banner fades over the objective bar (R-m-seed44840-rush-after). On desktop, "RUSH HOUR", "Crash!" and the bank pop stack in the centre (P-feat-seed66352-crash1).

## Medal guards (12 fresh cities, real time, one run at a time)

| City | Street (grid bot) | Lazy |
|---|---|---|
| 44840 | 2,325 Silver | 1,135 Bronze |
| 66352 | 3,389 Silver | 1,209 Bronze |
| 86749 | 3,862 Silver | 1,007 Bronze |
| 69865 | 3,223 Silver | 1,146 Bronze |
| 66633 | 2,729 Silver | 712 none |
| 54075 | 2,471 Silver | 1,071 Bronze |
| 81658 | **1,430 Bronze** (under load), reruns 3,240, 2,523, 2,526 Silver | 640 none |
| 53713 | 2,857 Silver | 1,400 Bronze |
| 39728 | 3,138 Silver | 883 none |
| 82412 | 5,440 Gold | 1,559 Bronze |
| 43361 | 4,068 Silver | 1,479 Bronze |
| 40118 | 2,277 Silver | 828 none |

- **Street Silver or better:** 12 of 12 on clean runs. The one Bronze (81658, 2 drops) ran while my deterministic batch pushed the load average to 17 on 10 cores. Three clean reruns all scored Silver. I count it as contaminated, but I flag it.
- **Lazy Bronze or below:** 12 of 12 (best 1,559).
- **No Ace:** pass. Best of any bot and mode is 6,503 (shortcut bot, deterministic). The best real-time score is 5,663. Ace is now 10,000.
- **Best lazy at least 300 below worst street:** 1,559 against 2,207 (a clean 40118 repeat) = **648**. Pass. With the contaminated run included, it fails.
- **Same-city repeats (best over worst):** 40118: 2,277, 2,207, 2,234 (1.03). 82412: 5,440, 5,533, 5,663 (1.04). 43361: 4,068, 3,379, 4,000 (1.20). 81658 clean: 3,240, 2,523, 2,526 (1.28). With the loaded run included: 2.27. Pass on clean runs.
- **Score level shifted down for grid flying.** The real-time street median is about 3,000 (round 17: about 5,100). Job picks now prefer pads that have a shortcut, so a pilot who ignores shortcuts flies longer legs. Gold (4,500) now needs shortcuts. Ace (10,000) is far: the best bot reaches 65% of it.

## Gates (seeds 22, 58, 130, real time)

| Run | 22 | 58 | 130 | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Low (music-run) | 2,156 Silver, 3 drops | 2,355 Silver, 3 | 2,709 Silver, 3 | 7,220 |
| High | 2,936 Silver, 6 | 2,920 Silver, 6 | **0, stalled** | 5,856 |
| Lazy | 1,032 Bronze | 1,255 Bronze | 725 none | 3,012 |

- Low over high **1.23** (needed 0.85). Pass, but only because the high run on 130 scored 0. Suppose the high bot had scored its round 17 value of 2,758 on 130. Then low over high is 7,220 / 8,614 = **0.84**, just under the line. The low runs scored about 40% less than in round 17 (12,051), for the reason above. So this gate is on the edge.
- No-delivery farms: all 0 (farm-probe 3, farm-loop, smart-farm near, pickupline and spendpickup on 22, 58, 130, plus carry and both farms that never delivered).
- Carry farm: 0.34 of street points a minute (honest 1,309, 1,698, 1,655 a minute. Carry: 0, 1,563, 0). Pass. Seed 58 alone is 0.92. It scores 2,300 Silver with 2 drops.
- Breakdown exact: diagnostics, card rows and total agree in all 41 real-time runs.
- Rush hour starts at 60.0 s in every run that reached 60 s.
- Overtime works: started in 17 real-time runs and was finished in 16 of them (the high run on 22 ran out).

## Seed 130 high-line stall: the bot, not the game

- The stall pad is "Bakery · Orchard & 2nd Ave", a doorstep beside a boulevard corner cut. The cut leaves a low stepped roof (about 7 to 8 m) with a rim, 1.5 to 2.5 m from the pad.
- The beeline bot arrives high, starts down 25 m out, and lands on that roof 2.5 m short. Then it holds Shift (descend) the whole time. The roof rim stops it from sliding off. Its camera-relative steering swings about 1 rad each way. So it rocks in place for 50 s (H-seed130-stall). Same in deterministic and real time.
- The pad is fair: placed 30 m straight above it and holding Shift, the drone lands and delivers in 1.6 s (H-seed130-descent). The game's pad audit is clean too.
- So it is a bot fault: when something blocks the bot, it never climbs. The game adds a mild trap: a pad hard against a low roof with a rim. A person can see the ring and hop over the rim.

## Pad audit

26 fresh cities, 2,023 pads: 0 buried, 0 overhang, 0 awning, 0 outside. 0 pads sit inside an alley strip (pads are kept out of alleys). 72 pads lie within 22 m of a tunnel. None is flagged, and none has a ceiling over it.

## Regressions

- **Crash-classify, 8 seeds:** 12 m: 609 s, 47 charged, 0 hop-like, 10 near the target, all on faces 3.4 to 14.1 m below the wall top, so **0 pad lip**. 20 m: 684 s, 43 charged, 14 near the target. 0 hop-like: the two rises had climb held. Faces were 3.7 to 16.1 m below the top, so **0 pad lip**. Pass.
- **Flat-frame probe:** 997 frames, 0 flat, 0 errors.
- **Music:** adaptive. Chains 0 to 3 give 1 to 4 layers (mean intensity 0.33 to 0.87). The final section starts at 9.96 to 10.0 s left. 0 late notes, 0 resyncs, 0 errors.
- **Hand-fly first payout:** desktop **8.8 s**, mobile **9.9 s**. Pass, but slower than round 17 (6.4 and 7.1). Mobile is 0.1 s from the line.

## Whole game, against the best polished indie arcade flying and delivery games

- **First 10 seconds:** strong. The boulevard diamond makes the title city more legible and more designed.
- **Game feel:** still the best part. The alleys add the best moments in the game: threading a lantern-lit slot with both walls feeding the draft.
- **Core loop:** balanced and fair, with a real end-of-run.
- **Depth:** better, but the decision is shallow. The best games of this kind make a route a bet. One line is faster but riskier. Another is slower but pays more. And when the bet pays, the game tells you. Here a shortcut is strictly better, almost always the same kind (a diagonal), and silent. The alleys and tunnels, which are the most memorable spaces, are mostly scenery for routing.
- **World:** prettier and more varied. Still passive: rush hour is lighting and ghost vans.
- **UI:** clean in flight. Centre messages still stack at busy moments.

## Single biggest remaining gap: shortcuts are one-note and silent

**The concern.** Route choice exists. But almost all of it is one rule: when a diagonal points your way, take it. Alleys and tunnels decide the route on very few legs. No shortcut carries a trade-off (risk against reward), and nothing tells the player a shortcut exists, what it is called, or that it paid. So the new spaces do not yet create decisions a player plans and remembers.

**Evidence.** 33 of 35 shortcut legs come from a boulevard. Only 2 of 97 legs have an alley or tunnel shortcut without a boulevard. The shortest route uses an alley on 8 and a tunnel on 5 of 97 legs. The HUD shows only an arrow and distance. Feature names are never shown, and one city repeats four names.

**Acceptance test** (12 fresh cities, deterministic, with `route-feat18.mjs` and `legs18.py` or equivalent):
1. An alley or tunnel is on the shortest route in at least 25% of legs (now 13%). It alone gives a 15% shortcut (no boulevard on that route) on at least 1 in 8 legs (now 2 of 97).
2. Each alley or tunnel route is a trade-off a probe can measure. Examples: more street bonus a second than the street, or a speed gate. A crash in it can cost more than the route saves. The shortcut bot still beats the grid bot by at least 10% in leg time on those legs. It has at most 0.5 charged crashes a minute.
3. Some legs have a shortest route through a feature. On 12 of 12 such legs, the screen names the feature within 1 s of the leg start, for example "via Clock Tunnel". Check desktop and iPhone held sideways. No city uses one name twice.
4. The round 17 and round 18 guards and gates above still pass.

## Other gaps (ranked)

1. **Rush hour is cosmetic.** The vans have no collider, no draft and no effect on jobs. Test: during rush hour, vans block (collider) or give draft. A bot that flies a rush lane shows a measurable change against the same street before 60 s, in crashes or street bonus a second.
2. **Centre messages still stack.** "RUSH HOUR", "Crash!" and the bank pop overlap (P-feat-seed66352-crash1). On iPhone the rush banner fades over the objective bar (R-m-seed44840-rush-after), and the nav distance label sits on the "FLY" label. Test: in 12 full runs on desktop and iPhone, no two centre messages overlap and no HUD label overlaps another.
3. **Grid flying lost its medal headroom.** The street median fell from about 5,100 to about 3,000. Gold needs shortcuts now. Ace (10,000) is 1.5 times the best bot. Test: on 12 fresh cities, the shortcut bot reaches Gold on at least 6. Some pilot (bot or tuned run) reaches at least 80% of Ace.
4. **First payout got slower:** desktop 8.8 s, mobile 9.9 s (round 17: 6.4 and 7.1). Test: hand-fly first payout under 8 s on both.
5. **Low roof traps next to pads at boulevard cuts** (seed 130). Test: the pad audit also flags any pad with a roof edge lower than 12 m within 2.5 m. The beeline bot delivers on 22, 58 and 130.

## Performance

Headless Chromium caps at 120 Hz (8.3 ms).
- Flight through 2 tunnels, 2 alleys and a boulevard (`perf18.mjs`, 12.5 s, real rAF): desktop 1,502 frames, **median 8.3 ms, p95 9.5, max 10.4, 0 over 20 ms**. iPhone 13 held sideways: 1,503 frames, median 8.3, p95 9.4, max 10.3, 0 over 20 ms. 266k triangles, 59 to 75 draw calls.
- Hand-fly 80 s: desktop 9,576 frames, median 8.30, p95 9.30, max 16.1, 0 over 20. Mobile 9,578 frames, median 8.30, p95 9.50, max 24.9, **1 over 20 ms**.
- First load, production build to a scratch folder: **about 0.81 MB** (JS 761 KB, or 208 KB gzipped. CSS 34 KB. HTML 10 KB). lil-gui 31 KB loads only for `?debug`. Budget 15 MB: pass.
- Page errors: 0.

## Screenshots (progress/round-18/critic/)

- Fresh loads: L-d-load1..6-seed*-title and -fly4s (fly4s frames show the title overlay still fading, because the shot is taken right after start).
- Features: T-feat-seed*-diagonal*/alley* (shortcut bot in flight). F-d-seed44840-tunnel-enter/inside/leave and -alley-* (desktop). F-m-seed44840-* (iPhone).

## Scripts and logs (progress/round-18/critic-scripts/)

builder.md
# Drone Dash, round 18 builder: route choice and a city that changes

Concern from the round 17 critic: no route choice and nothing new in the world. On the uniform grid every route between two points has the same length. So every leg plays the same, and rush hour changes only the parcels. Two leftovers came first. A one-delivery farm reached Silver through the time-up share. The saved best medal was sometimes lower than the run's medal.

The lead retired the cross-city 2.5 spread target. All other guards stay.

Time box: 01:10 to 03:40 (done at 03:05). Dev server on port 5188, stopped at the end.

**Result in short:** both leftovers are fixed. Every city now has four diagonal boulevards (a diamond across the middle), 10 to 17 alleys and 2 to 7 tunnels, all from the seed. Half of all legs have a shortcut at least 15% shorter than the best grid route. A street bot that takes them is 10.9% faster on those legs. At 60 s two rush lanes light up and hover-vans stream along them. Pads, farms, gates and regressions pass. Ace moved from 9,000 to 10,000 because the shortcut bot reached 9,155.

Short of the target:
- The shortcut bot has 3 charged crashes against 0 for the grid bot. Alley legs are not faster for this bot. Boulevard legs are 14.7% faster (section 4).
- One real-time street run on city 41272 scored 1,440 Bronze. Its two repeats scored Silver (2,076 and 2,373). So street Silver was 11 of 12, the lazy gap failed on that run, and that city's best over worst is 1.65 (section 5).
- The deterministic high-line bot stalled on a roof on seed 130 (0 points). Low over high still passes.

## 1. Leftovers

A. **Silver leak.** The time-up share is the street bonus banked on the leg in progress, paid by the share of the leg flown. It now needs at least 2 deliveries (`RUN.partialMinDrops`). It is also capped at the street bonus the run has paid per delivery so far. So a farmed bank cannot pay more at time-up than an honest drop paid. Code: `Game.timeUp`.

B. **Stale medal.** `Game.endRun` now settles the run's medal from the final score before it saves anything. Points paid at time-up can cross a medal line after the last medal check in flight. Before this fix, the saved best tier then stayed one medal low. The crossing is added to `goals.passList`. There is no fanfare, because the game-over card shows the medal.

Checks (deterministic `capfarm.mjs`, FARMMAX 12, the critic's short-farm case):

| Run | Seed 22 | Seed 58 | Seed 130 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Both legs farmed, 1 delivery | 1,296 Bronze | 1,517 Bronze | 1,639 Bronze |
| Carry farmed, 2 deliveries | 2,015 Silver | 2,297 Silver | 2,021 Silver |

No one-delivery farm reaches Silver (round 17: 2,243 and 2,356). The time-up share paid 0 on every one-delivery run. Two-delivery carry farms still reach Silver, as in rounds 15 to 17. They earn about 1,300 to 1,600 points a minute, below honest play (see the gates).

Saved best medal against the run's medal: see section 5 (MEDAL lines: `goals.tier` equals the medal of the final score in every real-time run).

## 2. Design: three features that make route choice, and a rush hour you can see

All features come from the seed, through their own random stream (`CityFeatures.featureRng`). `?seed=N` is still deterministic. The layout of a seed changes from round 17, because blocks are now cut and the job picker draws one more random number per leg. No feature blocks a street. Each one only opens a new way through the blocks, so the plain grid route still works everywhere and the critic's street bot still flies.

1. **Diagonal boulevards** (kind `diagonal`). Four straight 45-degree avenues cross the whole city, two each way, 88 m apart, so they form a diamond around the middle. Each one is 10 m wide and runs through the middle of every street segment it crosses. That is where the doorsteps are, so pads sit right next to the boulevards. The boulevard clips one corner of each block it passes. Lots that it cuts become stepped terraces (2 m strips), so it has building faces along it. The `facade` flag on those narrow strips lets the slipstream count them as walls, so the boulevard drafts. Look: brick-red paving with a glowing amber dashed centre line. Names: Kestrel Boulevard, Old Tram Way, Copper Diagonal, Harbor Slant, Union Cut, Lumen Parade. A boulevard cuts a diagonal leg by up to 29%.
2. **Alleys** (kind `alley`). In about 40% of ordinary blocks there is a 6 m passage straight through the middle, with walls on both sides. Look: warm cobbles and amber wall lanterns every 5 m. Tight, draftable and a little risky. Names: Lantern Alley, Tinker Lane, Cobble Row, and others.
3. **Tunnels** (kind `tunnel`). Some alleys near the middle of the city have a building bridged over them. There is 7 m of clear space under it, a lit ceiling and a gold sign band at both ends. To use one, fly under the bridge. The side lots are at least 4 floors, so the bridge sits inside a canyon.

Kept clear: trees, lamp posts and other soft props inside a boulevard or an alley mouth are removed. Depots never go on a block that a boulevard clips, because their hangar fills the corners. A boulevard can clip a park. Then only its trees go. A cut lot gets no rooftop pad. It gets a doorstep only on a street face at least 3 m clear of the cut.

**Jobs.** Only about 10% of pad pairs have a 15% shortcut, so few legs get one by chance. The job picker now prefers them. With chance `JOBS.shortcutBias` (0.85), it picks the leg's pad among the pads with a shortcut from the current pad. A shortcut is a feature route at least 15% under the grid route. The pad must still meet the same leg spec: kind, height and distance band, with the band widened one step at most. If no pad qualifies, the leg is picked as before. The first hop is never biased. The round 16 job mix (street drops, a rooftop on every third drop, last call) is unchanged, because the bias only chooses inside the spec.

**Rush hour in the world.** Each city has two rush lanes, one street each way. Before 60 s they are faint amber lane paint and chevrons. At rush hour they light up gold and pulse gently. Then 18 hover-vans stream in from the city edge along them, both ways. They are white and orange delivery vans on a glowing blue hover pad, 3 m up. The vans are scenery: they do not collide, and they stay below the 7 m street line. Diagnostics: `city.rushLanes` (0 to 1).

**Street graph and hooks** (for bots and probes): `window.__GAME__.streetRoute(from, to, features = true, narrowPenalty = 0)` returns the shortest route on the real street graph (roads, alleys, tunnels, boulevards), or on the plain grid with `features = false`. Each end joins the network at its nearest edges, plus its nearest road edges, so a feature can only add options. `features()` lists every feature with name and position. `rushLanes()` lists the lanes. `city.features` in the diagnostics counts the kinds.

**Medal line.** Ace 9,000 to 10,000. The shortcut-taking bot reached 9,155 on one fresh city (12810). The plain street bot got 7,359 there. Bronze, Silver and Gold are unchanged.

## 3. Route choice: results

12 fresh cities from `pick-seeds.mjs` (14 loads with no `?seed`, first 12 used): 89101, 27874, 55752, 43564, 41272, 12810, 42547, 41570, 99586, 49549, 64360, 47096. I picked them after the last game change, so they were not used for tuning. (An earlier set of 12 was used for tuning and then dropped.)

Bots (deterministic, `route-legs18-cut.mjs`): the critic's `route-legs17` street bot, with its route taken from `streetRoute`. CUT=1 takes alleys, tunnels and boulevards. CUT=0 routes on the plain grid graph, so it flies the same corner-to-corner line as route-legs17. Changes for the shortcut bot only: it brakes to 6 m/s into an alley (4.5 m/s on a sharp turn). Inside, it lines up before it speeds up. Under a tunnel it flies 4 m high. An alley or tunnel must save at least 12 m before it takes one. Each leg logs the grid route and the feature route at its start (LEG lines). `pairlegs.py` pairs legs of the two bots by seed, start and end (within 4 m).

| Test | Needed | Result | Pass |
|---|---|---|---|

## 4. What is short of the target, and why

- **Crashes.** The shortcut bot hit walls 3 times in 26.8 minutes. The grid bot did not hit any. Two hits were at the mouth of a tunnel at 4 m. One was near a doorstep after a boulevard turn. Earlier versions of the bot turned into alleys at 11 to 14 m/s and crashed 7 times. Braking to 5 m/s and lining up first brought that down to 0 to 3, but it also made alley legs slower than the grid. That is the price of a narrow alley for this bot. The alleys stay 6 m wide, because the lead asked for them to be tight and risky.
- **Alley legs are not faster for this bot.** It is 5% slower on them. The bot slows to 4.5 to 6 m/s at the mouth, and an alley saves only 10 to 30 m. A human who carries speed into an alley gains more. That is the skill the feature asks for, but this bot does not show it.
- **One city has no shortcut legs** (42547, 0 of 8). Its pads near the boulevards are few. The bias found no candidate inside the leg spec.

critic.md
# Drone Dash: round 17 critic report

**Verdict:** The ending is now fair. The cliff at the third drop is gone. Each delivery adds a similar amount, and a run that runs out of clock with a parcel aboard finishes it in overtime. Every gate and regression passes except one: the cross-city ratio is 2.78 (target 2.5). I recommend retiring that target. The street bot causes most of the spread, not the city. The game's biggest limit is now content, not balance: on a uniform grid every leg is the same drive, so there is no route to choose and little to discover after a few runs.

Build tested: working tree at commit 064109c plus the uncommitted round 17 changes. Dev server port 5188 (stopped at the end). Scripts are copies of round 16 in `critic-scripts/`. Their output folder is the relative `../critic/`, so the copies write here with no edit. New scripts are listed at the end.

## Round 16 gap (the run ends on a knife edge at the third drop): closed, with one smaller edge left

12 fresh random cities from `pick-seeds.mjs` (loads with no `?seed`), none found in any builder file: 55211, 52809, 95387, 16805, 14523, 15493, 88700, 68665, 65188, 25215, 83341, 61719. Real time, one run at a time.

Round 16 was 1,695 to 9,066 (5.35) with two Bronze cities and same-city swings up to 2.0. Now it is 2,495 to 6,927, no Bronze, and same-city swings at most 1.38.

What changed in the shape of a run:
- **Score per drop is flat now.** Real time: 3 drops about 3,050, 4 drops 2,495 to 4,268, 5 drops 5,045 to 6,354, 6 drops 5,094 to 6,972. Each drop adds about 1,000 to 1,100. Round 16: each drop roughly doubled the score.
- **Overtime almost always wins.** 16 of 16 overtime windows were finished by the street bots (real time), and 11 of 12 by the lazy bot. Windows were 8 to 15 s for 12 to 55 m left. Bots used 1.3 to 10 s of them.
- **The one edge left is at the pickup.** The clock can run out while flying to a pickup, and then there is no overtime. That happened in 8 of 20 real-time street runs: 55211, 95387, 14523, 83341 and 4 repeats. Each time the open leg was a short pickup leg of 26 to 38 m of street. Those runs lose a last-call drop. With a parcel aboard, overtime gives that drop. Its value is the overtime drops seen: 328 to 1,159, mean about 700, so 10 to 20 percent of the run. It is a step now, not a cliff. Examples: 55211 deterministic 3,512 (ended in overtime) and the same run with screenshot pauses 3,012 (ended 4 m short of the pickup). 68665 on iPhone ended 22 m short of a pickup, 249 points short of Gold (E-m-seed68665-over).

## The spread: city or bot? Mostly the bot

Evidence from the deterministic leg logs (`legs-*.log`, summary script `legs-summary.py`):
- **The cities are close.** The first three pickup and drop cycles are 586 to 696 m of street on all 12 cities (1.19 times).
- **A beeline bot sees that same small spread.** The high-line bot flies those cycles in 48.5 to 57.9 s (1.19 times). Time tracks distance.
- **The street bot does not.** It flies them in 70.4 to 98.0 s (1.39 times). Its average speed on the legs varies by city from 6.4 to 8.3 m/s. Pickup legs are the slow ones (5.2 to 7.4 m/s). They start at a drop pad. The bot climbs to 26 m to leave an off-road pad. Then it brakes to 7 m/s at every corner.
- **Two cities make it plain.** 55211 against 65188: the beeline bot scores 3,485 and 3,724 (the same). The street bot scores about 3,050 and about 6,700 (2.2 times). With faster corners (11 m/s), 55211 barely moves (3,628) and 65188 jumps to 8,232. So 55211's corners and pad exits are what slow this bot down.
- **A clock fed by drops amplifies it.** A run that is 15 percent slower earns fewer drops. So it also earns less clock, and it gets fewer drops again. That is how a 1.2 to 1.4 times difference in pace becomes 2.2 times in score.

**Is it a problem for a human player?** Not much. A human corners and leaves pads in their own way, not the bot's way. The pure city difference (about 1.2 times in distance) is normal for a game with random maps. Players who want to compare scores fairly have the daily city, where everyone flies the same map. On random cities the medal bands are wide (Silver 2,000 to 4,500, so 2.25 times). The street bot lands Silver or Gold on every city, and the lazy bot lands Bronze everywhere. That is the result that matters.

**Recommendation:** accept the spread and move on. Retire the "street best over worst at most 2.5" target. It now mostly measures how this one bot takes corners. Three rounds went into it. Do not build medal lines scaled to each city's par now. That adds a system to explain to the player. The builder can only tune it against the same bot. Keep these guards for future rounds instead:
  - street Silver or better 12 of 12
  - lazy Bronze or below 12 of 12
  - no bot at Ace
  - lazy at least 300 below the worst street run
  - same-city noise at most 1.4.

 Par medals can wait. A leaderboard on random cities is the point where the spread starts to matter.

## Exploits of overtime and the time-up share

- **No-delivery farms: all 0.** 8 farm-probe runs, farm-loop, and 15 smart-farm runs (near, line, pickup, pickupline, spendpickup) on seeds 22, 58 and 130. Overtime does not start without a parcel, and the time-up share needs one delivery.
- **Standard carry farm (gate): pass.** Capfarm with a farm phase of up to 60 s. Points a minute over the 3 seeds: honest 1,838, carry 781 (**0.42**), both 0 on two seeds. The carry farm on seed 22 still scores Silver (3,151) with 2 drops, as in rounds 15 and 16. A parcel held past 1.6 times its par gets no overtime and no time-up share, so this farm gains nothing from the new rules.
- **Short farm phases (new probe, `otfarm17.sh`): a real leak, but small.** With a short farm phase (12 s), the leg stays inside the schedule window. Then the time-up share pays the farmed bank by the share of the leg flown.
  - Farming both legs with **one delivery** scores 2,243 (seed 130) and 2,356 (seed 22), above the 2,000 Silver line. The time-up share pays 845 and 793 of that. The best lazy honest run is 1,792 Bronze.
  - Carry with 12 s farm phases scores 2,345 to 3,537 with 2 to 3 drops. That is 0.85 of honest points a minute, but 0.72 of the honest score per run, so farming still loses to delivering.
  - Bug found on the way: the medal state is not updated after the time-up share. On the two one-delivery runs above, the game reports tier Bronze at a score over 2,000. The game-over card computes the medal from the score, but the saved best tier comes from the stale state.
- **Overtime cannot be chained or farmed.** It happens once a run. It adds no clock and gives no new job. It pays the bank by the share of the leg flown at the start of overtime, no more.
- **Overtime cuts a bank the player earned honestly.** The bank from the pickup leg rides on the parcel. When overtime starts soon after a pickup, the share of the drop leg flown is low, so most of that bank is cut. 52809 (real time): bank 205, share 16 percent, paid 20, cut 185. The pop says "street bonus +20 (16%)" with no reason given.

## As a player (desktop and iPhone 13 held sideways, touch)

- **Is overtime exciting and readable?** Readable, yes. The timer turns into a gold "OT 11" pill. An "Overtime" banner, a horn, and the top music layer follow. The finish pays a big "+525 Made it! overtime delivery" (E-d-seed14523-ot-madeit). On iPhone the gold pill is the clearest thing on screen (E-m-seed52809-ot-start). Exciting, only a little. Overtime was won 16 of 16 times by the street bots and 11 of 12 by the lazy bot, with seconds to spare. It feels like a lap of honour, not a last sprint.
- **Messages collide at the busiest moment.** Overtime often starts just after a pickup. The "Rush order!" pop then lands on top of the overtime banner. It hides the banner line "11 s to finish this delivery · no new jobs" (E-d-seed14523-ot-start). A rush order also replaces the "Last call!" pop, so the player is never told that the job adds no time (E-d-seed88700-lastcall). On iPhone, the last-call pop did not show at all in our shot (E-m-seed52809-lastcall).
- **Is the ending fair now?** Mostly, yes. A run no longer ends with a fresh rooftop job you cannot finish. A parcel aboard always gets a fair try. The game-over card says "Time's up" even after "Made it!", which undersells the finish. The ending that still stings is the clock running out 10 to 30 m from a pickup. Nothing on screen says why that run got no overtime (E-d-seed95387-clock0).
- **Medal ladder.** Bronze 1,000, Silver 2,000, Gold 4,500, Ace 9,000. A steady pilot gets Silver or Gold. Gold now feels reachable and earned. Ace is far, which is right.
- **Mobile title:** the city buttons still look about 25 px tall on iPhone 13 held sideways (m-h01-title). On one iPhone shot the nav distance label sits on the "FLY" stick label (E-m-seed52809-lastcall).

## Whole game, against the best polished indie arcade flying and delivery games

- **First 10 seconds:** strong. A warm toy city in four light moods, a clear title, a quick first payout.
- **Onboarding:** good. First payout in 6 to 7 s on both devices.
- **Game feel:** still the best part. Momentum, banking, the camera lean, wall drafting.
- **Core loop:** pick up, draft, deliver, chain. Now balanced. The street line beats the beeline, the score is flat per drop, and farms do not pay.
- **Ending:** fair now, with a short overtime and a part-pay of the bank.
- **Art and audio:** coherent and finished. Adaptive music with a real overtime layer.
- **UI:** clean in normal flight. Busy at the end of a run. There, four rules (last call, rush order, overtime, bank share) speak in the same few seconds.
- **Depth and replay:** this is where it falls behind. The best games of this kind give each run choices and surprises: shortcuts through gaps and arches, a risky line under a bridge, districts that fly differently, set pieces that change mid-run. Here every city is the same street grid with new colours. On a grid every monotone route has the same length, so there is no route to choose. The skill is cornering and staying near walls, and after three or four runs a player has seen all the city has. Rush hour adds orders but nothing changes in the world.

## Single biggest remaining gap: no route choice and nothing new in the world

**The concern.** The loop is now balanced and fair, so the limit is what a run asks of the player. Every leg is a corner-to-corner drive on a uniform grid. Because all monotone grid routes are the same length, the "street line" is one choice repeated, not a decision. Cities differ in light and building mix, not in how they fly. A run at 2:30 looks and plays like a run at 0:30. That caps replay pull below the best arcade flyers, where reading a shortcut is half the fun.

**Evidence:**
- On all 12 cities, the street bot's legs are 45 to 200 m of grid with the same corners. The only city-to-city difference that matters is how many corners and pad exits a leg has.
- The beeline bot crosses the same cycles in 49 to 58 s against 70 to 98 s for the street bot. But it scores less (2,663 to 5,122), because the only alternative to the grid is flying over it, with no draft.
- Mood shots across rounds 16 and 17: four light moods on one grid, same props, no landmark to steer by.

**Acceptance test** (measurable, the build is the builder's choice):
1. On 12 fresh cities, at least 1 in 3 legs has a draftable alternative to the plain grid route. The alternative is at least 15 percent shorter. Examples: an alley, an arch, a passage through a block, a gap between towers, a low bridge. Verify with a probe that measures the route length of the alternative against the best grid route for each leg.
2. A routed bot that takes those alternatives beats the plain street bot by at least 10 percent in leg time on those legs. It must not have more charged crashes (deterministic, the same 12 cities).
3. Six fresh loads show at least 3 kinds of feature a player can name. Each is visible in the title shot or the first 10 s of flight.
4. Something in the world changes at rush hour (60 s) that a screenshot can show. Examples: traffic, a closed street, a new open gap.
5. No regressions. The round 17 guards above still pass. No-delivery farms score 0. The carry farm stays under 0.5. Low over high is at least 0.85. The breakdown is exact. Crash-classify shows 0 pad lip hits. Hand-fly first payout comes within 10 s.

## Other gaps (ranked)

1. **The end-of-run messages collide and do not explain themselves.** The Rush order pop covers the overtime banner (E-d-seed14523-ot-start). A rush order hides "Last call!" (E-d-seed88700-lastcall). "Street bonus +20 (16%)" gives no reason. The card says "Time's up" after "Made it!". Test: in 12 full runs on desktop and iPhone held sideways, no two centre messages are on screen at once. Every last-call pickup shows "no time bonus", including rush orders. Any bank cut says why in plain words. A run that ends on an overtime delivery has its own card title.
2. **The pickup edge.** 8 of 20 real-time street runs ran out of clock 26 to 38 m from a pickup. They got no overtime. Each lost a final drop worth 330 to 1,160. Test: at most 3 of 12 real-time street runs end in the pickup phase within 40 m. Or: before the clock reaches 0, the screen says why there will be no overtime.
3. **One delivery can earn Silver, and the medal state goes stale.** A 12 s farm on both legs with one delivery scores 2,243 and 2,356. Of that, 793 to 845 comes from the time-up share. The tier stays Bronze in the game state. Test: the capfarm "both" mode with FARMMAX 12 on seeds 22, 58 and 130 stays under 2,000. After every game over, the tier state equals the medal of the final score.
4. **Overtime is too safe to thrill.** It was won 27 of 28 times by bots, with 2 to 10 s to spare. Test: the street bot finishes 60 to 85 percent of overtime windows on 12 cities. No window is impossible: it gives at least the route left at 9 m/s.
5. **Mobile title and labels.** City buttons about 25 px tall on iPhone 13 held sideways (asked for 40 px since round 15). The nav distance label overlaps the "FLY" label. Test: buttons at least 40 px tall. No HUD label overlaps another in a full mobile run.

## Performance

Headless Chromium caps at 120 Hz (8.3 ms).
- Hand-fly desktop 1280x720, 80 s: 9,578 frames, **median 8.30 ms, p95 9.70, max 10.4, 0 over 20 ms**.
- Hand-fly iPhone 13 held sideways, touch: 9,579 frames, **median 8.30, p95 9.60, max 10.4, 0 over 20 ms**.
- First load, production build to a scratch folder: **about 0.79 MB** (JS 747 KB, 200 KB gzipped. CSS 34 KB. HTML 10 KB). lil-gui 31 KB only for `?debug`. Budget 15 MB: pass.
- Page errors: 0 in every run.

# Drone Dash, round 17 builder: the ending and the shape of the score

Concern from the round 16 critic: the run ends on a knife edge at the third drop. Each extra delivery roughly doubled the score. A run 18 m short at time-up lost all of its banked street bonus. The same street bot scored 1,695 to 9,066 on 12 cities (5.35 times).

**Result in short:** the ending is no longer a cliff. A parcel aboard at 0 s gets a short overtime. A late pickup gets a short job. No run in the acceptance set lost a banked bonus at a pad's edge. The breakdown is exact and the farms still score 0. But the spread across cities is still too wide. The street bot scored 1,774 to 8,006 in real time (4.5 times, target 2.5), and one city is Bronze. The cause is now run length (3 drops against 7), not the ending.

Time box: 21:26 to 23:26. Dev server on port 5188, stopped at the end.

## 1. Where the doubling came from (round 16 numbers)

Round 16 breakdowns of the street bot, from `round-16/critic-scripts/acc-low.log`:

| City | Drops | Deliveries | Fast | Combo | Street bonus | Lost at time-up |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 80258 | 3 | 741 | 225 | 982 | 1,934 | 1,139 |
| 40443 | 5 | 1,247 | 675 | 2,470 | 3,113 | 950 |

Causes:
- **Combo.** The steps were x1.5, x2, x2.5, x3 and x3.5. The combo line grew from 327 a drop (3 drops) to 494 a drop (5 drops). So each drop paid more than the last.
- **Street bonus lost at time-up.** The bonus was about 650 a drop, flat. But the clock ran out with a parcel aboard in most runs. Then the bank on it (often 700 to 1,100) went to 0, even 13 m from the pad.
- **Run length snowballs.** A drop gives 5 + distance/11 s (up to 20 s). The slow clock gives up to 8 s a leg. A bot that flies a cycle in 25 s earns about 30 s a cycle. Its run goes on until the drop decay catches it (6 to 8 drops). A bot that needs 35 s a cycle earns about 21 s. It stops at drop 3. This is the biggest factor that is left (section 4).
- **Rooftop on drop 3 with no time check.** A pickup with 1 s left got a 158 m rooftop job.

## 2. Design (what changed)

1. **Overtime.** The clock hits 0 with a parcel aboard: overtime starts (once a run). Its length fits the parcel in hand: street route left / 6 m/s + 4 s, from 8 to 15 s. The timer turns gold with an "OT 12" count and a quick double pulse. A banner says "Overtime: 12 s to finish this delivery, no new jobs". A three-note horn plays. The music holds its last-10-s section at full intensity with the lead layer on. Overtime cannot chain. The overtime delivery adds no clock and no new job. A "Made it!" beat follows, then the game-over card. Overtime has no slow clock. A crash still costs seconds.
2. **Overtime pays the bank by the share flown.** The overtime delivery pays its points as normal. Its street bonus pays the share of the leg flown at time-up (street route left plus any climb). So a parcel near its pad keeps nearly all of it. A bank farmed far from the drop does not cash in.
3. **Time-up share.** Sometimes the clock runs out for good (no parcel aboard, or overtime spent). Then the street bonus banked on the current leg pays by the share of the leg flown. It has its own game-over row: "Last leg, 62% flown at time-up". This needs at least one delivery in the run. So a no-delivery farm still scores 0.
4. **On schedule only.** Overtime and the time-up share need a leg on schedule. That is a leg flown in at most 1.6 times its par (route / 9 + 7 s). A parcel that sat aboard while its bank was farmed gets neither. This rule keeps the carry farm low (section 3).
5. **Last call.** A parcel picked up with under 22 s left gets a short drop. The drop fits the time left plus 8 s at 7 m/s (at least 55 m). It is at street level, never a rooftop. A last-call drop pays points as normal but adds no clock. So the end of a run is a set of short jobs on a falling clock. It is not a cliff. Short legs also cannot pay for themselves forever. A "Last call! Short job, no time bonus" pop shows on pickup. After a drop, the next pickup is never further than the clock left at 7 m/s (at least 30 m).
6. **Flatter score.** Combo step 0.5 to 0.15 (x1.15 to x1.75 at five, and the HUD shows two decimals). Street bonus pace weight max 2.5 to 1.8. The leg cap stays 7 points a metre. (I tried 3.5. Then the carry farm filled its share fast and delivered like an honest pilot.)
7. **Shorter snowball.** Slow-clock budget 8 to 5 s a leg (a fast run earned all of it on every leg). Drop time bonus decay 0.035 to 0.06 a drop. Start time 50 to 56 s, so a slow but steady run keeps its third drop.
8. **First payout.** The intro meter is 3 m (was 4). It counts from 3 m/s (was 4). This is for the mobile hand-fly first payout, which was 9.9 s.
9. **Medal lines.** Silver 2,500 to 2,000, Gold 6,000 to 4,500, Ace 10,000 to 9,000.

Kept: the street bonus (banked, paid on delivery) and the slow clock with its budget per leg. Rush hour at 60 s. The round 16 job spec (a rooftop every third drop, except on last call). The daily city, the bloom clamps in `ObjectiveMarker.ts` and all debug hooks.

New diagnostics: `ending` (overtime, finished, lastCall, overtimeSeconds, partial, partialShare, legRoute). Breakdown fields `partial`, `overtimeSeconds` and `overtimeDrop`. `partial` is a part of `slip`, so drops + fast + combo + slip still equals the score. Also `audio.music.overtime`, and score log entries `overtime`, `otshare`, `otcut`, `otdrop` and `partial`.

Tried and dropped: a "clutch" time bonus (more drop time at a low clock). It did not help the slow cities. They stop on a leg, not at a drop with little time left. A decay of 0.08 to 0.09 cut the top a little but also cost slow cities a drop.

## 3. Results

12 fresh cities from 14 loads with no `?seed` (`builder-scripts/pick-seeds.log`). None was used in round 16. I tuned on the round 16 cities and also checked these 12 deterministically before the real-time runs. So they are not fully blind. Real-time scripts ran one at a time: `route-play-rt-x-m-esc.mjs` (street) and `balance-probe-m-esc.mjs` (lazy, CRUISE=10, NOBOOST=1). Deterministic: `route-legs17.mjs` (route-legs16 plus log-only lines for breakdown and ending).

| City | Mood, parks | Street (real time) | Drops, run | Overtime | Lazy | Lazy drops | Street, deterministic | Det. ending |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32124 | Rose dusk, 3 | 5,877 Gold | 5, 149 s | none | 1,595 | 3 | 6,031 (6) | overtime drop |
| 14545 | Golden hour, 2 | 2,327 Silver | 3, 98 s | none | 1,031 | 2 | 2,811 (3) | overtime drop |
| 97836 | Rose dusk, 4 | 3,089 Silver | 4, 134 s | 9.7 s, delivered | 1,446 | 3 | 3,199 (4) | overtime drop |
| 48947 | Hazy noon, 2 | 2,945 Silver | 4, 123 s | none | 1,245 | 3 | 2,823 (3) | pickup leg, 56 m short, bank 0 |
| 96635 | Rose dusk, 4 | 2,975 Silver | 3, 105 s | none | 711 | 2 | 2,674 (3) | pickup leg, 20 m short, bank 0 |
| 97214 | Rose dusk, 3 | 4,523 Gold | 4, 127 s | none | 1,491 | 3 | 6,546 (6) | pickup leg, 37 m short, bank 0 |
| 79278 | Hazy noon, 2 | 6,710 Gold | 6, 167 s | none | 1,643 | 3 | 6,902 (6) | pickup leg, 19 m short, bank 0 |
| 59437 | Bright morning, 2 | 4,936 Gold | 5, 132 s | 7.0 s, delivered | 1,634 | 3 | 2,836 (4) | overtime drop |
| 29130 | Hazy noon, 2 | 8,006 Gold | 7, 183 s | 9.3 s, delivered | 1,535 | 3 | 8,277 (7) | overtime drop |
| 30593 | Golden hour, 3 | 5,197 Gold | 5, 138 s | none | 1,356 | 3 | 4,904 (5) | pickup leg, 30 m short, bank 17 |
| 32429 | Hazy noon, 3 | 3,006 Silver | 4, 123 s | 4.2 s, delivered | 1,528 | 3 | 2,957 (4) | overtime drop |
| 93049 | Bright morning, 4 | 1,774 Bronze | 3, 106 s | 9.0 s, delivered | 896 | 2 | 2,667 (3) | pickup leg, 24 m short, bank 0 |

| Test | Needed | Result | Pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| Street Silver or better | 12 of 12 | 11 of 12 (93049 1,774 Bronze) | No |
| Lazy Bronze or below | 12 of 12 | 12 of 12 (best 1,643) | Yes |
| No Ace from any bot | none | none (best real time 8,006, deterministic 8,277, Ace 9,000) | Yes |
| Best lazy at least 300 below worst street | 300 | 1,643 against 1,774: 131 | No |
| Street best / worst | at most 2.5 | 8,006 / 1,774 = 4.51 (deterministic 8,277 / 2,667 = 3.10) | No |
| Same city, 3 runs, best / worst at most 1.4 | 4 cities | 2 cities, 2 runs each: 93049 1,774 and 1,681 (1.06). 29130 8,006 and 7,800 (1.03) | Not fully run (2 of 4 cities, 2 of 3 runs) |
| Deterministic runs ending within 30 m of the next stop | at most 3, or keep half the bank | 6 end on an overtime delivery at the pad (bank paid, minus the share cut). 4 end on a pickup leg 19 to 30 m short, with 0, 0, 0 and 17 points banked | Yes on the bank clause (3 of the 4 have nothing banked; 30593 keeps 1 of 17) |

Breakdown: bdOk and domOk true in all 24 real-time runs. The game-over rows add up, including "Last leg" and the overtime time line.

Where the runs end now: in real time, 5 of 12 street runs and 8 of 12 lazy runs end with an overtime delivery. No run ended with a banked bonus lost at a pad's edge. Overtime cuts were small (101 to 295 points, from the share rule).

## 4. Gates (seeds 22, 58, 130) and regressions

Real-time gate runs were not run (time box). Deterministic stand-ins:
- **Low / high (deterministic, route-legs17):** low 4,032 + 3,926 + 4,162 = 12,120. High 3,948 + 4,189 + 4,093 = 12,230. Ratio 0.99 (needed 0.85). Pass. The high line now makes 7 to 8 drops at about 520 a drop. The low line makes 4 to 5 at about 900.
- **No-delivery farms:** all 30 (farm-probe 8, farm-loop, smart-farm near, line, pickup, pickupline, spendpickup) score 0.
- **Capfarm:** honest 1,878, 1,861 and 1,772 points a minute (5,511). Carry 0, 1,603 and 0 (1,603): 0.29 of honest (needed under 0.5). Pass. Both: 441, 1,123 and 0. Before the on-schedule rule, the carry farm was at 0.64 to 0.72: it farmed, then finished in overtime.
- **Breakdown exact:** yes in every run (see above).
- **Rush hour at 60 s:** the ESC lines in acc-low show `startedAt` 60 in every run that passed 60 s.
- **Hand-fly first payout:** desktop 6.3 s (was 7.2), mobile 7.1 s (was 9.9). 0 page errors.
- **Frame time (hand-fly, headless 120 Hz cap):** desktop p95 9.5 ms, max 10.4, 0 over 20 ms. Mobile p95 9.6 ms, max 10.4.
- **Build:** `npm run build` passes. First load about 0.79 MB (JS 746 KB, CSS 34 KB).
- **Crash-classify:** only an early run with an older config, under load from parallel jobs. 12 m: 24 charged, 0 hop-like, 5 near the target. 20 m: 13 charged, 1 hop-like (seed 130: the wall top was 3.6 m above the drone, so it is a real wall). No flight or collision code changed this round. Not re-run on the final build.
- **Flat-frame probe, music-run analysis, real-time gate runs:** not run.

## 5. What is left (honest view)

The ending is fixed. The spread is not. The street bot makes 3 drops on some cities and 7 on others, because its leg times differ per city (pickups 8 to 10 s on 29130, 16 to 18 s on 93049 and 14545). The bot climbs to 26 m to leave pads off the road edge, and that costs it more on some cities. A fast bot earns more clock per cycle than it spends. A slow one earns less. The decay and the smaller budget cut the snowball from 8 drops to 7, but the gap is still about 2 times in drops and 1.5 times in points a drop. The next fix would be on run length itself. Options: a fixed shift length with the clock as a soft limit, or a time bonus based on par rather than distance, so a slow leg earns as much as a fast one.

Small fix at the end: the overtime delivery now says "Made it! Overtime delivery" in the delivery pop, not in a second banner, and the pill says "Run complete". Known issue: an overtime banner from less than 3 s before still overlaps the delivery pop (`builder-shots/OT-madeit-d.jpg`, a teleport test). In normal play overtime lasts longer than the banner. This last change came after the real-time runs. It touches only the HUD text.
