# Drone Dash, round 13 critic report

**Verdict:** The slow clock no longer pays you to skip deliveries: farm runs now end in under 65 s. But the score still does. A pilot who never touches a parcel scores Silver every time, and per minute scores about twice as much as a pilot who delivers. The lazy pilot also reached Silver again in one of two passes.

Build tested: the working tree at commit cc95720 plus the uncommitted `src/game/config.ts` change (Silver 1,775 to 1,600). Dev server port 5188. Scripts are copies of round 12 in `critic-scripts/`. Their output folder is the relative `../critic/`, so the copies write here with no edit. New scripts: `smart-farm.mjs`, `clock-badge13.mjs`, `farm8.sh`, `queue13.sh`.

## Round 12 gap (the slow clock paid you not to deliver): closed as written

| Check | Needed | Result | Pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| farm-probe, 8 rows from round 12 | no Gold, none over 150 s | all **Silver**, 1,965 to 4,100. All 58 s long (round 12: up to 312 s and 21,935) | Yes |
| Slow clock with 0 deliveries | at most 20 s | **8.0 s** in every farm-probe row | Yes |
| farm-loop seed 22 | same | 1,820 Silver, 58 s, 8 s of slow clock, 1 crash | Yes |
| My smarter farms (15 runs) | same | best **4,390 Silver in 64 s** (110 below Gold). Most slow clock: **16.0 s** | Yes |

My smarter farms (`smart-farm.mjs`, seeds 22, 58, 130, 0 deliveries in all 21 runs):
- `near`: laps the block that holds the pickup, so it often flies toward the target. 655 to 1,345. Slow clock 4.5 to 7.3 s. The small block and its corners keep the pace down.
- `line`: flies the street through the target toward it, U-turns 15 m short. 1,570 to 2,690. 8 s.
- `pickup`, `pickupline`: teleports onto the pickup at the start (this saves the flight there, so it is an upper bound), then farms. Up to 3,955. Only 8 s of slow clock, because the pickup refills the budget to 8 s and does not stack.
- `spendpickup`: the strongest. It farms a long straight until the start budget is spent, then teleports onto the pickup to refill the budget, then farms again. **16.0 s** of slow clock, 61 to 65 s runs, 1,870 to **4,390**. This matches the code: at most 2 budgets of 8 s with no delivery.

So the clock exploit is gone. The rule works as the builder intended.

What is left: the points. A wall hug at cruise pays a slip payout about every 2 s, up to 145 points each, with no parcel. That is about **3,400 points a minute** on average (8 farm-probe rows, best 4,240). The routed street bot makes **1,900 a minute** and the roof bot **1,850**. On seed 58 both farm rows (2,650 and 4,100) beat both street runs (1,792 and 1,837). The 4,100 row also beats both roof runs (4,078). See the biggest gap below.

The margin rule fails, and no line can pass it. The best lazy run (1,728) and the worst standard street run (1,792) are only **64 points apart**. A line with 150 points on each side needs a gap of 300. Moving Silver again will not fix this.

Many runs sit within a single delivery of a line. A drop is worth about 300 to 600 with its fast bonus and combo. These runs are: lazy seed 22 B (its second drop made Silver), lazy seed 130, and both low seed 58 runs. Also four high runs short of Gold by 421 to 493, and the desktop journey short of Ace by 393. One parcel decides nearly every medal.

## Clock rule readability

Shots: `d-badge13-*`, `m-badge13-*` (test API, title overlay faded first), and real play in `d-j22-h05-low-payout-chain.jpg`, `m-j22-h05-low-payout-chain.jpg`.

- **What the badge says.** "CLOCK FROZEN · 7S" while drafting toward the target. "SLOW CLOCK SPENT" in muted white after 8.0 s of use. "SLOW CLOCK: WRONG WAY" about 1 s after you turn away. All three switch at the right time.
- **Mobile (iPhone 13 held sideways):** readable. The dark pill sits on the timer's lower edge.
- **Desktop 1280x720:** still **9.9 px text, 13 px tall**. If you look for it in real play, you can read it. You will not notice it change while you fly. In the test-API shots the top of the text sits under the timer's edge.
- **Too many seconds on screen.** Look at one frame. The timer says 0:31. The badge says 7S (budget left). The payout pop says "CLOCK +2S" (clock gained). That is three numbers in seconds near the top centre, with three meanings. Nothing explains that the 7S is a budget that a pickup or drop refills.
- **Fair or fussy?** Fair in effect. An honest street pilot still banks 14 to 42 s of slow clock a run (round 12: 14 to 44 s), so normal play barely changed. "WRONG WAY" is fair: on a street grid an honest route almost never heads away. But it is fussy to read. The rule now has a direction test, a pace test and a per-leg budget, and the only tutorial is a 40-word tagline. A player feels one thing: "when I fly low, the clock sometimes stops". That is enough. The badge text adds little.

## Whole game, as a player

Compared with the best polished indie arcade flying and delivery games I know.

- **First 10 seconds.** Strong. A warm golden-hour city seen from above, a bold logo, the medal ladder, a sound prompt. The tagline is now three sentences of rules. Good games say one verb here.
- **Onboarding.** Good in action. The first payout came 3.2 s after the first draft on desktop (7.1 s into the run) and 4.0 s on touch (8.4 s). The hint "Faster & closer to walls fills it faster" shows at the right moment. Weak in words: medals, combo, fast drops, chain, hug, boost, slow clock, budget and wrong way are all live in the first run.
- **Core loop.** Pick up, fly, drop, keep the combo, draft on the way. If you play it straight, it works. But the two halves pay separately, and the drafting half pays more. A player who learns that hugging a wall beats delivering stops playing a delivery game.
- **Game feel.** Still the best part: momentum, bank, a camera that leans, fair crashes with a clear "-3s".
- **Art.** Coherent, warm, finished low-poly. The city is the same city on every page load (default seed 7). Within a session the parcel order changes, but the streets do not.
- **Audio.** Adaptive and clean. Chain 0 to 3 goes from intensity 0.34 to 0.85 and from 1 to 4 layers. The final section starts at 9.96 to 9.99 s left. 0 late notes, 0 resyncs, 0 errors.
- **UI.** Clean and on-style. The payout pop still sits on the drone, on desktop and on touch.
- **Difficulty curve and run length.** Runs last 1:30 to 2:50 for good pilots and about 1:05 for a lazy one. That is a good arcade length. Nothing changes inside a run except leg distance: no new hazard, no traffic in the air, no rush hour, no weather.
- **Game over and restart.** Clear. The card adds up exactly and tells the clock story ("50 s start +74 s drops +43.4 s slipstream"). "Fly again" is quick.
- **Replay pull.** Medals and best score. That pull depends on the medals meaning something, and today Silver goes to a pilot who never delivers.

## Single biggest remaining gap: score does not need parcels

**The concern.** Slipstream payouts score on their own, with or without a parcel. A tight wall hug at cruise pays 45 to 145 points about every 2 s. Deliveries pay about 300 to 600 each, every 25 to 35 s. So the best way to score per minute is to hug a wall and ignore the parcels. The round 13 fix capped the clock that drafting buys. It did not touch the points.

**Evidence (this round, dev server 5188):**
- farm-probe, 8 rows, 0 deliveries: **Silver 8 of 8**, 1,965 to 4,100 in 58 s. About 3,400 points a minute on average, 4,240 at best.
- smart-farm spendpickup, 0 deliveries: up to **4,390, 110 short of Gold**.
- Routed bots that deliver: street 1,897 to 1,917 a minute, roof 1,845 to 1,857 a minute. The farm scores **1.8 to 2.2 times** as much per minute.
- On seed 58 the farm (2,650 to 4,100) beats both street runs (1,792, 1,837).
- The same split breaks the medal ladder from below. The lazy pilot and the street pilot sit 64 points apart. Both earn a large share of their score from payouts that do not depend on delivering well. No Silver line can sit 150 points from both.
- Slipstream is 42 to 48% of a street run's score (2,570 of 6,532, 1,875 of 3,915).

**Why it matters most.** Thirteen rounds tuned lines and rates around this split. Each fix moves the hole. While drafting pays separately from delivering, the medals measure wall hugging as much as courier play. This is the one gap that stops the core loop from being one loop.

**A direction (not tested).** Make drafting pay through the parcel. For example, slip payouts on a leg go into a "tip" on the carried parcel, shown on the parcel or the objective pill. The tip is paid on delivery, multiplied by the combo. If time runs out, the tip is lost. Payouts can still refill boost at once, so drafting still feels good right away. With no parcel, drafting gives boost only.

**Acceptance test** (dev server 5188, SIMT 600, the scripts in `critic-scripts/`):
1. Every 0-delivery run scores under **1,000** (Bronze): farm-probe (all 8 round 12 rows), farm-loop seed 22, smart-farm `near`, `line`, `pickupline` and `spendpickup` on seeds 22, 58 and 130.
2. A 0-delivery farm scores at most **0.5 times** the standard low bot's points a minute.
3. The round 10 test passes in two passes each. Low / high total at least 0.85. Low Silver 3 of 3 and Gold at least 1. High Silver at least 2 of 3. Lazy Bronze or below. No route bot at Ace. Breakdown exact.
4. The best lazy run and the worst standard low run are at least **300 points apart**, and Silver sits at least 150 points from both.
5. hug-probe still pays a wall hug at least 2 times the centre at 9 m/s. The first payout still comes within 10 s of the first draft, on desktop and on touch.
6. medal-journey stays below Ace on desktop and mobile.

## Other gaps (ranked)

1. **The lazy pilot reaches Silver.** 1,728 on seed 22 in one of two passes, with 0.8 s of slow clock. Silver was moved to 1,600 to fit a lazy run that missed a drop. Test: lazy Bronze or below in two passes (item 3 and 4 above).
2. **The city is the same on every load, and a run never changes.** Default seed 7. No escalation inside a run. Test: a fresh page load gives a different layout or district at least 2 times in 3. A daily city with its own best also passes. Something new appears in the second minute of a run in 3 of 3 bot runs. Examples: traffic drones, a rush-hour headwind, a moving pickup.
3. **Three "seconds" numbers at the top of the screen.** Timer, budget badge and "CLOCK +2S" in the payout pop. The desktop badge is 9.9 px. Test: badge text at least 12 px on desktop. In a full hand-fly run, at most one seconds figure other than the timer is on screen at any time.
4. **The payout pop sits on the drone.** Desktop and touch, see the h05 shots. Test: in a full run on both, the pop never overlaps the drone's screen box.
5. **One parcel decides most medals.** 10 of 20 bot and journey results sit within one delivery of a line. High seed 130 moved 1,068 points between passes. Test: after the scoring fix, at most 3 of the 18 bot runs within 300 points of a line.

## Regressions: none found

- **Lazy / standard low, score a minute** (at most 0.8): pass A 748 / 1,897 = **0.39**, pass B 986 / 1,917 = **0.51**.
- **Hug probe** (seed 22, roads -22, 22, 66): centre at cruise / centre at 9 m/s = 475 / 115 = **4.1** (needed 1.3). Hug at cruise / centre at 9 m/s = 1,200 / 115 = **10.4** (needed 2). Same as round 12.
- **First payout:** desktop 3.2 s after the first draft (7.1 s into the run). Mobile 4.0 s after (8.4 s). Both within 10 s.
- **Crash-classify, 8 seeds (11, 22, 33, 44, 7, 58, 91, 130):**
  - 12 m: 587 s of flight, 13 deliveries, 35 charged crashes, **0 hop-like**. 4 near the target, all at street pads (0.4 m), all building faces with tops of 7.4 to 13.8 m. **0 on a pad lip.** Flight time fell from 782 s, because this bot flies at 12 m and gets less slow clock now.
  - 20 m: 784 s, 30 deliveries, 34 charged, **1 hop-like**: seed 130 at 34.7 s. The drone was at 20.3 m, hit a face whose top is 33 m, lost 11.2 m/s and rose 0.9 m. The wall top was 12.7 m above it, so it is a real wall hit. It is the same case as round 12. 2 near the target, street pads, faces of 10.6 and 20.2 m, **0 on a pad lip.**
- **Flat-frame probe:** 872 frames, **0 flat**, 0 errors.
- **Music:** adaptive (see Audio). Seed 130 had 5 of 2,917 steps with no music, at time-up. 0 late notes, 0 resyncs.
- **Page errors:** 0 on desktop and mobile.

builder.md
# Drone Dash, round 13 builder: the slow clock serves delivering

Status: done inside the 90 minute box (22:07 to 23:10). The farm is closed and every regression check passes. Two checks do not pass on the letter:
- The low/high ratio. It depends on which high pass you compare against (section 4).
- The Silver margin rests on a lazy result that sits on a knife edge (section 5).

## 1. Design

The round 12 slow clock had no limit and no link to the objective. I added two limits. Payouts, crash rules, roof-line flight and drop time are unchanged.

1. **Only on the way.** The slow clock runs only while the drone flies toward its current objective (pickup or drop). The game compares the drone's horizontal velocity with the direction to the target:
   - cos 0.2 or more (within about 80 degrees): full effect.
   - cos -0.1 or less: no effect.
   - In between: a linear ramp.
   - Config: `towardLow`, `towardFull`.
2. **A budget per leg.** Each leg adds at most `clockBudget` = **8 s** of clock.
   - A pickup or a delivery refills the budget to 8 s. It does not stack.
   - A run with no deliveries therefore gets at most 16 s in total: the start budget plus one pickup. A farm that never picks up gets 8 s.
   - Honest pilots never hit the limit. In round 12 the routed street bot used about 3 to 4 s per leg (34 to 38 s over 11 legs on seed 22).
3. The rate (`clockRate` 1), the pace thresholds and the decay per delivery are unchanged. I tried a rate of 1.5 on seed 58 to lift the weak low seed. That run scored 1,542: 11 s more clock, still 2 drops, and one drop was not fast. So I reverted it (`t-low58-r15.log`).

**What the player sees.** The badge on the timer now shows the budget left on the leg:
- "CLOCK FROZEN · 4S" or "CLOCK X0.1 · 5S".
- A good draft that earns no clock shows a muted badge, and the teal ring and glow switch off:
  - "SLOW CLOCK SPENT": the budget is used up.
  - "SLOW CLOCK: WRONG WAY": the drone flies away from the objective.
- Shots: `d-/m-clock-hug-cruise.jpg` and `d-/m-clock-hug-spent.jpg`. The title overlay is still fading in these shots. That comes from the test API, as in round 12.
- The tagline now ends "slows the clock on the way to your next stop."

## 2. Farm acceptance (farm-probe.mjs, farm-loop.mjs, SIMT 600, `farm13.sh`)

| Seed | Road, offset | Run | Score | Medal | Slip clock | Frozen share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 22 | 66, 6.5 | 58 s | 3,375 | Silver | 8.0 s | 12% |
| 22 | -22, 6.5 | 58 s | 4,100 | Silver | 8.0 s | 13% |
| 22 | 66, 5 | 58 s | 3,665 | Silver | 8.0 s | 12% |
| 58 | 66, 6.5 | 58 s | 4,100 | Silver | 8.0 s | 13% |
| 58 | 22, 5 | 58 s | 2,650 | Silver | 8.0 s | 12% |
| 130 | 66, 6.5 | 58 s | 1,965 | Silver | 8.0 s | 11% |
| 130 | 22, 6.5 | 58 s | 3,085 | Silver | 8.0 s | 12% |
| 130 | -66, 6.5 | 58 s | 3,665 | Silver | 8.0 s | 13% |
| loop 22 | 22/66 x -110/110 | 58 s | 1,820 (1 crash) | Silver | 8.0 s | 13% |

- No farm run reaches Gold. The best is 4,100, which is 400 below Gold. **Pass.**
- No farm run lasts over 150 s. The longest is 58 s, against 312 s before. **Pass.**
- With 0 deliveries, the slow clock adds at most 8 s (the limit is 20 s). **Pass.**

**Remaining gap (outside my concern):** a 58 s farm with no delivery still scores Silver from payout points alone. Its best is 4,100, which beats a routed seed 58 street run (1,792). The clock is no longer the problem. The payout points are. One option for the next round: payouts that need a parcel on board, or a payout cap per leg.

The farm logs ran before a change that touched only the HUD text and the Silver line. The game logic is the same, so the numbers stand.

Note on the ratio: the high line barely uses the slow clock (1.9 to 6.3 s a run), so my change cannot move it. The two high passes differ by 3,000 points from crashes and drop count alone. The low line is unchanged from round 12. If the critic's next high pass looks like high A, the ratio fails. To close that gap, the street line must get stronger. The Ace margin has no room for that: in round 12, a rate of 1.15 put seed 22 at Ace.

## 5. Medal lines and margins

The lines are now Bronze 1,000, **Silver 1,600** (was 1,775), Gold 4,500 and Ace 7,500. Only Silver moved.

Why it moved: the lazy pilot's seed 22 run now misses its second drop. It gets 0.6 s of slow clock instead of 0.85 s, because the toward gate drops some frames. So it scores 844 instead of 1,728, the same in both passes. That frees room under the worst routed low run.

- Best lazy result: 1,141 = **459 below Silver**. **Pass.**
- Worst standard low result: 1,792 = **192 above Silver**. **Pass.**
- **Risk:** the lazy seed 22 second drop was within about 0.3 s of the time-out in round 12. If a lazy run lands it again, it scores about 1,728. That is 128 above Silver, so the lazy pilot gets Silver in that case. No 150-point line can hold both sides as long as lazy seed 22 and low seed 58 both make exactly 2 drops.

A commit does not change files, so the run was not affected. Since then the Silver line moved from 1,775 to 1,600. That change is uncommitted. I ran no git commands that change state.

# Drone Dash, round 12 critic report

**Verdict:** The round 10 gap is closed. The street line now scores as well as the roof line, and runs are the same length. But the slow clock opened a bigger hole. A pilot who never delivers a parcel can fly up and down one street along a wall, keep the clock frozen, and reach Ace. The delivery game is optional now.

## Round 10 gap (medals pay the roof line): closed

Dev server port 5188. Same bots as rounds 9 and 10. Scripts are copies in `critic-scripts/`. Only the output folder changed. It is a relative path, so no edit was needed. I set SIMT to 600 to give long runs room. No run hit that limit.

| Check | Needed | Result | Pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| Low total / high total | at least 0.85 | run A 14,220 / 13,443 = **1.06**. Run B 11,974 / 13,443 = **0.89**. Mean 0.97 (round 10: 0.54) | Yes |
| Low Silver | 3 of 3 | 3 of 3 in both runs | Yes |
| Low Gold | at least 1 | run A 2 (seeds 22, 130), run B 1 (seed 22) | Yes |
| High Silver | at least 2 of 3 | 3 of 3 (5,655 Gold, 4,078 Silver, 3,710 Silver) | Yes |
| No bot reaches Ace | none | route bots: none (best 6,522). **But the medal-journey pilot reached Ace on desktop (8,834).** The farm bot reached Ace in 6 of 8 tries (below) | Partly |
| Lazy pilot | Bronze or below | 1,728 / 696 / 1,141, rerun 1,723 / 721 / 1,141. Bronze at most | Yes |
| Breakdown exact | every run | diagnostics and game-over DOM add up in 9 of 9 bot runs and both journeys | Yes |
| Slipstream share of low score | at most 50% | 42% (A), 41% (B) | Yes |
| Run length | none over about 4 min | low 91 to 164 s, high 119 to 155 s, lazy 65 to 82 s, desktop journey 193 s. Farm runs up to **312 s** | Bots yes, farm no |

Per seed, low run A / run B (spread):
- Seed 22: 6,522 Gold / 6,382 Gold (140 apart). 162 s / 160 s.
- Seed 58: 1,792 Silver / 1,837 Silver (45 apart). 91 s / 94 s.
- Seed 130: 5,906 Gold / 3,755 Silver (2,151 apart). 164 s / 135 s. One extra delivery made the difference.
- Lazy: seed 22 1,728 / 1,723, seed 58 696 / 721, seed 130 1,141 / 1,141.

Why it closed: low runs now last as long as high runs. On seed 22 the low clock got 74 s from drops and 38 s from the slipstream. The high line got 2 to 7 s from the slipstream.

## Medal band margins

Medal lines: Bronze 1,000, Silver 1,775, Gold 4,500, Ace 7,500.

| Run | Score | Nearest line | Margin |
|---|---|---|---|
| Low seed 58, A / B | 1,792 / 1,837 | Silver | **+17 / +62** |
| Lazy seed 22, A / B | 1,728 / 1,723 | Silver | **-47 / -52** |
| Low seed 130 B | 3,755 | Gold | -745 |
| High seed 58 | 4,078 | Gold | -422 |
| High seed 130 | 3,710 | Gold | -790 |
| Low seed 130 A | 5,906 | Gold | +1,406 |
| High seed 22 | 5,655 | Gold | +1,155 |
| Low seed 22, A / B | 6,522 / 6,382 | Ace | -978 / -1,118 |
| Lazy seed 130 | 1,141 | Bronze | +141 |

The Silver line is a problem. The lazy pilot's best (1,728) and the routed street pilot on seed 58 (1,792) are only 64 points apart. Silver sits between them. One slip payout more or less (45 to 145 points) flips either result. The line was set to fit one bot run. The config comment says so too.

## Frozen clock

- **Readable: yes.** The timer gets a teal ring and glow. A pill under it says "CLOCK FROZEN" or "CLOCK X0.1". It is 13 px tall with 10 px text on both desktop and iPhone 13 held sideways. On the phone it reads well. On desktop it is small but clear because of the teal glow (`d-clock-hug-cruise.jpg`, `m-clock-hug-cruise.jpg`, `m-j22-h05-low-payout-chain.jpg`).
- **How strong it is** (desktop probe, 0 deliveries): crawl at the street centre: clock at full speed. Centre at cruise: about x0.1 to x0.4. Wall hug at cruise: **frozen** (0.02 s lost a second).
- **Fair and fun in a normal run: mostly yes.** A routed street pilot gets 14 to 44 s of clock from it over a run. Runs end at 1:31 to 2:44. The last-10-s music still arrives in every run. Drafting now feels like it earns time, which suits the game.
- **Tension: removed in the wrong case.** At 0 deliveries the clock freezes fully. Only deliveries shrink the effect (by 3.5% each, down to 55%). So the way to keep the clock frozen is to never deliver.
- **Farming: yes.** See the biggest gap below. Runs are not endless, because each U-turn leaks a few seconds. But they reach 5:12, and the score has no ceiling short of Ace.
- **Is the street line the medal chaser's line now?** Yes, and too much so. The best "street line" does not deliver at all.

## Whole game, as a player

- **First 10 seconds.** Strong. A warm golden-hour city, a clear title with the medal ladder, a sound prompt. The tagline now says that the slipstream slows the clock.
- **Onboarding.** Good. First payout 3.4 s after the first draft on desktop (7.3 s into the run) and 3.9 s on touch (8.2 s).
- **Core loop.** In a normal run, pick up, deliver and draft now support each other well. The frozen clock tells you that flying low and close is right. The weak point: the loop stops needing parcels once you know the trick.
- **Game feel.** Still the best part. Momentum, bank and fair crashes.
- **Art.** Coherent, warm, finished low-poly.
- **Audio.** Adaptive music works. Chain 0 to 3+ goes from intensity 0.36 to 0.85 and layers 1 to 4. The final section starts at 9.96 to 9.97 s left. 0 late notes, 0 resyncs.
- **UI.** Clean. The clock badge fits the style. On mobile the payout pop ("+70, SLIPSTREAM CHAIN X2, CLOCK +1S") still sits on top of the drone.
- **Difficulty curve and run length.** Runs are 1:30 to 2:45, and the clock arc works. The play itself still does not change during a run.
- **Game over and restart.** Clear breakdown, plus a nice "clock story" line ("50 s start +74 s drops +38 s slipstream"). Fly again to control: 68 ms desktop, 23 ms touch.
- **Replay pull.** Good for most players. Weak for a skilled one: the desktop journey pilot got Ace on its first full run. The card then says "Top medal. Nothing left but your best."

## Single biggest remaining gap: the slow clock pays you not to deliver

A wall hug at cruise freezes the clock. It also pays a slip payout every 1 to 2 s, up to 145 points each at chain 5. Nothing in it needs a parcel, and not delivering keeps the freeze at full strength. The best way to score is to hug one long street, turn around at the end, and repeat. A medal chaser will find this: the timer literally says "CLOCK FROZEN" while you hug a wall.

Evidence: a new deterministic bot, `farm-probe.mjs`. It never picks up or delivers. It flies one street at 7 m, 2.5 m (or 4 m) from a facade, at up to 15 m/s. At each end it makes a careful U-turn: brake, turn in place, go.

| Seed | Street, offset | Run length | Score | Medal | Clock from slipstream | Clock frozen |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 22 | x 66, 6.5 m | 172 s | 10,480 | Ace | 122 s | 65% of the run |
| 22 | x -22, 6.5 m | **312 s** | **21,935** | Ace | 261 s | 80% |
| 22 | x 66, 5 m | 260 s | 15,990 | Ace | 210 s | 74% |
| 58 | x 66, 6.5 m | 202 s | 13,380 | Ace | 152 s | 71% |
| 58 | x 22, 5 m | 125 s | 5,695 | Gold | 75 s | 52% |
| 130 | x 66, 6.5 m | 91 s | 3,310 | Silver | 41 s | 40% |
| 130 | x 22, 6.5 m | 270 s | 18,890 | Ace | 219 s | 78% |
| 130 | x -66, 6.5 m | 174 s | 10,770 | Ace | 124 s | 67% |

All with 0 deliveries and 0 crashes. The best routed street bot scores 6,522 in 162 s. The farm beats it in 6 of 8 tries and lasts up to 5:12. A lap around a block (`farm-loop.mjs`) did worse (3,250 Silver, 2 crashes), so the long straight is the exploit. The hand-fly street pilot also reached Ace: 8,834 in 3:13, with 52 s of clock from the slipstream. So one good normal run can now reach the top medal.

**Acceptance test** (dev server 5188, `farm-probe.mjs` with the 8 seed, street and offset rows above, SIMT 600):
1. No farm run reaches Gold (4,500). No farm run lasts over 150 s.
2. With 0 deliveries, the slipstream adds at most 20 s of clock in any farm run.
3. The round 10 test still passes on seeds 22, 58, 130. Low total is at least 0.85 of high. Low gets Silver 3 of 3 and Gold at least once. High gets Silver at least 2 of 3. Lazy gets Bronze at most. No route bot gets Ace. The breakdown is exact.
4. `medal-journey.mjs` on desktop and mobile stays below Ace.
5. Every medal line sits at least 150 points from every bot result in this set (seeds 22, 58, 130, two runs each).

Options (not tested): run the slow clock only while carrying a parcel, or cap it per leg (for example 10 s of clock per pickup).

## Other gaps (ranked)

1. **The Silver line is set to one bot run.** The routed seed 58 run clears it by 17 to 62 points. The lazy best misses it by 47 to 52 points. Test: rule 5 above.
2. **Ace is reachable in a normal good run.** Hand-fly street pilot: 8,834 on seed 22. After the farm fix, check that Ace still needs a near-perfect run. Test: medal-journey below Ace on desktop and mobile, two runs each.
3. **Same run, very different result.** Seed 130 low: 5,906 Gold and then 3,755 Silver with the same bot. One more delivery is worth about 2,000 points through the combo. That is fine for skill, but it means the medal often depends on one parcel. Watch it after the farm fix.
4. **Mobile payout pop covers the drone.** The pop and its tag ("SLIPSTREAM CHAIN X2 · CLOCK +1S") sit on the drone and the street ahead. Test: in a full touch run the pop never overlaps the drone's screen box.
5. **The clock badge is small on desktop.** 10 px text on a 1280x720 screen. Test: the badge text is at least 12 px on desktop.

## Regressions: none found

- **Lazy / standard low, score a minute** (at most 0.8): 984 / 1,947 = **0.51** (run A 0.48, run B 0.53).
- **Hug probe** (seed 22, roads -22, 22, 66): centre at cruise / centre at 9 m/s = 475 / 115 = **4.1** (needed 1.3). Hug at cruise / centre at 9 m/s = 1,200 / 115 = **10.4** (needed 2). Same as round 9.
- **First payout:** desktop 3.4 s after the first draft, mobile 3.9 s. Both under 10 s.
- **Crash-classify, 8 seeds:** 12 m: 782 s, 25 deliveries, 44 charged, **0 hop-like**. 6 near the target, all street pads (0.4 to 0.5 m), all building faces with tops of 7.4 to 20.2 m. **0 on a pad lip.** 20 m: 766 s, 29 deliveries, 34 charged, **1 hop-like**: seed 130 at 33.2 s. The drone was at 20.2 m, hit a face whose top is 33 m, lost 8 m/s from 15.9, and rose 1.3 m after. The wall top was 12.8 m above it, so this is a real wall hit, not a ledge hop. 4 near target, all street pads, building faces, **0 on a pad lip.**
- **Flat-frame probe:** 1,071 frames, **0 flat**.
- **Music:** still adaptive (see Audio above). Fanfare 13.5 to 17.5 dB above the ducked music.
- **Page errors:** 0 desktop, 0 mobile.

builder.md
# Drone Dash, round 12 builder: slipstream feeds the clock

Status: **incomplete. The acceptance test was not finished.** I ran out of time. The code is in, it type-checks and builds. The tuning is not proven. Read section 4 before you trust any number.

## 1. Design

Today every slipstream payout adds 0.5 s. Deliveries add 7 to 20 s. The roof line delivers more often, so its runs last longer and it wins the medals.

New rule: a payout adds clock time by **chain level** and by **pace**.

- Every payout still gives the base **0.5 s**.
- A chained payout adds up to `chainSeconds[chain - 1]` = **0, 3, 3, 3.5, 3.5** s (chain x1 to x5).
- That extra time is scaled by the meter's **pace**: draft metres per second while drafting. This is the same measure as the HUD chevrons. At or below **5** it adds nothing (a slow, centred crawl). From **11** it adds all of it (fast and close to a facade). The result is rounded to half seconds.
- **Budget per delivery:** the slipstream can add at most **10 s** between two drops. The budget shrinks with the run in the same way as the drop time bonus (x0.965 per delivery, floor 0.55). This cap keeps drafting from making a run endless. When the budget is used up, the pop says "time full, deliver".

Measured pace (round 12 PAY logs):

| Pilot | Chain 1 pace | Chain 2+ pace |
|---|---|---|
| Lazy (centre, 10 m/s, no boost) | 1.5 to 5 | 2.8 to 5.1 |
| Standard low bot | 2 to 8.5 | 4 to 14.6, mostly 7 to 14 |

So a lazy pilot gets exactly 0.5 s per payout, the same as before. In the round 12 lazy run every payout paid 0.5 s, and the lazy scores were 1,728, 861 and 1,141. All are Bronze or below, the same as round 10.

What the player sees:

- **Payout pop:** the points, plus the time in teal next to them, for example "+120 +3.5s".
- **Timer:** the "+Ns" by the timer now shows the real amount, for example "+3.5s". Before it always showed "+0.5s".
- **Game over:** the Slipstream row reads "×27 · +37.5 s". The "Flew" line already counted slipstream seconds, and it still adds up exactly.
- **Title tagline:** "Fly fast and low, close to the walls: the slipstream pays points and buys time."

Not changed: crash rules, roof-line flight and headwind, points per payout, medal thresholds, the bloom clamps in `ObjectiveMarker.ts`, and every existing debug hook. New fields in diagnostics `slipstream`: `lastPace`, `lastSeconds`, `legSeconds`, `legCap`.

## 2. Files changed

- `src/game/config.ts`: in `SLIPSTREAM`, added `chainSeconds`, `paceLow`, `paceFull` and `legSeconds`, with comments.
- `src/systems/Slipstream.ts`: tracks draft metres and drafting time for each meter. The payout event now carries `pace`.
- `src/systems/DeliverySystem.ts`: new `clockDecay` getter. This is the existing drop-time decay. The drop bonus now uses it, so drop time is unchanged.
- `src/game/Game.ts`: `slipClock()` and `slipLegCap()`. The budget resets on each delivery and at run start. Pop and timer flash show the real time. New diagnostics fields.
- `src/ui/Hud.ts`: `slipPop(points, chain, seconds, capped)`. New `fmtSec` helper. The over-card Slipstream row shows the seconds.
- `index.html`: new `#slip-pop-time` element inside the pop. Tagline updated.
- `src/styles.css`: `.slip-pop-time` is teal. An empty one is hidden.
- `src/vite-env.d.ts`: types for the new diagnostics fields.

## 3. Scripts

`builder-scripts/` holds copies of the round 9 and round 10 critic scripts. In every copy only the output folder changed (`../builder-shots/`). There are two extra tuning copies, `route-play-rt-x-mp.mjs` and `balance-probe-mp.mjs`. They have the same control logic as the `-m` scripts, plus one `PAY` log line per payout (chain, pace, seconds, budget).

## 4. Numbers (low line, `route-play-rt-x-m(p).mjs`, SIMT 400)

Round 10 baseline: low 3,658 / 1,792 / 2,612 (total 8,062). High 6,789 / 4,078 / 4,124 (total 14,991).

| Try | chainSeconds | pace low / full | budget per delivery | Seed 22 | Seed 58 | Seed 130 | Low total / round 10 high |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| t1 | 0, .5, 1.5, 2.5, 3.5 | 5 / 12 | 15 | 6,367 Gold, 153 s | 1,792 Bronze, 87 s | 3,870 Silver, 128 s | 12,029 = 0.80 |
| t2 | 0, 2, 2.5, 3, 3 | 5 / 11 | 15 | 6,232 Gold, 161 s | 1,907 Bronze, 94 s | (page reloaded, run lost) | n/a |
| t3 | 0, 3, 3, 3.5, 3.5 | 5 / 11 | 15 | (bot stalled, invalid) | 2,795 Silver, 119 s | **9,722 Ace, 239 s** | n/a |
| t4 | 0, 3, 3, 3.5, 3.5 | 5 / 11 | 8 | 6,222 Gold, 161 s | 1,772 Bronze, 93 s | 3,870 Silver, 126 s | 11,864 = 0.79 |
| t5 (in the code now) | 0, 3, 3, 3.5, 3.5 | 5 / 11 | 10, shrinking | 6,277 Gold, 161 s | (page reloaded at 55 s, run lost) | not run | n/a |

Lazy (t1 settings, `balance-probe-mp.mjs` CRUISE=10 NOBOOST=1): 1,728 Bronze (86 s), 861 none (68 s), 1,141 Bronze (74 s). Every payout paid 0.5 s.

The breakdown added up (`bdOk`, `domOk`) in every run that reached game over.

Findings:

- **The pace gate works.** Lazy flight never earns extra time. Fast chained flight earns 2 to 4 s per payout.
- **The result is very sensitive to one extra delivery.** Each delivery also adds 14 to 20 s of drop time and raises the combo. So small changes in slipstream time flip a run between "one more delivery" and "time-up". With a 15 s budget, seed 130 ran 239 s and reached Ace. With an 8 s budget, seed 58 stayed at 2 deliveries and Bronze. The 10 s shrinking budget is a guess between the two and was only measured on seed 22.
- **Seed 58 is the hard case.** There the low bot climbs to rooftop pads. Each climb breaks the chain for 10 to 18 s, so it rarely gets past chain 3. It reached Silver in 1 of 3 tries.
- **Seed 22 is stable:** Gold at about 6,250 in 161 s in every valid run. That is about 1,200 below Ace.
- **Two runs died** with "Execution context was destroyed" and no Vite reload logged. One run stalled at 892 s of wall time. The host clock also jumped about 1.5 hours during the session. I think the machine slept or was throttled. Those runs are not valid.

## 5. Not done

- The full low, high and lazy acceptance on the final settings.
- High line on the new code. I expect little change: high-line payouts are slow chain 1 payouts, so they still get 0.5 s.
- Regressions: balance-probe ratio, hug-probe, hand-fly on desktop and mobile, crash-classify at 12 m and 20 m, flat-frame, music diagnostics, p95 frame time, screenshots.
- Done: `tsc` and `vite build` pass (`builder-scripts/build.log`, built to the scratchpad). The production JS is 726 KB.

## 6. Suggested next step

Run the final settings on seeds 22, 58 and 130 at least twice each, one at a time. If seed 130 goes over Ace, lower `legSeconds` to 9. If seed 58 stays Bronze, the honest options are these:

- (a) Accept "Silver in 2 of 3" for the low line.
- (b) Make chain 2 easier to hold on rooftop legs, through a change to the chain window.
- (c) Retune Silver. Risk: lazy seed 22 sits at about 1,730 against Silver 2,250. A lower Silver can let the lazy pilot reach it.

# Drone Dash, round 11 critic report

**Verdict:** All four round 10 audio problems are fixed. The music has no clicks. The title and run sit at about -16 to -18 LUFS. The title is no longer mostly sub-bass. The run music repeats only every 61 s. Every gameplay cue stays at least 6 dB over the music. The only exceptions are 3 slip chimes of 61, in the master. Nothing regressed. Two smaller audio points remain: the game-over loop is still 4 dB quiet and bass-heavy, and in flight the music sits under the rotor and wind.

## How I measured

- Dev server on port 5188, Playwright with channel `chromium` and the autoplay flag. A key press (desktop) or a tap (iPhone 13 held sideways) was the gesture.
- An init script tapped three points of the real graph with a ScriptProcessor: the master output (after the limiter and the new trim, the signal sent to the speakers), the music bus and the cue bus. Same tap as round 10.
- **Capture latency.** At the start of each capture I played a known 10 ms noise burst into all three taps. I knew its audio-clock time. I found it again with a matched filter. The latency was 170.67 ms (8,192 samples, two ScriptProcessor buffers) on every channel in every capture, match score 0.97 to 1.01. All cue timing below is corrected for it. Game sound reaches the master 12.0 ms after the buses (the two compressors' look-ahead), the same as round 10. After the correction, cue sound starts a median 11 to 23 ms after the game's scheduled cue time.
- Loudness is BS.1770 K-weighted. "Integrated" is gated over the clip. "Short-term" uses 3 s windows. Round 10 used an ungated approximation. For steady music the two differ by under 1 dB.
- Captures:
  - Low line, seeds 22, 58 and 130, desktop.
  - Low line, seed 22, iPhone 13 held sideways.
  - High line, seeds 22, 58 and 130, desktop. The crashes come from these runs.
  - One forced capture. `musicForce` held chain 0 for 40 s, then chain 3 for 95 s, then the final section for 20 s. The clock was set to 200 s. The low line bot did not crash once, so the crash numbers come from the high line runs.
- Raw recordings (about 30 MB each) are in the session scratchpad, not in the project.

## Round 10 audio problems

### 1. Clicks on the 16th-note grid: fixed

| Where | Round 10 | Round 11 |
|---|---|---|
| Round 10 detector, music bus, whole run | 118 | **0** (every capture: 4 low runs, 3 high runs, forced) |
| Round 10 detector, master, whole run | 26 | **0** |
| Last 10 s, music bus | 47 (4.1 a second) | **0** in all 7 runs |

| Stricter detector, master | 125 a minute | 21 to 41 a minute, none from the music (see below) |

- My stricter detector flags a step over 5 times the RMS step in a 5 ms window, with the centre left out. The step must also be over 0.002 on the music bus. On the master the floor is 0.005, because the master now runs about 9 dB hotter. The slope itself must jump, so smooth steep edges do not count. I ran it on the round 10 raw capture for the baseline above.
- The master hits are not from the music. About 70% sit on cue sounds (slip chime, chimes, the square-wave fanfare brass). The rest fall on the rotor and wind sound. The ones I opened were steep edges spread over 5 to 10 samples, not one-sample spikes. I do not count them as clicks.

- Peaks: the loudest sample in any clip is **-1.2 dBFS** (a crash). **0 samples over -1 dBFS** and 0 clipped. The limiter now works, up to 3.6 to 3.8 dB of gain reduction at peaks.

### 4. Run music repeats every 7.68 s: fixed

Correlation of 4-bar windows of the music bus with the same window one or more whole bars later. "Mean" is over all start points.

| Capture | Round 10 | Round 11 |
|---|---|---|

# Drone Dash, round 11 builder: music audio quality

Scope: the procedural music in `src/systems/AudioSystem.ts` and `src/systems/music.ts`, plus the master level. No gameplay or scoring code changed. The bloom clamps in `src/entities/ObjectiveMarker.ts` and all debug hooks are untouched (one test hook added).

## 1. Cause of the clicks

**Cause: a GainNode starts at gain 1.** Every note made a new GainNode and set its envelope with `setValueAtTime(0.0001, t)`. Before that first event, the node passes signal at its default gain of 1. The step grid adds 0.12 s again and again. So a note often starts a tiny bit (around 1e-12 s) after a sample frame. Chromium then starts the source on that frame but applies the envelope's first event one frame later. So one sample of the source got through at full level. On an oscillator that sample is near zero. On a noise hat or clap it is a full-scale random value. The 7.2 kHz hat filter (or the 1.5 kHz clap filter) rings it into a short spike.

Evidence:
- **Shape and timing in the round 10 capture** (the raw capture in the session scratchpad): all 118 music-bus clicks sit at the same phase of the 0.12 s step grid (48.06 ms). Each one is a 6 to 7 sample ringing at about 7 kHz, which is the impulse response of the hat bandpass.
- **Reproduced offline** (`builder-scripts/click-repro.mjs`, log `click-repro.log`): 40 hats on a grid, in an OfflineAudioContext.

  | Start offset from the frame | Round 10 envelope (spikes / 40) | Fix, gain 0 at creation |
  |---|---|---|
  | 0 (0.1 + k x 0.02, float error only) | 4 | 0 |
  | +-1e-12 s | 20 | 0 |
  | +-1e-10 s | 19 | 0 |
  | +-1e-8 s | 20 | 0 |
  | +-3e-6 s | 0 | 0 |

  Spike size: up to 0.46. Fixed: under 0.003. The round 10 critic's per-voice render started every voice exactly on a sample frame. That is why it found nothing.
- **Why the rate grew with the music:** layer 1 has no noise voices, so 0 clicks. Chain 3 adds off-beat hats and claps, so about 0.7 a second. The last 10 s put a hat on every 16th note plus claps, so about 4 a second.

**Fix at the source:** `envGain()` makes each note's gain node with `gain.value = 0`. It is used by every music voice (`mNote`, `kick`, `hit`) and by the SFX `tone` and `noise`.

**A second, smaller source showed up at the louder level:** master-only clicks during boost. I tapped each input of the master bus on its own channel (`builder-scripts/bisect-master.mjs`): SFX, reverb, rotor, wind, draft and music. Only the SFX bus had them, as periodic edges at 220 to 440 a second. That is the boost whine, a plain `sawtooth` with a one-sample edge every period. It now uses a soft saw (12 harmonics with a Lanczos taper). After the fix all six channels and their sum show 0. I first suspected the rotor saw. An offline rotor render (`rotor-edges.mjs`) ruled it out, and the rotor is unchanged.

Other edges were removed on the way:
- The scene fade used to set a target of 0, then cut the tail with `setValueAtTime(0)`. It is now a straight 40 ms ramp to exactly 0.

## 2. Changes

- **Click fix:** zero-initialised envelope gains (above). Soft saw for the boost whine.
- **Level:** master gain 0.8 to 3.1, then a fixed 0.8 trim after the limiter, so peaks stay under -1 dBFS. The limiter's automatic make-up gain lifts its ceiling, and the trim pulls it back. The glue compressor and limiter settings are unchanged. Music bus level (`MUSIC_VOL` 0.5) is unchanged, so music against SFX stays as before.
- **Title midrange:** pad harmonics an octave up (sines, past the pad filter). Plucks louder, with a sine an octave above. A second high lead note per chord. Bass softer relative to the rest. Title voices about +4 dB overall.
- **Run pad colour:** the chord's top note an octave up as a quiet sine, for phone speakers.
- **Run form:** 32 bars instead of 4, in eight 4-bar phrases.
  - First pass: C Am F G / C Am Dm G / F G Em Am / F G C G.
  - Second pass: Am F C G / C Em F G / Dm Em F G / Am Dm G G.
  - The lead reads one of 16 written bars per bar. Bass rhythm and arpeggio order change every phrase (3 variants each, so the notes repeat exactly only every 96 bars). A drum fill comes on the last bar of every other phrase (chain 2+).
- **Cues over the louder music:** slip duck 0.7 to 0.45 with a 0.35 s hold. Game-over duck 0.5 to 0.35. Slip chime and game-over sting each +2.3 dB (x1.3).
- **Diagnostics:** `audio.music.compDb` and `limiterDb` (current gain reduction). New test hook `__GAME__.musicForce(chain | null, final?)` holds the music at a chain level for audio tests. It does not change gameplay.

## 3. Files changed

- `src/systems/AudioSystem.ts`: envelope fix, master and trim, soft saw, title and run voicing, 32-bar sequencing, ducks and cue levels, forced state hook, reduction readout.
- `src/systems/music.ts`: `RUN_FORM` (32 bars), `RUN_LEAD` (16 bars) plus `RUN_LEAD_ORDER`, `RUN_ARP_ORDERS`, `RUN_BASS_VARIANTS`. Dm and Em chords added.
- `src/game/Game.ts`: `musicForce` test hook.
- `src/vite-env.d.ts`: type for the hook.

## 4. Numbers

Recording: same method as round 10 (`builder-scripts/music-run.mjs`, a copy of the critic's script with only the output paths changed). Seed 22, low line, TAP=1, measured with the critic's `analyze-audio.py` (same click detector). Clips are in `builder-audio/` (0.26 to 0.68 MB each). The raw capture is in the session scratchpad.

| Clip | Peak dBFS | Loudness (LUFS-like) | Below 150 Hz | Above 6 kHz | Phone band | Clicks music / master |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| title | -4.1 | **-17.4** (round 10: -32.7) | **35.0%** (73%) | 0.0% | -18.7 (-37.3) | 0 / 0 |
| run-chain0 | -2.8 | **-16.6** (-27.6) | 36.4% | 0.03% | -17.7 | 0 / 0 |
| run-chain3 | -1.9 | **-15.9** (-25.1) | 41.8% | 0.22% | -17.9 | 0 / 0 (was 10 / 4) |
| last-10s | -2.0 | **-16.6** (-26.3) | 44.3% | 0.21% | -19.1 | 0 / 0 (was 47 / 11) |
| medal-fanfare-1 | -1.8 | -16.2 | 33.3% | 0.63% | -18.3 | 0 / 0 |
| medal-fanfare-2 | -2.0 | -15.5 | 32.4% | 0.70% | -17.4 | 0 / 0 (was 20) |
| game-over | -2.2 | -20.9 | 55.8% | 0.07% | -23.6 | 0 / 0 (was 2) |

- **Clicks:** 0 on every clip, music bus and master.
- **Peaks:** highest -1.8 dBFS. 0 clipped samples.
- **Title phone band:** within 1 dB of the run (round 10: 10 dB below).
- **Loudness:** the run and title are in the -16 to -18 range. Run-chain3 at -15.9 is 0.1 dB above it, with SFX included.
- **Game over:** -20.9. It was not in the target. It swells in slowly under the sting.
- **Short-term loudness (3 s windows, forced-chain capture `quick-rep-analysis.log`):** title -17.7 to -17.0. Chain 3 -18.0 to -17.3. Hovering at chain 0 is about -19.5, because the rotor is quieter than in flight.
- **No pumping:** glue compressor reduction at most 0.6 dB. Limiter median 0 dB, worst 0.4 dB in music-only sections. It reaches about 2 dB only during boost with cues.
- **Fanfare over music:** 14.0 and 14.2 dB on the captured buses. The game meter says 16.3 (seed 22), 16.7 (58) and 17.5 (130).
- **Cues over the ducked music (round 10 method):** slip 7.6 (round 10: 4.6), pickup 9.9, delivery 16.0, medal 11.8, game over 8.6. All at least 6 dB.
  - Note for the critic: the ScriptProcessor capture lags the audio clock by about 0.18 s. With `OFF=0.18` (the analyzer's own correction argument), the measured ducks match their set values (slip -7.5 against -6.9). The margins become slip 12.3, pickup 12.4, delivery 17.5, medal 22.1 and game over 37.0. Without it, the window takes in about 80 ms of music from before the duck, so those margins jump around from run to run.
- **Repetition:** the music bus is held at one chain level for 70 s (`quick-audio.mjs` REP=1). At chain 0 and chain 3, the highest correlation at any lag under 30 s is 0.65 (round 10: 0.86 at 7.68 s). The first correlation of 0.8 or more is at **61.4 s** (0.95 and 0.98), where the chords come round again. Exact note-for-note repetition is every 184 s.

## 5. Round 10 behaviour and regressions

- **Adaptive music:** chain 3+ above chain 0 on all 3 seeds. Mean intensity at chain 0 / chain 3: seed 22 0.37 / 0.86, seed 58 0.36 / 0.84, seed 130 0.32 / 0.87.
- **Last 10 s:** the final section starts at 9.98, 10.00 and 9.98 s left.
- **Scheduler:** late 0, resyncs 0, page errors 0.
- **Toggle** (`toggle.log`): the chip and the M key work. "Music off" writes 0, survives a reload, and stays off after the next gesture. Same on desktop and iPhone 13 held sideways.
- **Medals:**
  - Low line: Silver 3,768, Bronze 1,792, Silver 2,712.
  - High line: Silver 4,052, 4,123 and 3,755. No Ace.
  - Lazy bot: Bronze 1,728, then 741 and 255 with no medal. Bronze at most.
  - The breakdown adds up in all 9 runs (diagnostics and game-over DOM).
- **Crash-classify, 8 seeds:**
  - 12 m: 661 s, 36 charged, **0 hop-like**.
  - 20 m: 757 s, 28 charged, **0 hop-like**.
  - **0 on a pad lip.** Seven of the near-target hits are on building faces at street pads (wall tops 10.6 to 58.6 m). The eighth is on seed 7 at 20 m: a face 18 m from a rooftop pad (wall top 33 m, pad at 32.5 m).
- **Flat-frame probe:** 839 frames, **0 flat**.
- **Frame time** (desktop medal journey, music on): 12,834 frames, median 8.30 ms, **p95 10.00 ms** (round 10: 9.00), max 10.5, 0 over 20 ms.
- **Build:** `npm run build` passes. JS 725 KB.

# Drone Dash, round 10 critic report

**Verdict:** The music is in and it works. It plays on every screen. It rises with the chain and turns tense in the last 10 s. The medal fanfare sits 15 dB above it. Nothing regressed. But the music has a crackle: short clicks on the beat in the busy parts. It is also quiet, and the title is mostly sub-bass. The biggest gap is now a design one: the game says "fly fast and low", but the high roof line still wins the medals by almost 2 to 1.

## Round 9 gap (no music): closed

All checks ran on the dev server (port 5188). Scripts are in `critic-scripts/`. The audio run used Chromium with `--autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required` and a key press as the gesture. The toggle test used no flag, only a real click or tap.

| Check | Needed | Result | Pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| Title music | plays after first press | desktop click and iPhone tap on the sky: context running, `playing` true, `gain` 0.5, track `title`. Seeds 22, 58, 130: playing in 100% of samples | Yes |
| Run music | plays | 6,358 samples over 3 runs, playing in all but 16 (the 0.24 s gap at run start and the switch to game over) | Yes |
| Game over music | plays | track `over`, section by medal (`bronze`, `silver`), playing in 88 to 97% of samples (the 0.14 s gap and fade in) | Yes |
| Diagnostics | `audio.music` | present: playing, track, section, layer, intensity, bpm 125, gain, duck, late (0), resyncs (0) | Yes |
| Chain 3+ above chain 0 | 3 of 3 low runs | mean intensity chain 0 / chain 3+: seed 22 0.36 / 0.87, seed 58 0.37 / 0.85, seed 130 0.33 / 0.86. Layers 1 vs 4 | 3 of 3 |
| Last 10 s changes | 3 of 3 | track switches to `final` at 9.96 to 9.99 s left in all 3. Layer 5, intensity 0.94 to 0.97 (0.53 to 0.73 in the 10 s before). Tempo stays 125 BPM. Harmony, drums and a ticking high C change | 3 of 3 |
| Fanfare audible | fanfare over music | measured on the captured buses: fanfare 15.1 and 14.5 dB above the ducked music (seed 22). Game meter: 15.2, 17.0, 15.9 dB on seeds 22, 58, 130 | Yes |
| Toggle | exists, remembered | chip top right on title, pause and game over, plus the M key. "Music off" writes `0`, survives reload, music stays off after the next gesture. Same on iPhone 13 held sideways | Yes |
| p95 frame time | under 12 ms | desktop 9.00 ms, mobile 8.90 ms | Yes |

## Audio measurements

How: an init script tapped three points of the real graph with a ScriptProcessor. These are the master output (after the limiter, the signal sent to the speakers), the music bus and the cue (one-shot SFX) bus. Seed 22, low line, Silver run. Rotor and wind are in the master but not in the two buses. The clips are mono 22.05 kHz 16-bit WAV, 0.26 to 0.68 MB each. Loudness is ungated K-weighted (LUFS-like). "Phone band" is the RMS above 200 Hz, roughly what a phone speaker can play.

| Clip | Length | Peak | Clipped samples | Loudness | Phone band | Below 150 Hz | Above 6 kHz | Clicks (music bus) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| title | 14.7 s | -21.7 dBFS | 0 | -32.7 | -37.3 dBFS | 73% | 0.0% | 0 |
| run-chain0 | 8.2 s* | -12.9 | 0 | -27.6 | -29.7 | 49% | 0.07% | 0 |
| run-chain3 | 15.0 s | -7.1 | 0 | -25.1 | -27.0 | 38% | 0.31% | 10 (0.7 a second) |
| last-10s | 11.5 s | -9.2 | 0 | -26.3 | -28.7 | 46% | 0.36% | 47 (4.1 a second) |
| medal-fanfare-1 (Bronze) | 6.0 s | -7.8 | 0 | -25.3 | -27.3 | 34% | 0.65% | 0 |
| medal-fanfare-2 (Silver) | 6.0 s | -7.8 | 0 | -24.9 | -26.9 | 33% | 0.78% | 20 |
| game-over | 15.5 s | -11.1 | 0 | -31.2 | -34.1 | 60% | 0.08% | 2 (before the switch) |

\* The longest stretch at chain 0 in a low run was 8.2 s. The bot starts drafting within 4 to 6 s.

- **Clipping:** none. The loudest peak in the whole run is -7.1 dBFS. The limiter never works.
- **Harshness:** none. Energy above 6 kHz is under 1% everywhere. The music has a 6.5 kHz low-pass.
- **Loudness:** low. The run sits at about -25 to -28, the title and game over at -31 to -33. Typical mobile and web games sit near -16 to -20. There are 7 dB of unused headroom.
- **Phone speakers:** the title has 73% of its energy below 150 Hz (bass at 73 to 98 Hz, pads behind a 700 Hz filter). In the phone band the title is -37 dBFS, 10 dB below the run. On an iPhone speaker the title is likely very faint.
- **Ducking** (music bus before and during each cue, median, with the set value in brackets): slipstream payout -2.4 dB (-3.1, n 18). Pickup -3.0 (-4.4). Delivery -4.8 (-6.9). Medal -9.3 (-11.1). Game over -5.7 (-6.0). Cues sit 4.6, 9.7, 16.6, 11.5 and 7.2 dB above the ducked music. The slip chime is the least clear (4.6 dB).
- **Clicks:** real, and in the master output. On the music bus there are short spikes, 3 to 4 samples wide and about 0.07 to 0.1 in size. The surrounding music sample-to-sample step is about 0.005. Each one shows up in the master exactly 12.00 ms later, which is the two compressors' look-ahead, so it is not a capture fault. They fall exactly on the 16th-note grid. Only the drum and arp layers have them. Rates: 0 on the title and at run layer 1. 0.7 a second at chain 3. About 4 a second in the last 10 s. I rendered each voice alone (kick, hat, clap, bass, arp, lead, urgency tick) in an OfflineAudioContext with the same envelopes and filters. None of them spikes. So the cause is in the live graph, not one voice. I did not find it. Listen to `last-10s.wav` from 0 to 4 s and `run-chain3.wav` at 11.5 s and 14.1 s.
- **Repetition:** the in-run music repeats every 7.68 s (4 bars). Correlation of the music bus at chain 3: 0.86 at 7.68 s, 0.89 at 15.36 s. Only the layers change with the chain. A 108 s run hears the same 4 bars about 14 times. The title and game-over loops are 15.36 s (8 bars).
- **Loop and section boundaries:** no clicks at the run-to-final or final-to-over switches beyond the grid clicks above. The title loop is clean (0 clicks).

**Files for the owner to listen to** (`progress/round-10/critic/audio/`):
- `title.wav`: title loop, 15 s
- `run-chain0.wav`: in run, no chain, 8 s
- `run-chain3.wav`: in run, chain 3 to 5, 15 s
- `last-10s.wav`: the last 10 s section into the time-up sting, 11.5 s
- `medal-fanfare-1.wav`, `medal-fanfare-2.wav`: Bronze and Silver passes, 6 s each
- `game-over.wav`: game-over loop after a Silver, 15.5 s
- `measurements.json`: all numbers above, plus every duck

## Whole game, as a player

- **First 10 seconds.** Strong. A warm golden-hour city, a clear title and the medal ladder. A "Click or press a key for sound" chip now invites the first press. After it, a soft loop plays. On a phone that loop is mostly bass, so it is likely close to silent.
- **Onboarding.** Good and unchanged. First payout 1.5 s after the first draft on desktop, 4.0 s on touch.
- **Core loop.** Pick up, deliver, draft. It works and now has music that answers it. Chain 3 adds the lead melody, and you can hear yourself doing well.
- **Game feel.** Still the best part. Momentum, bank, fair crashes.
- **Art.** Coherent, warm, finished-looking low-poly.
- **Audio.** A big step. The run has an arc. Pad and bass come first. Drums join at chain 1, arp at 2, lead at 3. The last 10 s get a tense minor section. Game over gets a warm or wistful loop by medal. The fanfare cuts through. Weak spots: the click crackle in the busiest parts, the low overall level, and a 7.68 s loop that gets samey by the third minute.
- **UI.** Clean. The music chip fits the style. Unchanged weak spots: the HUD goal row is still 15 px tall. On mobile the medal banner still overlaps `#slip-pop` (2 of 2 passes) and the objective pill (1 of 2).
- **Difficulty curve and run length.** Low runs 83 to 108 s, high runs 120 to 153 s. The music gives the run an arc now. The play itself still does not change over a run.
- **Game over and restart.** Fast. "Fly again" to control: 90 ms desktop, 23 ms touch. The game-over loop is a nice touch.
- **Replay pull.** Good. "817 more for Gold" pulls you back. The pull points you to the wrong line, though (below).

## Single biggest remaining gap: the medals reward the roof line, not the game's own idea

The title says "Fly fast and low, close to the walls". The street line is where the game feels best, and now it is where the music is best: the chain is what lifts it to drums, arp and lead. But the medals pay the high, straight roof line far better. A medal chaser learns this in a few runs. Then they fly at 40 m over the roofs and get the plainest version of the game. That includes the music: the high line gets 1.44 slip payouts a minute, so its music stays mostly at layers 1 and 2.

Evidence (same bots as round 9, seeds 22, 58, 130, every run to its own time-up):
- Standard low: 3,658 Silver, 1,792 Bronze, 2,612 Silver. Total 8,062.
- High line at 40 m: 6,789 Gold, 4,078 Silver, 4,124 Silver. Total 14,991.
- Low / high per run: **0.54** (round 9: 0.59). Seed 22 high came within 711 of Ace.
- Why: drops feed the clock. The low line delivers 1.47 a minute, the high line 2.59. Low runs end 25 to 55 s sooner (83 to 108 s against 120 to 153 s).
- Slipstream share of the low score: 3,785 of 8,062 = 47%. The street line's own reward is not the problem. Its clock is.
- The best low run reaches Silver at 76 s. Only the high line reaches Gold (1 of 3 here, 1 of 3 in round 9).

**Acceptance test** (dev server 5188, `route-play-rt-x-m.mjs` LINE=low and LINE=high, `balance-probe-m.mjs` CRUISE=10 NOBOOST=1, seeds 22, 58, 130, SIMT 400):
1. Standard low per-run total is at least **0.85** of the high line's total.
2. Standard low reaches Silver in 3 of 3 runs and Gold in at least 1 of 3.
3. The high line still reaches Silver in at least 2 of 3. No bot reaches Ace.
4. Lazy still gets Bronze at most.
5. Strict slipstream share of the low score stays at or below 50%. The breakdown still adds up in every run.
6. Crash-classify: 0 hop-like and 0 on a pad lip at 12 m and 20 m on all 8 seeds. p95 frame time stays under 12 ms.

One option that adds no points: let a slipstream chain feed the clock, for example +1 s per payout from chain 3. Then a street run lasts as long as a roof run.

## Other gaps (ranked)

1. **Music clicks.** Spikes on the 16th-note grid: 0.7 a second at chain 3 and about 4 a second in the last 10 s. They are about 0.08 in size against music steps of 0.005, and they reach the master output. Test: run `music-run.mjs` TAP=1 on seed 22, low line, full run. The click count on the music bus is 0 (now 118). A click is a step over 10 times the local 2 ms RMS step and over 0.004.
2. **Music level and phone balance.** Run -25 to -28, title -33, game over -31 LUFS-like, peak -7 dBFS. The title has 73% of its energy below 150 Hz. Test: the run measures -18 ± 3. In the phone band (above 200 Hz) the title is within 4 dB of the run. Peak stays at -1 dBFS or below, with 0 clipped samples.
3. **The run loop repeats every 7.68 s.** One 4-bar phrase for the whole run. Test: the in-run music bus shows no exact repeat (correlation over 0.8) within 30 s at a fixed chain level. For example, an 8 or 16 bar form with an A and B section, or a variation every second pass.
4. **The same city on every load.** Seed 7 and the same first pickup, every time. Test: two loads on different days give different seeds, and the title shows which city it is and its best.
5. **HUD goal and mobile pops** (unchanged from round 9). The goal row is 15 px tall. On iPhone the medal banner overlaps `#slip-pop` at 2 of 2 passes and the objective pill at 1 of 2. Test: the goal row is at least 20 px tall and shows a "to Gold" number. In a full touch run the banner, slip pop and objective never overlap.

## Regressions: none found

- **Medals** (needed: lazy Bronze at most, low and high Silver in 2 of 3, no Ace): lazy 1,773 Bronze, 811 none, 1,066 Bronze. Low 2 of 3 Silver. High 3 of 3 Silver or better (one Gold). Best 6,789, no Ace. Breakdown adds up in diagnostics and the game-over DOM in 9 of 9 bot runs plus both journeys. The fanfares heard equal the passes in all 9 runs.
- **Crash-classify, 8 seeds, verbose:** 12 m: 617 s, 19 deliveries, 42 charged (4.1 a minute, round 9 3.2), **0 hop-like**. 20 m: 801 s, 31 deliveries, 30 charged (2.2 a minute), **0 hop-like**. The 12 m rate is higher. 39 of the 42 came from under 10 m/s. None rose without climb. I count the higher rate as bot noise.
- **Pad lip:** 10 crashes within 30 m of the target. All targets are street pads (0.4 m). All hits are building faces with tops of 8.8 to 58.6 m at 14.5 to 17 m/s. **0 on a pad lip.**
- **Flat-frame probe:** 858 frames, **0 flat**.
- **Page errors:** 0 on desktop and mobile. Music scheduler: late 0, resyncs 0 in all runs.

## Performance

Headless Chromium caps at 120 Hz (8.3 ms).
- Desktop 1280x720, medal journey (107 s of flight, music on): 12,864 frames, **median 8.30 ms, p95 9.00 ms, max 9.4, 0 over 20 ms**.
- iPhone 13 held sideways, touch: 10,503 frames, **median 8.30, p95 8.90, max 9.4, 0 over 20 ms**.
- Round 9: 8.3 / 9.2 ms. The music costs nothing measurable.
- First load, production build: **about 0.76 MB** (JS 723 KB, CSS 28 KB, HTML 9 KB). lil-gui (31 KB) loads only with `?debug`. Budget 15 MB: pass.

## Screenshots (progress/round-10/critic/)

- Music chip and gesture path: d-title-locked, d-title-music-on, d-title-music-off-after-reload, d-pause-chip, d-over-chip, and the same with m- for iPhone 13 held sideways
- Medal journey, desktop seed 22: d-j22-h01-title, h02-low-drafting, h03-low-meter-half, h04-low-payout-pop, h05-low-payout-chain, h08-end, h09-goal-hud, h10-medal1, h10-medal2, h11-over, h12-restart, h13-title-after
- Medal journey, mobile seed 22: m-j22-h01 to h13 (same set)
- Medal passes from bots: M-low-seed22/58/130-pass*, M-high-seed22/58/130-pass*, M-low-c10-seed22/130-pass1 (lazy)
- Route crashes: Q-high-seed22/58/130-crash*. Near-target crashes: N-alt12-*, N-alt20-*

Scripts (progress/round-10/critic-scripts/): copies of all round 9 scripts, plus:

# Drone Dash, round 10 builder: adaptive music

Concern: the game had no music. The title was silent, and nothing in the audio followed the chain, the clock or a medal chase.

## Musical design

- **Key and tempo.** C major at 125 BPM, on a 16th-note grid (one step = 0.12 s). The medal fanfare uses the same grid: its notes are 0.12 s apart. The start sting notes are 0.06 s apart. The pickup and delivery chimes are C major. The slipstream ticks climb D-F-Ab-B, and the no-medal game-over sting falls C-Ab-F-C. So the borrowed chords Ab, Bb and Fm come from sounds that are already in the game.
- **Title loop.** Fmaj7, Em7, Dm7, Gsus, two bars per chord (about 15 s). It has a soft triangle pad and a bass note on each bar. A plucked eighth-note arpeggio has a dotted-eighth echo. Each chord gets one high bell. There are no drums. It fades in over 1.2 s after the first press.
- **Run track.** C, Am, F, G, one chord per bar. The layers build with the slipstream chain:

| Chain | Section (`audio.music.section`) | `layer` | Layers playing | Target intensity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | base | 1 | pad + syncopated bass | 0.30 |
| 1 | drums | 2 | + kick on 1 and 3, offbeat hats, octave bass pickup | 0.50 |
| 2 | arp | 3 | + four-on-the-floor kick, eighth-note arpeggio | 0.68 |
| 3+ | lead | 4 | + claps on 2 and 4, 16th arpeggio, ghost hats, lead melody | 0.85 |

  A close medal chase (the last 15% of the way to the next medal) adds ghost hats and +0.05 intensity. The pad lowpass opens from 450 Hz to 2.1 kHz as intensity rises (smoothed, about 0.6 s).
- **Last 10 s ("final", layer 5).** The harmony changes to Ab, Bb, Ab, G7. The bass plays driving eighth-note octaves. The section adds four-on-the-floor, claps, 16th hats, a 16th arpeggio and a ticking high C on the eighths. Target intensity is 0.92 to 0.98. The change lands on the next beat, so the groove stays in time. If a time bonus lifts the clock above 12 s, the run section comes back. The gap between 10 s and 12 s stops the music from flipping back and forth.
- **Game over.** The sting depends on the medal. With no medal it is the old falling C-Ab-F-C. With a medal it is a rising G-C-E with a held C major chord and one bell for each tier. A slow loop then swells in over 1.8 s under the sting:
  - No medal ("calm"): Fm, C, Am, Gsus with a falling sigh note.
  - With a medal: C, Fmaj7, Am, G with bells that climb the chord. Silver adds a falling line. Gold and Ace add a quiet octave sparkle.
- **Ducking.** The music bus has its own duck gain. Each cue sets a depth and a hold time, and overlapping ducks keep the deeper level and the later end.

| Cue | Duck level | Hold |
|---|---|---|
| Medal fanfare (timed to the banner delay) | 0.28 (−11 dB) | 1.25 s |
| Crash | 0.35 | 0.55 s |
| Delivery | 0.45 | 0.7 s |
| Game-over sting | 0.5 | 1.0 s |
| Pickup | 0.6 | 0.35 s |
| Slip payout | 0.7 | 0.25 s |

- **Mix and safety.** The music runs at 0.5 of the 0.8 master. It goes through a 55 Hz highpass and a 6.5 kHz lowpass, so there are no harsh highs. Small speakers cannot play notes below 55 Hz, and those notes waste headroom. Hats are band-passed at 7.2 kHz at very low level. Bass sits in octave 2-3 (73 to 130 Hz) with triangle harmonics, so phones still reproduce it. The master is now glue compressor (−14 dB, 4:1), then a brick-wall limiter (−2 dB, 20:1, 2 ms attack). The music never uses the `square` oscillator. The fanfare brass stays the only square wave below 1 kHz, which the critic's fanfare count depends on.
- **Scheduler.** A lookahead scheduler on `AudioContext.currentTime` schedules 0.2 s ahead. It wakes on a 25 ms interval and also on every game frame. There is no setTimeout per note. A note scheduled with a start time in the past counts as `late`. If the timer was starved for more than 0.25 s, the grid skips forward. That skip counts as `resyncs`, and no burst of notes plays. When music is off, nothing is scheduled. On the title and game-over screens a hidden tab suspends the context. When the tab is visible again, the context resumes. Cost is about 40 short oscillator or noise nodes a second at full intensity. There is one shared filter per drum voice and one echo delay. No second convolver was added.
- **Gesture and title.** Any pointerdown, touchend, click or keydown anywhere (the title card too) starts the AudioContext. The title loop then plays. Pressing Play still starts the run in one press. Until then a pulsing amber chip at the top right reads "Click or press a key for sound" (desktop) or "Tap for sound" (touch).
- **Music toggle.** The chip turns into "Music on" or "Music off" after the first press. It shows on the title, pause (below the pause button) and game-over screens. The M key toggles music anywhere. The setting is stored in localStorage `drone-dash-music-v1`, wrapped in try/catch. It only affects music: SFX and the rotor are unchanged. There was no existing sound toggle.

## Diagnostics and hooks

- `diagnostics.audio = { state, music: { enabled, unlocked, playing, track, section, layer, layers, intensity, target, chain, chase, bpm, gain, duck, ducks, lastDuck, late, resyncs, notes, meter, lastFanfare } }`
- `__GAME__.audioMeter(true)` reads the RMS of the music bus and the SFX bus with AnalyserNodes every frame. For each medal fanfare it records `lastFanfare = { sfxRmsDb, sfxPeakDb, musicRmsDb, musicBeforeDb, marginDb }` over the 1.2 s fanfare window.
- `__GAME__.music(on)` works like the chip.
- All existing hooks are unchanged (`start`, `advance`, `externalClock`, `tune`, `place`, `sites`, test hooks). The bloom clamps in `ObjectiveMarker.ts` are untouched.

## Files changed

- `src/systems/AudioSystem.ts`: limiter, music bus, layer buses, sequencer, ducking, meters, `musicInfo()`, medal-aware `gameOver(tier)`, ducks on the cues.
- `src/systems/music.ts` (new): chords, progressions, lead line and patterns. Data only.
- `src/game/Game.ts`:
  - gesture unlock anywhere and scene changes (title, run, over)
  - `setRunState(chain, timeLeft, chase)` and `musicFrame(dt)` each frame
  - chip and M key
  - hidden-tab suspend on title and over
  - `audio` in diagnostics, `audioMeter` and `music` hooks
- `src/ui/Hud.ts`: `musicButton`, `setMusic()`, `musicLocked`.
- `index.html`: `#music-toggle` chip.
- `src/styles.css`: chip styles. The chip pulses while locked. When reduced motion is set, it does not pulse.
- `src/vite-env.d.ts`: types for `audio`, `audioMeter` and `music`.

## Numbers (scripts and logs in `builder-scripts/`, shots in `builder-shots/`)

**1. Music on every screen** (`music-screens.mjs`, 10 s per screen, sampled every 0.5 s, `screens-desktop.log` and `screens-mobile.log`).

| Screen | Desktop: playing, min gain | iPhone 13 held sideways: playing, min gain | Track / section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Title (after the first click or tap on empty sky) | 20/20, 0.17 | 20/20, 0.20 | title / loop |
| Run | 20/20, 0.50 | 20/20, 0.50 | run / base |
| Game over | 20/20, 0.08 (swelling in) | 20/20, 0.08 | over / calm |

Before the first press: context `none`, playing false, and the chip invites the press (`m-01-title-before-press`, `d-01-title-before-press`). Page errors: 0.

**2. Follows the run** (`route-play-music.mjs` = round 9 `route-play-rt-x-m.mjs` with the same control and log-only music sampling, LINE=low, SIMT=400, `low-music.log`). Intensity is the median of samples where the chain level had held for 1.2 s or more.

| Seed | Chain 0 | Chain 3+ | Higher at 3+ | Last 10 s: before → in final | Layer before → final |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 22 | 0.35 | 0.851 | yes | 0.709 → 0.958 | 3-4 → 5 |
| 58 | 0.317 | 0.85 | yes | 0.671 → 0.938 | 3-4 → 5 |
| 130 | 0.30 | 0.90 | yes | 0.845 → 0.98 | 4 → 5 |

3 of 3 on both checks. The high line (`m-high.log`) never chains past 1-2, stays at "base" at 0.30 and moves to final at 0.92 in 3 of 3.

**3. Fanfare audible.** Over the 1.2 s fanfare window, the SFX bus RMS minus the music bus RMS was:
- Low line, 5 fanfares: +12.7 to +17.6 dB.
- High line, 7 fanfares: +18.3 to +21.2 dB.

The duck reached 0.28 in every run. The music fell from about −30 to −35 dBFS open to −38 to −45 dBFS under the fanfare. The critic's fanfare count (square below 1 kHz) still equals the passes: low 2/1/2, high 2/2/3.

**4. Toggle.** The chip changes to off and stores "0". After a reload, music is still off (enabled false, playing false). M turns it on and stores "1", which survives a reload. Pass on desktop and mobile.

**5. Performance and scheduler.** Headless runs are capped at 120 Hz.

| Run | Frames | p95 | Max | Over 20 ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Low line, 3 seeds | 10,099 to 13,089 | 9.0 to 9.1 ms | 16.7 ms | 0 |
| High line, 3 seeds | 14,607 to 19,512 | 9.1 to 9.2 ms | 17.6 ms | 0 |
| Hand-fly desktop | 9,580 | 9.60 ms (round 9: 9.20) | 10.4 ms | 0 |
| Hand-fly mobile | 9,578 | 9.70 ms (round 9: 9.30) | 10.4 ms | 0 |

Scheduler: **0 late events and 0 resyncs** in every run (low, high, hand-fly, screens). Music adds about 0.4 ms to p95, still under 12 ms.

## No regressions

- **crash-classify, 8 seeds, 0 hop-like at both heights:**
  - 12 m: 644 s, 19 deliveries, 30 charged (2.8/min).
  - 20 m: 779 s, 29 deliveries, 21 charged (1.6/min).
  - Verbose 12 m: 31 charged (3.1/min). Verbose 20 m: 29 charged (2.3/min).
- **Pad lip: 0.** Near-target crashes:
  - Three are building faces near street pads (0.4 m), with wall tops at 10.6, 14.7 and 20.2 m.
  - One is seed 7 near the Bay Lofts rooftop pad (32.5 m). The drone hit at 21 m, 12 m below the 33 m roof edge, so it hit the facade, not the lip.
- **Medals:**

| Pilot | Seed 22 | Seed 58 | Seed 130 | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lazy (centre, 10 m/s, no boost) | 1,728 Bronze | 766 none | 255 none | Pass (Bronze at most) |
| Standard low | 3,658 Silver | 1,792 Bronze | 2,562 Silver | Pass (2 of 3) |
| High | 4,007 Silver | 4,123 Silver | 4,850 Gold | Pass (3 of 3) |

  - No Ace.
  - The breakdown and the game-over DOM add up in 9 of 9 runs.
  - The lazy seed 130 run made no delivery (round 9: 1,186). This is bot noise from real-time control. The music does not touch game state: it only reads chain, clock and score.
  - High seed 130 scored 4,850 (round 9: 5,466).
- **Flat-frame probe:** 958 frames, 0 flat.
- **Build:** `npm run build` passes. First load is about 0.76 MB: JS 723 KB, CSS 28 KB, HTML 9 KB. lil-gui loads only with `?debug`.

## Limits

- I did not listen to the music. The mix levels come from the meters: open music sits at about −30 to −35 dBFS RMS, 10 to 15 dB under the fanfare RMS before ducking. If it sounds too quiet on real speakers, raise `MUSIC_VOL` in `AudioSystem.ts` (0.5 now).
- Pausing still suspends the whole AudioContext (existing behaviour), so the pause screen is silent. The chip there still works.
- The medal fanfare lifts by a whole tone for each tier: D for Silver, E for Gold, F# for Ace. Above Bronze it is not strictly in C. The −11 dB duck keeps it clear of the music.
