# Drone Dash, round 9 critic report

**Verdict:** Medals work. Every run now has a target, a verdict and an honest breakdown, and the round 8 mobile miss is fixed. Nothing regressed. The biggest gap is now audio: the game has no music at all. That is the clearest thing separating it from a polished arcade game.

## Round 8 gap (nothing to play for beyond one number): closed

Scripts are copied to `critic-scripts/`. Output folders are relative (`../critic/`), so no path edits were needed. To read medals I made two log-only copies: `route-play-rt-x-m.mjs` and `balance-probe-m.mjs`. Their control logic is the same as the `-h` scripts. They also log medal passes, the breakdown and the game-over DOM. They count the medal fanfare with a hook on oscillator starts. They save the HUD goal text and a screenshot 0.9 s after each pass. Runs used seeds 22, 58 and 130, with SIMT 400 so every run ended on its own clock. Every run reached game over (none was cut short). Real-time scripts ran one at a time.

Medal lines: Bronze 1,000, Silver 2,250, Gold 4,500, Ace 7,500.

| Pilot | Seed 22 | Seed 58 | Seed 130 | Needed | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lazy (centre, 10 m/s, no boost) | 1,728 Bronze | 696 none | 1,186 Bronze | tier 1 at most | Pass |
| Standard low | 3,658 Silver | 1,722 Bronze | 2,682 Silver | Silver in 2 of 3 | Pass (2 of 3) |
| High line, 40 m | 4,052 Silver | 4,123 Silver | 5,466 Gold | Silver in 2 of 3 | Pass (3 of 3) |
| Any bot at Ace | | | | none | Pass (best 5,466) |

- **Tiers visible.** The title shows all four medals and their scores, desktop and iPhone 13 held sideways (`d-j22-h01-title`, `m-j22-h01-title`). Won medals light up after a run, and the best line reads "BEST 3,658 SILVER" (`d-j22-h13-title-after`). The HUD shows the next medal and its score under the score, for example "BRONZE 1,000", plus a progress bar (`d-j22-h09-goal-hud`). Game over shows the medal, the score and "842 more for Gold" (`d-j22-h11-over`, `m-j22-h11-over`).
- **Breakdown adds up.** Deliveries + fast drops + combo + slipstream equals the final score in 12 of 12 runs: 9 bot runs, 2 medal journeys and the default-city journey. This was checked in diagnostics and in the game-over DOM. The "Flew 1:48" line also adds up (start + drops + slipstream − crashes).
- **Pass is a moment.** Each pass shows a big medal banner with rays, "Next: Gold 4,500", a sparkle burst and a small shake. It plays a three-note fanfare. Diagnostics count it. In all 9 bot runs the fanfares heard equal the passes counted (lazy 1/0/1, low 2/1/2, high 2/2/3). The AudioContext was running. A pass fired in 3 of 3 standard low runs.
- **Saved best.** Best score and best medal survive a reload.

## Scoring checks (round 7 set)

| Check | Needed | Round 8 | Round 9 | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lazy / standard low, score a minute | ≤ 0.8 | 0.39 | **0.57** (963 / 1,697) | Pass |
| Centre 16.3 m/s / centre 8.9 m/s slip points | ≥ 1.3 | 4.2 | **4.1** (475 / 115) | Pass |
| Hug 2.5 m at 16.3 m/s / centre 8.9 m/s | ≥ 2 | 10.8 | **10.4** (1,200 / 115), same on 3 roads | Pass |
| Low / high, score a minute | (0.9 old target) | 1.05 | **0.85** (1,697 / 2,001) | See below |
| High deliveries a minute | ≥ 2.3 | 2.50 | **2.49** | Pass |
| Low crashes a minute | ≤ 1.5 | 0 | **0** | Pass |
| Desktop: first payout after first draft / chain x2 | 10 s / 50 s | 1.1 / 20.5 | **1.4 s / 21.1 s** | Pass |
| Mobile: first payout after first draft / chain x2 | 10 s / 50 s | 11.0 / 19.1 (fail) | **3.7 s / 24.0 s**, rerun **4.2 s / 24.1 s** | Pass |
| Strict slipstream share of low score | ≤ 50% | 62% | **47%** | Pass |

**Strict share.** The street multiplier on drops and the par pause are gone (I checked the code). So the "Slipstream" line is now every point paid by drafting: 3,785 of 8,062 low-line points = 47%. One indirect part remains. Payouts add 0.5 s to the clock (24 s over 3 runs), and the low line earns 15 non-slip points a second. That is about 360 more points, which gives 51%. If you count clock time, it is on the line. On the direct count it is a pass.

## Street line: is it still a real choice?

The number: **0.85** score a minute (1,697 against 2,001). Per run it is much lower: **0.59** (2,687 against 4,547). Street runs end sooner (82 to 108 s against 120 to 164 s). Drops feed the clock, and the street line delivers 1.47 a minute against 2.49.

As a player, the street line still feels like the best part of the game. You fly down a canyon of warm facades at 15 m/s. The chevrons climb. "CLOSER TO WALL" tells you what to do. The chain ticks up with a chime, and the payout pop lands every few seconds. The roof line is calmer and, honestly, duller: a long straight hop at 40 m with a headwind. On the game-over card the street line's "Slipstream ×19 +1,680" is the biggest single line. That reads as a reward, not a consolation.

But the medals now judge the run, not the minute. A player who follows the title ("Fly fast and low") reaches Silver near the end of the run (76 s of about 100). A player who flies high reaches Silver at 80 s and Gold at 147 s. Within a few runs a medal chaser learns that the roof line wins. So the street line is a real and rewarding way to play. It is not the best way to win medals. I rank that as the top "other gap" below, not the biggest one.

## Whole game, as a player

- **First 10 seconds.** Strong. A golden-hour city, a chunky drone, a clear title with controls and now the medal ladder. One press and you fly. The clock starts at once (10 s idle costs 10 of 50 s), which is fine for an arcade game.
- **Onboarding.** Good. The tagline gives the rule. The slip cue names one action. The first payout comes 1.4 s (desktop) or about 4 s (touch) after the first draft. The touch fix is real.
- **Core loop.** Pick up, deliver, draft. It pays for speed, line and wall distance, and now it has a target. It works.
- **Game feel.** Still the best part. Momentum, bank, the drop guide and fair crashes (0 hop-like, 0 on a pad lip).
- **Art.** Warm, coherent low-poly with moving traffic. Finished-looking. The medals (bronze, silver, gold, teal "Ace") match the style.
- **Audio.** Rotor hum, wind, draft whistle, chimes, ticks and the new fanfare. **There is still no music.** The title is silent (the audio starts on the first press). The run is rotor hum and chimes. Game over is a four-note sting, then silence.
- **UI.** Clean. The game-over card is now the best screen: medal, score, "New best", points to the next medal and a breakdown that teaches you where points come from. Weak spots: the HUD goal row is 15 px tall. Its progress bar is a thin dark line that disappears against dark walls (`d-j22-h09-goal-hud`). On mobile the medal banner overlaps the slipstream pop (`#slip-pop`) at both passes. The delivery pop sits on the objective pill (`m-j22-h10-medal1`).
- **Difficulty curve and run length.** Runs last 67 to 164 s. Legs get longer and clock bonuses shrink. Nothing new appears over a run. The fifth delivery plays like the first, and the soundscape does not change either.
- **Game over and restart.** Fast and clear. "Fly again" to control: 77 to 84 ms desktop, 23 to 26 ms touch.
- **Replay pull.** Much better. "842 more for Gold" is a real reason to press "Fly again". The thresholds feel right. Bronze comes about 45 s in for a decent pilot. Silver is a solid run. Gold needs a clean, fast run (1 of 6 bot runs). Ace is out of reach for every bot (best 5,466 of 7,500), which is the right place for a top medal. One weak point: every fresh load is still the same city (seed 7) with the same first pickup.

## Single biggest remaining gap: the game has no music

The best arcade flying and delivery games carry their energy in music. A loop on the title sets the mood. In the run the track lifts as you chain and tightens as the clock runs out. Game over gets its own short cue. Drone Dash now has a full loop, honest scoring and medals, so the missing layer is the soundtrack. The sound you hear for 80 to 160 s of every run is a rotor drone.

Evidence:
- `src/systems/AudioSystem.ts` has rotor, wind, draft, chimes, ticks, a fanfare, a start sting and a game-over sting. There is no music bus, loop or sequencer anywhere in `src/`.
- The title is silent until the first press, because the AudioContext starts on that gesture. A new player's first impression has no sound.
- Nothing in the audio responds to the state of the run. A x5 slipstream chain, a Gold chase with 8 s left, and an idle hover all sound the same apart from one-shot chimes.
- Round 8 ranked this as the top "other gap". It is unchanged.
- The run has no rising arc (see "Difficulty curve" above). Music is the cheapest way to give it one without touching balance.

**Acceptance test** (dev server on 5188, desktop and iPhone 13 held sideways):
1. **Music exists.** A procedural music layer plays on the title after the first tap or key, during the run, and on game over. Diagnostics expose `audio.music = { playing, layer, gain, bpm }`. Over 10 s on each screen `playing` is true and `gain` is above 0.
2. **It follows the run.** Run `route-play-rt-x.mjs` on the low line, seeds 22, 58, 130. In 3 of 3 runs, `audio.music.layer` (or intensity) is higher at a slipstream chain of 3 or more than at a chain of 0. In the last 10 s of the clock it changes again (faster tempo or an extra layer) in 3 of 3 runs. A medal pass ducks or lifts the music for the fanfare, so the fanfare stays audible.
3. **It is mixable.** A mute or music toggle exists on the title or pause screen and is remembered after reload.
4. **No regressions.** Frame time p95 stays under 12 ms on desktop and mobile. First load stays under 15 MB. The round 9 scoring table above stays within 10%.

## Other gaps (ranked)

1. **Medals reward the roof line.** The title says "fly fast and low". But per run, the low line scores 0.59 of the high line (2,687 against 4,547). Low runs end 25 to 55 s sooner because they deliver less (1.47 against 2.49 a minute). Low pilots reach Silver at about 76 s. High pilots reach Gold. Test: on seeds 22, 58, 130, standard low reaches at least 0.8 of the high line's per-run score. The strict share stays at or below 50%. One option: give the clock more time from slipstream chains, which adds no points.
2. **The same city on every load.** Seed 7 and "Juniper Lofts Rooftop" are always first. A daily or rotating city with its own best and medals can add a lot of replay pull to the medal ladder. Test: two loads on different days give different seeds, and the title shows which city it is and its best.
3. **The HUD goal is hard to read.** The row is 15 px tall, 18 px from the left. The progress bar is a thin dark bar that vanishes on dark facades. The run shows no "points to go" number. Test: the goal row shows "1,240 to Gold" or similar, and the bar has a light track at least 4 px tall.
4. **Pops stack on mobile.** The medal banner overlaps `#slip-pop` at 2 of 2 passes in the touch run. The delivery pop "+502" covers the objective pill. When the off-screen marker is clamped bottom-left it sits under the touch stick. Test: no overlap between the medal banner, slip pop, objective pill and stick in a full touch run.
5. **No arc inside a run.** Leg length and clock bonus change, but nothing new appears and nothing on screen marks the run's phases. Music (main gap) is the first step. A late-run event (a rush order or a double-points street) is a good second step.

## Regressions: none found

- **crash-classify, 8 seeds, 12 m:** 650 s sim, 19 deliveries, 31 charged (2.9/min), **0 hop-like**. **20 m:** 804 s, 31 deliveries, 32 charged (2.4/min), **0 hop-like**. Verbose reruns: 12 m 33 charged (3.2/min), 20 m 25 (2.1/min), 0 hop-like.
- **Pad lip:** 6 crashes within 30 m of the target across both verbose runs. All targets are street pads (0.4 m). All hits are building faces with tops of 10.6 to 20.2 m at 13.5 to 17.1 m/s. **0 on a pad lip.**
- **arrival-metrics, 8 seeds:** 64 legs, 62 arrived. The seed 91 timeout is the known straight-line bot case. The seed 7 timeout is the clock running out, after the bot stalled 30.5 s on the parapet beside the first rooftop pad (`A-seed7-stall-final-approach.jpg`). That leg gave all 10 stalls and 110 of the 136 "slow and high" samples. On a rerun of seed 7 the same leg took 2.8 s, with 0 stalls on all 9 legs. I count it as bot noise. Median cruise 6.1 s, median final approach 3.3 s, marker off screen 2.0%.
- **Flat-frame probe:** 1,050 frames, **0 flat**.
- **Page errors:** 0 on desktop and mobile.

## Performance

Headless Chromium caps at 120 Hz, so 8.3 ms is the cap.

- Desktop 1280x720, medal journey (about 107 s of flight): 12,834 frames, **median 8.30 ms, p95 9.20 ms, max 9.5 ms, 0 over 20 ms**. Hand-fly (80 s): 9,577 frames, median 8.30, p95 9.20, max 16.7, 0 over 20 ms.
- Mobile (iPhone 13 held sideways, touch), medal journey: 12,663 frames, median 8.30, p95 9.20, max 9.5, 0 over 20 ms. Hand-fly runs: p95 9.30, max 9.5, 0 over 20 ms.
- Round 8: 8.3 / 8.8 ms. p95 is 0.4 ms higher, well inside 12 ms.
- First load, production build: **about 0.74 MB** (JS 708 KB, CSS 27 KB, HTML 8 KB). lil-gui (31 KB) loads only with `?debug`. Budget 15 MB: pass.

## Screenshots (progress/round-9/critic/)

- Medal journey, desktop seed 22: d-j22-h01-title, h02-low-drafting, h03-low-meter-half, h04-low-payout-pop, h05-low-payout-chain, h08-end, h09-goal-hud, h10-medal1, h10-medal2, h11-over, h12-restart, h13-title-after
- Medal journey, desktop seed 58 (first attempt, logs lost to a script bug, shots valid): d-j58-h01 to h13
- Medal journey, mobile seed 22: m-j22-h01-title, h02 to h05, h08-end, h09-goal-hud, h10-medal1, h11-over, h12-restart, h13-title-after
- Medal passes from bots: M-low-seed22/58/130-pass*, M-high-seed22/58/130-pass*, M-low-c10-seed22/130-pass1 (lazy)
- Hand flight: d-h01 to d-h08, m-h01 to m-h08 (the second mobile run wrote over the first)
- Player journey (default city): J-00-title, J-01-idle-01s/04s/10s, J-02-delivery-1, J-03-gameover, J-04-restart
- Crash classify: K-alt12-*, K-alt20-*. Near target: N-alt12-*, N-alt20-*. Route crashes: Q-high-seed58/130-crash*. Arrival stall: A-seed7-stall-final-approach

Scripts (progress/round-9/critic-scripts/): copies of all round 8 scripts, plus `route-play-rt-x-m.mjs` and `balance-probe-m.mjs` (log-only medal additions) and `medal-journey.mjs` (hand-fly pilot on the street line for a whole run, with title, HUD, pass, game-over and restart checks). `queue*.sh` ran the timing-sensitive scripts one at a time. Logs: m-lazy, m-low, m-high, hf-desktop, hf-mobile, hf-mobile-2, hug, flat, cc12, cc20, ccv12, ccv20, am-all, am-seed7-rerun, journey, mj-desktop, mj-mobile, build.
builder.md
# Drone Dash, round 9 builder

Main concern: there was nothing to play for beyond one unexplained number. Two leftovers: the mobile first payout (11 s) and the strict slipstream share (62%).

**Honest summary: one acceptance number fails.** The strict share is now 46%, but low score a minute is 0.76 of high (needed 0.9). The two targets cannot both be met with the current bots. The section "Leftover B" shows why. Everything else passes.

## Design

### Medals (score goals)

There are four medals for one run's score: **Bronze 1,000, Silver 2,250, Gold 4,500, Ace 7,500** (`GOALS` in config.ts).

Why these thresholds (deterministic sim, plus real-time checks, seeds 22, 58, 130):
- Lazy pilot runs: 1,723 / 791 / 255 (real time: 1,728 / 816 / 1,141). Silver sits above the best lazy run with a margin of 30%. A slow, centred flier gets Bronze at most.
- Standard low runs: 3,688 / 1,792 / 2,782 (real time: 3,553 / 1,792 / 2,537). Silver in 2 of 3.
- High runs: 6,859 / 4,123 / 4,760 (real time: 5,524 / 4,078 / 5,421). Gold in 2 of 3, Silver in 3 of 3.
- Ace is 9% above the best bot run seen (6,859) and 36% above the best real-time bot run. Ace needs a long, clean run with a deep combo.
- The steps roughly double (1,000, 2,250, 4,500, 7,500), so each medal feels like a new level.

Where the medals show:
- **Title:** a row of four medal chips with names and scores, under Play. Chips for medals already won get a gold outline. The best line reads "Best 3,733 Silver".
- **In-run HUD:** one compact row under the score, in the top-left corner: next medal disc, its name and score ("SILVER 2,250"), and a thin 56 px progress bar from the last medal. No change to the area below the drone, which was already crowded on mobile.
- **Medal moment:** a large medal banner shows ("SILVER!"). The medal flips in, rays turn behind it, and a pill says "Next: Gold 4,500". A three-note fanfare plays. It rises one tone per medal and adds one bell per medal. A sparkle burst in the medal colour comes off the drone, the camera shakes a little, and the HUD goal row flashes. A drop usually carries the score across a line. So if a delivery pop is still showing, the banner waits until that pop has shown for about 1 s, then replaces it. The sound waits with it. On short (phone) screens the medal sits beside the text, so the banner stays clear of the objective pill.
- **Game over:** medal reached (or "No medal yet"), the score, "New best!", "767 more for Gold", then a breakdown:
  - Deliveries ×n (100 + 1.2 per metre of each leg)
  - Fast drops ×n (+75 each, before the combo)
  - Combo bonus (up to x2.5): the extra points from the combo multiplier
  - Slipstream ×payouts
  - Score (total)
  
  The game counts each line as a whole number at the moment it is earned. So the lines sum exactly to the score. Below that is the clock story: "Flew 1:48. 50 s start, +48 s drops, +10 s slipstream, −3 s 1 crash". Crashes cost seconds, not points, so they show in the time line. The time line sums exactly to the seconds flown. It also explains why street runs are shorter. Then come the best score and best medal, and "Fly again".
- **Storage:** the best score is in `drone-dash-best-v1` (unchanged). The best medal is in `drone-dash-best-tier-v1`. Each read and write is in try/catch.
- **Diagnostics:** `goals = { tier, tierName, next, passes, passList: [{tier, name, score, t}], best, bestTier, thresholds }` and `breakdown = { drops, fast, combo, slip, fastCount, dropSeconds, slipSeconds, crashSeconds, total }`. When one drop crosses two lines, both are counted.

I did not move the desktop slipstream meter. It was optional, and I kept the risk low.

### Leftover A: mobile first payout

On the first meter of a run only, the speed factor is at least 0.6 (`introSpeedFloor`) once the drone is above 4 m/s. So speed counts once on the intro meter, not twice. A touch pilot drafting at 6 m/s now fills the 4-metre intro meter in about 1.5 s. Every later meter is unchanged, so the lazy pilot gains one early 45-point payout and nothing more.

### Leftover B: strict slipstream share

Every point that exists only because of drafting is now in the "Slipstream" line. So the strict share and the direct share are the same number:
- **Street multiplier removed.** A slipstream chain held at the drop no longer multiplies the delivery.
- **Par pause removed.** Drafting no longer stops the fast-drop clock.
- **Par loosened** so that the street route can make it without drafting: par = street-route length / 9 m/s + 7 s (was / 12.5 + 5 with the draft pause). The standard low bot makes 7 of 7 fast drops, the same as before with the pause. The high line already made every par.
- **Payouts smaller:** 45 + 25 per chain step, so x5 pays 145. Before, it was 50 + 30, and x5 paid 170.

Why the 0.9 ratio cannot also be met: if the share is at most 50%, low score can be at most 2 × low non-draft points. Low non-draft points are about 900 a minute in the sim (about 900 real time). High is about 2,200 a minute. So the best possible ratio at a 50% share is about 0.80. In real time I got 0.76 at a 46% share. The low bot delivers 1.48 a minute against 2.62 for the high bot, and the high bot builds deeper combos (x3.5). Per-delivery changes scale both lines alike. I tested a combo cap of 3 or 4, a stronger headwind and other combo curves in the sim. None reaches 0.9 at a 50% share without cutting the high line below about 2.3 deliveries a minute or gutting the combo. The only other way is a new non-draft reward for the street route (for example a bonus for a leg flown under the roofline). I did not add it. It can look like the street multiplier moved into a new category. This is a choice for the next round: accept the ratio, weaken the roof line, or add a street-route reward.

## Files changed

- src/game/config.ts: `GOALS` (medals). In `RUN`: `fastBonus`, `parSpeed` 9, `parSlack` 7, `comboStep` (0.5, unchanged behaviour). In `SLIPSTREAM`: `introSpeedFloor` 0.6, points 45 and chainStep 25. `parQuality` and `hotStep` removed.
- src/game/goals.ts (new): `tierFor`, `tierName`, `nextGoal`, best-medal storage.
- src/systems/DeliverySystem.ts: `tally` (breakdown in points and seconds). Street multiplier and par pause removed. Par from config.
- src/systems/Slipstream.ts: intro speed floor. `hotPoints` stays at 0 for older scripts.
- src/systems/AudioSystem.ts: `medal(tier, delay)` fanfare.
- src/game/Game.ts: medal tracking and moment (`checkMedal`), game-over summary, best medal, diagnostics `goals` and `breakdown`. New test hooks, added only: `__GAME__.externalClock(on)` (only `advance` moves the game, fully deterministic) and `__GAME__.tune(patch)` (patch tunables for builder sims). Existing hooks are unchanged.
- src/ui/Hud.ts: `setBest(best, bestTier)` with the title medal row, `setGoal`, `medalPop`, `showOver(summary)`.
- index.html: HUD goal row, medal banner, title medal row, new game-over card (the `#over-screen` and `#again-button` ids are kept).
- src/styles.css: medal discs, goal row, banner, title row, game-over card, phone layout. The old `.over-stats` styles are removed.
- src/vite-env.d.ts: diagnostics and hook types.
- Not touched: the bloom clamps in src/entities/ObjectiveMarker.ts, flight, crash rules, the headwind.

## Numbers

Scripts: progress/round-8/critic-scripts copied to progress/round-9/. Only the output folder changed (`./builder-shots/`). Dev server on 5188. The real-time scripts ran one at a time (tools/rt-batch.sh). Logs are in progress/round-9/logs/.

| Test | Needed | Result | Pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lazy pilot medal (bp-lazy, real time) | Bronze or none | 1,728 Bronze / 816 none / 1,141 Bronze | yes |
| Standard low medal (rp-low) | Silver or better in 2 of 3 | 3,553 Silver / 1,792 Bronze / 2,537 Silver | yes |
| High medal (rp-high) | Silver or better in 2 of 3 | 5,524 Gold / 4,078 Silver / 5,421 Gold | yes |
| No bot at Ace | below 7,500 | best real-time 5,524, best sim 6,859 | yes |
| Breakdown sums to score | every run | diagnostics: 12 of 12 sim runs (4 pilots × 3 seeds). DOM rows and shown score: 10 of 10 runs that reached game over (2 high runs hit the 150 s script cap first) | yes |

| Hand-fly mobile (iPhone 13 held sideways, touch) | 10 s / 50 s | draft 4.1 s, payout 5.7 s (**1.6 s**), x2 at 23.5 s | yes |
| Strict slipstream share, standard low | at most 50% | 3,605 / 7,882 = **46%** (direct = strict, hotPoints 0) | yes |

Wall-offset pilot (sim only): 63% slipstream share. That is a choice of style, not the standard low test.

Regressions:
- **crash-classify-v, all 8 seeds.** 12 m: 603 s, 17 deliveries, 35 charged (3.5/min), **0 hop-like**. 20 m: 737 s, 27 deliveries, 30 charged (2.4/min), **0 hop-like**.

The crash rules have not changed since round 8. **0 on the pad lip itself.**

critic.md
# Drone Dash, round 8 critic report

**Verdict:** The lazy pilot no longer wins: speed and wall distance now pay, and nothing broke. Two acceptance lines miss (mobile first payout, strict slipstream share). The scoring loop is good enough now. The biggest gap is no longer balance: the game never tells a player what a good run is, so there is little to come back for.

## Round 7 gap (the meter paid for time near walls): closed in substance, two lines missed

Scripts are copied to `critic-scripts/`. Output folders are relative (`../critic/`), so no path edits were needed. For the share, I ran `route-play-rt-x-h.mjs` and `balance-probe-h.mjs`. They are the same scripts with one log-only addition: `slipstream.hotPoints` in the result line. Control logic is identical. Real-time scripts ran one at a time.

| Test | Needed | Round 7 | Round 8 | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Lazy / standard low score a minute | at most 0.8 | 1.01 | **0.39** (847 / 2,174) | Pass |
| 2a. Centre 16.3 m/s / centre 8.9 m/s slip points (each road) | at least 1.3 | 1.0 | **4.2** (550 / 130) | Pass |
| 2b. Hug 2.5 m at 16.3 m/s / centre 8.9 m/s | at least 2 | 1.9 | **10.8** (1,400 / 130), same on all 3 roads | Pass |
| 3a. Low / high score a minute | at least 0.9 | 1.22 | **1.05** (2,174 / 2,072) | Pass |
| 3b. High deliveries a minute | at least 2.3 | 2.71 | **2.50** | Pass |
| 3c. Low crashes a minute | at most 1.5 | 0 | **0** | Pass |
| 3d. Desktop: first payout after first draft / chain x2 | 10 s / 50 s | 2.1 s / 8.0 s | **1.1 s** / 20.5 s | Pass |
| 3e. Mobile: first payout after first draft / chain x2 | 10 s / 50 s | 3.5 s / 14.8 s | **11.0 s** / 19.1 s (rerun: **11.3 s** / 20.1 s) | **Fail** |
| 4. Slipstream share of low score | at most 50% | 68% | 41% direct, **62% strict** | **Fail (strict)** |

Route pilots, seeds 22, 58, 130, SIMT 150:

| Pilot | Time | Deliveries/min | Score/min | Score per run | Crashes | Slip pts | Street bonus on drops |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lazy: centre, 10 m/s, no boost | 203 s | 0.89 | 847 | 955 | 0 | 1,260 | 428 |
| Standard low | 285 s | 1.47 | 2,174 | 3,442 | 0 | 4,230 | 2,183 |
| Wall offset 5.5 m | 252 s | 1.19 | 2,119 | 2,967 | 1 | 4,930 | 1,555 |
| High line, 40 m | 408 s | 2.50 | 2,072 | 4,697 | 4 | 480 | 0 |

Mobile miss, in detail. The touch pilot first drafts at 4.5 to 4.7 s at 5.8 to 5.9 m/s. The speed factor is then about 0.2 (no draft below 4 m/s, full at 13). So the short intro meter takes 11 s to fill. On desktop the same pilot fills it in 1.1 s. A new touch player who has not yet pushed the stick to the rim sees the meter crawl for 11 s. That is exactly the player the intro meter was for.

## Slipstream share, both ways

- **Direct:** slipstream payouts are 4,230 of 10,325 standard low points = **41%**.
- **Strict:** add the street multiplier on deliveries (x1 + 0.15 per chain step held at the drop). It paid 2,183 points that exist only because of drafting. Total 6,413 = **62%**. Fail.
- The street bonus is 36% of all low-line delivery points (2,183 of 6,095).
- A third part is not counted: drafting at quality 0.55 or more stops the fast-drop par clock. Some fast-drop bonuses (+75 and the combo step) exist only because of this. So the true strict share is 62% or more.
- Wall-offset pilot: 55% direct, 73% strict.

## Overcorrection check

- **Centred street flight is not worthless at speed.** At 16.3 m/s the centre earns 550 slip points in 12 s. That is 39% of the wall hug (1,400). It is a fair middle tier.
- **Centred slow flight is nearly worthless.** At 8.9 m/s: 130 points in 12 s, 2 payouts. The lazy pilot fell from 2,783 to 847 a minute. That is intended. But a slow beginner is that pilot, and the mobile result above shows the cost.
- **The wall hug does not dominate.** On a straight it pays 2.5 times the centre at cruise. In route play it does not convert: the 5.5 m offset pilot scored 2,119 a minute against 2,174 centred. It made fewer deliveries (1.19 against 1.47 a minute) and crashed once. The skill reward lives on straights only. Corners and kerbs eat it. This is fine, not overcorrected.
- **HUD.** One-word cues ("FASTER!", "WALL HUG!") read well on both screens. The three chevrons are about 10 px on desktop. You must look for them to read them. On desktop the whole meter sits in the bottom-left corner, 18 px from the edge, far from where the eye is (the drone, centre). On mobile the area below the drone still holds up to five rows: the first-run hint, the cue, the label and chevrons, the meter and the boost bar. The payout pop sits on the drone itself (`m-h03-low-meter-half.jpg`, `m-h04-low-payout-pop.jpg`). It is readable, but it is noise over the street you are flying down.

## Whole game, as a player

- **First 10 seconds.** A strong first look: golden-hour city, a chunky readable drone, a diamond marker with distance, a clear title card with controls. The clock starts the moment you press Play. Hovering 10 s costs 10 of 50 s, with no countdown (`J-01-idle-01s.jpg`, `J-01-idle-10s.jpg`). That is acceptable for an arcade game.
- **Onboarding.** The title gives the rule in one line, and a first-time hint sits under the meter. Pickup, carry and drop are clear. The first payout comes fast on desktop, slow on touch.
- **Core loop.** Pick up, deliver, draft along streets. It now pays for speed and line. It works.
- **Game feel.** Flight is the best part. Momentum, bank and drop guide feel good. Crashes are fair (0 hop-like charges, 0 on a pad lip).
- **Art.** Warm, coherent, low-poly. Moving traffic. It looks finished.
- **Audio.** Rotor hum, wind, a draft whistle, chimes and ticks. **There is no music at all**, on the title, in the run or on game over.
- **UI.** Clean and legible. The game-over card is the weakest screen: score, best, deliveries, top combo, one button (`J-03-gameover.jpg`).
- **Difficulty and run length.** Runs last 52 to 150 s. Legs get longer (70 + 6 m per delivery) and clock bonuses shrink to 55%. Nothing in the run shows this. Nothing new appears. The fifth delivery plays like the first.
- **Game over and restart.** Restart is instant (32 ms from "Fly again" to control).
- **Replay pull.** Weak. The only thing to chase is one number. The player is never told whether 3,653 is good.

## Single biggest remaining gap: nothing to play for beyond one unexplained number

The best score-attack arcade games give every run a target and a verdict. You know what "good" looks like before you start. You see the next goal while you fly. You learn on the results screen why you got what you got. Drone Dash has none of this. The title says "Best 0". The HUD shows score, clock and deliveries. Game over shows four numbers and "Fly again".

Evidence:
- Skill now separates runs clearly: per run, lazy 955, standard low 3,442, high 4,697, my default-city run 3,653. That is a 5x range. The screen turns all of it into bare digits, with no tier, target or rank.
- Score has three sources (drops and combo, slipstream, the street bonus) and two routes with a real trade. The street pays more a minute, and the roof pays more a run (4,697 against 3,442). None of this is shown, so a player cannot learn it.
- Every fresh load is the same city (seed 7) with the same first pickup (Juniper Lofts Rooftop). Only the best score is saved. There is no other memory between runs.
- Seven rounds of balance work made the score mean something. The game does not yet use that meaning.

**Acceptance test** (dev server on 5188, seeds 22, 58, 130, SIMT 150, one browser at a time):
1. **Targets exist and are visible.** The game shows score targets in tiers (for example three medals). The title shows them. The HUD shows the next target and the distance to it during the run. Game over shows the tier reached and the points to the next one. Check in the DOM on desktop and iPhone 13 held sideways.
2. **Targets are calibrated to skill.** Use per-run score. Lazy pilot (`OFF=0 CRUISE=10 NOBOOST=1 balance-probe.mjs`): tier 1 or none in 3 of 3 runs. Standard low and high route pilots (`route-play-rt-x.mjs`): tier 2 or better in at least 2 of 3 runs each. No bot reaches the top tier.
3. **Game over explains the score.** It shows at least: deliveries (with fast drops and combo), slipstream, and street bonus. The lines sum exactly to the final score in 3 of 3 runs, checked against diagnostics.
4. **Crossing a tier is a moment.** Each time the player passes a target, the game gives a visible and audible beat and counts it in diagnostics. It fires at least once in at least 2 of 3 standard low runs.
5. No regressions: route ratios in the table above stay within 10%. Frame time p95 stays under 12 ms.

## Other gaps (ranked)

1. **No music.** The game is silent apart from effects. A light procedural loop that lifts with a chain or a low clock can add more feel than any balance pass. Test: music plays on the title and in the run. Its intensity changes with the chain and when the clock is under 10 s. Diagnostics show this as a gain or layer value.
2. **Mobile first payout regressed to 11.0 s and 11.3 s** after the first draft (needed 10 s, round 7 was 3.5 s). The speed factor makes the intro meter crawl for a touch player at about 6 m/s. Test: under 10 s in two mobile hand-fly runs.
3. **Strict slipstream share is 62%** (needed 50%). The street multiplier on drops is the main cause (2,183 points, 36% of low-line delivery points).
4. **Slip HUD placement.** On mobile, up to five stacked rows below the drone, and the pop sits on the drone. On desktop, the meter and cue sit in the far bottom-left corner, out of the eye line, with 10 px chevrons.
5. **The street and roof trade is invisible.** The low line delivers 1.47 a minute (2.3 a run), and the high line 2.50 (5.7 a run). Low runs end 25 to 45 s sooner. A player who follows "fly low" has shorter runs and does not know why. The breakdown in the main test shows this.

## Regressions: none found

- **crash-classify, all 8 seeds, 12 m:** 735 s sim, 25 deliveries, 37 charged (3.0/min), **0 hop-like**. **20 m:** 765 s, 29 deliveries, 33 charged (2.6/min), **0 hop-like**. (Round 7: 3.8 and 2.1/min.)
- **Pad lip (verbose rerun, all 8 seeds, 12 m and 20 m):** 7 crashes within 30 m of the target. All hit building faces with tops of 10.6 to 35 m at 12 to 16.9 m/s. Street pads are 0.4 m high. The one rooftop target (22.9 m) was hit beside a 35 m wall. **0 on a pad lip.**
- **arrival-metrics, all 8 seeds:** 67 legs, 66 arrived, 1 timeout on seed 91 (the known straight-line bot case, not investigated again). Median final approach 3.3 s, 0 stalls in the final 30 m. Marker off screen 1.4%. Slow and high 0.0%.
- **Flat-frame probe:** 1,018 frames, **0 flat**.
- No page errors on desktop or mobile.

## Performance

Headless Chromium runs at a 120 Hz cap, so the 8.3 ms median is the cap.

- Desktop 1280x720, 80 s hand flight: 9,574 frames, **median 8.30 ms, p95 8.80 ms, max 9.4 ms, 0 over 20 ms** (round 7: 8.3 / 9.6 ms).
- Mobile (iPhone 13 held sideways, touch), 80 s: 9,578 frames, median 8.30 ms, p95 8.80 ms, max 9.4 ms, 0 over 20 ms. Rerun: p95 9.20 ms, max 16.7 ms, 0 over 20 ms.
- First load, production build: **about 0.73 MB** (JS 702 KB, CSS 21 KB, HTML 7 KB). lil-gui (31 KB) loads only with `?debug`. Budget 15 MB: pass.

## Screenshots (progress/round-8/critic/)

- Hand flight, desktop: d-h01-title, d-h02-low-drafting, d-h03-low-meter-half, d-h04-low-payout-pop, d-h05-low-payout-chain, d-h06-high-wind, d-h08-end
- Hand flight, mobile: m-h01-title, m-h02-low-drafting, m-h03-low-meter-half, m-h04-low-payout-pop, m-h05-low-payout-chain, m-h06-high-wind, m-h08-end (the second mobile run wrote over these)
- Player journey (default city): J-00-title, J-01-idle-01s, J-01-idle-04s, J-01-idle-10s, J-02-delivery-1, J-03-gameover, J-04-restart
- Crash classify: K-alt12-*, K-alt20-*. Near target: N-alt12-*, N-alt20-*
- Route pilots: Q-high-seed22/58/130-crash*, B-off5.5-seed130-crash1

Scripts (progress/round-8/critic-scripts/): copies of all round 7 scripts, plus `route-play-rt-x-h.mjs` and `balance-probe-h.mjs` (log-only hotPoints) and `journey.mjs` (new: title, 10 s idle, full run with per-delivery log, game over, restart time). Logs: hug.log, bp-lazy.log, rp-low.log, rp-high.log, bp-hug.log, hf-desktop.log, hf-mobile.log, hf-mobile-2.log, flat.log, journey.log, cc12.log, cc20.log, ccv12.log, ccv20.log, am-all.log.

# Drone Dash, round 8 builder

Concern: the slipstream paid for time spent near walls, not for flying well. A lazy pilot (centred, 10 m/s, no boost) scored the most per minute.

## Design

1. **The meter fills by distance, and speed counts twice.** Fill per second = draft quality x speed (m/s), so it is "draft metres". Draft quality = wall factor x speed factor. The speed factor is 0 below 4 m/s and full from 13 m/s. So 16 m/s fills about 4 to 7 times faster than 9 m/s on the same street, and a crawl barely fills.
2. **The street centre is no longer full strength.** The wall factor is full only within 4 m of a facade (was 9.5 m). The street centre (9 m from both facades) is about 0.7. Hugging a facade (inside 5 m, full at 2.5 m) adds up to 1.6x on top. Reach is unchanged at 16 m.
3. **A chain needs quick payouts.** The chain also resets when the next payout takes more than 9 s. A crawl cannot build x3 to x5. The chain is still lost on a charged crash, and after 6 s out of the draft.
4. **The par pause no longer rewards slowness.** The fast-drop clock only pauses while draft quality is at least 0.55, which means fast and near a facade. The lazy pilot (10 m/s, centred, about 0.47) no longer pauses it.
5. **Deliveries carry the street reward ("street multiplier").** A delivery pays +15% per slipstream chain step held at the drop (x5 = x1.75). The drop pop reads, for example, "Fast drop · street x1.6". These points count as delivery score. Diagnostics track them on their own as `slipstream.hotPoints`. I report them on their own lines below so the critic can judge the split.
6. **Payouts:** 50 points, plus 30 per chain step (x5 = 170). Meter sizes are 14 draft metres at chain 0, plus 4 per chain step. The first meter of a run is 4 draft metres (`introMeter`), so a new player gets a payout about 2 s after the first real draft.
7. **The HUD teaches the rule while you fly.**
   - Three chevrons next to "Slipstream" light up with fill speed. A crawl lights 1, the street centre at cruise 2, a wall hug or boosting 3.
   - A one-word cue above the meter names the limit: "Faster!" (near walls but too slow; this also shows the meter while you are not drafting), "Closer to wall" (fast but centred), or "Wall hug!".
   - Cues are hidden within 25 m of the pad and while the first-run hint shows.
   - The first-run hint now reads "Faster & closer to walls fills it faster". The title tagline reads "Fly fast and low, close to the walls, to ride the slipstream."
   - On mobile the cue sits on its own line above the meter, so it does not collide with the label (see m-* shots).

Not changed: flight, headwind, the high line, crash rules, arrival help, street-distance par formula, the bloom clamps in ObjectiveMarker.ts, and debug hooks. The diagnostics only add fields.

## Files changed

- src/game/config.ts: SLIPSTREAM block rewritten. New keys: `parQuality`, `chainWindow`, `introMeter`, `rateGood`, `rateTop`, `hotStep`. `holdsPar` removed. `fill` and meter sizes are now in draft metres.
- src/systems/Slipstream.ts: distance-based fill, `wall` and `speedFactor` split, `rate`, chain window, intro meter, `hotPoints`.
- src/systems/DeliverySystem.ts: `update(..., hot)` multiplies delivery points and records `lastHotPoints`. The event has a `hot` field.
- src/game/Game.ts: par hold uses `parQuality`, street multiplier at the drop, delivery pop text, HUD rate tier and cue, diagnostics fields.
- src/ui/Hud.ts: `setSlip(..., rate, cue)`, chevrons and cue element.
- index.html: chevrons, cue element, hint and tagline text. src/styles.css: chevron and cue styles.
- src/vite-env.d.ts: diagnostics type.

## Numbers (dev server 5188, one browser at a time; logs in progress/round-8/logs/)

Scripts were copied from round-7/critic-scripts to progress/round-8/scripts/. Only the output folder changed (`../builder-shots/`).

| Test | Result | Target | Pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lazy pilot (bp-lazy) | 907 /min (round 7: 2,783) | | |
| Standard low (rp-low) | 2,220 /min, 1.47 del/min, 0 crashes | | |
| Lazy / standard | **0.41** | at most 0.8 | yes |
| Hug probe, centre 16.3 vs 8.9 m/s | 550 vs 130 = **4.2x**, all 3 roads | at least 1.3 | yes |
| Hug probe, hug 2.5 m at 16.3 vs centre at 8.9 m/s | 1,400 vs 130 = **10.8x** | at least 2 | yes |
| High line (rp-high) | 1,883 /min, **2.45 del/min**, 0.6 crashes/min | at least 2.3 del/min | yes |
| Low / high score a minute | **1.18** | at least 0.9 | yes |
| Low crashes | 0.0 /min | at most 1.5 | yes |
| Slip points share of low score | 4,450 / 10,545 = **42%** | at most 50% | yes |
| Hand-fly desktop | first draft 4.1 s, first payout 5.4 s (**1.3 s**), x2 at 21.3 s | within 10 s, x2 by 50 s | yes |
| Hand-fly mobile (iPhone 13 landscape, touch) | first draft 3.9 s, first payout 8.7 s (**4.8 s**), x2 at 23.2 s | within 10 s, x2 by 50 s | yes |

Honest notes:
- **Street multiplier share.** Use the sim numbers below for the split: in the deterministic sim the street multiplier is about 21% of standard low score. So, for the standard low line: direct slipstream points about 41 to 42%, street multiplier on deliveries about 21%, base delivery points about 37%. Counting the multiplier as slipstream, the street share is about 62%. I counted it as delivery score, because it is paid only by delivering. The critic should judge if that counts.
- **High line numbers move between runs.** Earlier runs in this round: 2,178/min at 2.62 del/min, then 1,883/min at 2.45 del/min. The difference is noise from crashes and combo breaks. The high line's code path is unchanged; slip is 2 to 4% of high score.
- **Standard low also moves between runs.** 1,975, 2,336 and 2,220 per minute in three runs, from small payout tuning between them and run-to-run noise.
- **Hug-offset bot.** In the deterministic sim, the hug-offset bot (OFF 5.5) now beats the standard bot (2,542 vs 2,339 per minute). In round 7 it lost to the lazy pilot.

Deterministic tuning sim (builder tool, not a critic script; same control logic as balance-probe with G.advance steps), final config, seeds 22, 58, 130, SIMT 150:
lazy 792/min (slip 50%), standard 2,339/min (slip 41%, street multiplier 21%), high 2,255/min at 2.71 del/min, hug-offset 2,542/min.

## Regressions

- **crash-classify, all 8 seeds.**
  - 20 m: 26 deliveries, 27 charged (2.2/min), **0 hop-like**.
  - 12 m: 20 deliveries, 37 charged (3.4/min), **1 flagged hop-like**: seed 44 at t 27.45, 3.8 m/s, rose 0.8x m.
  - A seed 44 rerun with the same script gave 0 hop-like. A per-step trace of that crash shows a head-on hit into a facade 6 m above the drone (wallTop 16.95, drone at 11.0) at 14.5 m/s, with no ledge contact. So it is a real crash, and the rise is the bot's altitude hold. These bots steer from the camera, and payout shake now lands at different times, so runs diverge from round 7.
- **Pad lip:** I did not run the verbose crash-classify-v. In the 12 m and 20 m runs, every charged crash near the target (7 and 3) hit a facade; none was on a pad. No code near the crash or pad-edge rules changed.
- **arrival-metrics, all 8 seeds:** 68 legs, 67 arrived, 1 timeout (seed 91, the known tower case). Median final 3.2 s. Street legs: 0 stalls. Marker off screen 1.5%.
  - One outlier: seed 7, first leg (rooftop, 22.9 m), final 17.1 s with 4 stalls. Two seed 7 reruns gave 2.9 s and 3.2 s. A one-off like the 15.5 s case round 7 saw once.
- **Flat-frame probe (acceptance-probe):** 992 frames, **0 flat**.
- **`npm run build` passes.** JS 702 KB, CSS 21 KB, HTML 7 KB.
- **Frame time (hand-fly, 80 s).** Desktop median 8.30 ms, p95 9.70 ms, max 10.4 ms. Mobile median 8.30 ms, p95 9.60 ms. 0 frames over 20 ms. An earlier run this round: p95 8.9 and 9.0 ms. Round 7: median 8.3 ms, p95 9.6 ms.
- No page errors.

- HUD states:
  - d-/m-slow-centre: 1 chevron, "Faster!". On mobile the first-run hint is on top, so the cue is hidden.
  - d-/m-fast-centre: 2 chevrons, "Closer to wall".
  - d-/m-fast-hug: 3 chevrons, "Wall hug!", chain x4 pop.

critic.md
# Drone Dash, round 7 critic report

**Verdict:** The round 6 gap is closed with room to spare, and the high line was not nerfed further. But the street reward now pays for time spent near walls, not for flying well. A slow, centred, no-boost pilot scores as much a minute as anyone. The "dash" in Drone Dash no longer pays.

## Round 6 gap (slipstream too small and too slow): closed

Scripts are copied to `critic-scripts/`. The output folder is relative (`../critic/`), so no edit was needed to write to `round-7/critic/`. One browser at a time for all real-time scripts. Note: the builder had already put screenshots in `round-7/critic/`. Files with the same name were overwritten by mine.

| Pilot (seeds 22, 58, 130, SIMT 150) | Time | Deliveries/min | Score/min | Crashes/min | Slip payouts/min | Slip share of score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Low, round 6 | 277 s | 1.52 | 1,278 | 0.0 | 3.25 | 27% |
| **Low, round 7** | 295 s | 1.42 | **2,756** | **0.0** | 13.8 | **68%** |
| High, round 6 | 373 s | 2.41 | 1,826 | 0.5 | 0.16 | |
| **High, round 7** | 420 s | **2.71** | 2,259 | 0.7 | 3.1 | 8% |

- Low score a minute / high = **1.22** (needed 0.9). Pass.
- High deliveries a minute = **2.71** (needed 2.3). Pass. Headwind is now 20% (was 30%), so the high line got a little faster.
- Low crashes = **0** a minute. Pass.
- Hand flight, desktop: first draft at 3.9 s, first payout at 6.0 s (**2.1 s** after). Chain x2 at 8.0 s, x5 at 20.8 s. Pass.
- Hand flight, mobile (iPhone 13 held sideways, touch): first draft 3.7 s, first payout 7.2 s (**3.5 s** after). x2 at 14.8 s, x5 at 23.3 s. Pass.

## Balance and skill gradient: the street now pays for presence, not skill

Two new probes. `balance-probe.mjs` is the low route bot with a lateral offset, a speed cap and an option to never boost. `hug-probe.mjs` is deterministic: it places the drone on a straight street at 7 m and flies 12 s.

Route play, seeds 22, 58, 130, SIMT 150:

| Pilot | Score/min | Deliveries/min | Crashes | Final score per run |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lazy: centred, 10 m/s, never boosts | **2,783** | 1.12 | 0 | 4,129 |
| Standard low bot: centred, 16 m/s, boosts | 2,756 | 1.42 | 0 | 4,517 |
| Wall offset 5.5 m, 16 m/s, boosts | 2,556 | 0.99 | 1 | 3,450 |
| High line, 40 m | 2,259 | 2.71 | 5 | 5,271 |

Straight street, 12 s, three roads on seed 22 (all three gave the same result):

| Line | Speed | Payouts | Slip points |
|---|---|---|---|
| Centre | 8.9 m/s | 5 | 500 |
| Centre | 16.3 m/s | 5 | 500 |
| 2.5 m from a facade | 8.9 m/s | 7 | 800 |
| 2.5 m from a facade | 16.3 m/s | 8 | 950 |

What this means:
- **Speed is worth nothing to the meter.** Full draft starts at 8 m/s. The meter fills by time, not distance. Going 16 m/s instead of 9 gives the same payouts.
- **Slow is not punished.** Drafting pauses the fast-drop par clock, and each payout adds 0.5 s. So a slow street crawl keeps the combo alive and refills the clock.
- **The street centre is already full quality** (mean quality 0.96 to 0.97). Facades are 9 m away and "full" is 9.5 m. No steering skill is needed.
- **The only skill lever is the wall hug.** It is worth up to 1.9x on a straight. In route play it did not convert: corners and kerbs cost more than it paid, and the offset bot crashed once.
- **The roof line is not pointless.** Per run, high still scores most (5,271), because more deliveries buy more clock. High runs last 120 to 150 s, low runs 72 to 112 s. But a player cannot see this trade. The HUD shows score a minute climbing faster on the street.
- **Deliveries are now the minor part of a street run.** 68 to 77% of low score is slipstream points. The game is called a delivery game.

So there is a gradient, but on the wrong axis. Lazy, centred, low flight earns as much as the standard bot and more than the wall-offset bot.

## Seed 91: bot fault, not game fault

Arrival-metrics on all 8 seeds: 67 legs, 66 arrived, 1 timeout (seed 91). I ran seed 91 alone five more times with a per-second trace (`seed91-watch.mjs`).
- Every run had exactly one timeout. In 4 of 5, the bot spent 31 to 36 s on the fifth leg (Florist, Juniper and 4th). It hovered at 40 to 62 m, 43 to 67 m from the target, and crashed 2 to 4 times into one tower. Screenshots `S91-leg5-plus14s.jpg` and `S91-leg5-plus22s.jpg` show a slab tower taller than the bot's 40 m cruise height, directly on the straight line to the pad. The bot steers straight at the target and never routes around. A player goes around.
- The run then ends with the clock at 0 during the next leg. The clock is 50 s plus delivery bonuses. With only 2 deliveries, a timeout around 70 s is the normal end of a run, not a fault.
- The one-off 15.5 s rooftop arrival did not come back. Longest final approach over all 8 seeds: 4.5 s. Five seed 91 runs: final approaches 2.9 to 4.0 s, 0 stalls in the final 30 m.

## Single biggest remaining gap: the score rewards time near walls, not fast or skilful flying

The game sells a dash: fast drops, combos, boost through streets. The scoring now says the opposite. The best score a minute comes from crawling down the middle of a street at 9 m/s without boosting. The meter fills by time, the street centre is already full strength, and drafting stops the par clock. Two thirds of a street run's score comes from this meter. The best arcade flyers make the risky, fast, tight line pay clearly more than the safe one. Speed and precision multiply the reward, and a lazy run looks lazy on the score screen. Here a skilled run and a lazy run score the same.

Fix direction (the builder's call). Fill the meter by distance flown in the draft, or scale it by speed. Narrow full strength so the street centre is not full. Make the hug the main way to reach high chains. Stop the par pause from rewarding slowness.

**Acceptance test** (dev server on 5188, from the game folder, one browser at a time):
1. `OFF=0 CRUISE=10 NOBOOST=1 LINE=low SEEDS=22,58,130 SIMT=150 node progress/round-7/critic-scripts/balance-probe.mjs` (lazy). Then `LINE=low SEEDS=22,58,130 SIMT=150 node progress/round-7/critic-scripts/route-play-rt-x.mjs` (standard). Pass: lazy score a minute is at most **0.8 times** standard. Now 1.01.
2. `node progress/round-7/critic-scripts/hug-probe.mjs`. Pass: on each road, centre at 16.3 m/s earns at least **1.3 times** the slip points of centre at 8.9 m/s (now 1.0). Hug at 2.5 m and 16.3 m/s earns at least **2 times** centre at 8.9 m/s (now 1.9).
3. The round 6 test still passes. Standard low score a minute is at least 0.9 times high. High deliveries are at least 2.3 a minute. Low crashes are at most 1.5 a minute. In hand-fly, the first payout comes within 10 s of the first draft, and x2 within 50 s, on desktop and mobile.
4. Slipstream points are at most **50%** of standard low score. Now 68%.

## Other gaps (ranked)

1. **No difficulty curve, and runs are short and flat.** Runs last 70 to 150 s. Nothing changes over a run except smaller time bonuses (down to 55%). No new hazards, no harder sites, no rush hour. The tenth delivery feels like the first.
2. **Game over screen does not explain the score.** It shows score, best, deliveries and top combo (`m-r7-gameover.jpg`). It does not split delivery, combo and slipstream points, or show the street versus roof trade. A player cannot learn why a run was good.
3. **Up high at crawl speed, the headwind chip still shows.** At 55 m and 4 m/s, it reads "High wind · slower up here" (`S91-leg5-plus14s.jpg`). Round 6 asked for it only at speed.
4. **Mobile bottom centre is crowded during a payout.** Four items stack below the drone: the pop, the hint line, the meter and the boost bar. They cover the street ahead (`m-h04-low-payout-pop.jpg`). Desktop is fixed: the pop now sits by the drone (`d-h05-low-payout-chain.jpg`).
5. **Tall towers on the straight line can trap a player.** On seed 91, the nav marker points through a tower taller than normal cruise height. It gives no hint to go around. A route-around hint, or a marker that rises above the blocker, can help.

## Regressions: none found

- **crash-classify, all 8 seeds:** 12 m: 23 deliveries, 45 charged (3.8/min), **0 hop-like**. 20 m: 31 deliveries, 28 charged (2.1/min), **0 hop-like**.
- **Near-target crashes** (verbose rerun, seeds 11, 22, 7, 44 at 12 m and 11, 22, 7, 130 at 20 m): all hit building faces with tops 10.6 to 58.6 m at 13.9 to 17.1 m/s. Pads are 0.4 m. **0 on a pad lip.**
- **arrival-metrics, all 8 seeds:** 66 of 67 legs arrived. Median final 3.2 s, longest 4.5 s, 0 stalls. Marker off screen 1.3%. Slow and high 0.5%. The one timeout is explained above.
- **Flat-frame probe:** 869 frames, **0 flat**.
- No page errors on desktop or mobile.

## Performance


- Desktop 1280x720, 80 s hand flight: 9,577 frames, **median 8.30 ms, p95 9.60 ms, max 10.4 ms, 0 over 20 ms**.
- Mobile (iPhone 13 held sideways, touch), 80 s: 9,579 frames, median 8.30 ms, p95 9.50 ms, max 10.4 ms, 0 over 20 ms.
- First load, production build: about **0.73 MB** (JS 701 KB, CSS 20 KB, HTML 7 KB). The lil-gui chunk (31 KB) loads only with `?debug`. Budget 15 MB: pass.

## Screenshots (progress/round-7/critic/)

- Hand flight, desktop: d-h01-title, d-h02-low-drafting, d-h03-low-meter-half, d-h04-low-payout-pop, d-h05-low-payout-chain, d-h06-high-wind, d-h07-high-boost, d-h08-end
- Hand flight, mobile: m-h01-title, m-h02-low-drafting, m-h03-low-meter-half, m-h04-low-payout-pop, m-h05-low-payout-chain, m-h06-high-wind, m-h07-high-boost, m-h08-end
- Game over: d-r7-gameover, m-r7-gameover
- Seed 91: S91-leg5-plus6s, S91-leg5-plus14s, S91-leg5-plus22s, S91-t41/t50/t58 (a run that took a different path), A-seed91-stall-final-approach
- Crash classify: K-alt12-*, K-alt20-*. Route pilots: Q-high-*. Balance probe: B-off5.5-seed130-crash1

builder.md
# Drone Dash, round 7 builder: slipstream as a skill reward

## Design

The problem: the slipstream paid too little, too late, and the chain broke on every block.

1. **The street centre counts.** Draft range is now 16 m, full strength at 9.5 m. A street centre is 9 m from each facade, so normal street flight at cruise drafts at full quality. Full draft speed is now 8 m/s (was 14). Touch players and corners at 7 m/s still draft. A facade whose roof is up to 1.5 m below the drone still counts.
2. **Wall hug is the skill.** Within 5 m of a facade the meter fills faster: up to 1.7x at 2.5 m or closer. The meter glows hotter while you hug.
3. **Faster meter, quick first payout.** 0.45 meter a second at full quality. The first meter of a chain is 0.65 in size. Each chain step adds 0.1, so x4 and up need 1.05. You get a quick first payout that teaches the rule. A long chain pays more but less often.
4. **The chain survives the grid.** The meter holds 3 s out of the draft, then drains slowly (0.05 a second). The chain resets only after 6 s out of the draft (was 3 s). A charged crash still empties the meter and the chain (`Slipstream.lose()`, unchanged).
5. **Payout size.** 50, 75, 100, 125 and 150 points for x1 to x5, plus 0.5 s and 30% boost. The delivery combo no longer multiplies these points. The chain is their multiplier. Without this cap, x5 times combo ran to 4,500 a minute.
6. **Feedback.**
   - The payout pop sits next to the drone on desktop and mobile (was bottom left on desktop). It shows "+N" with "Slipstream chain xN" under it. It grows and brightens at x3, x4 and x5.
   - The chime climbs a whole tone per chain step, plays one more arpeggio note per step and gets louder. The burst and shake grow with the chain, with a second white burst at x3 and up.
   - The fill glows only while it is filling and looks dim while it waits. The chain tag glows at x3 and up.
   - The first two runs on a device show a one-line hint above the meter for 6 s: "Stay low & fast beside walls". The hint uses localStorage inside try/catch.
   - The title tagline adds "Fly low along the streets to ride the slipstream."
7. **Headwind softened from 30% to 20%.** The low line now passes the test without help from the wind. So the high line gets back part of its round 6 loss. The wind chip now shows only above 7 m/s (critic gap 1: no chip at rooftop pads).

## Files changed
- `src/game/config.ts`: SLIPSTREAM values (reach, full, hug*, roofSlack, speeds, fill, drain, grace, chainReset, points, chainStep, firstMeter, meterPerChain, seconds). `headwindSlow` changed from 0.3 to 0.2.
- `src/systems/Slipstream.ts`: hug factor, roof slack, meter size by chain, `firstPayoutAt` debug field.
- `src/systems/DeliverySystem.ts`: `addBonus(points, seconds, useCombo = true)`.
- `src/game/Game.ts`: payout feedback scales with the chain. The flat points no longer take the combo. Wind chip needs speed above 7 m/s. Hint armed at run start. Diagnostics add `slipstream.hug` and `slipstream.firstPayoutAt`. All existing hooks are kept.
- `src/ui/Hud.ts`: `setSlip` adds hug, hint timer and chain data attribute. `armSlipHint()` is new. `slipPop(points, chain)` is new.
- `src/systems/AudioSystem.ts`: `slipPayout` scales with the chain.
- `index.html`, `src/styles.css`: payout pop moved to the HUD centre. Hint line, idle and hug fill states, chain styles, title line.
- `src/vite-env.d.ts`: diagnostics type.
- Not touched: ObjectiveMarker bloom clamps, crash rules, arrival help, street-distance par.

## Numbers (dev server 5188, one browser at a time)

route-play-rt-x.mjs, seeds 22, 58 and 130, SIMT 150. These are the final runs (`rp-low-4.log`, `rp-high-4.log`):

| Line | Sim | Deliveries/min | Score/min | Crashes/min | Slip payouts/min |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Low | 295 s | 1.42 | **2,644** | **0.0** | 13.4 |
| High | 420 s | **2.71** | **2,339** | 0.6 | 2.7 |

- Low/high score = **1.13** (needed 0.9). High deliveries = **2.71/min** (needed 2.3, round 6 was 2.41). Low crashes = 0.
- Tuning path, for the record:
  - First pass with points times combo: low 4,537/min (ratio 2.3, far too rich).
  - Flat points: low 2,401/min.
  - Headwind 0.2: high 2,077/min, ratio 1.12.
  - Meter size by chain and 8 m/s full speed: the final row above.

hand-fly.mjs (50 s low, then 30 s high):

| | First draft | First payout | Gap | First x2 | Max chain |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop | 3.8 s | 6.0 s | **2.2 s** | **8.0 s** | x5 by about 21 s |
| Mobile (touch) | 4.1 s | 7.9 s | **3.8 s** | **15.6 s** | x5 at 23.8 s |

- Before the meter-size change, mobile was 11.5 s and failed. The mobile pilot drafts at 5 to 8 m/s. At that speed the old speed factor cut quality in half.

Regressions:
- **crash-classify, 8 seeds.** 12 m: 37 charged (3.3/min), **0 hop-like**, 5 near target. 20 m: 28 charged (2.3/min), **0 hop-like**, 3 near target.
- **Verbose rerun at 12 m, 8 seeds.** All 5 near-target hits are on building faces. Their tops are 10.6 to 20.2 m. Speed 0.3 s before was 15.8 to 16.9 m/s. **0 on a pad lip.** This is the same bot overshoot as rounds 5 and 6.
- **arrival-metrics, 8 seeds.** 67 legs, 66 arrived. Median final 3.2 s. Marker off screen 1.3% and 2.0%. Slow and high 1.1% and 3.3%.
  - The 1 "timeout" is seed 91: a cruise leg cut off by the run clock. It never came within 30 m, as in round 6 builder. The rerun of seed 91 shows the same.
  - One seed 91 first leg (Fountain Park) took 15.5 s in the final, with 4 stalls on a rooftop. It did not repeat on the rerun (3.5 s median). I log it as bot variance but have not proven that.
  - "Slow and high" rose from 0.4% to 3.3% on the second seed group. That is still small, but it is up.
- **Flat-frame probe:** 1,017 frames, **0 flat**.
- **Frame time (hand-fly, 80 s).** Desktop median 8.30 ms, p95 9.10 ms, max 9.5 ms. Mobile median 8.30 ms, p95 9.20 ms. 0 frames over 20 ms. Round 6 was 8.3 ms and 9.8 ms.
- **`npm run build` passes.** JS 701 KB (was 699 KB). 0 page errors.

## Known limits
- Street flight now pays 13 payouts a minute for the bot. It is a steady drip, not a rare event. The pop size and the chime pitch carry the chain, but some players can find the pop too frequent.
- The high line also gets more payouts on descents (2.7/min), worth about 170 points a minute.
- The hint is stored per device. A cleared localStorage shows it again.

## Files in this folder

- New: `hand-fly-trace.mjs` (hand-fly plus TRACE=1 half-second meter log).
- Logs: `rp-*.log`, `hf-*.log`, `cc*.log`, `am*.log`, `ap.log`.
- Screenshots: `critic/` (d-h02 to d-h05 and m-h02 to m-h05 show the hint, meter, pop and chain).

critic.md
# Drone Dash, round 6 critic report

**Verdict:** The street line now pays, and the round 5 test passes on deliveries. But half of the change came from slowing the roof line down, and the street line still earns 30% less score a minute. It is now a fair second choice, not the stylish best line.

## Round 5 gap (low line safe but paid nothing): closed, narrowly

Scripts are copied to `critic-scripts/`. Only the output folder changed (it is relative, so it now writes to `round-6/critic/`). I ran `route-play-rt-x.mjs`. It is `route-play-rt.mjs` plus log-only fields (slipstream payouts, payout times, mean headwind). The control logic is the same. One browser at a time.

| Pilot (seeds 22, 58, 130, SIMT 150) | Time | Deliveries/min | Score/min | Crashes/min | Slipstream payouts/min |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Low, round 5 | 215 s | 1.12 | 348 | 0.0 | none existed |
| Low, round 6 | 277 s | **1.52** | **1,278** | **0.0** | **3.25** |
| Low, round 6 repeat | 278 s | 1.51 | 1,281 | 0.0 | 3.45 |
| High, round 5 | 450 s | 3.33 | 2,439 | 1.3 | |
| High, round 6 | 373 s | **2.41** | **1,826** | 0.5 | 0.16 |

- Deliveries: low/high = **0.63** (needed 0.6). Pass, by a margin of under one delivery in this sample.
- Score: low/high = **0.70** (needed 0.75). Fail on its own. The test needs only one of the two.
- Visible low-line reward: 3.25 to 3.45 payouts a minute, each with a "+N slipstream" pop, "+1s" at the timer, a burst and a sound. Pass.
- Low crashes: 0 per minute in 555 s. Pass.
- High-line deliveries a minute dropped **28%** (3.33 to 2.41). High runs now end at 120 to 129 s. In round 5 they all ran to the 150 s cap.

## How the pass was achieved

Three changes:
1. **Headwind above 20 m** (full from 28 m) takes 30% off top speed. Measured: cruise 16.3 m/s at 10 m, 11.8 m/s at 40 m. Boost 29.4 m/s at 10 m, 21.4 m/s at 40 m.
2. **Slipstream meter** below 18 m beside facades. Each full meter pays 40 points (plus 15 per chain step) times combo, plus 1 s, plus 30% boost. It made up 27% of low score (1,622 of 5,899).
3. **Leg par uses grid distance**, and drafting pauses the par clock. So street routes can now earn fast-drop bonuses. Low score without slipstream points rose from 348 to 926 a minute, so this quiet change did more for low score than the meter did.

Split: the gap went from 0.34 to 0.63. In log terms, almost exactly half came from the low line getting better (+36%) and half from the high line getting worse (-28%). With the round 5 high rate, low/high is 1.52/3.33 = 0.46, a fail. So the pass depends on the nerf. That is the weaker way, as the brief warned. The headwind is at least honest. It has a chip ("High wind · slower up here"), pale streaks and an audio change.

**Mid-line check (exploit test).** Same high bot at 19 m, just under the wind: 2.50 deliveries/min, but 3.1 crashes/min and 0 payouts. No dominant mid line. Good.

## Single biggest remaining gap: the slipstream reward is too thin to make the street the line you want

The street line is now safe and paid, but a player still scores more by going over the roofs (1,826 against 1,278 a minute). The reward that must flip that is small and slow:
- One payout is 40 points before combo. One delivery is about 400 to 800. Three payouts a minute is worth less than one delivery.
- In hand flights, the first payout came **16.5 s** (desktop) and **26 s** (mobile) after the first draft. The meter fills in 2 s only at full quality, which needs a facade within 4 m at 14 m/s. Flying the middle of a street gives low quality.
- The chain never went above x1 in 5 hand payouts. Crossing an intersection breaks the draft, and 3 s out resets the chain. On this 44 m grid, that happens on every block. So the x2 to x5 chain, the skill ceiling, is rarely reached.
- The title screen does not mention it. You learn it by seeing a meter appear.

The best arcade city flyers make the risky low line the fastest and richest line. You hear the wind, the bonus counter runs up as you hug the wall, and a good run feels obviously better than a safe one. Here the low line is "less bad".

**Acceptance test** (dev server on 5188, from the game folder):
1. `LINE=low SEEDS=22,58,130 SIMT=150 node progress/round-6/critic-scripts/route-play-rt-x.mjs`, and the same with `LINE=high`. Unchanged bots.
2. Pass: low score a minute is at least **0.9 times** high. Now 0.70.
3. Pass: high deliveries a minute stay at **2.3 or more**. Now 2.41. No further high nerf.
4. Pass: run `hand-fly.mjs` on desktop and with `MOBILE=1`. The first payout comes within **10 s** of the first draft. A chain of **x2 or more** happens at least once in 50 s of low flight. Now 16.5 s and 26 s, and x1.
5. Low crashes stay at 1.5 per minute or less.

## Other gaps (ranked)

1. **The headwind chip shows at rooftop pads.** At a 29 m rooftop pad at 2 m/s, it shows "High wind · slower up here" (`d08-stuck-near-drop.jpg`). It is noise there and makes rooftop jobs feel penalized. When the drone moves fast up high, show it. Otherwise, hide it.
2. **Desktop payout pop sits in the bottom-left corner,** far from the drone (`d-h04-low-payout-pop.jpg`). On mobile it is centred near the drone and reads much better (`m-h04-low-payout-pop.jpg`). Desktop players watch the drone.
3. **The slipstream label is ghosted until drafting starts** (`d-h02-low-drafting.jpg`). A new player sees a faint word with no explanation.
4. **High flight is slower in towers' own band.** At 26 m beside a 50 m tower there is wind but no draft (`d-h06-high-wind.jpg`). Drafting is capped at 18 m, so a tower canyon at 25 m feels punished twice. Minor, but players will notice.
5. **crash-stakes finds no boost crash on seeds 22 and 58 now.** The slower high bot ends its second delivery in a different place. The straight boost then finds open street. The bot path causes this, not the game. A retry variant (`crash-stakes-x.mjs`) and `boost-probe.mjs` show hits still charge. Seed 130: 17.3 m/s, -4 s, combo x2 lost. Seed 58: 15.8 m/s, -4 s. Seed 22: a 29.4 m/s boost into a wall was charged.

## Regressions: none found

- **crash-classify, all 8 seeds:** 12 m: 16 deliveries, 30 charged (3.1/min), **0 hop-like**. 20 m: 31 deliveries, 31 charged (2.3/min), **0 hop-like**. 40 m reference: 35 deliveries, 5 charged (0.3/min).
- **Near-target crashes** (verbose rerun, seeds 22, 58, 91 at 12 m and 11, 22, 33 at 20 m): all hit building faces with tops 10.6 to 20.2 m. Pads are 0.4 m. Speed 0.3 s before was 16 to 17 m/s. **0 on a pad lip.** Same bot overshoot as round 5.
- **arrival-metrics, all 8 seeds:** 67 legs, against 82 in round 5, because cruise is slower. **0 timeouts.** Longest final 4.5 s, median final 3.4 s. Marker off screen 1.3% and 2.5%. Slow and high 0.0% and 0.4%. Pass.
- **Flat-frame probe:** 148 sampled frames, **0 flat**.
- No page errors on desktop or mobile.

## How it plays

- **Street flight is pleasant and now has a pulse.** The meter fills, ticks, and pays with a pop, a burst and a sound. Wind streaks peel off the drone while drafting. The mobile layout puts the meter just above boost, centred, and it reads well (`m-h03-low-meter-half.jpg`).
- **High flight is slower but not hateful.** The wind is explained right away, and boost still gets you to 21 m/s. Some players will resent a speed cap they cannot see in the world. The chip helps.
- **HUD is busy but not crowded.** On mobile the wind chip and slipstream meter share one slot and never show together. No overlap with the stick, boost or climb buttons. On desktop, bottom-left now stacks pop, slipstream, wind, boost and telemetry, which is the busiest corner.

## Performance

- Desktop 1280x720, 80 s of flight (both lines): 9,578 frames, **median 8.30 ms, p95 9.80 ms, max 10.4 ms, 0 over 20 ms**. Same as round 5.
- Mobile emulation (iPhone 13 held sideways, touch), 80 s: 9,578 frames, median 8.30 ms, p95 9.60 ms, max 10.4 ms, 0 over 20 ms.
- First load, production build: **0.73 MB** (JS 699 KB, CSS 19 KB, HTML 7 KB, lil-gui chunk 31 KB). Budget 15 MB: pass.

## Screenshots (progress/round-6/critic/)

- Hand flights, desktop: d-h01-title, d-h02-low-drafting, d-h03-low-meter-half, d-h04-low-payout-pop, d-h06-high-wind, d-h08-end
- Hand flights, mobile: m-h01-title, m-h02-low-drafting, m-h03-low-meter-half, m-h04-low-payout-pop, m-h06-high-wind, m-h08-end
- Crash classify: K-alt12-*, K-alt20-*, K-alt40-*. Near target: N-alt12-seed22-t34.8/t65.3, N-alt12-seed91-t34.9, N-alt20-seed22-t32.3
- Crash stakes: X-seed130-crash, X-seed58-crash-x, X-seed130-crash-x
- Route pilots: Q-high-* (seed 58 from the 40 m run. Seeds 22 and 130 overwritten by the 19 m mid-line run)
- Flow probe: d01-title, d02-takeoff, d03-flying, d04-near-pickup, d08-stuck-near-drop (old bot without back-off, stuck by a rooftop structure. bot cause), d08b-after-bump, d09-game-over

New scripts (progress/round-6/critic-scripts/): route-play-rt-x.mjs (log-only fields, optional HIGHY), crash-stakes-x.mjs (retries other headings), boost-probe.mjs (top speeds by altitude), hand-fly.mjs (both lines, desktop or MOBILE=1, frame times, HUD rects).
builder.md
# Drone Dash, round 6 builder: a reward for the low street line

## Design

**Slipstream (low line reward).** Fly below 18 m, faster than 4 m/s, beside a building face taller than the drone (within 12 m; full strength at 4 m or closer; a second face across the street adds a canyon bonus). A meter fills while you draft (about 2 s at full quality, 5 to 10 s at street centre and cruise speed). It holds 1.2 s after you leave the draft, then drains slowly. Each full meter pays out:
- points: 40, then +15 for each chained payout (up to x5), times the combo multiplier,
- +30% boost tank,
- +1 s on the clock.

While you draft, the fast-drop clock (leg par) does not run. A charged crash empties the meter and the chain.

Feedback: an amber "Slipstream" meter above the boost bar, shown only while it matters. It shows "x2" and up for a chain. A "+40 slipstream" pop rises from the meter, and the timer shows "+1s". Faint speed lines and warm wind streaks peel off the drone. A whistling air band rises in pitch as the meter fills. There is a blip at each quarter, and a whoosh and chime on payout that climbs with the chain.

**Par uses the street route.** The fast-drop par now uses grid distance (|dx| + |dz| + |dy|) instead of the straight line. Following the streets is no longer a slow drop by definition. The time bonus is unchanged.

**High wind above the roofline.** From 20 m up (full at 28 m), top cruise and boost speed drop by up to 30%. Speed carried in from below bleeds at the normal rate instead of gently. Feedback: a "High wind · slower up here" chip in the same slot as the slipstream meter, pale wind streaks blowing past from ahead, and a louder, lower, gusting wind layer. High cruise still works (it delivers about 1.6 times as fast as the street bot). Skimming the low roofs under 20 m is now a middle line.

**Crash severity no longer depends on input (critic gap 1).** The forward thrust added in a contact frame is subtracted from the wall loss. Holding forward into a wall no longer adds to the measured hit. Wall-speed-sweep (critic's 2 m gap) after the fix: held 10 m/s charges 18/18 because the drone really hits at about 11 m/s. Released 12 m/s hits at about 9.5 m/s and is free. By real impact speed, the result no longer depends on the key: `wall-impact-consistency.mjs` gives free at 10 m/s or below and charged at 11 to 12 m/s and up, with or without W. Loss/impact ratio: 0.62 held, 0.65 released. The rest of the old held/released difference was real approach speed: drag slows a released drone over the last 2 m.

## Files changed
- `src/systems/Slipstream.ts` (new): draft quality, meter, chain, payouts.
- `src/game/config.ts`: `SLIPSTREAM` block; `FLIGHT.headwindStart/Full/Slow`.
- `src/game/Game.ts`: slipstream update and payout, wind streaks, HUD and audio wiring, par hold, diagnostics (`slipstream`, `leg`, `player.headwind`).
- `src/entities/Drone.ts`: headwind top speed and bleed; thrust taken out of `wallLoss`.
- `src/systems/DeliverySystem.ts`: `addBonus`; par on grid route; par hold while drafting.
- `src/systems/AudioSystem.ts`: draft whistle layer, `slipTick`, `slipPayout`, gusts in `updateRotor`.
- `src/ui/Hud.ts`, `index.html`, `src/styles.css`: slipstream meter, slip pop, high-wind chip.
- `src/vite-env.d.ts`: diagnostics types.
- Not touched: `ObjectiveMarker.ts` (bloom clamps), `__GAME__` and test hooks.

## Numbers (dev server 5188, one browser at a time for timing-sensitive runs)

Acceptance, `route-play-rt` (real time; I ran `route-play-rt-slip.mjs`, the same bot with extra result fields), seeds 22, 58, 130, SIMT 150:

| Line | Sim | Deliveries/min | Score/min | Crashes/min | Slipstream payouts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Low (7 m streets) | 277 s | **1.52** | 1,255 | **0.0** | 15 (3.2/min; 5, 3, 7 per run) |
| High (40 m straight) | 373 s | **2.41** | 1,761 | 0.5 | 0 |
| Round 5 low / high | | 1.12 / 3.33 | | 0.0 / 1.3 | |

- Deliveries ratio **0.63** (pass, needs 0.6). Score ratio 0.71 (under 0.75, but the test passes on either one).
- Low: visible reward 3.2 times a minute, crashes 0/min. Pass.
- Deterministic `route-play-slip.mjs` agrees: low 1.54/min and 1,345/min; high 2.44/min and 1,845/min.
- The low bot's own pace limits it. Even with unlimited boost it only reaches 1.58/min, because it caps itself at 16 m/s and 7 m/s corners. So most of the ratio change comes from the high-wind nerf: high went from 3.6 to 2.4 deliveries a minute. The par change and slipstream mostly raise low score (590 to 1,255 a minute) through payouts and combos.

Regressions:
- crash-classify 12 m (8 seeds): 37 charged, 1 flagged "hop-like" (seed 33, rise 0.81 m, Space not held at the hit). It is not a game hop: the game's hop did not fire, or the hit would have been free. Its rise is on the 0.8 m threshold, and the bot holds altitude at 12 m ± 1.2. The verbose rerun (`crash-classify-v`) flags 1 too: seed 130, wall top 20.2 m with the drone at 15.8 m. That is a real wall 4.4 m above the drone. Near target: 5, all hits on facades (no pad lip).
- crash-classify 20 m: 32 charged, **0 hop-like**, 2 near target.
- crash-stakes 22, 58, 130: every hit charged (29.3, 28.2, 16.9 m/s): clock down 4 to 5 s within 1 s, combo x2 lost.
- arrival-metrics, all 8 seeds: 33 + 32 legs, longest final 4.3 / 4.6 s, 0 finals over 10 s, marker off screen 1.5% / 2.6%, slow and high 0.0% / 0.4%. There was 1 timeout, on seed 91. It started at t = 60 s and never came within 30 m: an end-of-clock cruise leg, as in round 5. There are fewer legs than in round 5 (43 and 39) because the arrival bot cruises at 40 m, which is now in the high wind.
- Flat-frame probe: 1,044 frames, **0 flat**.
- Frame time (long-run, seed 22, 60 s, bloom on): 7,173 frames, **median 8.30 ms, p95 9.70 ms**, max 10.4 ms, 0 over 20 ms. Same as round 5.
- `npm run build` passes. JS 699 KB (was 693 KB).

## Scripts and shots (progress/round-6/)
- `scripts/`: copies of the round 5 critic scripts. Only the output folder changed (`../shots/`). New: `route-play-rt-slip.mjs`, `route-play-slip.mjs`, `wall-speed-sweep-gap.mjs`, `wall-impact-consistency.mjs`, `wall-trace.mjs`, `headwind-check.mjs`, `slip-shots.mjs`, `long-run-perf.mjs` (round 5 builder copy).
- `shots/`: `s1-street-drafting.jpg`, `s2-street-payout.jpg`, `s3-high-wind.jpg`; raw outputs `rt-low.txt`, `rt-high.txt`, `classify-12.txt`, `classify-12-v.txt`, `classify-20.txt`, `crash-stakes.txt`, `arrival-A.txt`, `arrival-B.txt`.

## Open
- The high-wind nerf is bigger than "a little": high deliveries fell 28%. With an unchanged bot, no low-only reward could reach 0.6, because the bot sets its own speed. To soften it, lower `FLIGHT.headwindSlow` (0.25 gave a ratio of 0.59).
- The slipstream's speed and boost rewards matter more to a human than to the bot, which brakes above 19 m/s.
