critic.md
# Drone Dash, round 5 critic report

**Verdict:** The crash cost is now fair. Low street flight no longer gets charged for skims or pad edges. But the low line still pays nothing. A street route delivers about a third as fast as cruising over the roofs, so the best plan is still to fly over the city.

## Round 4 gap (crash cost fired on hops and pad edges): closed

Scripts are copied to `critic-scripts/`. Only the output folders changed. New scripts have their own names.

**crash-classify.mjs, all 8 seeds**

| Cruise | Sim time | Deliveries | Charged crashes | Hop-like | Within 30 m of target |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12 m | 606 s | 19 | 28 (2.8/min) | **0** | 5 |
| 20 m | 703 s | 26 | 36 (3.1/min) | **0** | 2 |
| 40 m (reference) | 876 s | 39 | 18 (1.2/min) | 0 | 1 |

Round 4 at 12 m: 40% of charged crashes were hop-like. Now 0 at both heights.

**Near-target crashes.** I reran seeds 22, 44, 91 and 130 with a logging variant (`crash-classify-v.mjs`). It records the game's own crash record and the speed 0.3 s before the hit. All 5 near-target crashes hit a real building face: wall tops 10.6 to 55 m, far above the pad (0.4 m). The drone was moving at 14 to 17 m/s just before. 0 were on the pad's own lip, kerb or edge. In one screenshot the bot overshoots a street pad into the shop front behind it (`N-alt12-seed44-t54.1-near.jpg`). In another it drops fast beside a facade (`N-alt20-seed22-t32.9-near.jpg`). This is the bot's own action after a real wall hit, not a game fault.

The bot's "from" speed is low (2 to 6 m/s) because the game decides 0.2 s after first contact. By then the drone has already stopped. Speed 0.3 s earlier was 13 to 17 m/s in every logged case.

**crash-stakes.mjs (seeds 22, 58, 130, plus repeats with crash counter)**
- Seed 22: 29.0 to 10.1 m/s. Within 1 s: clock down 4 s on top of normal ticking, combo x2 lost.
- Seed 58: 28.9 to 10.5 m/s, 4 s and combo lost. Repeat run: same result.
- Seed 130: 18.5 to 10.0 m/s, 3 s and combo lost. In the first run the bot measured a follow-up scrape after the real crash. The screenshot shows "-3 SEC · X2.0 COMBO LOST" was already applied (`X-seed130-crash.jpg`).
- Seed 58, first run: no hit over 8 m/s within 8 s of boosting at 10 m. The street ahead was clear, or the drone brushed through trees and lamp posts, which are now free. Free thin props are fair. They look soft, and a player expects to glance off a tree.

**Scrapes are free (new controlled sweep, `wall-speed-sweep.mjs`).** 18 real block faces on seed 22, head-on at 10 m. With forward held: 0 of 126 charged at 3 to 7 m/s, 2 of 18 at 8 m/s, 18 of 18 at 10 m/s and above. With forward released: 0 charged up to 12 m/s, 18 of 18 at 16 m/s.

**arrival-metrics.mjs, all 8 seeds twice**
- Run B (clean, one browser at a time): seeds 11, 22, 33, 44: 43 legs, 0 timeouts, longest final 4.9 s, marker off screen 1.2%, slow and high 0.6%. Seeds 7, 58, 91, 130: 39 legs, 1 end-of-clock cruise leg, longest final 4.5 s, 1.2% off screen, 0.0% slow and high. Pass.
- Run A was run in parallel with other browsers (CPU contention). It showed 4 finals over 10 s (18 to 33 s) and far fewer legs (29 and 25). The clean rerun did not repeat any of them. Treat run A as invalid.

**Flat-frame probe:** 905 frames, **0 flat**. Mobile run: 15,164 frames, 0 flat.

## Seed 11: not a game fault

- Clean, alone, 5 runs in a row: 52 legs, **0 finals over 10 s**, longest 6.1 s (Tailor, Juniper & 6th, the same rooftop canyon leg as round 4), median 3.2 s.
- Under CPU contention (5 runs plus run A): 3 finals over 10 s (18.4, 20.3, 25.4 s), all with bot stall and back-off cycles.
- So the long seed 11 finals follow host load, not the seed. When the bot polls more slowly, it misses the pad and loops. The game's arrival is fine.

## Low street line against high cruise

New routed pilots (`route-play.mjs` deterministic, `route-play-rt.mjs` real keyboard). The low pilot follows the street grid at 7 m. It goes corner to corner and brakes into turns. It boosts only on long straights, and it rises up the facade for rooftop pads. The high pilot flies straight at 40 m and boosts.

| Pilot | Seeds | Time | Deliveries/min | Crashes/min | Mean speed | Run length |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Low, real time | 22, 58, 130 | 215 s | **1.12** | **0.0** | 8 to 9 m/s | 64 to 81 s |
| High, real time | 22, 58, 130 | 450 s (150 s cap) | **3.33** | 1.3 | 14 to 16 m/s | all hit the cap |
| Low, deterministic | 11, 22, 58, 130 | 303 s | 1.39 | 0.0 | | 62 to 85 s |
| High, deterministic | 11, 22, 58, 130 | 666 s | 3.24 | 1.6 | | 124 to 217 s |
| Low, aggressive (corners 11 m/s) | 11, 22, 58, 130 | 124 s | 0.97 | 2.4 | | 24 to 38 s |

- **Fair now.** 518 s of careful street flight gave 0 crashes. Corner-cutting at 11 m/s gives crashes into real corners, which is fair.
- **Not rewarding.** The street line delivers at a third of the high rate, and runs end in about half the time. My pilot is slower than a good player. But even at 15 m/s average, a street route is about 1.3 times longer than the straight line and can rarely boost. My estimate for that player is still only about 55% of the high rate.
- High cruise is also where the hard crashes happen (boosting into towers at 30 to 45 m/s, 4 to 5 s each). It still wins by a wide margin.

## Single biggest remaining gap: the street line is safe but pays nothing, so the high line wins by 3 to 1

Evidence: see the table above. The game has no near-miss, low-flight or street bonus. The time bonus uses the straight-line leg distance, so a street route earns nothing extra for the longer path. Leaving the street costs nothing either. In the best arcade city flyers, the street line is the stylish, risky line. It pays back in score, time or speed. Here it is just slower. The crash rework removed the punishment, but nothing gives the player a reason to go down there.

**Acceptance test** (dev server on 5188, run from the game folder):
1. `LINE=low SEEDS=22,58,130 SIMT=150 node progress/round-5/critic-scripts/route-play-rt.mjs` and the same with `LINE=high`, both unchanged bots.
2. Pass: low deliveries per minute are at least **0.6 times** high. Now: 1.12 against 3.33 (0.34 times). Or: low score per minute is at least **0.75 times** high. Now: 348 against 2,439.
3. Pass: the low run shows a visible low-line reward at least once a minute, for example a HUD pop or a meter. Low crashes stay at or under 1.5 per minute.
4. No regression: crash-classify at 12 m and 20 m still has 0 hop-like and 0 pad-edge charges. crash-stakes still charges every hit over 8 m/s.

## Other gaps (ranked)

1. **Holding forward changes what counts as a crash.** Head-on at 10 m/s with forward held: 18 of 18 charged. Head-on at 12 m/s with forward released: 0 of 18 charged. Thrust during the 0.2 s window adds about 2 to 4 m/s to the measured loss. Players almost always hold forward. So the real threshold is about 9 m/s. Letting go of the key before a hit is an odd way to dodge a penalty.
2. **Pitched roofs are still walls.** The drone met a gable slope at 13.7 m/s. The ridge was 0.6 m above the drone's middle. The game charged -3 s (`P-low-seed22-crash1.jpg`). A player expects to ride up a slope that low.
3. **Crash feedback lands 0.2 s after impact.** At the moment of impact there is no cue yet (`X-seed22-crash.jpg`). When the window closes, the "Crash!" text, shake and sound follow. It reads fine. A short cue on first contact (spark or thud) can tie the cost to the hit more tightly.
4. **Rooftop canyon beside street pads (seed 11 Tailor).** Still the slowest leg, at 4.5 to 6.1 s. It is fair, and it is no longer an outlier.

## How it plays

- **Crash feel is good.** You get a big coral "Crash!" and a chip with seconds and combo lost. The combo badge is struck through. A red vignette, shake and sound follow. Three tiers (3, 4, 5 s) feel proportionate. Tree and lamp brushes are free and look free.
- **Street flying feels safe but slow.** Corners at 7 m/s are clean. Long avenues are pleasant to fly. But each leg starts on a rooftop pad, so you climb out, drop into the street, and fly a longer path for the same reward.
- **Full loop works** on desktop and on iPhone 13 held sideways (touch): title, pickup, delivery, combo, crashes, game over, Fly Again (clock 50.9 s after the mobile restart). Mobile touch controls stay clear of the HUD (`m07-bump.jpg`). The mobile run made 3 deliveries in the first 41 s.

## Performance

- Desktop 1280x720, bloom on, 40 s of flight: 4,854 frames, **median 8.30 ms, p95 9.80 ms, 0 frames over 20 ms**. Same as round 4.
- Mobile emulation (iPhone 13 held sideways, touch, DPR 2), 60 s: 7,161 frames, median 8.30 ms, p95 9.60 ms, max 18.6 ms, 0 over 20 ms.
- First load, production build: **0.72 MB** (JS 693 KB, CSS 17 KB, HTML 6 KB, plus a 31 KB lil-gui chunk). Budget 15 MB: pass.

## Screenshots (progress/round-5/critic/)

- Crash stakes: X-seed22-crash, X-seed130-crash, X2-seed58-crash-421/746, X2-seed130-crash-89
- Crash classify: K-alt12-*, K-alt20-*, K-alt40-* (first 8 crashes each); near-target checks N-alt12-seed44-t54.1-near, N-alt12-seed91-t34.3-near, N-alt20-seed22-t32.9-near, N-alt20-seed130-t54.7/t98.0-near
- Routed pilots: P-low-* (aggressive low run, incl. pitched roof P-low-seed22-crash1), P-high-*, Q-high-* (real-time high run; the real-time low run had no crashes, so no shots)
- Arrival stalls from the contended run A (invalid run): A-seed7/11/22/58-stall-final-approach
- Desktop flow: d01-title to d09-game-over
- Mobile (iPhone 13 held sideways, touch): m01-title to m09-restart

New scripts (progress/round-5/critic-scripts/): wall-speed-sweep.mjs, crash-classify-v.mjs, route-play.mjs, route-play-rt.mjs, route-play-debug.mjs.
builder.md
# Drone Dash, round 5 builder report: fair crash classification

## Cause

The round 4 crash check fired on the game's own skim helpers. Four separate faults caused this:

1. **The ledge hop counted as a crash.** A hop cancels the drone's speed into the ledge. The crash check then counted that speed as "lost".
2. **The speed loss was a raw before/after delta.** It included drag, the S brake and the drop guide's pull near pads. So near a pad, a light touch plus braking was enough to pass 7 m/s.
3. **Edge clips counted as wall hits.** Sometimes the drone's underside clipped a roof edge or the rim of a box (contact normal 20 to 45 degrees up). The bounce then took off horizontal speed, and the game charged it.
4. **Lamp posts and trees counted as walls.** These are "soft" props. Near the camera, the game hides them. One head-on post hit stopped the drone dead (the critic's "nothing in view looks like an obstacle", grass, 10 m from a park pad). In a probe I placed the drone in front of a park lamp post: it stopped at 0 m/s and stayed pinned.

## Design

- **Only real walls can cost you.** Only a wall contact counts toward a crash. These contacts are never counted:
  - a low lip the drone can skim (the same test the game uses for its hop)
  - an underside clip on an edge (normal y 0.35 to 0.7)
  - a lamp post or tree
- **Severity is the speed the collision itself takes off.** It is the horizontal speed before the sub-stepped collision loop minus the speed after it. Thrust, drag, braking and the guide all run before the loop, so none of them count. The 3, 4 and 5 s tiers and the 7 m/s threshold are unchanged.
- **A hop always wins.** The crash is judged 0.2 s after first contact (the same span the loss was already summed over). If the game's own ledge hop fires inside that span, the collision is a skim and costs nothing.
- **The pad's own edge is free.** The rule applies within 30 m of the current pad. A wall there is free if its top is within 1.5 m of the pad height and the skids are less than 4 m below that top. This covers a roof lip, a kerb or a lawn edge you clip as you drop in.
- **Low lines keep their speed.** This is the low-flying reward. I kept it inside the physics and added no new scoring rule.
  - Lips up to 0.9 m above the skids are stepped over at full speed. This covers parapets (0.7 m), kerbs and fountain rims. The body eases up visually.
  - Taller ledges up to 2.2 m still hop. The pop is faster the harder you meet the ledge. Once you clear the top, the hop gives back 85% of the forward speed it absorbed.
  - Posts and trees brush you aside with 80% of your speed. There is one glance per brush, so you slide off instead of sticking.
- **Round 4 feedback is unchanged for real crashes:** HUD pop, -Ns chip, vignette, sparks, shake, tumble and sound. Brushes and skims keep the light scrape feedback.

I did not add a slipstream or combo bonus. Fair skims plus speed carry already make the low line pay. A scoring rule needs its own balancing round.

## Files changed

- `src/entities/Drone.ts`:
  - `FlightEvents` gains `wallLoss`, `wallTop` and `wallNormalY`.
  - Collision loop: soft-prop glance, edge-clip class, step-up, hop speed carry and impact-scaled hop lift.
  - New `columnTop()` helper.
  - New `place()` debug method.
- `src/game/Game.ts`:
  - `checkCrash` rewritten: wall-only loss, 0.2 s judge, hop skim and pad edge rule.
  - New `isTargetEdge`.
  - Diagnostics gain `lastCrash` and `contact`.
  - Hooks gain `__GAME__.place()` and `__GAME__.sites()`. All existing hooks are unchanged.
- `src/systems/CollisionWorld.ts`: `deepestSoft` flag.
- `src/game/config.ts`:
  - `FLIGHT.stepUp`
  - `CRASH.padEdgeRange` and `CRASH.padEdgeDepth`
  - comments on `chainGap` and `hitSpan`
- `src/vite-env.d.ts`: types for the new diagnostics and hooks.
- `src/entities/ObjectiveMarker.ts`: not touched. The bloom clamps are intact.

## Scripts

The critic scripts are copied to `progress/round-5/scripts/`. Only the output folder changed (now `../shots/`). The logic is unchanged.

I added three extra scripts of my own:
- `crash-classify-diag.mjs`: adds target y, the game's `lastCrash`, and a trace of climb input after each crash.
- `crash-stakes-trace.mjs`: logs contacts after the hit.
- `obstacle-probe.mjs`: places the drone in front of a fountain or post.

## Numbers

**crash-classify.mjs (official copy, deterministic, 8 seeds):**

| Cruise | Sim time | Deliveries | Charged crashes | Per minute | Hop-like | Near pad, on its surface |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12 m | 526 s | 14 | 29 | 3.3 | **1** | **1** (seed 22, see below) |
| 20 m | 744 s | 29 | 35 | 2.8 | **0** | 0 |
| 40 m (diag copy) | 905 s | 43 | 17 | 1.1 | 0 | 0 |

The round 4 critic measured 12 m at 45 crashes, 18 of them hop-like.

Over 6 more diagnostic runs at 12 m and 20 m:
- 0 to 1 hop-like matches per run. Every one is a flat wall hit: normal y 0, wall top 2.4 to 12 m above the drone. Then the bot presses Space within 0.3 s, from its unstick routine (S plus Space) or its altitude hold. No residual case was a game hop.
- Every flagged "near pad, on its surface" case, checked by screenshot, was a building facade or the depot building hit head-on at street level. Example: `shots/K-alt12-seed22-crash6.jpg` shows a shop front 10 m from the café pad. `D-alt12-seed44-crash2` (the depot front wall) came from a diagnostic run, and I deleted that run's screenshots before the final classify runs. None was a lip, kerb or lawn edge.

**Honest result:** criterion 1 is not a clean 0 at 12 m. The critic's hop-like test cannot tell the bot's own climb after a real wall hit from a hop.

**Real time (crash-classify-rt.mjs, seeds 11, 22, 58, 130):**
- 12 m: 3.2 crashes a minute, 9 deliveries (2.25 a run).
- 40 m: 0.4 crashes a minute, 17 deliveries (4.25 a run).
- I ran the two in parallel. That seems to slow the 40 m bot: seeds 11 and 58 made only 2 deliveries each, with 0 crashes.
- Deterministic deliveries per run: 1.75 at 12 m against 5.4 at 40 m.
- The optional target (12 m at half of 40 m) is **not met**. Most remaining 12 m crashes are real: the straight-line bot flies head-on into 13 to 57 m buildings without avoiding them.

**crash-stakes.mjs (22, 58, 130):**
- 58: 28.5 to 10.8 m/s, -4.8 s (bot reading).
- 130: 16.7 to 7.6 m/s, -3.8 s, combo 2 to 0.
- 22: 16.7 to 3.5 m/s, **free**. The bot boosted at 2 m into the park fountain's centre pillar (`shots/X-seed22-crash.jpg`). The pillar top is 1.4 to 2.2 m above the skids, so by the game's own rule this is a ledge hop. The bot releases the keys at the hit, so the drone does not carry its speed on. I count this as the hop rule working, but it does not pass the critic's "every hit over 8 m/s" line literally.
- On the earlier run, seed 58 was a 13.5 m/s rooftop parapet hop, also free. It is now a full-speed step-over.

**Scrapes:** the free bump counts above are 165 to 231 per run, with no charge.

**arrival-metrics.mjs:**

| Run | Legs | Final-approach timeouts | Longest final | Off screen | Slow and high |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 11, 22, 33, 44 | 43 | 0 | **15.8 s** | 3.2% | 3.2% |
| 7, 58, 91, 130 | 40 | 0 | 4.6 s | 0.9% | 0.3% |
| 11, 11 | 21 | 0 | 3.7 s | 2.1% | 4.1% |

- The second set has 1 timeout, but it is a cruise leg (seed 91), not a final approach. The clock ran out before the bot got within 30 m, as in round 4.
- The 15.8 s final is seed 11, Willow Lofts Rooftop. It is the same leg that took 16.6 s in round 4's builder run. The bot dropped beside a taller tower, stalled 4 times, then landed (`shots/A-seed11-stall-final-approach.jpg`).
- On the re-runs of seed 11, the same leg took 3.7 s both times.

**Other checks:**
- Flat-frame probe: 1,021 frames, **0 flat**.
- Frame time (long-run, 120 s each, bloom on): seed 22 median 8.30 ms, p95 9.80 ms. Seed 58 median 8.30 ms, p95 9.80 ms. 0 frames over 20 ms. This equals round 4.
- `npm run build` passes (JS 693 KB).
- The dev server on port 5188 is stopped.

critic.md
# Drone Dash, round 4 critic report

**Verdict:** Crashes now cost something, and the feedback reads well. But the cost also fires on the game's own ledge hop and on low contacts near pads. So flying low through the city is a trap. The best plan is to cruise above every roof.

## Round 3 gap (crashes had no cost): closed

Scripts are copied to `critic-scripts/`. Only the output folder and image format changed (JPEG, quality 80). Variants with extra logging have their own names.

**crash-stakes.mjs, seeds 22, 58, 130.** 4 runs, 12 hits measured by the bot as a speed loss of more than 8 m/s.
- 11 of 12 cost something within 1 s: 3 or 4 s off the clock, and the combo was lost (x2.0 to 0) every time a combo was running. Example seed 22: 29.2 to 10.5 m/s, clock 31.7 to 27.7 s at the hit, combo 2 to 0, "Hard crash! -4 SEC · x2.0 COMBO LOST" (`critic/X-seed22-crash.jpg`).
- 1 of 12 was free: seed 130, run 1, 14.0 to 5.7 m/s (8.3 m/s in the bot's 30 ms sample), no time lost, no combo running. The game measures loss per frame against a 7 m/s threshold, so this is a borderline case where drag adds to the bot's number. The 3 later seed 130 runs all charged 3 s (`critic/X2-seed130-crash-*.jpg`).
- Scrapes stay free. Across the probes, 363 speed drops of 2 to 7 m/s per sample were not charged. Two charged crashes showed a loss under 6 m/s in the bot's samples (seeds 58 and 22). In both, the real loss happened between samples.
- Score is never taken. Parcels are never lost. That is a fair choice.

**arrival-metrics.mjs, all 8 seeds, twice (plus seed 11 three more times).**

| Run | Seeds | Legs | Final-approach timeouts | Longest final | Sum final / sum cruise | Marker off screen | Slow and high |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | 11, 22, 33, 44 | 42 | 0 | 5.1 s | 129.7 / 201.5 s | 0.7% | 1.0% |
| A2 | 7, 58, 91, 130 | 38 | 0 | 4.4 s | 113.5 / 178.2 s | 0.9% | 0.6% |
| B1 | 11, 22, 33, 44 | 45 | 0 | 5.5 s | 143.9 / 219.0 s | 0.9% | 2.7% |
| B2 | 7, 58, 91, 130 | 42 | 0 | 4.1 s | 129.3 / 228.8 s | 1.0% | 0.1% |
| C | 11, 11, 11 | 33 | 0 | 6.6 s | 113.4 / 157.2 s | 0.6% | **5.5%** |

- All criteria pass on all runs A and B. Median final approach is 3.0 s.
- Two runs in A ended in a cruise leg (seed 44 rooftop pickup, seed 91 street pickup), not in a final approach. The clock ran out before the bot got within 30 m.
- **Seed 11:** no leg went over 10 s in 5 runs (55 seed 11 legs). The slowest leg is the Tailor street pickup at Juniper & 6th Ave: 4.5 to 6.6 s, with about 25% of its final samples slow and more than 4 m above the pad. That alone pushes seed 11 to 5.5% slow and high in run C. Screenshots (`critic/W-seed11-Tailor-2.7s.jpg`, `-5.4s.jpg`) show why: the bot cruises at 40 m. It arrives over a 33 m building beside a deep street canyon. It sits on the roof edge for about 3 s, then drops off. This is the bot's straight-line route, not a game fault. A player sees the pad in the street and comes off the roof at once.

**Flat-frame probe (acceptance-probe.mjs):** 1,003 frames, **0 flat**. Mobile play: 53,397 frames, 0 flat.

## Single biggest remaining gap: the crash cost punishes the ledge hop and low play near pads, so flying low is a trap

The ledge hop is meant to let you skim over parapets, roof boxes and rims. It still removes your forward speed, and the crash check counts that speed loss. So every hop above about 7 m/s head-on is charged as a full crash: minus 3 s and the combo. Low contacts at the pad itself (roof lips, kerbs, park edges) are charged the same way. The player sees "Crash!" for things that look like a skim or a landing.

Evidence (`critic-scripts/crash-classify.mjs` and `crash-classify-rt.mjs`, same bot, cruise at 12 m against 40 m, no boost):
- Low cruise (12 m), 8 seeds: 45 charged crashes. **18 (40%) were hop-like**: the drone rose more than 0.8 m in the next 0.3 s with climb not held. 11 were within 30 m of the target. Real-time repeat on 4 seeds: 20 crashes, 9 hop-like (45%), 5 near the target.
- `critic/K-alt12-seed11-crash3.jpg`: the drone skims a roof box at 21 m, 11.5 to 4 m/s. "Crash! -3 SEC · x1.5 COMBO LOST".
- `critic/R-alt12-seed22-crash7.jpg`: on the grass at 0 m, 10 m from a park pad, 14.5 to 6.8 m/s, "-3 SEC". Nothing in view looks like an obstacle.
- `critic/R-alt12-seed11-crash1.jpg`: clipping the roof lip of the building whose roof holds the pickup pad, 9 m out, combo lost.
- Result for the run (real time, seeds 11, 22, 58, 130): at 12 m the bot crashed 4.6 times a minute. Runs lasted 39 to 80 s, with 8 deliveries in total (scores 0 to 1,487). At 40 m the same bot crashed 0.5 times a minute. Runs lasted 122 to 174 s, with 27 deliveries (scores 3,259 to 6,609). The 40 m mobile run made 12 deliveries in 220 s.

Some low crashes are fair: the 12 m bot also flies straight into taller walls. But 40% of them are the game's own skim helper. In the best arcade city flyers, the low line between buildings is risky and it pays. A ledge you can skim never punishes you. Here the low line costs more and gives nothing back. So you fly over the city, not through it.

**Acceptance test** (start the dev server, run from the game folder):
1. `ALT=12 node progress/round-4/critic-scripts/crash-classify.mjs` and `ALT=20 ...` on all 8 seeds: **0 charged crashes are hop-like** (rose more than 0.8 m within 0.3 s, climb not held). A ledge hop must never show "Crash!".
2. Same runs: 0 charged crashes within 30 m of the target where the drone ends up on the surface it hit (rooftop pad lip, kerb, lawn edge). Use the log fields `hd < 30`, `rose >= 0`, and `y` within 1.5 m of the target height. Check each match by screenshot.
3. No regression: `crash-stakes.mjs` (seeds 22, 58, 130) still charges a cost on every head-on wall hit over 8 m/s, and `arrival-metrics.mjs` still passes on all 8 seeds.
4. Optional design target: in `crash-classify-rt.mjs`, deliveries per run at ALT 12 reach at least half of those at ALT 40 (now 2.0 against 6.75).

## Other gaps (ranked)

1. **Nothing rewards a low or risky line.** Even with fair crashes, high cruise is both the safest and the fastest route. Near misses, low flight or threading a gap earn nothing. A small reward for close, fast flight gives the crash cost a purpose.
2. **Game over does not say why the run ended.** A careless run lost 18 s to 5 crashes in 32 s. The card says only "TIME'S UP", score 0, deliveries 0 (`critic/F-game-over.jpg`). Show crashes and time lost, so the player learns why.
3. **Crash popups cover the nav marker.** The "-4 SEC" chip sits on the "61 m" marker label (`critic/F-crash1-400ms.jpg`). The "-3s" and "+15s" flashes sit half under the timer pill (`critic/K-alt12-seed22-crash1.jpg`).
4. **Rooftop canyons beside street pads.** Seed 11 Tailor pickup: a 33 m building edge next to the pad holds the drone for about 3 s (`critic/W-seed11-Tailor-2.7s.jpg`). It is fair. When the pad is straight below, a small push off the roof edge can help.
5. **Pitched roofs are walls.** A cruise contact with a sloped roof at 12.8 m reads as a crash (`critic/K-alt12-seed22-crash1.jpg`). Players expect to slide up a slope.

## How it plays

- **Crash feedback is readable and strong.** You get a big coral "Crash!" or "Hard crash!" and a chip with seconds and combo lost. The combo badge is struck through. A red flash, shake, hit-stop and a sound follow. It reads at a glance on desktop and on iPhone 13 held sideways. Three tiers (3, 4, 5 s) feel proportionate.
- **Fair on walls, unfair on skims.** Hitting a tower at boost now hurts the right amount. Skimming a roof box or touching a kerb next to the pad hurts the same, and that feels wrong.
- **Landing is free.** Vertical drops onto pads were never charged in any run.
- **Full loop works.** Title, routing, pickups, deliveries, combos, crashes, game over and Fly Again all work. Desktop Enter and mobile tap both restart the clock at 49.5 to 49.7 s. Mobile touch controls stay clear of the HUD. A clean mobile run lasts 220 s with 12 deliveries. A careless run ends in 32 s.

## Performance

- Desktop 1280x720, bloom on, 100 s of active flight: 12,054 frames. **Median 8.30 ms, p95 9.80 ms, p99 10.2 ms, max 10.4 ms.** **0 frames over 20 ms.** Same as round 3 (8.3 / 9.8).
- Mobile emulation (iPhone 13 held sideways, touch), 220 s: 26,270 frames, median 8.30 ms, p95 9.50 ms, 3 frames over 20 ms (max 50 ms).
- First load, production build: **0.71 MB** (JS 690 KB, CSS 17 KB, HTML 6 KB). lil-gui (31 KB) is a separate chunk. Budget 15 MB: pass. The dev server serves 7.0 MB unbundled.

## Screenshots (progress/round-4/critic/)

- Crash stakes: X-seed22-crash, X-seed58-crash, X-seed130-crash, X2-seed*-crash-* (repeats)
- Crash classification, deterministic probe at 12 m: K-alt12-seed11-crash1 to 6, K-alt12-seed22-crash1/7/8
- Real-time probe: R-alt12-seed11-crash1 to 4, R-alt12-seed22-crash5 to 8, R-alt40-seed11-crash1 to 3, R-alt40-seed130-crash4/5
- Trace run: T-alt12-seed58-crash1 to 3
- Seed 11 slow leg: W-seed11-Tailor-0.0s to 6.0s
- Careless desktop flow: F-crash1/2 at 0, 400, 1000 ms, F-game-over, F-restart
- Desktop flow: d01-title to d09-game-over (d09 is taken at the end of a 100 s window, the run was still going)
- Mobile (iPhone 13 held sideways, touch): m01-title to m09-restart

Scripts (progress/round-4/critic-scripts/): crash-stakes.mjs, arrival-metrics.mjs, acceptance-probe.mjs, play-desktop.mjs, play-mobile.mjs and the other round 3 scripts (output path and JPEG only). New: crash-stakes-v.mjs (adds crash counter), crash-classify.mjs, crash-classify-rt.mjs, crash-trace.mjs, arrival-watch.mjs, desktop-crash-flow.mjs.

# Drone Dash, round 4 builder report: crash stakes

## Design

A crash is measured by the speed it takes off the drone (horizontal m/s), summed over the first 0.2 s of one collision. That is the same thing the player feels and the same thing the critic measures.

| Speed lost in one hit | Name | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| under 7 m/s | scrape | free (old spark + thud only) |
| 7 to 16 m/s | Crash | -3 s, combo broken |
| 16 to 26 m/s | Hard crash | -4 s, combo broken |
| 26 m/s and up | Wreck | -5 s, combo broken |

Why this set:
- **Time plus combo, nothing else.** Time is the run's only life bar, so it always matters, even with no combo. The combo break is the sharp extra cost for players who are on a streak. Both are already on screen, so no new meter is needed. I left out parcel damage to keep it to one rule the player can learn.
- **Fair.** One charge per collision: follow-up contacts within 1.2 s only top up to a harder tier, so being pinned against a wall does not drain the clock. A slow slide along a parapet never adds up to a crash (only the first 0.2 s counts). A crash never takes the clock below 1 s, so a crash alone never ends the run.
- **Arrival work stays free.** The guide pull, ledge hop and braking near a pad move at low speed and lose well under 7 m/s. A ledge hop now reports its impact. A full-speed boost into a parapet stops the drone dead, so it is a crash. The gentle hop over a parapet is still free.
- **Readable in the moment.**
  - HUD: a "Hard crash!" pop in coral with "-4 SEC · X2.0 COMBO LOST" under it. A large coral "-4s" drops out beside the timer, and the timer shudders with a coral flash. The combo chip turns coral, keeps the lost multiplier, is struck through, then tips and falls away.
  - VFX: a heavier red vignette (0.45 s) and orange and white spark bursts sized by severity. The camera shakes harder, the hit-stop is a little longer (0.10 to 0.16 s), and the drone tumbles for one second. The parcel swings hard and the status bar blinks red.
  - Audio: a deep crunch (low sine thud plus filtered noise) and a falling two-note "lost it" cue. When a combo breaks, the cue is pitched lower.
- Art direction: the existing palette tokens (coral, ink, cream) and the existing stroke-text pop style.

## Files changed

- `src/game/config.ts`: new `CRASH` block (threshold, tiers, window, chain gap, hit span, clock floor).
- `src/systems/DeliverySystem.ts`: `penalize(seconds, floor, breakCombo)`.
- `src/game/Game.ts`: `checkCrash` (speed-loss measurement, tiers, one charge per collision) and `crashFeedback`. Diagnostics now include `crashes` (a run counter). Existing fields are unchanged, so the bot hooks still work.
- `src/entities/Drone.ts`: `FlightEvents.ledge` (impact absorbed by a ledge hop), `crash()` visual tumble, cargo jolt and red status blink. Flight physics are unchanged.
- `src/ui/Hud.ts`: `flashTimePenalty`, `breakCombo`, heavy `hitFlash`, `crash` pop kind.
- `src/systems/AudioSystem.ts`: `crash()`.
- `src/styles.css`, `index.html`: `#time-penalty`, timer hit shudder, broken combo chip, crash pop, heavy vignette.
- `src/vite-env.d.ts`: an optional `crashes` field in the diagnostics type.
- `src/entities/ObjectiveMarker.ts`: not touched (bloom clamps intact).

## Acceptance numbers

The scripts are copied to `progress/round-4/scripts/`. The logic is unchanged. Only the screenshot folder now points to `progress/round-4/shots/`. `scrape-check.mjs` is my own extra check.

**crash-stakes.mjs (seeds 22, 58, 130), final run:**

| Seed | Before | 1 s after | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| 22 | 28.6 m/s, 33.0 s, combo 2 | 5.8 m/s, 28.8 s, combo 0 | 3.0 s extra off the clock, combo lost |
| 58 | 12.3 m/s, 31.9 s, combo 2 | 1.8 m/s, 26.7 s, combo 0 | 4.0 s extra, combo lost |
| 130 | 21.0 m/s, 35.8 s, combo 0* | 1.1 m/s, 31.5 s | 3.1 s extra |

\*On seed 130 the bot crashed once on the way down to 10 m, so the combo was already broken. Earlier runs: on seed 22, hits at 31.5 and 36 m/s cost 4 s plus the combo. On seed 130, hits at 16 to 17 m/s cost 3 s plus the combo. The 1 s "after" values include 1 s of normal drain.

**Scrapes (scrape-check.mjs, 90 s autopilot on seeds 22, 58, 130):** 126 sampled drops were under 6 m/s. None of them cost anything: no crash, no combo change, no extra time, no score change. 1 drop was over 8 m/s, and it cost 3 s and the combo.

**arrival-metrics.mjs:**

| Run | Legs | Timeouts | Longest final | Sum final / cruise | Off screen | Slow and high |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 11, 22, 33, 44 (run 1) | 41 | 0 | not recorded | 136.5 / 198.9 | 1.0% | 3.5% |
| 11, 22, 33, 44 (run 2) | 45 | 0 | **16.6 s** | 152.7 / 214.6 | 3.7% | 1.9% |
| 7, 58, 91, 130 | 44 | 0 | 4.3 s | 136.0 / 223.5 | 1.0% | 0.2% |
| 11 x3 (re-check) | 33 | 0 | Willow Lofts leg 3.6, 3.6, 4.0 s | 109.2 / 155.2 | 0.6% | 4.2% |

Honest note: run 2 had one 16.6 s final approach (seed 11, Willow Lofts Rooftop, 4 bot stalls and 3 bumps). That breaks the "no final over 10 s" line for that run. I re-ran seed 11 three times, and the same leg took 3.6 to 4.0 s with 0 stalls. Flight physics did not change this round, so I read it as bot variance at that rooftop, but I cannot prove it. Run 1 printed only the summary lines, so its longest final was not recorded.

**Flat-frame probe (acceptance-probe.mjs):** 866 frames, 0 flat. Bloom on.

**Frame time (long-run.mjs, 3 min per seed, 1280x720, bloom on):** seed 22: median 8.30 ms, p95 9.70 ms, max 10.4 ms. Seed 58: median 8.30 ms, p95 9.80 ms, max 10.4 ms. 0 frames over 20 ms. Round 3 was median 8.3 ms, p95 9.8 ms.

**Build:** `npm run build` passes.

Screenshots: `progress/round-4/shots/X-seed22-crash.png`, `X-seed58-crash.png`, `X-seed130-crash.png`.

critic.md
# Drone Dash, round 3 critic report

**Verdict:** Arrivals now feel clean and fair, and the round 2 gap is closed. The game is now too forgiving: a 40 m/s head-on crash costs nothing, so flying fast and badly is never punished.

## Round 2 gap (final approach to street targets): closed

Scripts are copied to `critic-scripts/` with no logic changes. The screenshot folder is relative, so it now writes to `round-3/critic/`.

| Run | Seeds | Legs | Timeouts | Longest final | Sum final / sum cruise | Marker off screen | Slow and >4 m above |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 11, 22, 33, 44 (tuned) | 43 | 0 | 6.6 s | 137.4 / 221.4 s | 0.9% (18 of 2,112) | 3.5% |
| B | 11, 22, 33, 44 (tuned) | 46 | 0 | 4.6 s | 144.3 / 222.7 s | 0.7% (16 of 2,215) | 1.5% |
| C | 7, 58, 91, 130 (new) | 40 | 1 | 4.4 s | 119.5 / 219.4 s | 0.9% (16 of 1,841) | 0.3% |

Round 2 numbers were 46% off screen, 16.6% on a roof, and sum final 180 s against sum cruise 113 s.

- All criteria pass on the tuned seeds in both runs. Median final approach is 3.0 s on street and raised targets alike. There were 0 final-approach stalls.
- On the new seeds, all criteria pass except one timeout. It is not a final-approach failure. On seed 91 the clock ran out 0.5 s into a final approach, after a 40.2 s cruise leg. The bot cruises at 40 m. In that leg it hit a tower taller than that, again and again (`critic/C-seed91-cruise-stuck.png`, 52 m altitude, 147 m out). A re-run with a trace (`cruise-trace.mjs`) gave the same result. This is mostly a bot limit. A player can see the tower and climb. It is listed below as a minor gap.
- Flat-frame probe (`acceptance-probe.mjs`): 1,018 frames, **0 flat**. Mobile play: 14,657 frames, 0 flat.

### How the arrival help feels

- **It is fair and does not fly the game for you.** `assist-probe.mjs` runs 8 seeds with fixed time steps. I committed 10 m from the pad, 7 to 31 m above it. With descend held and no steering, the pad triggered on 6 of 8 legs, median 1.55 s. When I held descend and flew away, it triggered on **0 of 6** legs. The pull never overrides intent.
- **It is generous.** Holding one button 10 m out finishes the drop. The two misses were rooftop pads where the drone sank past the roof edge. That is a fair miss.
- **Camera:** on the final approach it looks down at about 55 to 63 degrees from 13 to 16 m away. The pad and street read clearly (`P-seed22-commit-A.png`). Pitch rate is p50 0.09 rad/s and p95 0.64 rad/s. I saw no sickness-level whipping. The camera came closer than 2.5 m to the drone in 8 of 4,254 samples (min 1.95 m).
- **X-ray ring:** it reads as "the pad is here, behind this". It is small and faint behind bright walls (`A-seed22-stall-final-approach.png`, 16 m out, ring barely visible behind a sunlit wall). It did not confuse me.
- **Ledge hop:** I saw no clipping through roofs in screenshots. Stalls are now rare: 4 street stalls in 6 minutes of long-run play.

## Single biggest remaining gap: crashes have no cost

The drop is no longer the hard part, so the only skill left is routing. Routing has no risk, because hitting a wall costs nothing. In the best arcade delivery flyers, the fun is threading a fast line past towers while a mistake is expensive. Here, full boost straight into a tower is the same as braking.

Evidence (`critic-scripts/crash-stakes.mjs`): two deliveries to build a x2.0 combo with a parcel on board, then boost at 10 m into the first wall.
- Seed 22: 39.8 m/s head-on into a tower (`critic/X-seed22-crash.png`). One second later: time left 30.8 to 29.5 s (normal drain only), combo still 2, score 1,123 unchanged, parcel still carried.
- Seed 58 (12.6 to 1.2 m/s) and seed 130 (15.6 to 0.4 m/s): same result. Nothing lost.
- Mobile play: a chain of 3 bumps from 40.8 to 19.5 m/s, then a delivery 2 s later that *added* time (`critic/m07-bump.png`). Desktop play logs about 4 bumps per minute.
- Combo only resets on a slow delivery, so crashing is in practice the fastest way to brake.

**Acceptance test:** start the dev server and run `node progress/round-3/critic-scripts/crash-stakes.mjs` (seeds 22, 58, 130) unchanged.
1. On every seed, a hit that drops speed by more than 8 m/s must cost something visible and lasting within 1 s. That means at least one of: the combo drops, more than 2 s comes off the clock beyond normal drain, or score is lost. The HUD must show what was lost.
2. Light scrapes must stay free. In `play-desktop.mjs`, bumps that drop speed by less than 6 m/s must change none of these values.
3. No regression: `arrival-metrics.mjs` still passes on seeds 11, 22, 33, 44 and 7, 58, 91, 130 with final-approach criteria as above.

The builder chooses the cost (parcel damage, combo break, time). It must be readable, not a silent number.

## Other gaps (ranked)

1. **Run start still faces away from the first target** (round 2 gap 1, not fixed). At takeoff the marker is pinned at the bottom-right edge, 67 m away. The title copy is still fading over gameplay (`critic/d02-takeoff.png`).
2. **Landing is close to automatic.** Descend held from 10 m finishes 75% of drops in about 1.5 s. Options: a smaller pull radius, or more points for a manual, centred drop, to reward precision.
3. **Towers taller than cruise height trap a straight-line flyer.** Seed 91 cost a 40 s leg and the run (`C-seed91-cruise-stuck.png`). Seed 44 had a 22.8 s cruise. At 52 m the camera looks steeply down, so the tower face fills the view and it is not obvious that you should climb.
4. **The nav marker still covers the objective pill** (round 2 gap 5, not fixed). "Juniper" is hidden (`critic/m03-flight.png`).
5. **At boost the camera trails 13 to 15 m** (p50 13.1 m against 7 to 10 m at cruise). The drone gets small. In 14% of cruise samples it sits in the top 30% of the frame, near the HUD pill (`critic/d08-stuck-near-drop.png`, 30 m/s). The file name is from the script. The drone is not stuck.

## Performance

- Desktop 1280x720, bloom on, 120 Hz: two 3-minute runs (`long-run.mjs`), about 43,000 frames. **Median 8.30 ms, p95 9.80 ms, p99 10.3 ms.** **Max 18.1 ms, 0 frames over 20 ms.** p95 is up 1 ms from round 2 (8.8 ms). There is still large headroom.
- Mobile emulation (iPhone 13 held sideways, touch, post off, 9-pixel probe on): 6,902 frames, median 8.30 ms, p95 9.60 ms, 5 frames over 20 ms, one 492 ms start or compile hitch.
- First load (production build): 0.71 MB (JS 686 KB, CSS 15 KB, HTML 6 KB). lil-gui (31 KB) loads only with `?debug`. Budget 15 MB: pass.
- About 80 to 86 draw calls and 298k triangles.
- The clock now produces pressure: a crude bot run lasts about 3 minutes and 9 deliveries.

## Screenshots (progress/round-3/critic/)

- Arrival help: P-seed11-commit-A/H, P-seed22-commit-A/H, P-seed33-commit-A/H (the title overlay in the seed 33 shots is a test artifact from starting through the test hook)
- Stall and cruise: A-seed22-stall-final-approach (long run), C-seed91-cruise-stuck
- Crashes: X-seed22-crash, X-seed58-crash, X-seed130-crash
- Long run end: L-seed22-end, L-seed58-end
- Desktop flow: d01-title to d09-game-over
- Mobile (iPhone 13 held sideways, touch): m01-title to m09-restart

Scripts (progress/round-3/critic-scripts/): arrival-metrics.mjs, acceptance-probe.mjs (copied, unchanged logic), assist-probe.mjs, cruise-trace.mjs, long-run.mjs, cam-distance.mjs, crash-stakes.mjs, play-desktop.mjs, play-mobile.mjs.
builder.md
# Round 3 builder note: final approach to street-level targets

## Causes found
I traced the critic's autopilot sample by sample. I also read the colliders around each slow target.

1. **The camera never looked down at the pad.** The chase camera keeps a shallow pitch. Take a pad 20 m below and 10 m ahead. It sits about 60 degrees below the horizon. The vertical FOV is only 60 degrees, so the pad leaves the frame. Only a special case for "far and high" existed.
2. **Parapets pinned the drone on roofs.** Every flat roof has a 0.7 m parapet that is solid. A drone that lands on a roof and flies toward the edge hits the parapet with its contact normal mostly horizontal. It bounces back. Holding descend pulls it back down, so it stays inside the parapet ring. This was the main roof stall (seed 44 pharmacy: the pad is 1.6 m past the parapet of a 6.6 m building).
3. **The drone arrived over the pad while still high.** It drops at 10 m/s, and the bot starts its descent 25 m out. It then reaches the pad at 20 to 30 m altitude, hovers, drifts and wobbles, and often settles on the next roof. Boost speed bled off at 35% of the normal drag, so arrivals after a boost overshot by 10 to 20 m.
4. **Tree colliders started too low.** Each one is a box that starts at the lowest point of the canopy. The round canopy is an ellipsoid, so the lower corners of the box were invisible. At street level they wedged the drone between a facade and a tree (seed 22 Records: 4 stalls).
5. **Some pads were hidden behind a tower.** From the arrival side, a tower stood in the way. One example is seed 44 Deli on Copper & 4th, beside a 70 m tower. Coming from the far side, a straight approach runs into the tower wall. This is the critic's original seed-44 screenshot.
6. The trigger radius and the landing tolerance were not the problem. I did not change them.

## Changes (and why)
- **Approach camera** (`CameraRig.ts`, `CAMERA.approach*`). The effect starts when the target is within 45 m and more than 2 m below. It is fully on at 18 m. The camera rises up to 4.5 m and pulls in 18%. It pitches down until the pad sits in the lower part of the frame. The pitch is capped so the drone stays in frame. Only the pitch changes, so the heading still follows the drone. The effect blends in over about 0.4 s.
- **Through-roof ground ring** (`ObjectiveMarker.ts`). This is an additive ring with no depth test, drawn at the pad. You can see where the pad is through roofs and towers from 6 to 90 m. It uses a basic material and no `pow()`. The round-2 beam and wall clamps are untouched.
- **Ledge hop** (`Drone.ts`, `FLIGHT.hop*`). Some obstacles are low: their top is less than 2.2 m above the skids, with nothing taller behind. If you fly into one, the drone skims up over it instead of bouncing. This covers parapets, roof units and fountain rims. Collision still applies. The hop only adds lift.
- **Faster drop, crisper stop** (`FLIGHT.descendSpeed` 16, `sinkBrakeResponse` 7). Climb stays at 10 m/s. Getting down to a street drop now feels snappy. When you release descend, the drop stops fast, so you do not sink past a roof edge.
- **Dive airbrake.** Within 28 m of the pad, when you descend, leftover boost speed bleeds at the normal rate. So you do not sail past the pad.
- **Drop guide** (`FLIGHT.guide*`). The guide works within 11 m of the pad. You must be descending, or hovering less than 6 m above the pad. The drone then eases toward the pad centre at up to 6 m/s. Pulling back weakens the pull, and climbing or boosting cancels it.
- **Tree colliders fit the canopy** (`CityGenerator.ts`). The canopy box now starts where the ellipsoid is as wide as the box (2.2 x scale instead of 1.6 x scale). A thin trunk collider was added. Pines are unchanged.
- **Pad placement** (`DeliverySystem.ts`). When possible, the game picks a next target that you can glide to. The test line runs from 25 m out on the arrival side to the pad, and must clear solid buildings. This uses the same `isClear` test the first pickup already used. When nothing else fits, hidden pads still appear.

## Files changed
- src/systems/CameraRig.ts
- src/entities/ObjectiveMarker.ts (ring only, bloom clamps intact)
- src/entities/Drone.ts
- src/game/config.ts
- src/game/Game.ts (gives the active pad to the drone, clears it at game over)
- src/systems/DeliverySystem.ts
- src/world/CityGenerator.ts
- src/systems/DebugTools.ts (descendSpeed slider)

Debug hooks and diagnostics fields are unchanged.

## Acceptance numbers
The original `arrival-metrics.mjs` saves stall screenshots into `progress/round-2/critic/`, and I must not edit round 2. So I ran a copy in which only the `OUT` path differs (a scratch folder). I checked the logic with a `diff` against the original. Default seeds 11, 22, 33, 44, default URL, bloom on.

| run | legs / timeouts | longest final | sum final vs sum cruise | marker off screen | slow and >4 m above |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| round 2 (critic) | 28 / 1 | 32.4 s | 180.0 vs 112.9 | 46.1% | 16.6% |
| final A | 46 / 0 | 6.5 s | 148.3 vs 222.8 | 0.6% | 1.8% |
| final B | 41 / 0 | 6.8 s | 136.0 vs 203.3 | 0.7% | 4.4% |

- Stalls in the final approach: 0 in both final runs (round 2: 24).
- Run-to-run variance is real. Two runs before the last two tweaks (crisper stop, guide range 8 to 11 m) each had one 18 to 20 s leg. Slow-and-high has ranged from 1.5% to 5.2% across builds, and was 1.8% and 4.4% on the final build. It comes from 1 to 2 s spells resting on a neighbouring roof or tree top before the hop or guide frees the drone.
- `acceptance-probe.mjs` (unmodified): 1,025 frames, 0 flat.
- `npm run build`: passes (JS 686 KB).
- Frame time (`play-desktop.mjs` copy, 1280x720, bloom on, 120 Hz): median 8.30 ms. p95 was 9.2 to 9.9 ms across runs, with 0 frames over 20 ms.
  - This p95 is higher than the critic's 8.8 ms. I ran an A/B with the new camera, guide and ring disabled, and it gave the same p95 (9.7 ms). So the difference is machine load (other sessions and dev servers were running), not this change.
  - The runs are also about 20k frames long now, against 8k in round 2, because the bot makes more deliveries.

## Screenshots (progress/round-3/)
- approach-20m.png: the camera rises and frames the beam at 41 m.
- approach-9m.png: street level, the pad framed beside the facade.
- xray-ring-through-tower.png: from an intermediate build. The ring shows the pad through a tower. That target type is now avoided from that side.

critic.md
# Drone Dash, round 2 critic report

**Verdict:** The blank bloom render is fixed and the game now flies cleanly on desktop and mobile. The weakest part is now the last 30 m of every street-level leg: the drone settles on a roof, the target is out of view, and the clock runs out.

## Round 1 gap: closed

- Acceptance probe (`critic-scripts/acceptance-probe.mjs`), default URL, 1280x720, `renderer.post === true`:
  - W+Space 3 s: 326 frames, 0 flat (fewest distinct samples in a frame: 8 of 9)
  - W+E 3 s: 337 frames, 0 flat
  - W+A 3 s: 335 frames, 0 flat
  - **Total 998 frames, 0 flat. PASS.** Round 1 was 187 of 331 flat.
- `play-desktop.mjs` (round 1 script, copied to `critic-scripts/play-desktop.mjs`, now logs retries): **all 10 screenshots saved on the first try**. Every file is 351 KB or larger. PASS.
- Other ways to find a blank frame: `long-session.mjs` ran the 9-pixel probe on every frame through 2 runs. That covered climbing, boosting, a deliberate boost crash at 6 m, 4 deliveries, game over, the over screen, and an Enter restart. **29,422 frames, 0 flat, 0 read errors.** Mobile (post off) had 18,192 frames and 0 flat.

## Single biggest remaining gap: the final approach to street-level targets

Flying between targets feels good. Arriving at street-level targets does not. On the way down, the drone lands on whatever roof is between it and the pad. The chase camera then sits low behind the drone and shows only roof surface and parapet. The target is below the roof edge, and the nav marker is stuck at the bottom of the screen with a down arrow. The player has no view of the pad and no clear way down to it. This is the same problem round 1 listed as gap 1. It is now the main cost in a run.

Evidence (`critic-scripts/arrival-metrics.mjs`, seeds 11, 22, 33, 44, desktop, bloom on). The autopilot steers at the marker and cruises at 40 m. Inside 25 m it descends. If it stalls for 3 s, it backs off and climbs. It plays like a casual player who flies straight at the marker.
- Run A: 28 legs. **The last 30 m took 180.0 s in total. The cruise took 112.9 s.** The last 30 m is about a quarter of the distance. It used 61% of travel time. 6 of 28 legs needed more than 10 s for the last 30 m (32.4, 19.1, 13.7, 11.7, 10.0 s, and one that never arrived). 21 of 24 stalls were on street-level targets (y < 2).
- Run B (same seeds, plus visibility sampling): last 30 m 128.4 s, cruise 84.7 s. **In 3 of 4 runs, the clock ran out during a final approach.** I took 3,275 final-approach samples. **The nav marker was off screen in 46.1% of them.** In 16.6%, the drone was slower than 3 m/s and more than 4 m above the target. That means it sat on a roof.
- Desktop autopilot run (`play-desktop.mjs`): it hovered on a roof at 23 m altitude, 17 m from the "Noodle Bar" street drop, for 30 s until time ran out. The camera was jammed into the drone (`critic/d08-stuck-near-drop.png`).
- Screenshots: `critic/A-seed44-stall-final-approach.png` (6 m from the pharmacy drop; the drone sits on a roof at 7 m and only the roof shows), `critic/A-seed22-stall-final-approach.png` (27 m, roof parapet, marker pinned bottom), `critic/A-seed11-stall-final-approach.png`, `critic/A-seed33-stall-final-approach.png`.
- The trigger is not too small. The pickup zone is about 4.1 m for a rooftop and about 3.9 m for a doorstep, which roughly matches the drawn pad. The problem is view and route, not the hit radius.

The best arcade delivery flyers handle the drop moment in a few ways. They tilt the camera to look down at the target as you close in. They keep the pad or beam readable through occluding roofs. And they gently pull the craft into the zone, or over the edge, once you commit to it. The builder can choose how to fix it.

**Acceptance test:** Start the dev server. Run `node progress/round-2/critic-scripts/arrival-metrics.mjs` without changing the script (default seeds 11, 22, 33, 44, default URL, bloom on). It must print:
1. 0 timeouts (no run ends during a final approach), and no leg with `final` over 10 s.
2. `sum final` at or below `sum cruise`.
3. Nav marker off screen in under 15% of final-approach samples.
4. "slow and >4 m above target" under 5% of final-approach samples.

Rerun `acceptance-probe.mjs` too: 0 flat frames, so the fix does not break the round 1 fix.

## Other gaps (ranked)

1. **Run start still faces the wrong way.** I pressed Enter and gave no input. The camera flew in from 237 m away to 7.5 m in about 0.7 s. After that, the target nav marker stays off screen for the full 2.5 s sampled, on desktop and on mobile (`start-probe.mjs`). The first pickup sits at the left edge, 78 m away (`critic/d02-takeoff.png`, and after restart `critic/L05-restart-300ms.png`, 47 m to the left). The title copy is still fading over gameplay at 300 ms. Test: within 1.0 s of Enter, with no input, the nav marker is on screen and within 25% of screen width from center.
2. **Crashes have no stake.** A boost crash into a wall at 6 m altitude dropped speed from 17.9 to 9.5 m/s. 600 ms later the drone was at 1.4 m/s with no time lost (`critic/L01-crash-frame.png`, `L02`, `L03`). Typical runs log 5 or 6 bumps. Walls slow you down but never feel dangerous.
3. **The camera crowds the drone near walls.** In the long session, camera-to-drone distance fell under 2.5 m in 110 of 28,990 playing frames. The minimum was 1.92 m. When wedged, the props fill the screen (`critic/d08-stuck-near-drop.png`). This is rare but ugly, and it overlaps with the main gap.
4. **No difficulty curve.** Legs stay the same kind of task from start to end. The +17 to +19 s time bonuses keep the clock generous. Three deliveries (1,459) earned "New best" (`critic/L04-game-over.png`).
5. **The nav marker covers the objective pill.** The target can be ahead and above. Then the arrow and distance chip sit over the objective name. See `critic/m03-flight.png`, where "Juniper" is hidden, and `critic/m07-bump.png`.

What meets the bar:
- Golden-hour art and a city that reads at a glance.
- The drone model, the beam and the pad ring.
- Pop text and combo chip (`critic/d07-delivery.png`), and a clean game-over card.
- A clean mobile HUD with no control overlaps. The stick is 110 px, climb and descend are 54 px, boost is 76 px.

Physics feels weighty but controllable:
- Climb: 12.9 m in 1.5 s.
- 0 to 16 m/s: 1.95 s.
- Coast to a stop: 1.8 s over 8.9 m.
- S brakes from 15 m/s in 0.37 s.

## Performance

- Desktop 1280x720, bloom on, Apple GPU via ANGLE, 120 Hz. `play-desktop.mjs` with no per-frame readback: 8,306 frames (about 70 s of active flight). **Median 8.30 ms, p95 8.80 ms, p99 9.2 ms, max 9.4 ms, 0 frames over 20 ms.** 60 fps is met with large headroom.
- There is one hitch of about 241 ms on the first gameplay frame after Enter (`start-probe.mjs`), likely shader compile.
- With the 9-pixel readback running every frame (`long-session.mjs`): p95 16.7 ms and 30 frames over 20 ms. That is cost from the probe, not from the game.
- Mobile emulation (iPhone 13 held sideways, DPR 2, post off): 8,668 frames, median 8.3 ms, p95 9.1 ms, 6 frames over 20 ms, one max of 499 ms (a start or compile hitch). Confirm on a real device.
- First load: dev server 6.95 MB over 35 requests. The production build loads about 0.70 MB (JS 683 KB, CSS 15 KB, HTML 6 KB; source maps are not fetched). Both are well under the 15 MB budget. Draw calls are 66 to 85, with about 291k triangles.

## Note on test tooling

The first mobile run looked like the descend button climbed. It was my driver: CDP `touchEnd` ends the touch points it lists, so I lifted the stick finger instead of the button finger (`critic-scripts/mobile-lift-check.mjs`). With the fix, the touch controls work correctly. Not a game bug.

## Screenshots (progress/round-2/critic/)

- Desktop flow: d01-title, d02-takeoff, d03-flying, d04-near-pickup, d05-parcel-picked, d06-carrying-enroute, d07-delivery, d08-stuck-near-drop, d08b-after-bump, d09-game-over
- Long session: L01-crash-frame, L02-crash-plus120ms, L03-after-crash-600ms, L04-game-over, L05-restart-300ms
- Arrival stalls: A-seed11/22/33/44-stall-final-approach

builder.md
# Round 2 builder note: blank desktop render with bloom on

## Root cause
The objective sky beam (and its ring wall) shader computed `pow(1.0 - vUv.y, ...)`. The composer renders into a 4x MSAA HalfFloat target, and on partly covered edge pixels MSAA evaluates varyings at the pixel centre, so `vUv.y` lands just above 1.0 on the beam's top rim and `pow()` of a negative base returns NaN (about 15 to 18 pixels near the top of the screen). The clamp pass lets NaN through (NaN fails every comparison), and UnrealBloomPass blurs it across every mip, so the composite becomes NaN everywhere and the output shows one flat colour.

How it was proven: per-pass readback on a blank frame showed NaN first appearing in the RenderPass output (18 values), the high-pass target at 9 values, and the bloom output at 100% NaN. Hiding each visible object in turn on that frame showed that only hiding the beam mesh brought the NaN count to 0. The same frame rendered to non-MSAA Half or Float targets had no NaN, which matches the MSAA extrapolation explanation.

## Fix
`src/entities/ObjectiveMarker.ts`: clamp `vUv.y` (wall and beam) and `vFacing` (beam) to [0,1] before `pow()`. No change to the post chain, bloom settings or quality. The look is unchanged.

## Files changed
- src/entities/ObjectiveMarker.ts

## Acceptance test (1280x720, default URL, Playwright chromium, `renderer.post === true`)
- W+Space 3 s: 329 frames, 0 blank
- W+E 3 s: 296 frames, 0 blank
- W+A 3 s: 309 frames, 0 blank
- Total: 934 frames, 0 blank (was 184 of 323 for W+Space before the fix)
- play-desktop.mjs (copy that writes to a scratch folder so progress/round-1 stays untouched): all 10 screenshots saved on the first try, smallest 365 KB
- Frame time (play-desktop, 8,265 frames): median 8.30 ms, p95 9.00 ms, p99 9.30 ms, max 9.4 ms, 0 over 20 ms (round 1: median 8.3, p95 9.1)
- `npm run build`: passes

critic.md
# Drone Dash, round 1 critic report

**Verdict:** A charming, well-built arcade courier game that is unplayable on desktop as shipped. With bloom on (the desktop default), the 3D view turns into a flat orange screen for most of the flight.

## The single biggest gap: the desktop render goes blank in flight

With the default desktop settings (post-processing on), the whole 3D view regularly turns into one flat peach-orange colour. Only the HUD stays visible. This happens while you climb, boost, hover high, and even hover still at 14 m. It lasts for seconds at a time, and some single frames flicker back to normal, so it strobes. With `?post=0` the same flight renders perfectly. On touch devices post-processing is off by default, so mobile does not have the bug.

Evidence:
- I read back pixels inside the page after each frame (9 sample points per frame, Apple M5 Metal GPU through ANGLE). While I held W+Space for 3 s, **187 of 331 frames (56%)** were one flat colour with post on. With `?post=1` it was 202/348, and with `?post=0` it was **0/361**. Script: `critic-scripts/pixel-probe.mjs`, `pixel-probe2.mjs`.
- Key probe (`critic-scripts/key-probe.mjs`): standing still and W alone render fine. After about 0.6 s of W+Space the view goes flat. W+E (boost) was flat for 6 of 8 screenshots.
- In a full autopilot run, my screenshot helper retried 25 times over about 1 s and still could not get a non-blank frame at four key moments: `critic/d03-flying-BLANK.png`, `d04-near-pickup-BLANK.png`, `d05-parcel-picked-BLANK.png`, `d08b-after-bump-BLANK.png`. Also `d10-blank-frame-post-on.png` and `probe-boost-held.png`.
- The same moments with post off look great: `critic/nopost-d03-flying.png`, `nopost-d08b-after-bump.png`, `nopost-d06-carrying-enroute.png`.
- The camera is not inside a building. During blank frames it was in open air at y 40 to 48 (logged in the probe run). The background colour you see is the sky/fog horizon colour, which means the post chain outputs a flat result. A NaN or Inf from an HDR highlight that spreads through bloom is a likely cause, but the builder must find the real cause.

**Acceptance test the builder must pass:**
Load `http://127.0.0.1:5188/` with default settings (no URL params) in Playwright with channel `chromium` at 1280x720. Press Enter, then hold W+Space for 3 s, W+E for 3 s, and W+A for 3 s. After every rAF, read back 9 pixels spread across the canvas. **Zero frames may have all 9 samples identical** (the same metric as `critic-scripts/pixel-probe.mjs`). Bloom must stay on, with `renderer.post === true` in `__THREE_GAME_DIAGNOSTICS__`. Then run `node progress/round-1/critic-scripts/play-desktop.mjs`. Every screenshot in `critic/` it writes must succeed on the first try, with no file under about 100 KB.

## Other gaps for later rounds (ranked)
1. **Arrival is fiddly.** Pickup radius is 3.2 m and the vertical tolerance is tight. My autopilot circled a rooftop pickup 4.4 m away for over 4 s, and twice hovered on a roof edge 21 to 24 m from a street-level drop it could not drop down to (`nopost-d08-stuck-near-drop.png`). A good arcade courier game pulls you into the zone at the end of the approach, or shows a clear landing cone so the player knows where to descend.
2. **Collisions feel like walls of rubber, not crashes.** I logged 5 to 7 bumps per run. Speed drops from about 30 to 10 m/s with a small flash. There is no visible drone wobble or spin and no lasting penalty, so walls never feel dangerous. The timer is the only stake.
3. **Boost is tiny on mobile.** One 2 s boost press drained the bar almost to empty and flung the drone out over the water (`m03-boost-turn.png`). The boost button sits right next to climb, so it is easy to hit by mistake.
4. **Run start is disorienting.** At 0.3 s the title text is still fading over the gameplay view, and the target is 78 m away behind your left shoulder (`d02-takeoff.png`). The drone should spawn facing the first pickup with the camera already behind it.
5. **No sense of difficulty curve.** Three legs per run, all of the same kind. Time bonuses (+19 s) make the clock generous early and nothing ramps up. Two deliveries scored 1,188 and earned "New best" (`d09-game-over.png`).

What already meets the bar: the golden-hour art direction, readable building silhouettes, the drone model with banking, the strong objective beam and pad ring (`nopost-d08b-after-bump.png`), the edge-of-screen nav arrow with distance, the clear pop text and combo chip (`d07-delivery.png`), and a clean game-over card. The best polished browser arcade flyers have a camera that never hides the target, a world that reads at a glance, landings that snap in, and impacts you feel in the controller. The main things missing here are the stable render and the landing snap.

## Performance
- Desktop, 1280x720, Apple M5 on a 120 Hz display, about 85 s of active autopilot flight (10,283 rAF samples): **median 8.3 ms, p95 9.1 ms, p99 9.3 ms, max 10.3 ms, 0 frames over 20 ms.** In an earlier run there was a single 300 ms hitch on the first gameplay frame, likely shader compile. It is locked at 120 fps, so 60 fps is met with large headroom. The blank frames cost no time, so they are not a perf symptom.
- With post off: median 8.3 ms, p95 9.0 ms, one 151 ms hitch at start.
- Draw calls 71 to 85, about 291k triangles.
- First-load transfer (dev server, unminified): **6.95 MB over 35 requests**, under the 15 MB budget. The existing `dist/` is 4.1 MB on disk.
- Mobile (iPhone 13 landscape viewport, DPR 2, post off): 120 fps reported most of the time. One reading of 33.7 fps came during a boost and turn with two CDP touches held. This is unconfirmed and needs a real device check.

- nopost-d01-title.png to nopost-d09-game-over.png (the same flow with `?post=0`)
